alerting.journeyCheck.intervalMinutes.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_ALERTING_JOURNEY_CHECK_INTERVAL_MINUTES within the declared range and set `OnUnitActiveSec` in the host's `docsfab-journey-check.timer` systemd unit to the same cadence.
alerting.journeyCheck.intervalMinutes.rationale: How often the host-side journey health-check timer runs (issue 645, owner address the gaps 2026-09-29). J3 ran at about 20% success for hours before anyone looked; 30 minutes is fast enough to catch a multi-hour degradation early without adding a second host job for every dispatcher tick. The minimum keeps one run's own read-only queries from overlapping the next; the maximum is one day, the digest's own cadence, below which a health check that runs less than daily would miss the digest's purpose entirely.
alerting.journeyCheck.intervalMinutes.docSummary: How often the journey health-check timer runs.

alerting.journeyCheck.dedupeWindowMinute.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_ALERTING_JOURNEY_CHECK_DEDUPE_WINDOW_MINUTES within the declared range; a shorter window posts more repeats of the same still-open failure, a longer one delays the next repeat if the first alert is missed.
alerting.journeyCheck.dedupeWindowMinute.rationale: One alert message per failure class per window (owner decision 2026-09-28, clearly labelled messages, posted to the project's report channel, which is docsfab-status since owner decision 2026-10-09). At the 30-minute check interval, 4 hours is 8 checks; a still-failing journey or host signal gets one Slack message for the first check that finds it, then silence for the rest of that span instead of a new message every 30 minutes, while a genuinely new failure a few hours later still gets its own alert. The minimum keeps a repeat further apart than the check interval itself (or every run would count as new); the maximum is one week, so a long-open incident still gets a fresh reminder before the pilot's own weekly cadence.
alerting.journeyCheck.dedupeWindowMinute.docSummary: One alert per failure class within this window; a still-failing class stays silent until it elapses.

alerting.journeyCheck.digestIntervalMinu.rationale: The one short daily digest the task names, independent of whether anything is failing. One day matches the existing daily `journeys.py status` scoreboard cadence and the pilot's own daily hypervisor-snapshot rhythm, so on-call reads one digest per day rather than one per check. The minimum is one hour (finer than that is an alert, not a digest); the maximum is one week.
alerting.journeyCheck.digestIntervalMinu.docSummary: How often the daily digest posts, regardless of journey health.

alerting.journeyCheck.serviceLogTailByte.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_ALERTING_JOURNEY_CHECK_SERVICE_LOG_TAIL_BYTES within the declared range; a smaller bound may miss an older catalog-fingerprint refusal line between checks, a larger one costs more read time on every run.
alerting.journeyCheck.serviceLogTailByte.rationale: Bytes read from the tail of `/var/log/docsfab/service.log` to count `docsfab.forge-change-source.catalog-fingerprint` refusal lines (host health signal 3 of 3). 64 KiB comfortably covers several hundred JSON log lines, more than one run's worth at the 30-minute check interval on the pilot's observed log volume, without reading the whole file on every check. The maximum, 10 MiB, is a generous multiple of that for a much noisier host; the minimum keeps the scan from being too small to span even one check interval.
alerting.journeyCheck.serviceLogTailByte.docSummary: Bytes of service.log tail scanned per check for catalog-fingerprint refusal lines.

alerting.journeyCheck.docsfabStatusTimeo.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_ALERTING_JOURNEY_CHECK_DOCSFAB_STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS within the declared range; `docsfab-status` itself bounds its own loopback probe well under this, so a timeout here means the process did not exit at all.
alerting.journeyCheck.docsfabStatusTimeo.rationale: Wall-clock bound on the one `docsfab-status` subprocess call the check makes (host-health signal 1 of 3). `docsfab-status` bounds its own `/healthz` probe with `deploy.statusProbeTimeoutSeconds` (a few seconds) and reads a small number of log lines, so 30 seconds is generous headroom above its expected runtime without letting a wedged child block the whole 30-minute check cycle. The minimum is one second, below which even a healthy fast host could false-positive; the maximum keeps one signal from starving the rest of the run against `alerting.journeyCheck.intervalMinutes`.
alerting.journeyCheck.docsfabStatusTimeo.docSummary: Wall-clock bound on the docsfab-status subprocess call.

alerting.journeyCheck.docsfabStatusMaxBu.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_ALERTING_JOURNEY_CHECK_DOCSFAB_STATUS_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES within the declared range; `docsfab-status --logs` is the only flag this check could add that would need more, and this check never passes `--logs`.
alerting.journeyCheck.docsfabStatusMaxBu.rationale: Largest combined stdout the `docsfab-status` subprocess may produce before Node's `execFile` refuses it (host-health signal 1 of 3). Without `--logs` (never passed here) its output is a handful of small tables, so 1 MiB is generous headroom; the minimum, 64 KiB, still comfortably covers that output, and the maximum matches other dispatcher byte allowances in `config/limits/host.yaml` rather than inventing a new order of magnitude.
alerting.journeyCheck.docsfabStatusMaxBu.docSummary: Largest docsfab-status subprocess output the check buffers before refusing it.

alerting.journeyCheck.healthzTimeoutMs.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_ALERTING_JOURNEY_CHECK_HEALTHZ_TIMEOUT_MS within the declared range; a loopback request over this bound on a live host is itself worth investigating, not just extending.
alerting.journeyCheck.healthzTimeoutMs.rationale: Wall-clock bound on the one loopback `GET /healthz` call the check makes to read `pendingForgeEffects` (host-health signal 2 of 3), independent of the separate `docsfab-status` subprocess call. `service-status.sh`'s own equivalent probe uses `deploy.statusProbeTimeoutSeconds` (a few seconds); 15 seconds is headroom above that for a loopback call with no network hop. The minimum is one second; the maximum keeps this one signal from consuming half of `alerting.journeyCheck.intervalMinutes` by itself.
alerting.journeyCheck.healthzTimeoutMs.docSummary: Wall-clock bound on the loopback /healthz request.

alerting.journeyCheck.successRateWarnRat.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_ALERTING_JOURNEY_CHECK_SUCCESS_RATE_WARN_RATIO within the declared range; a higher ratio alerts on milder degradation, a lower one waits for a worse run.
alerting.journeyCheck.successRateWarnRat.rationale: The task's own motivating case (issue 645) was a partial outage, not a total one -- a journey at about 20 percent success for hours, which the pure last-success state alone reads as LIVE the moment even one attempt still succeeds within a day. Below this fraction of successful attempts in the last 24 hours (and at or above successRateMinAttempts, so a single failed attempt out of one is never a false alarm) the journey counts as failing for alert purposes, alongside the existing no-success-in-7-days state. One half is worse than a coin flip and clearly a working journey in name only; it is not zero, because zero would miss exactly the case this limit exists to catch.
alerting.journeyCheck.successRateWarnRat.docSummary: Below this share of successful attempts in 24 hours, a journey alerts even though it still shows a recent success.

alerting.journeyCheck.successRateMinAtte.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_ALERTING_JOURNEY_CHECK_SUCCESS_RATE_MIN_ATTEMPTS within the declared range; a lower value judges a ratio from fewer samples and risks a false alarm on one failed attempt.
alerting.journeyCheck.successRateMinAtte.rationale: The fewest attempts in 24 hours before the success-rate signal (alerting.journeyCheck.successRateWarnRatio) judges a journey by its ratio rather than staying silent. One failed attempt out of one is 0 percent and would otherwise always alert; three is enough that a single failure is at most a third, below the default warn ratio only when at least two of three have failed.
alerting.journeyCheck.successRateMinAtte.docSummary: Fewest 24-hour attempts before the success-rate signal judges a journey by ratio.

alerting.hostHealth.outboxBacklogWarnCou.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_ALERTING_HOST_HEALTH_OUTBOX_BACKLOG_WARN_COUNT within the declared range; investigate `docsfab.forge-outbox.stalled` in service.log before raising it.
alerting.hostHealth.outboxBacklogWarnCou.rationale: Host-health signal 2 of 3, the outbox backlog — above this many pending forge effects (`/healthz`'s own `pendingForgeEffects`, the same field the window runbook already reads as healthz degraded — knowledge, pendingForgeEffects N) the check treats the backlog itself as a failing signal, separately from whichever journey it is blocking. One in-flight merge reconciliation is routine (observed on the pilot mid-deploy); 25 is an order of magnitude above that single-digit steady state without waiting for the backlog to be large enough to also starve every journey before anyone is told.
alerting.hostHealth.outboxBacklogWarnCou.docSummary: Pending forge outbox effects above this count are reported as an unhealthy backlog.

alerting.hostHealth.catalogFingerprintRe.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_ALERTING_HOST_HEALTH_CATALOG_FINGERPRINT_REFUSAL_WARN_COUNT within the declared range only to tolerate a known, already-diagnosed source of the refusal; the persistence-chain pins (COMMON-RULES rule 19) are the actual fix.
alerting.hostHealth.catalogFingerprintRe.rationale: Host-health signal 3 of 3, catalog fingerprint refusals — `forge-change-source/postgres.ts` writes one `docsfab.forge-change-source.catalog-fingerprint` line to service.log every time the connected cluster's `service_catalog_fingerprint` does not match the pinned `FORGE_CHANGE_SOURCE_CATALOG_FINGERPRINT_PG16/17`. On a correctly pinned, deployed pilot this never happens, so the default is zero — any occurrence at all is worth naming in an alert. The maximum, 1000, still refuses a runaway retry loop from paging on every single line individually once the first alert has already fired (the de-duplication window in `alerting.journeyCheck.dedupeWindowMinutes` is what actually stops the repeats).
alerting.hostHealth.catalogFingerprintRe.docSummary: Any catalog-fingerprint refusal line in the scanned log tail is reported as unhealthy.

alerting.dailyRun.deadlineMinutes.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_ALERTING_DAILY_RUN_DEADLINE_MINUTES within the declared range; it counts minutes after midnight America/Los_Angeles, so 480 is 08:00 Pacific in summer and winter alike.
alerting.dailyRun.deadlineMinutes.rationale: When, in minutes after midnight America/Los_Angeles (the zone a daily run's day is counted in), the journey health check starts reporting that today's nightly benchmark run is missing from the dashboard's published progress page. Owner decision 2026-10-12 - the nightly publishes a result every morning, partial results included, and if none is published by 08:00 Pacific the owner sees it in the status channel. Before the deadline the advisory signal reads healthy, so a run still in progress never alerts. The range is the minutes of one day.
alerting.dailyRun.deadlineMinutes.docSummary: Minutes after midnight Pacific by which today's nightly benchmark run must be published before the health check reports it missing.

alerting.dailyRun.progressTimeoutMs.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_ALERTING_DAILY_RUN_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_MS within the declared range; a loopback read of a static file that takes longer than this is worth investigating on the dashboard server, not only extending.
alerting.dailyRun.progressTimeoutMs.rationale: Wall-clock bound on the one loopback GET of the dashboard's published progress.json that the advisory daily-run signal makes each check, body included. The dashboard server answers a static file on loopback, so this is the same headroom alerting.journeyCheck.healthzTimeoutMs gives the loopback health probe. A slower answer reads as an unreadable page, alerted only after the deadline, and never fails the check. The minimum is one second; the maximum keeps one advisory read from consuming a large share of alerting.journeyCheck.intervalMinutes.
alerting.dailyRun.progressTimeoutMs.docSummary: Wall-clock bound on the loopback GET of the dashboard's progress.json.

alerting.dailyRun.progressMaxBytes.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_ALERTING_DAILY_RUN_PROGRESS_MAX_BYTES within the declared range when the published progress.json legitimately grew past this bound, as its run list grows with the nightly history; a page larger than the maximum needs the dashboard to publish less, not a larger read.
alerting.dailyRun.progressMaxBytes.rationale: Largest progress.json body the advisory daily-run signal reads into memory before it reports the page unreadable with this limit's refusal. Measured 2026-10-12 on synthetic pages - about 0.1 MiB with two weeks of history, and 0.94 MiB with a year of two runs a day, since the page lists every daily run it holds. 16 MiB is many years of that growth with the requested headroom; the maximum keeps a runaway page from being buffered by a host timer job.
alerting.dailyRun.progressMaxBytes.docSummary: Largest dashboard progress.json body the daily-run signal reads.

alerting.backup.timerIntervalHours.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_ALERTING_BACKUP_TIMER_INTERVAL_HOURS within the declared range and set `OnCalendar` in the host's `docsfab-backup.timer` systemd unit to the same cadence.
alerting.backup.timerIntervalHours.rationale: How often the scheduled `docsfab-backup` systemd timer runs the existing backup identity end to end, independent of the pre-deploy hook it already runs inside today (the gap this slice closes — no scheduled backup; backups run only inside the pre-deploy hook). Once a day matches the recovery documentation's own daily-drill cadence and the pilot's existing daily snapshot window, without adding a second concurrent base backup while one is already running (`docsfab-backup` always takes a fresh base backup; there is no republish mode). The maximum is one week, beyond which scheduled backup coverage would not meaningfully improve on the existing per-deploy hook alone.
alerting.backup.timerIntervalHours.docSummary: How often the scheduled backup timer runs `docsfab-backup`, independent of the pre-deploy hook.

compositionExecution.timeoutMs.docSummary: Host ceiling for one step attempt; a narrower installed composition still wins.

compositionExecution.maxResponseBytes.remediation: Reduce the provider response size or raise this limit in config/limits/compositionExecution.yaml.
compositionExecution.maxResponseBytes.rationale: Host response ceiling; override may only lower it.

compositionExecution.answerNowElapsedSha.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_COMPOSITION_EXECUTION_ANSWER_NOW_ELAPSED_SHARE_BASIS_POINTS to an integer from 1000 through 4000.
compositionExecution.answerNowElapsedSha.rationale: Share of one composition step attempt a judgment step may spend reading before the host stops offering tools and asks for the answer it already has. Basis points of the effective attempt timer, so the share follows whatever timer the installed composition seals. Measured basis, 2026-09-25 review probe attempt 1 of the provisional judgment step - 160,765 output tokens over 24 turns inside a 30-minute attempt, 89 tokens per second sustained including tool round trips - and the two later attempts of the same step, which answered in 11 and 2 turns once the host told them to. At the default the answer turn and its one continuation still fit the remainder at that measured rate. Override may only lower it, so an operator can force the answer sooner but never later; the floor keeps a step from being asked to answer before it has read anything.
compositionExecution.answerNowElapsedSha.docSummary: Reading share of one judgment step attempt before the host asks for the answer.

compositionExecution.answerPlan.defaultT.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_COMPOSITION_EXECUTION_ANSWER_PLAN_DEFAULT_TOKENS to an integer from 11800 through 65536, or declare an answer plan entry for the step in config/limits/compositionExecution.yaml.
compositionExecution.answerPlan.defaultT.rationale: Output tokens the answer plan of a step with no compositionExecution.answerPlan entry of its own reserves for the answer the host asks for inside its attempt. docsfab doctor --limits lists every step that uses it, so the fallback is never silent. 11,800 is the largest whole structured answer the closed-schema answer records decision (#1961, section 4.2) plans with, so an unmeasured step gets the most conservative plan, the earliest ask. It and the per-step entries replaced a fixed 1,100,000 ms reserve (two 32,768-token turns at 60 tokens per second) that exceeded the 300,000 ms attempt timer 13 of 16 sealed compositions carry, so the answer-now reading share never armed there (#1978). Override may only raise it, which moves the ask earlier; the maximum is the former reserve's two 32,768-token turns. A reserve at or above the attempt timer leaves the budget unarmed, and doctor names that.
compositionExecution.answerPlan.defaultT.docSummary: Planned answer size for a step with no measured plan of its own; docsfab doctor --limits lists those steps.

compositionExecution.answerPlan.assessRe.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_COMPOSITION_EXECUTION_ANSWER_PLAN_ASSESS_READINESS_TOKENS to an integer from 2300 through 65536.
compositionExecution.answerPlan.assessRe.rationale: Output tokens the answer plan of the assess-readiness step reserves for the answer the host asks for inside its attempt. The step's answer-now reserve is this answer's decode time at compositionExecution.answerNowDecodeTokensPerSecond plus one compositionExecution.answerNowTurnLatencyMs for the answer turn and each length-stop continuation, capped at what those turns can carry under the bound composition's per-turn output limit (#1978). Measured basis, the answerOutputTokens of every succeeded attempt of this step in the retained run index of the r9-measure lane (2026-10-07; 102 runs from 2026-09-30 through 2026-10-06 across Super, Ultra, gpt-6-sol and gpt-oss on build.nvidia.com and the inference hub), read with docsfab runs query --group-by stepId,answerOutputTokens. answerOutputTokens sums the answer turn and any continuation. Only succeeded attempts are counted, so an answer that a cut or a refusal ended is not in the basis. 9 attempts, p50 1,339, p90 and max 1,503 tokens; 1.5 times the maximum, rounded up to 100. Override may only raise it, which moves the ask earlier. A step with no entry of its own uses compositionExecution.answerPlan.defaultTokens, and docsfab doctor --limits lists which steps do.

compositionExecution.answerNowDecodeToke.docSummary: Decode rate the answer reserve assumes for a step's asked-for answer.

Override may only raise it, which moves the ask earlier; the maximum is two minutes, where the two planned turns alone take 240,000 ms of a 300,000 ms attempt. It is a declared design planning default for every composition, not a per-composition measurement, and it can be optimistic for long answer turns. The retained step 8 attempts measured per-turn upper bounds (attempt duration over provider turns, decode included) with a median of 9.4 seconds on Super through build.nvidia.com, and up to 118 seconds on two-turn continuation attempts at a 300,000 ms timer. The composition re-qualification of issue 1973 replaces it with measured latencies when it reseals each composition.
compositionExecution.answerNowTurnLatenc.docSummary: Latency the answer reserve charges each turn of a step's asked-for answer.

retry.maxRetries.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_READ_ONLY_MAX_RETRIES to an integer from 0 through 3.
retry.maxRetries.rationale: Read-only step retries default to the existing admitted maximum. Operators may lower the retry count, including zero; retry delays are unchanged. Write steps remain single-attempt, except the CREATE revision writer (replay reset-write-step), which retries any retryable malformed-response, such as a model-correctable accounting refusal, within this count after its host restores candidate 0 (#1266). The override keeps its historical name DOCSFAB_READ_ONLY_MAX_RETRIES for host compatibility and bounds that revision writer too. It also bounds the hinted correction rounds of one read-only first pass (#1284). Each round re-asks the model after a model-correctable first-pass rejection, and the first-pass model-turn budget grows by this count, so a round never spends a mandatory phase or evidence-expansion turn.
retry.maxRetries.docSummary: Contract-correction retries for read-only inference failures, and retryable malformed replies of the `create-documentation` revision writer, such as model-correctable revision-accounting refusals. Throttled and transport-fault attempts use `retry.maxTransportRetries` instead, so a read-only step makes at most 1 + 3 + 6 = 10 attempts.

retry.baseDelayMs.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS to an integer from 0 through 30000.
retry.baseDelayMs.rationale: Closed backoff floor for the read-only retry policy.

retry.maxDelayMs.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_RETRY_MAX_DELAY_MS to an integer from 0 through 30000 that is at least the base delay.
retry.maxDelayMs.rationale: Closed backoff ceiling for the read-only retry policy.

retry.maxTimeoutRetries.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_READ_ONLY_MAX_TIMEOUT_RETRIES to an integer from 0 through 3 that is at most the read-only retry count.
retry.maxTimeoutRetries.rationale: Read-only retries for an attempt that ended in a timeout, counted as timeout retries already scheduled in the step and held under retry.maxRetries, so the worst case stays (retry.maxRetries + 1) attempt timers. The retry is not the same ask - its prompt says the previous attempt reached its time limit and to read only what the answer needs - and the attempt records which timer fired (attempt-deadline or provider-timeout). Measured basis, Inference Hub matrix 2026-10-01 (development evidence) - all three timed-out cells timed out once and were declined with retries unused - update Super derive-source-obligations ef1c1dfc stalled after 24 turns and 49 s of provider time inside a 300 s attempt, update Ultra evaluate-document-quality 9e5c3a84 ran 41 reading turns, focused review Ultra test-audience-understanding bad283ee looped on reads. One retry recovers a stall and costs at most one more attempt timer. A catalog default above a lowered DOCSFAB_READ_ONLY_MAX_RETRIES applies as that count and doctor shows the applied value; only an explicit override above it is refused.
retry.maxTimeoutRetries.docSummary: Retries of a step attempt that timed out, counted per step and held under the read-only retry count.

retry.maxCutAnswerRetries.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_READ_ONLY_MAX_CUT_ANSWER_RETRIES to an integer from 0 through 3 that is at most the read-only retry count.
retry.maxCutAnswerRetries.rationale: Read-only retries for a structured answer cut at the output limit with no continuation left, or completed by continuation and then refused, counted as cut-answer retries already scheduled in the step and held under retry.maxRetries. Each such attempt pays the whole output allowance, so the count is small, and the retry tells the model its answer ran past the limit and to return it complete and well inside it. Measured basis - step 8 baseline 41ae5075 (2026-09-30) had one degenerate cut in five answers and the fresh sample succeeded; Ultra plan-documentation ran away twice in two runs on Inference Hub (61ba16da 16,384 tokens in 130 s, e2f4c3d4 18,428 tokens in 251 s), so further fresh samples are unlikely to pay for their cost. A catalog default above a lowered DOCSFAB_READ_ONLY_MAX_RETRIES applies as that count; only an explicit override above it is refused.
retry.maxCutAnswerRetries.docSummary: Retries of a step whose structured answer was cut at the output limit, or completed by continuation and then refused.

retry.maxNoProgressRetries.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_READ_ONLY_MAX_NO_PROGRESS_RETRIES to an integer from 0 through 3 that is at most the read-only retry count.
retry.maxNoProgressRetries.rationale: Read-only retries for an attempt the host stopped as no-progress (execution.readLoopWithheldReads, execution.readLoopUnchangedReReads, or the hard tool-call ceiling compositionExecution.maxToolCallsPerStep), counted as no-progress retries already scheduled in the step and held under retry.maxRetries. A read loop repeats deterministically unless something changes, so the one retry differs from the attempt that looped - at the first re-read the read-evidence ledger withholds, the host withdraws the tools and asks for the answer from what the model already read - and the answer is still decoded against the same contract. Measured basis, Inference Hub matrix 2026-10-01 (development evidence) - focused review Ultra test-audience-understanding bad283ee re-read one result at 29 output tokens per turn for 90 turns, and the same attempt shape stopped by name once read-loop supervision landed; a second identical retry would spend another attempt timer on the same loop. The tool-call ceiling stop shares this budget because the attempt that reaches it is the same failure, a model that kept calling tools instead of answering - runs ad6fab22 (evaluate-document-quality) and 48ef1a5c (derive-source-obligations) reached 126 of 126 calls on attempt 1 and succeeded on a later attempt. A catalog default above a lowered DOCSFAB_READ_ONLY_MAX_RETRIES applies as that count; only an explicit override above it is refused.
retry.maxNoProgressRetries.docSummary: Retries of a step attempt the host stopped for re-reading unchanged content or at its tool-call ceiling; the retry withdraws the tools at its first withheld re-read and asks for the answer.

retry.maxTransportRetries.remediation: Wait for the provider's rate limit or availability to recover, or reduce other traffic on the same key and deployment, then run the step again. DOCSFAB_READ_ONLY_MAX_TRANSPORT_RETRIES may only lower this count, from 0 through 6.
retry.maxTransportRetries.rationale: Read-only step attempts that may end in a transport fault (throttled, or provider-transient - a 5xx or a stream that closed before it finished) without spending retry.maxRetries. Those attempts never delivered an answer the contract could judge, so charging them to the contract-correction count left a step its correction attempts only on a quiet route; on build.nvidia.com runs 28b5d50f and e1fa56af (2026-10-01) 3 of the 4 step attempts of evaluate-document-quality ended throttled in both runs. Six is a conservative ceiling, not a measured need. With providerAttempt.maxThrottledAttemptsPerTurn about 1% of 60-turn attempts still end throttled at the measured 429 rate, and hosted Ultra run facc5e4a lost 2 attempts of one step to streams that closed mid-answer. retry.transportMaxElapsedMs bounds the same retries by wall clock, whichever is reached first. 0 restores a stop on the first transport-failed attempt; it never moves the cost back onto retry.maxRetries.
retry.maxTransportRetries.docSummary: Read-only step attempts that may end throttled or in a provider transport fault without spending `retry.maxRetries`.

retry.transportMaxDelayMs.remediation: Lower retry.transportMaxDelayMs in config/limits/retry.yaml; a longer server-requested Retry-After is waited only up to it, and the next attempt may be throttled again.
retry.transportMaxDelayMs.rationale: Ceiling on one wait before a transport retry of a step, a honoured Retry-After included. The wait is the read-only exponential from retry.baseDelayMs by transport retry number, lengthened to the provider's Retry-After. Sixty seconds covers a per-minute provider rate window; build.nvidia.com sent no Retry-After on any of the 15 terminal 429s it returned in runs 28b5d50f and e1fa56af, so the exponential decides there.
retry.transportMaxDelayMs.docSummary: Ceiling on one wait before a step's transport retry, a honoured `Retry-After` included.

retry.transportMaxElapsedMs.remediation: Wait for the provider's rate limit or availability to recover, or reduce other traffic on the same key and deployment, then run the step again; lower retry.transportMaxElapsedMs in config/limits/retry.yaml to stop sooner.
retry.transportMaxElapsedMs.rationale: Wall clock one step may spend in transport-failed attempts and the waits after them before no further transport retry is scheduled. One hour, the host ceiling compositionExecution.timeoutMs for a single attempt. Installed compositions clamp an attempt to 300,000 or 1,800,000 ms, so this admits from 2 to 12 full-length transport-failed attempts, and retry.maxTransportRetries usually stops sooner; the attempt already running when the bound is crossed still finishes. The host job deadline still cancels the whole run.
retry.transportMaxElapsedMs.docSummary: Wall clock one step may spend in transport-failed attempts and their waits.

firstPass.evidenceExpansionModelTurns.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_FIRST_PASS_EVIDENCE_EXPANSION_MODEL_TURNS, up to 16, when first pass stops at maxRounds with obligations unresolved, and raise DOCSFAB_FIRST_PASS_MAX_SOURCE_FILES with it so each round keeps its share of sources, or name the sources the request needs by path or with --source.
firstPass.evidenceExpansionModelTurns.rationale: Evidence-expansion assessments after the first assessment round. Each one reads more sources for the obligations still unresolved, ranked by their terms and led by any file an open obligation names, and runs only while the previous round left fewer obligations open, or an open obligation names a file not yet read, or the request names a source first pass could not read; a round that leaves as many open, or finds nothing new, ends the loop (#2113). The first-pass model-turn budget is the three mandatory model phases (decomposition, completeness, assessment), plus this allowance, plus retry.maxRetries correction rounds (#1284). Each round reads an even share of firstPass.maxSourceFiles, so that limit grows with this one. In the real-world benchmark rerun at main f6f4c902b, the 57 first passes (16 tasks) used 1 to 4 rounds, median 1, and 9 of them used all four rounds of the former allowance of 3. Those were recorded as needing a fifth round, and at main 1a293eabb (rerun rr-20261007a) SR-1, DY-1, and MB-3 used all seven rounds of this default and were recorded as needing an eighth. Each value was one past the limit by construction, and those passes kept obligations open that no repository source closed. Six stays, since a pass that leaves fewer obligations open each round, or follows a named file, can use them, and a round that leaves as many open no longer spends the rest. Each round took under 17 seconds there on a composition with a 30-minute timer; firstPass.assessmentInputWindowShare names the compositions whose 5-minute timer is tighter. The first pass records maxRounds only when this allowance ended a loop that would otherwise have run another round, which is when its last round left fewer obligations open, an open obligation still names a file not yet read, or the request names a source first pass could not read, a run that stops unless every gap closes. A loop that had converged ended before the allowance, so none is recorded one past the limit for it.
firstPass.evidenceExpansionModelTurns.docSummary: Evidence-expansion assessments after the first one. Each reads more sources for the obligations still unresolved, and runs only while the previous round left fewer of them open or an open one names a file not yet read.

firstPass.modelInputTokensPerTurn.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_FIRST_PASS_MODEL_INPUT_TOKENS_PER_TURN, up to 4194304, when first pass stops at its cumulative input budget or a first-pass stop names this setting as the assessment prompt bound; the model profile's maxInputTokens still caps each turn's share.
firstPass.modelInputTokensPerTurn.rationale: Cumulative first-pass input budget per budgeted model turn, clamped per turn to the model profile's maxInputTokens. One turn's share also caps one assessment prompt, its evidence frames included, at the bridge's estimate of three bytes per token. The default is the largest input window an installed composition seals, sealed.compositionLimits.maxInputTokens (1,050,000 tokens), so on every installed composition the model's window, through firstPass.assessmentInputWindowShare, sizes the prompt, and a first pass that spends every turn on a full assessment still fits. A model without an attested window gets one turn's share as its window. The worst case on the benchmark composition, two obligation phases and ten full assessments (seven rounds and three correction rounds) of about 784,900 estimated tokens each, is about 7.8 million input tokens a pass, inside the 12.6 million cumulative budget of 12 turns. A host lowers it to cap first-pass input cost, and the prompt shrinks with it. The former 262,144 tokens was exactly the former 786,432-byte prompt, so raising firstPass.maxPresentedBytes alone could not raise the prompt.
firstPass.modelInputTokensPerTurn.docSummary: Cumulative first-pass input budget per budgeted model turn, and a cap on one assessment prompt. The model profile's input limit caps each turn's share.

firstPass.modelOutputTokensPerTurn.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_FIRST_PASS_MODEL_OUTPUT_TOKENS_PER_TURN, up to 131072, when first-pass answers are cut at the response bound or the request policy's minimum output tokens is above it; the model profile's maxOutputTokens still caps each answer.
firstPass.modelOutputTokensPerTurn.rationale: The first-pass response bound for one model answer, and the cumulative first-pass output budget per budgeted model turn, clamped per turn to the model profile's maxOutputTokens. The knowledge first pass asks for at most this many output tokens per answer. It is the former fixed 16384-token cumulative cap divided by the former four-turn budget; a host can raise it for requests with many obligations.
firstPass.modelOutputTokensPerTurn.docSummary: The first-pass response bound for one model answer, and the cumulative output budget per budgeted model turn.

firstPass.maxScannedFiles.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_FIRST_PASS_MAX_SCANNED_FILES above the tracked file count, up to 10000000, or name the sources the request needs by path or with --source.
firstPass.maxScannedFiles.rationale: Tracked files of the selected revision that first pass lists, ranks, and matches against paths the request names. It was a 256-file breadth-first walk from the repository root until issue 1915, which never reached implementation sources in repositories of about 1,200 files. Representative repositories hold 1,000 to 10,000 tracked files; the default keeps ten times the larger. Listing a path reads no bytes.
firstPass.maxScannedFiles.docSummary: Tracked files first pass lists, ranks, and matches against the paths a request names. Listing a file reads none of its bytes.

firstPass.maxSourceFiles.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_FIRST_PASS_MAX_SOURCE_FILES, up to 100000, or name the sources the request needs by path or with --source; first pass reads named sources before it ranks the rest.
firstPass.maxSourceFiles.rationale: Repository files whose evidence spans one first pass offers the model, across all its rounds. Each round may use an even share of what is left, so expansion rounds keep a share; named sources, targets, and --source selections are read before the share applies. 32 files filled with documentation pages before any code was read (#1915, Dynamo, Megatron Bridge, AutoModel). The default is 64 files for each of the seven rounds firstPass.evidenceExpansionModelTurns allows, the share each round had before. In the benchmark rerun at main f6f4c902b, first passes that settled in one round cited evidence from as deep as the 64th file they read, so a smaller first-round share would have missed it. Evidence bytes, not this count, bound the prompt. A round's share ends the round before this limit is charged, so the limit is recorded only when it refuses a file a round would have read (#2113).
firstPass.maxSourceFiles.docSummary: Repository files whose evidence first pass offers the model, across all rounds. Sources the request names are read first.

firstPass.maxFileBytes.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_FIRST_PASS_MAX_FILE_BYTES above the file's size, up to 1073741824, or select a smaller source.
firstPass.maxFileBytes.rationale: Largest single unnamed repository file first pass reads. A file under it is read whole and offered in windows around the request's terms, so a long source no longer costs its whole size in evidence; a file the request names is read past it, within firstPass.maxTotalReadBytes. Files over the former 64 KiB bound were skipped silently until issue 1915; generated code and implementation diffs in representative repositories reach a few MiB.
firstPass.maxFileBytes.docSummary: Largest single file first pass reads unless the request names it. A larger unnamed file is not read, and the record names the bound.

firstPass.maxTotalReadBytes.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_FIRST_PASS_MAX_TOTAL_READ_BYTES, up to 4294967296, or name fewer and smaller sources.
firstPass.maxTotalReadBytes.rationale: Repository bytes one first pass reads across all rounds. It holds firstPass.maxSourceFiles sources at a typical source size with room for several files near firstPass.maxFileBytes. A round stops reading ranked files at the first file the remaining budget cannot hold, and the record names the bound. The former 1 MiB budget held 16 files at the old per-file bound.
firstPass.maxTotalReadBytes.docSummary: Repository bytes one first pass reads across all rounds.

firstPass.maxSpans.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_FIRST_PASS_MAX_SPANS, up to 1000000, or name fewer sources.
firstPass.maxSpans.rationale: Evidence spans one first pass offers. A span is a window of at most 120 lines, and its frame counts against the assessment prompt bound, so prompt bytes usually bind first; this count keeps a prompt of many tiny spans bounded. 96 spans ran out before 32 files were offered. In the benchmark rerun at main f6f4c902b one round offered up to 202 spans and one pass at most 610, and every prompt averaged at least 1,289 presented bytes a span, its request and obligations included. Seven rounds of 202 spans are 1,414 spans, and 2,048 spans at that average overfill the 2,353,284-byte prompt of a 1,050,000-token window, so prompt bytes still bind before this count.
firstPass.maxSpans.docSummary: Evidence spans one first pass offers the model.

firstPass.maxPresentedBytes.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_FIRST_PASS_MAX_PRESENTED_BYTES, up to 67108864, when a first-pass stop names it as the assessment prompt bound; when the stop names firstPass.assessmentInputWindowShare or firstPass.modelInputTokensPerTurn, raise that setting instead. Or name fewer sources.
firstPass.maxPresentedBytes.rationale: Ceiling on the bytes of one first-pass assessment prompt, the request and its obligations plus every evidence span with its frame, so the frames that wrap each span are counted, not only its text. The host sizes the prompt from the bound model's input window (firstPass.assessmentInputWindowShare) and one turn's input share (firstPass.modelInputTokensPerTurn), at the bridge's estimate of three bytes per token, and applies this ceiling over both. 4 MiB is above the whole input window of every installed composition at that estimate, 3,150,000 bytes for 1,050,000 tokens, so the window sets the prompt and this ceiling binds only when a host lowers it. Once the prompt is full, first pass stops reading ranked files, still reads the sources the request names, and records the files it left unread. The former fixed 786,432 bytes stopped 18 of the 57 first passes of the benchmark rerun at main f6f4c902b, each with the prompt full and 786,559 to 794,513 bytes wanted.
firstPass.maxPresentedBytes.docSummary: Ceiling on the bytes of one first-pass assessment prompt, every evidence frame included. The model's input window sets the prompt below it.

firstPass.assessmentInputWindowShare.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_FIRST_PASS_ASSESSMENT_INPUT_WINDOW_SHARE, up to 1, so one assessment prompt may fill more of the model's input window, run with a model whose input window is larger, or name fewer sources.
firstPass.assessmentInputWindowShare.rationale: Share of the bound model's admitted input window, after its context reserve, that one first-pass assessment prompt may fill, at the bridge's estimate of three bytes per token, the way sources.readInputWindowShare sizes a step's source reads. firstPass.modelInputTokensPerTurn and firstPass.maxPresentedBytes cap the result. A model without an attested window, such as an endpoint that matches no installed composition, gets one turn's input share as its window. The prompt is the whole assessment request, so it takes most of the window. Each figure here assumes the 4,096-token context reserve of the shipped profiles; the 1,024-token reserve docsfab setup writes for a custom endpoint adds 6,912 bytes. On the 1,050,000-token window of the benchmark composition, 0.75 holds 2,353,284 bytes, 2.96 times the largest demand of the 18 first passes the former fixed 786,432-byte prompt stopped in the rerun at main f6f4c902b (794,513 bytes), and room for seven rounds at its 90th-percentile growth of 305,690 bytes a round after a first round of up to 403,832. That rerun measured 3.10 to 3.85 bytes per provider token, so a full prompt leaves about a quarter of the window for the answer and denser text. Windows under about 353,600 tokens get a smaller prompt than the former fixed bound, 580,608 bytes at 262,144 tokens, 278,784 at 128,000, and 138,240 at 65,536, against 786,432, 384,000, and 196,608 before. A share of 1 gives 371,712 bytes at 128,000 tokens, not the former 384,000, because the reserve now counts. The five installed compositions with a window of 262,144 tokens or more and a 5-minute attempt timer (nvidia-nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b-pi, nvidia-inference-nemotron-3-super-v3-pi, nvidia-inference-nemotron-3-ultra-pi, nvidia-inference-deepseek-v4-pro-pi, and nvidia-inference-qwen3-5-397b-a17b-pi) now get prompts of up to about 2.35 MB over up to seven rounds within that timer, so a first pass that selects one with --composition may stop at its deadline.
firstPass.assessmentInputWindowShare.docSummary: Share of the model's input window, after its context reserve, that one first-pass assessment prompt may fill at three bytes per token.

firstPass.readDeadlineMs.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_FIRST_PASS_READ_DEADLINE_MS, up to 3600000, on a host whose repository reads are slow.
firstPass.readDeadlineMs.rationale: Wall clock first pass may spend listing and reading repository files, and checking them for DocsFab's own configured credentials, separate from model time. 30 seconds was sized for 256 listed files and 1 MiB of reads; issue 1915 lists every tracked file and reads up to firstPass.maxTotalReadBytes.
firstPass.readDeadlineMs.docSummary: Wall clock first pass may spend listing, reading, and screening repository files, apart from model time.

firstPass.modelDeadlineMs.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_FIRST_PASS_MODEL_DEADLINE_MS, up to 14400000; an installed composition with a shorter attempt timer still applies its own.
firstPass.modelDeadlineMs.rationale: Wall clock for all first-pass model calls, applied with the installed composition's attempt timer, whichever is shorter. It was a fixed 10 minutes; with several evidence-expansion rounds of larger assessments, 30 minutes matches the longest sealed composition attempt timer.
firstPass.modelDeadlineMs.docSummary: Wall clock for all first-pass model calls. A composition with a shorter attempt timer still applies it.

firstPass.maxContradictionSides.remediation: The first-pass assessment named more disagreeing sides for one contradicted obligation than one question can carry and is re-asked for fewer; name the sources the request needs by path or with --source so fewer sources compete.
firstPass.maxContradictionSides.rationale: Disagreeing sources one contradicted first-pass obligation may name, each one span and its verbatim value. Two is structural (a contradiction needs two sides) and is not this bound. Every side becomes an option of the operator question, so the bound keeps one question answerable. The pilot conflicts name two or three sides (service port, cell 658 - docs/deployment.md, deploy.yaml and src/server.ts); eight leaves more than twice that headroom. Sealed with no override because the question shape, not a host, owns it.

firstPass.maxContradictionValueChars.remediation: The first-pass assessment quoted a disagreeing value longer than the bound and is re-asked for the shortest verbatim text that carries the disputed value.
firstPass.maxContradictionValueChars.rationale: UTF-16 code units of one disagreeing value, copied verbatim from its span into the operator question. A value is the disputed fact itself - a port, a status code, a command, a flag default - not the surrounding sentence. The pilot conflicts were 4 characters (9090, 8088) and 12 characters (202 Accepted); a full install command line runs to about 120. Two hundred keeps each option of the question one readable line, with headroom over the longest seen. Sealed with no override because the question shape, not a host, owns it.

firstPass.maxObligationConditionChars.remediation: State that constraint of the request in a shorter sentence, then run again; first pass records each constraint whole and never shortens it. Raising firstPass.maxObligationConditionChars in config/limits/firstPass.yaml changes the sealed first-pass support record and needs a DocsFab change, not an override.
firstPass.maxObligationConditionChars.rationale: UTF-16 code units of one first-pass obligation condition. It bounds the conditions the model writes in its decomposition and completeness answers, and each constraint an admitted request intent seeds, which first pass records whole as the slice of the request as written. The support record keeps every condition and the runtime support decoder holds this bound, so a record reads the same on every host and no override tier applies. An intent quote may run to requestIntent.maxQuoteChars, measured on the normalized request; no condition bound admits every such quote, since the text as written can be several times longer than its normalized form, so a longer constraint stops before any model call with this code, the observed length, and the bound, and is never cut. 500 is the bound conditions carried before they moved to this catalog. The pilot requests run 172 to 326 characters in total, so any one of their clauses fits with headroom, and one condition stays a single readable requirement in the completeness and assessment prompts.
firstPass.maxObligationConditionChars.docSummary: Characters of one first-pass obligation condition, counted in the request as written. A request-intent constraint longer than this stops first pass before any model call; first pass never shortens it.

liveAgent.taskActivityMaxBytes.remediation: Split an unusually long task into smaller requests; an exceeded capture is retained with clipped coverage and cannot support a complete activity claim.
liveAgent.taskActivityMaxBytes.rationale: Public content-free event metadata for one noninteractive task. The 16 MiB capacity matches the supported downstream per-file import ceiling; the bound JSON export and companion together still fit the 64 MiB aggregate-output ceiling for representative tasks. It is an evidence-capacity bound, not a smaller provider-turn budget. Crossing the bound marks capture clipped rather than silently omitting events; representative direct and workflow journeys measure headroom.
liveAgent.taskActivityMaxBytes.docSummary: Maximum public event metadata for one task; an exceeded capture is marked clipped.

liveAgent.taskActivityFieldMaxBytes.remediation: Narrow an unusually long path, query, or command. The public capture marks the field clipped and cannot claim complete audit coverage.
liveAgent.taskActivityFieldMaxBytes.rationale: One public audit argument must remain inspectable without turning the activity file into a copy of source or model text. The default equals the existing live-agent workflow-context ceiling, enough for an ordinary path, URL, or search expression. Longer action metadata is represented by an explicit clipped marker; no field is silently shortened.
liveAgent.taskActivityFieldMaxBytes.docSummary: Maximum bytes for one public action argument; longer fields are marked clipped.

liveAgent.taskProviderTurns.remediation: Reduce provider turns in this task, or raise DOCSFAB_LIVE_AGENT_TASK_PROVIDER_TURNS within the catalog maximum before preparing the request.
liveAgent.taskProviderTurns.rationale: Whole noninteractive task physical provider-request capacity shared by parent Pi and bounded children. Synthetic supported workload from the installed workflow catalog has two 14-step create-documentation runs plus one parent segment; at 512 logical turns per segment and one physical retry per turn it spends 29,696 requests, below default 32,768 by 3,072. The raisable maximum 393,216 covers those 29 segments at the existing 12,288 physical-request-per-step ceiling (356,352 requests), leaving 36,864. This is provisional synthetic capacity evidence rather than real-model cost measurement. Missing token and cost usage remains unavailable.
liveAgent.taskProviderTurns.docSummary: Shared physical provider requests for one noninteractive live-agent task, including bounded workflows. The operator can raise it within the catalog maximum.

liveAgent.agentCausedRefusalRetries.rationale: One agent-driven workflow resubmission after a live-agent-workflow-request-not-verbatim refusal or a proposal-scope refusal of a request the agent assembled (issues 1127 and 1177). The agent resubmits the user's consecutive messages verbatim; the host never substitutes text. A second refusal reaches the operator. Zero disables the resubmission; more than one would repeat the same request without new information.
liveAgent.agentCausedRefusalRetries.docSummary: Live-agent workflow resubmissions, with your exact words, after a refusal the agent caused. `0` disables them.

liveAgent.workflowContextMaxChars.remediation: Shorten the live-agent workflow context, or lower DOCSFAB_LIVE_AGENT_WORKFLOW_CONTEXT_MAX_CHARS within max.
liveAgent.workflowContextMaxChars.rationale: Ceiling for the non-authoritative context a live agent attaches beside the user's verbatim instruction (issue 1177). It reaches every workflow step prompt, so it reuses the existing 16,384-character reader response contract bound in harness/pi-session.ts. Longer context is cut at this bound with a coded marker in the prompt, and the cut is recorded on the run and returned to the agent.
liveAgent.workflowContextMaxChars.docSummary: Non-authoritative context a live agent attaches to a workflow request. Longer context is cut with a coded marker.

liveAgent.commandProcessStopMs.remediation: End the processes the command left running in the repository before retrying. On a heavily loaded host, raise DOCSFAB_LIVE_AGENT_COMMAND_PROCESS_STOP_MS within max.
liveAgent.commandProcessStopMs.rationale: How long an approved live-agent host command's remaining process-group members may keep answering SIGKILL after the command closes its output. The command's own timeout is already cleared by then, so without this bound a process that SIGKILL cannot end, such as one in uninterruptible I/O, would hang the tool call with no refusal. A normal member ends on the first kill; on a loaded macOS host a kill can miss a member and a few more rounds end it, well inside five seconds. The 100 ms floor still allows several kill rounds; the one-minute ceiling keeps a mistyped value from holding the operator's turn open.
liveAgent.commandProcessStopMs.docSummary: How long `live-agent` keeps stopping an approved host command's remaining background processes after the command ends. Past it, the command fails with a refusal that names the limit.

liveAgent.commandOutputBytes.remediation: Narrow the command's output, for example by filtering it or writing it to a file the agent reads in parts, before retrying. Lower DOCSFAB_LIVE_AGENT_COMMAND_OUTPUT_BYTES within max to tighten it.
liveAgent.commandOutputBytes.rationale: Combined stdout and stderr bytes an approved live-agent host command may write before the host stops it and refuses the call. The whole output reaches the model in one tool result after the credential screen and host-root replacement, so an unbounded stream would hold the command and the operator's turn open and flood the model context. One mebibyte holds a full test or build log; the command is stopped, never truncated, so the model never sees a clipped result as complete. Override may only lower it.
liveAgent.commandOutputBytes.docSummary: Combined stdout and stderr an approved `live-agent` host command may write. Past it, DocsFab stops the command and returns no partial output.

liveAgent.sessionMaxAgeDays.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_LIVE_AGENT_SESSION_MAX_AGE_DAYS to a whole number of days from 0 through 3650. 0 turns automatic removal off.
liveAgent.sessionMaxAgeDays.rationale: Opt-in retention bound for local live-agent sessions. When it is positive, docsfab live-agent removes, before it opens a session, every local transcript whose last write is older than this many days, and the task-branch state of a repository left with no session. The default is 0, which turns removal off, because deleting a user's conversation history is a destructive action DocsFab does not take until the user configures it; docsfab sessions delete removes sessions on request either way. The ceiling of 3650 days (about ten years) is longer than any retention a user would choose, so a larger value would only make a mistyped number look like a retention promise.
liveAgent.sessionMaxAgeDays.docSummary: Removes local `live-agent` sessions whose last write is older than this many days when `live-agent` starts. `0` turns removal off.

liveAgent.askIndexPages.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_LIVE_AGENT_ASK_INDEX_PAGES within max so each question approves more of the pages its terms match, or ask again with target=<page> to answer from one page you choose.
liveAgent.askIndexPages.rationale: Most pages one Slack question approves when it names no target= (issue 2400). DocsFab indexes the project's tracked Markdown pages at the answer revision, ranks them against the question, and approves only the best matches; their text joins the model input within liveAgent.askIndexPageTextBytes and liveAgent.askIndexTextBytes, so the whole documentation set never enters the model's context. Six held the expected page for each of 20 representative questions about this repository (measured 2026-10-14 over its 1,149 indexed pages). The run record and the answer name the approved pages and how many pages matched, so a match past the bound is disclosed, never silently dropped. The ceiling is reviewScope.maxTargets, the most entries an approved-path list may hold.
liveAgent.askIndexPages.docSummary: Pages a Slack question without `target=` may approve from the project's documentation index. The answer names them and, when more pages matched, how many.

liveAgent.askIndexPageTextBytes.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_LIVE_AGENT_ASK_INDEX_PAGE_TEXT_BYTES within max so more of each approved page reaches the model, or ask about that page with target=<page>; the model can also read the rest of a clipped page with its read tool.
liveAgent.askIndexPageTextBytes.rationale: Most bytes of one approved page a Slack question without target= places in the model input (issue 2400). A longer page is cut after the last whole character within the bound, a letter kept with its accents, not at a line break or space, because a product reference model is one 57 KB line of JSON whose spaces all lie in its first 2 KB; its evidence block names the bytes shown and the page size, the answer marks the page as partial, and the run record lists it as clipped, so a cut is disclosed, never silent; the model can read the rest with its read tool. 32 KiB holds 95 percent of this repository's 1,456 tracked Markdown pages whole (measured 2026-10-14, 95th percentile 30 KB) and keeps one long page, such as a 58 KB product reference model, from taking the whole per-question allowance. The ceiling is the live-agent command output allowance, the most text one live-agent tool result may return.
liveAgent.askIndexPageTextBytes.docSummary: Bytes of one approved page a Slack question without `target=` passes to the model. A longer page is cut at the bound, and the evidence and the answer say so.

liveAgent.askIndexTextBytes.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_LIVE_AGENT_ASK_INDEX_TEXT_BYTES within max so more of the approved pages reach the model, or ask a narrower question; the model can also read a clipped page with its read tool.
liveAgent.askIndexTextBytes.rationale: Most bytes of approved page text one Slack question without target= places in the model input, across all its approved pages (issue 2400). The allowance is shared, so each page gets its whole text, within liveAgent.askIndexPageTextBytes, or an equal share of what the shorter pages leave, so no approved page arrives as a few bytes (spending in rank order left the last pages slivers). A page cut short is disclosed in its evidence block, in the answer, and in the run record, so nothing is silently dropped. 96 KiB is three full 32 KiB pages, about 25,000 tokens, a small share of the 131,072-token contexts measured hosted runs use, and it leaves room for the question, the conversation window, and the capsule. The ceiling is the live-agent command output allowance.
liveAgent.askIndexTextBytes.docSummary: Bytes of approved page text one Slack question without `target=` passes to the model, shared across its pages. Each page gets its whole text or an equal share; a page cut short is marked in the answer.

hostInvoker.contextPreflightBudgetMs.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_HOSTED_CONTEXT_PREFLIGHT_BUDGET_MS within the closed ceiling, or raise hostInvoker.contextPreflightBudgetMs in config/limits/hostInvoker.yaml.
hostInvoker.contextPreflightBudgetMs.rationale: Wait allowance for one hosted structural compile, defaulting to the existing admitted maximum. This bounds how long the runner waits, not the lifetime of the index build.
hostInvoker.contextPreflightBudgetMs.docSummary: Wait for one hosted structural compile; this does not terminate the index build.

hostInvoker.frozenInputMaxBytes.remediation: Reduce the frozen input or qualify a coordinated carrier change; live-agent turns use their separately derived question envelope.
hostInvoker.frozenInputMaxBytes.rationale: Names the existing 96 KiB per-input representation boundary without changing ordinary workflows. The live-agent event envelope is derived from maximum question bytes plus maximum admitted metadata and JSON escaping.

hostInvoker.frozenInputsMaxBytes.remediation: Reduce combined frozen inputs or qualify a coordinated carrier change; the live-agent allowance preserves this envelope's non-question remainder.
hostInvoker.frozenInputsMaxBytes.rationale: Names the existing 128 KiB aggregate frozen-input representation boundary. Live-agent turns add only the growth of their computed event beyond the ordinary per-input capacity.

hostInvoker.requestMaxBytes.remediation: Reduce the complete runtime request or qualify its representation; live-agent request capacity includes the measured extra JSON escaping of its larger question event.
hostInvoker.requestMaxBytes.rationale: Names the existing 512 KiB complete worker-request boundary for ordinary workflows. The live-agent wire adds twice its event-capacity growth because the event JSON is carried as a JSON string; actual serialized bytes are checked before dispatch and again at the worker.

hostInvoker.credentialMaxBytes.remediation: Supply the model credential within the shared one-shot custody envelope; a larger handle needs the writing producer and this reader qualified together.
hostInvoker.credentialMaxBytes.rationale: Shared model-credential handle capacity. The producer enforces the same number on its single write and the worker reads at most that many bytes before zeroing them, so the two sides declare one value. The protected authority-file allowance covers configuration and plan reads and is a different envelope that must not be substituted here.

hostInvoker.descriptorNumberMax.remediation: Pass the request, credential and replay inputs on inherited descriptor numbers within the admitted range, or qualify a wider spawn contract on both sides first.
hostInvoker.descriptorNumberMax.rationale: Largest inherited file-descriptor number this worker accepts on its command line. Descriptors zero through two are the standard streams, so three is the lowest inheritable slot; the upper value is this contract's own admission and is not an operating-system ceiling.

hostInvoker.requestStepIdsMax.remediation: Dispatch a workflow whose installed step list fits the admitted request shape; a longer installed workflow needs this capacity and the installed catalog qualified together.
hostInvoker.requestStepIdsMax.rationale: Admitted length of the step-identifier list on a hosted runtime request. It is a shape bound checked before any execution decision. The exact installed workflow identity and step order are still compared against the installed catalog afterwards, so this value never selects which steps run.

hostInvoker.capsuleEvidenceMaxItems.remediation: Select fewer evidence entries for the projected capsule, or qualify the projecting producer and this reader together before raising the count.
hostInvoker.capsuleEvidenceMaxItems.rationale: Admitted number of selected-evidence entries in a projected context capsule. The producing source admission is smaller today, so this is the reader's outer shape bound rather than an external protocol maximum. Capsule digest and expiry checks stay independent of it.

hostInvoker.capsuleEvidenceItemMaxBytes.remediation: Shorten the individual evidence entry, or qualify the projecting producer and this reader together before raising the per-entry capacity.
hostInvoker.capsuleEvidenceItemMaxBytes.rationale: Admitted size of one selected-evidence entry's content in a projected context capsule. Producers project smaller per-source excerpts today; this is the outer per-entry framing bound, and the aggregate projected-evidence capacity applies in addition to it rather than instead of it.

hostInvoker.capsuleEvidenceJsonMaxBytes.remediation: Select less evidence for the projected capsule, or qualify the context-budget producer and this reader together before raising the aggregate capacity.
hostInvoker.capsuleEvidenceJsonMaxBytes.rationale: Admitted serialized size of the projected selected-evidence collection measured by this reader. It measures that projection only, and the complete request envelope and the dispatcher's context budget are separate envelopes with their own numbers, and aliasing them to this one would silently change what each admits.

hostInvoker.editorialEvidenceRefsMax.remediation: Reduce the editorial outcome's evidence references, or qualify the deciding producer and this reader together before raising the count.
hostInvoker.editorialEvidenceRefsMax.rationale: Admitted number of evidence references in a projected editorial outcome. The producing decision validates its own references first and this reader keeps the same count so a projected outcome and its replay stay comparable; evidence is never truncated to fit a smaller envelope.

hostInvoker.editorialLimitationsMax.remediation: Reduce the editorial outcome's limitations, or qualify the producing decision policy, the projector's added diagnostic codes and this reader together before raising the count.
hostInvoker.editorialLimitationsMax.rationale: Admitted number of limitation codes in a projected editorial outcome. The projector unions the decision's own limitations with added diagnostic codes, so headroom for those additions belongs to this count. It is deliberately not aliased to the evidence-reference count even though both currently carry the same number.

hostInvoker.editorialLimitationMaxChars.remediation: Shorten the individual limitation code, or qualify the producing decision policy and this reader together before raising the per-code capacity.
hostInvoker.editorialLimitationMaxChars.rationale: Admitted length of one limitation code in a projected editorial outcome, counted in UTF-16 units. Count, code grammar and length carry distinct semantics, so a shorter list never licenses a longer code and the producing policy's own code syntax still applies.

hostInvoker.approvedModelBaselineMaxByte.remediation: Stage a smaller admitted baseline, or qualify the staging producer, the custody reference reader and the content-addressed carrier together before raising the capacity.
hostInvoker.approvedModelBaselineMaxByte.rationale: Admitted size of the one private file carrying a complete admitted approved-model baseline for a native job. It matches the content-addressed object capacity the same deployment already admits, because the staged bytes are the whole closure (claims, conflicts and provenance) rather than the model text alone. The producer checks it before it opens the file and the reader checks the declared size before it allocates, so both sides refuse the same number instead of trusting a caller-declared length.

hostInvoker.gitOutputMaxBytes.remediation: Narrow the Git invocation so it returns less, or qualify the hardened invocation and every caller that passes this ceiling together before raising it.
hostInvoker.gitOutputMaxBytes.rationale: Largest combined standard-output and standard-error size the hardened Git invocation accumulates before it kills the process group. It is the ceiling passed by the callers that copy a whole selected revision, not the ordinary per-call allowance, and crossing it is a refusal rather than a truncation, so the caller never reads a silently shortened tree or patch. It is sealed because an environment override on a confinement bound would widen what an untrusted working tree can return.

hostInvoker.gitTimeoutMs.remediation: Split the work into separately bounded Git invocations, or qualify the hardened invocation and its confinement contract before changing this deadline.
hostInvoker.gitTimeoutMs.rationale: Wall-clock deadline after which the hardened Git invocation kills its whole process group. It bounds one child process rather than a workflow step or a hosted run, and the kill is a refusal the caller sees rather than an empty successful result. It is sealed because a per-process override on a confinement deadline would let a hung or hostile invocation outlive the bound the worker relies on.

hostInvoker.gitDefaultOutputMaxBytes.remediation: Pass an explicitly qualified larger ceiling at the one call that needs it, or qualify this ordinary allowance and its callers together before raising it.
hostInvoker.gitDefaultOutputMaxBytes.rationale: Output allowance an ordinary hardened Git invocation gets when the caller names none. It is deliberately smaller than the whole-revision ceiling so that status, rev-parse and diff calls refuse early instead of inheriting a copy-sized budget; a caller that genuinely needs more passes the larger catalogued ceiling by name. It is sealed for the same reason the whole-revision ceiling is, being a confinement bound rather than a work allowance.

context.localPacketInputShareBasisPoints.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_CONTEXT_LOCAL_PACKET_INPUT_SHARE_BASIS_POINTS, up to 10000 (the whole input window), so a local or change-scoped context packet fits. A run without an attested input window sizes packets from DOCSFAB_CONTEXT_PACKET_FALLBACK_INPUT_TOKENS; raise that instead, or bind an installed composition or a model profile with current metadata so packets follow its window.
context.localPacketInputShareBasisPoints.rationale: Share of the bound model's input window, in basis points, that one local or change-scoped context packet may use. The packet is pasted into the step's prompt, so its budget follows that window instead of a fixed figure; node, edge, and path counts never bind before this token budget. 313 basis points of the smallest window an installed composition seals (65,536 tokens) is 2,051 tokens, at least the former fixed 2,048-token budget, and the 1,050,000-token window gets 32,865. A packet over its budget is trimmed, lowest-ranked paths, edges, and nodes first, and the step records this bound. A read-only step whose packet cannot fit even trimmed to its first target continues without one; a write step stops with this bound named.
context.localPacketInputShareBasisPoints.docValue: 313 basis points (3.13% of the input window)
context.localPacketInputShareBasisPoints.docSummary: Input-window share of one local or change-scoped context packet. A larger packet is trimmed, and the step records the bound.

context.corpusPacketInputShareBasisPoint.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_CONTEXT_CORPUS_PACKET_INPUT_SHARE_BASIS_POINTS, up to 10000 (the whole input window), so a corpus context packet fits. A run without an attested input window sizes packets from DOCSFAB_CONTEXT_PACKET_FALLBACK_INPUT_TOKENS; raise that instead, or bind an installed composition or a model profile with current metadata so packets follow its window.
context.corpusPacketInputShareBasisPoint.rationale: Share of the bound model's input window, in basis points, that one corpus context packet may use. The packet is pasted into the step's prompt, so its budget follows that window instead of a fixed figure; node, edge, and path counts never bind before this token budget. 1,250 basis points of the smallest window an installed composition seals (65,536 tokens) is the former fixed 8,192-token corpus budget, and the 1,050,000-token window gets 131,250. A packet over its budget is trimmed, lowest-ranked paths, edges, and nodes first, and the step records this bound. A read-only step whose packet cannot fit even trimmed to its first target continues without one; a write step stops with this bound named.
context.corpusPacketInputShareBasisPoint.docValue: 1,250 basis points (12.5% of the input window)
context.corpusPacketInputShareBasisPoint.docSummary: Input-window share of one corpus context packet. A larger packet is trimmed, and the step records the bound.

context.packetFallbackInputTokens.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_CONTEXT_PACKET_FALLBACK_INPUT_TOKENS so runs without an attested input window, and models whose window is smaller, get larger context packets, or bind a composition or attested model profile so the packet follows its window.
context.packetFallbackInputTokens.rationale: Input window the context packet shares are taken of when the run has no attested window, and the floor for one that is smaller. A run has none with an injected harness, the offline acceptance chain, the hosted offline fixture, or an endpoint that matches no installed composition, whose setup window is a placeholder DocsFab does not admit against. An installed composition or a profile with current metadata supplies its own window. 65,536 tokens is the smallest window an installed composition seals; there the shares give the former fixed budgets, so no setup gets a smaller packet than before.
context.packetFallbackInputTokens.docSummary: Input window the context packet shares use when the run has no attested window, and the floor for a smaller one.

context.packetMaxDepth.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_CONTEXT_PACKET_MAX_DEPTH, up to 16, so a context packet walks further from its targets; the input-window share still bounds the packet's size.
context.packetMaxDepth.rationale: Structural hops a context packet walks from its targets. Two hops reach a page's sections, their subsections, and directly linked or sibling pages. The input-window share, not this depth, bounds the packet's size, so a host may raise it; 16 hops is deeper than any heading or link structure a documentation tree needs.
context.packetMaxDepth.docSummary: Structural hops a context packet walks from its targets.

context.semanticEvidenceBytes.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_CONTEXT_SEMANTIC_EVIDENCE_BYTES up to 131072, the most one capsule carries; split a larger file.
context.semanticEvidenceBytes.rationale: Bytes of one authorized evidence file the Global Context Manager reads from Git for a context capsule (issue 2521). A merge reconciliation reads the approved model generation's canon here. The pilot's activation canon (v0.28) was 13,691 bytes, so the former fixed 32 KiB passed; its promoted generations are 58,406 to 61,220 bytes (v0.32 to v0.38), and every merge stalled on the old bound. 128 KiB is about twice the current canon, holds the largest model file in the repository (98,429 bytes, v0.29), and equals the largest context budget. That budget (131,072 bytes) is also the maximum, because one capsule cannot carry a larger file, so a higher allowance would only move the refusal to an unnamed capsule overflow.
context.semanticEvidenceBytes.docSummary: Bytes of one evidence file read from Git into a context capsule.

context.semanticSnapshotBytes.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_CONTEXT_SEMANTIC_SNAPSHOT_BYTES up to 2097152, or seal fewer evidence files for the project.
context.semanticSnapshotBytes.rationale: Total bytes of all evidence files one context snapshot reads from Git, formerly a fixed 256 KiB in the reader and moved here unchanged (issue 2521). Two evidence files at context.semanticEvidenceBytes fit; the pilot reads one 61,220-byte canon, about a quarter of it. The maximum is 16 evidence files, the snapshot's record cap, at the per-file maximum; what one capsule carries stays bounded by the context budget.
context.semanticSnapshotBytes.docSummary: Total bytes of the evidence files one context snapshot reads from Git.

foundation.claimLabelMaxChars.remediation: Shorten the claim subject, assertion, statement or applicability label, or qualify the strict record decoder's own string ceiling and this admission together before raising it.
foundation.claimLabelMaxChars.rationale: Admitted length of one Foundation claim label, counted in UTF-16 units. Inherited approved statements are complete sentences, so the ceiling is the strict decoder's own string bound rather than a shorter label-shaped guess; anything longer is already refused before this admission runs. The label is never truncated to fit.

init.gitignoreMaxBytes.remediation: Inspect the selected repository's .gitignore. If its size is expected, raise DOCSFAB_INIT_GITIGNORE_MAX_BYTES or init.gitignoreMaxBytes in the host limits file and rerun init; otherwise maintain the private entries manually. Init never truncates or edits an oversized file.
init.gitignoreMaxBytes.rationale: Largest regular .gitignore file one init preview reads in full to identify exactly which private entries it would append. A 2026-10-14 measurement of the supported DocsFab checkout found 3,546 bytes in its root .gitignore and 1,341 bytes in the runtime package's .gitignore; an additional local project sample measured 170 bytes. The 262,144-byte default retains the existing read ceiling and leaves more than 70 times headroom over the largest measured file. Preview still reports an oversized optional file as skipped with this bound's code, observed bytes, repository-file scope, and remediation; it never clips a file or claims an append. The 4,096-byte override floor fits the largest measured supported file, and the 16 MiB maximum permits larger legitimate generated ignore files while bounding one in-memory read and string conversion.

publishPackage.commandOutputBytes.remediation: Inspect the release job's command and the exact npm version and dist-tag in the registry before retrying, because npm publish may have reached the registry even when its output was cut off. If a qualified package legitimately needs more command output, raise publishPackage.commandOutputBytes in config/limits/publishPackage.yaml and regenerate the mirrors through a reviewed change.
publishPackage.commandOutputBytes.rationale: Maximum stdout or stderr bytes captured from each child command in the package publisher, including tar extraction, npm version and dist-tag views, exact-version tarball metadata views, and npm publish. The inherited 16 MiB ceiling is retained so this migration introduces no new refusal for a previously accepted release. Version and dist-tag views are small JSON documents, while publication output may grow with npm diagnostics. Current release output distribution has not been measured, so this is a provisional technical memory ceiling and the first qualified release should record captured output sizes for review. Node terminates a child stream that exceeds maxBuffer and may truncate it; the publisher names this bound and never treats truncated output as success. Publication state is unknown if npm publish or its tag readback overflows. The bound applies to the repository-controlled CI release script only, so no host override widens it without reviewed source and regenerated mirrors.

publishPackage.ancestryFetchDepth.remediation: Keep the publication refusal when the current channel winner falls outside retained local history. Reconcile the source ancestry or raise publishPackage.ancestryFetchDepth in config/limits/publishPackage.yaml through a reviewed qualification and regenerate the mirrors.
publishPackage.ancestryFetchDepth.rationale: Maximum additional protected-default-branch commits fetched to prove that the candidate is eligible and the existing channel winner is its ancestor. It bounds history needed by local Git ancestry checks without granting repository API access to CI_JOB_TOKEN. The default allows a typical release train while refusing to promote if an older winner cannot be proven within the fetched graph. No successful-depth distribution is recorded yet; the first qualified promotion should record observed depth and retained history for review. An unavailable or incomplete graph remains unknown and never promotes.

publishPackage.diagnosticArchiveBytes.remediation: Preserve the failed reproducibility gate and review the retained archive sizes before raising this bound through a reviewed change.
publishPackage.diagnosticArchiveBytes.rationale: Maximum compressed archive bytes accepted by the hash-only reproducibility diagnostic. This bound permits diagnostics for the current product package while limiting memory and prevents an oversized or malformed archive from producing unbounded diagnostic work. The diagnostic emits hashes and member metadata only, never member bytes.

publishPackage.registryArchiveBytes.remediation: Keep registry reconciliation unknown and inspect the exact package version before retrying. Raise this bound only after measuring qualified archive sizes through a reviewed change.
publishPackage.registryArchiveBytes.rationale: Maximum retained tarball bytes accepted from either the verified artifact or an exact-version registry readback. The publisher checks file size before reading or comparing the archive in memory, and an oversized readback remains unknown rather than green. The value is a technical bound chosen above the current package size; release evidence should record observed archives before any increase.
