publishPackage.registryArchiveDownloadTi.remediation: Keep exact-version reconciliation unknown and inspect registry availability before retrying. Raise this timeout only after recording qualified transfer durations through a reviewed change.
publishPackage.registryArchiveDownloadTi.rationale: Maximum elapsed time to retrieve one exact-version registry archive, including redirects and streamed body receipt. The five-minute ceiling is provisional because archive transfer distributions are not yet recorded. An aborted request removes its partial temporary file, preserves unknown state, and cannot pass the byte digest check.

publishPackage.registryArchiveRedirects.remediation: Keep the readback unknown and verify the registry's documented tarball URL. Increase this redirect count only through a reviewed qualification and regenerated mirrors.
publishPackage.registryArchiveRedirects.rationale: Maximum HTTPS redirects followed for one exact-version tarball request. Registry-origin credentials are sent only while the redirected URL remains under the configured project registry path; external signed-download hops receive no bearer token. The small bound permits expected object-store redirects while preventing unbounded redirect chains.

publishPackage.versionReadbackAttempts.remediation: Leave immutable upload unknown after the bounded exact-version reads and inspect the registry before retrying. Raise attempts only after measuring qualified registry propagation behavior.
publishPackage.versionReadbackAttempts.rationale: Maximum exact-version archive readback attempts after one npm publish call, including a lost publish response. Only an absent exact version retries; all other failures and byte conflicts stop immediately. The five-attempt budget is provisional and mirrors the existing channel readback policy until qualified package visibility data is available.

publishPackage.versionReadbackDelayMs.remediation: Leave immutable upload unknown if exact-version visibility exceeds the bounded interval. Change this delay only through reviewed qualification and regenerated mirrors.
publishPackage.versionReadbackDelayMs.rationale: Delay between absent exact-version reads after one upload. Four waits cap intentional sleep at four seconds; each metadata request has its own governed timeout. This is provisional pending measured registry propagation data.

publishPackage.versionReadbackTimeoutMs.remediation: Keep immutable upload unknown if an exact-version metadata request times out. Raise the per-request timeout only after recording qualified registry response durations.
publishPackage.versionReadbackTimeoutMs.rationale: Maximum elapsed time for one npm exact-version metadata read after upload. A timeout stops the retry loop because it does not establish absence. The 30-second budget is provisional and matches the channel metadata readback policy.

publishPackage.channelReadbackAttempts.remediation: Leave promotion unknown after the bounded readback attempts and inspect the channel before retrying. Raise attempts only after measuring qualified registry propagation behavior.
publishPackage.channelReadbackAttempts.rationale: Maximum channel readback attempts after a dist-tag update. The bounded retries allow a short registry propagation delay; malformed and authorization failures stop immediately, and exhaustion remains non-success. Each npm request also has the separately governed publishPackage.channelReadbackTimeoutMs ceiling.

publishPackage.channelReadbackDelayMs.remediation: Keep promotion unknown if channel propagation exceeds the bounded interval. Change this delay only through reviewed qualification and regenerated mirrors.
publishPackage.channelReadbackDelayMs.rationale: Delay between transient channel readback attempts. Together with publishPackage.channelReadbackAttempts, this caps intentional sleep time at four seconds; request runtime is separately bounded by publishPackage.channelReadbackTimeoutMs. This permits eventual visibility without treating unknown, malformed, or unauthorized reads as success.

publishPackage.channelReadbackTimeoutMs.remediation: Keep promotion unknown if the registry readback times out. Raise the per-attempt timeout only after recording qualified registry response durations.
publishPackage.channelReadbackTimeoutMs.rationale: Maximum elapsed time for one npm channel readback attempt. The bounded attempt count and delay cap aggregate retry work; a timed-out attempt may retry within that policy, while exhausted outcomes remain unknown and never green.

publishPackage.diagnosticExpandedBytes.remediation: Preserve the failed reproducibility gate and review expanded archive size before raising this bound through a reviewed change.
publishPackage.diagnosticExpandedBytes.rationale: Maximum decompressed tar bytes accepted by the hash-only reproducibility diagnostic. Gunzip is capped at this size, so a compressed expansion bomb cannot consume unbounded memory. The diagnostic remains advisory and never changes a failed byte-reproducibility gate into success.

publishPackage.diagnosticMembers.remediation: Preserve the failed reproducibility gate and review archive member counts before raising this bound through a reviewed change.
publishPackage.diagnosticMembers.rationale: Maximum tar members inspected per archive by the hash-only reproducibility diagnostic. It bounds per-member metadata allocation and comparison work while accommodating the current package file set. Exceeding the bound fails diagnostic generation and does not relax the strict reproducibility gate.

ia.inputPackageMaxBytes.remediation: Narrow the IA task scope or target so the provisioned package holds fewer indexed documents, or raise ia.inputPackageMaxBytes in config/limits/ia.yaml and regenerate the mirrors.
ia.inputPackageMaxBytes.rationale: Default admitted size of one canonical IA input package, the immutable governed task bundle a planning or analysis run reads, applied whenever a caller names no allowance of its own. It bounds a host-written private file, not model output; a package over it is refused whole and never truncated, because a partial package would change the digest the run is bound to. A caller may name its own allowance below ia.packageAllowanceMaxBytes and gets exactly that; an allowance above that ceiling is refused by name, never honoured and never silently narrowed.

ia.packageAllowanceMaxBytes.remediation: Reduce the analysed documentation set so the derived planning package is smaller, or raise ia.packageAllowanceMaxBytes in config/limits/ia.yaml and regenerate the mirrors.
ia.packageAllowanceMaxBytes.rationale: Absolute admitted size of one IA input package, and the exact allowance the hosted planning arm names when it derives a planning package from an already admitted analysis output. A caller-supplied allowance above this value is refused as package-too-large on the maxPackageBytes field, so a caller can never widen its own bound; the default a caller gets without naming one stays the smaller ia.inputPackageMaxBytes. It equals the retained analysis bound because a derived planning package restates that admitted analysis alongside its governed task binding, and a derived package over it is refused rather than admitted on the strength of its own measured size.

ia.analysisOutputMaxBytes.remediation: Reduce the analysed documentation set so the retained analysis package is smaller, or raise ia.analysisOutputMaxBytes in config/limits/ia.yaml and regenerate the mirrors.
ia.analysisOutputMaxBytes.rationale: Admitted size of one retained IA analysis output package and of each artifact either hosted IA job stores, because both jobs share one artifact store bound. It is larger than the default input-package bound because one analysis restates its own governed input alongside the produced ontology, candidates and navigation evaluation. An output over it is refused, never truncated. A retained planning-input record is bounded separately by ia.packageAllowanceMaxBytes plus the fixed canonical bytes of the discriminator wrapper retention adds.

siteBootstrap.bundleMaxBytes.remediation: Reduce the approved plan's output scope, topic set or evaluation input so the signed application bundle is smaller, or raise siteBootstrap.bundleMaxBytes in config/limits/siteBootstrap.yaml and regenerate the mirrors.
siteBootstrap.bundleMaxBytes.rationale: Admitted size of one signed site-bootstrap application bundle, the single document that carries the approved plan, its reviewer signature, the navigation evaluation it was judged on together with the content index that evaluation read, the selected topics and the two policy bindings. All three readers of that document apply this one bound, each on the declared size before a byte is read - the operator import on the signed file it is given, the parked command-line reader on the file it opens, and the hosted arm on the byte count custody recorded for bytes the import registered, because custody authenticates that count and the digest but never bounds them. An oversize bundle is refused whole, by its own code rather than as a malformed document, and never truncated, because a partial bundle would not verify against the signature the reviewer produced over the complete document.

siteBootstrap.reviewerPolicyMaxBytes.remediation: Remove reviewers who no longer approve plans from the reviewer policy so the registered document is smaller, or raise siteBootstrap.reviewerPolicyMaxBytes in config/limits/siteBootstrap.yaml and regenerate the mirrors.
siteBootstrap.reviewerPolicyMaxBytes.rationale: Admitted size of the reviewer policy document the hosted site-bootstrap arm reads from project custody to verify the reviewer signature over an approved plan. Custody authenticates that document's digest and exact byte count but never bounds them, so the arm refuses a registered policy over this bound on its declared size, before reading it. The value equals the bound the operator's reviewer-policy file reader applies, so every policy an operator can approve a plan with is also admitted when the host executes that plan; that reader serves every IA reviewer-policy consumer and keeps its own bound.

siteBootstrap.runRecordMaxBytes.remediation: Narrow the approved output scope so the retained operation record carries fewer scaffolded pages, or raise siteBootstrap.runRecordMaxBytes in config/limits/siteBootstrap.yaml and regenerate the mirrors.
siteBootstrap.runRecordMaxBytes.rationale: Admitted size of the one operation record the host retains for a site-bootstrap run before the private workspace is removed. The record carries, per approved output, its path, format, template and schema identity, content digest and evidence-gap and todo codes, plus the page validations, the write-transaction summary and the repository-check report; it never carries page bodies, templates or the signed application document, and the impact and change evidence belong to the outer run record. Its size therefore grows with the number of approved outputs rather than with the documentation set that dominates the bundle, and at the roughly 2.5 KiB per output a scaffold records, a quarter of the bundle bound still admits several thousand approved outputs. A record over the bound is refused rather than admitted on the strength of its own measured size, which is what keeps a run from widening its own retention allowance.

inference.rejectionReasonLength.remediation: Raise inference.rejectionReasonLength in config/limits/inference.yaml; a longer reason is refused rather than truncated, because a truncated reason reads as a real one.
inference.rejectionReasonLength.rationale: Longest retainable inference rejection code or location, an order of magnitude above the 45-character longest shipped vocabulary entry and far too short to carry model prose or a host path.

inference.rejectionSegmentLength.remediation: Raise inference.rejectionSegmentLength in config/limits/inference.yaml; both rejection grammars are generated from it, so neither can drift from the other.
inference.rejectionSegmentLength.rationale: Longest identifier segment either inference rejection grammar admits, for a whole kebab-case code and for one dot-separated location member.

inference.echoedKeySegmentRandomChars.remediation: A retry repair counts a reply key instead of naming it when one of the key's segments is at least this long and mixes letters with digits. Lower inference.echoedKeySegmentRandomChars in config/limits/inference.yaml to withhold more keys; the count still tells the model how many undeclared keys it wrote.
inference.echoedKeySegmentRandomChars.rationale: Shortest key segment, split on underscores, hyphens, and dots, that a retry repair treats as random-looking and so never repeats to the model. Schema keys are words of at most 16 letters per segment with no digits, while access keys, tokens, and hex digests run 16 to 64 mixed letters and digits, so a credential the shared detector cannot recognize inside an identifier is counted, not echoed.

inference.rejectionSubjectPathMaxChars.remediation: The attempt's rejectionSubject records withheld over-bound instead of a path longer than this. Raise inference.rejectionSubjectPathMaxChars in config/limits/inference.yaml if a repository's own paths are longer.
inference.rejectionSubjectPathMaxChars.rationale: Longest repository path an attempt's rejectionSubject retains for a refused source citation or a revision's changed paths. The subject keeps only paths the host already knows (a plan write path or a tracked regular file at the run's revision), never model text; 512 is the longest member path original source authority admits, and record readers accept any value up to the maximum so lowering it later keeps older records readable. A longer path is withheld, never truncated, because a cut path names a different file.

inference.rejectionSubjectMaxPaths.remediation: The attempt's rejectionSubject records how many declared and observed changed paths there were, without the paths, when either list is longer than this. Raise inference.rejectionSubjectMaxPaths in config/limits/inference.yaml to list more.
inference.rejectionSubjectMaxPaths.rationale: Most paths one changed-paths rejectionSubject lists in each of its declared and observed lists. Both lists are subsets of the plan's write paths, and the revision accounting decoder admits at most 512 changed paths, the maximum here. A CREATE plan writes one to a few pages, so 64 lists every recorded case while bounding one attempt to about 64 KiB of paths at the path bound. Over the bound, the counts are kept and the paths withheld, never cut.

inference.rejectedReplyShapeMaxDepth.remediation: The attempt's rejectedReplyShape.truncation states how many containers below this depth were not described. Set DOCSFAB_INFERENCE_REJECTED_REPLY_SHAPE_MAX_DEPTH (1 through 32) on the host, or raise inference.rejectedReplyShapeMaxDepth in config/limits/inference.yaml, if a response contract nests deeper.
inference.rejectedReplyShapeMaxDepth.rationale: Deepest JSON nesting that a rejected attempt's reply shape fingerprint describes (#1178). The deepest shipped response contract path, a verification fact locator under $.factInventory.dimensions[].facts[].locators[], is six levels; eight leaves headroom. Containers below the bound are counted, never silently dropped. The fingerprint never records string contents.

inference.rejectedReplyShapeMaxEntries.remediation: The attempt's rejectedReplyShape.truncation states how many distinct key paths or top-level keys were not listed. Set DOCSFAB_INFERENCE_REJECTED_REPLY_SHAPE_MAX_ENTRIES (8 through 1024) on the host, or raise inference.rejectedReplyShapeMaxEntries in config/limits/inference.yaml, if a response contract has more distinct paths.
inference.rejectedReplyShapeMaxEntries.rationale: Most distinct key paths, and most top-level keys, that one rejected attempt's reply shape fingerprint lists (#1178). Array members share one [] path, so this bounds the contract's shape rather than the reply's size. A path is at most inference.rejectedReplyShapeMaxDepth segments of at most inference.rejectionSegmentLength characters, so one attempt adds under 96 KiB to the run record in the worst case and a step at most retry.maxRetries + 1 times that; a shipped contract reply adds a few KiB.

inference.rejectedReplyExcerptChars.remediation: The attempt's rejectedReplyExcerpt states the reply length, the retained segments, and how many characters were not retained under this bound. Set DOCSFAB_INFERENCE_REJECTED_REPLY_EXCERPT_CHARS (0 through 4096) on the host, or change inference.rejectedReplyExcerptChars in config/limits/inference.yaml, to retain more or less of each segment; 0 retains no reply text.
inference.rejectedReplyExcerptChars.rationale: Most reply characters (UTF-16 code units) that one retained segment of a rejected attempt's redacted excerpt copies (#1690). The bound applies per segment and is a host retention policy, hence per-host. Record readers accept any recorded bound, so lowering the maximum later leaves older records readable. An excerpt keeps at most three segments (head, tail, and a window around the strict parser's stop position), so one attempt retains at most three times this value plus redaction markers, and a step at most retry.maxRetries + 1 times that. 512 shows whether a reply opened with reasoning prose, a fence, or an object and how it ended; the rejected 2026-09-30 replies were 6,109 and 19,573 characters, so a whole reply would add tens of KiB per attempt to private run records. 0 keeps the structural fingerprint only and still states the reply length.

inference.maxLengthStopContinuations.remediation: The attempt declined with the existing text-truncated message naming the step, the output limit and the characters retained. Shorten the step's answer, raise the composition maxOutputTokens through an activation amendment, or set DOCSFAB_INFERENCE_MAX_LENGTH_STOP_CONTINUATIONS (0 through 4) on the host, or raise inference.maxLengthStopContinuations in config/limits/inference.yaml. Each continuation spends one more provider turn inside the same attempt deadline.
inference.maxLengthStopContinuations.rationale: Continuation turns one inference attempt may spend completing a structured-reply answer whose turn was cut at the output limit with its partial text retained. Only that shape is continued; a cut that surfaced nothing has no retained prefix to continue. 0 restores the decline-on-cut behaviour without a code change. Default 1 because the four retrievable pilot records of 2026-09-23 were cut after 63,545 to 82,789 characters against a 32,768-token budget, under three characters per token, so a single further budget carries the remainder, while the same records show cut attempts already spending 3.9 to 23.7 minutes of a 30-minute attempt deadline, so a second continuation is more likely to trade the cut for a timeout than to finish. Ceiling 4 admits five budgets, past any recorded answer, and the admitted provider-turn envelope and the attempt deadline still bound continuation independently.

inference.answerRecordAllowanceShareBasi.remediation: Change inference.answerRecordAllowanceShareBasisPoints in config/limits/inference.yaml only with a re-qualification of every records composition, because it sizes their sealed per-message record budget.
inference.answerRecordAllowanceShareBasi.rationale: Share of a route's per-turn output allowance one answer message may plan for record bytes (closed-schema-answer-records-decision.md §4.1 and §4.4, from v10.1 §11.4). The remaining 20% covers the call wrappers, reasoning tokens a route spends before the tool calls, and estimate error, so a planned message never reaches the length stop. The premise probe (#1967) sizes phase B's top rung with the same value.

inference.answerRecordBytesPerTokenFloor.remediation: Change inference.answerRecordBytesPerTokenFloorMilli in config/limits/inference.yaml only with a new measurement of JSON bytes per token on the route's answers and a re-qualification of every records composition.
inference.answerRecordBytesPerTokenFloor.rationale: Lowest JSON bytes per output token measured over the 22 staged Nemotron Super step 8 answers (v9 §2, used by v10.1 §11.4 and closed-schema-answer-records-decision.md §4.1), in thousandths. Sizing record messages never assumes a higher ratio, so a planned message in bytes stays inside the token allowance. The premise probe (#1967) sizes phase B's top rung with the same value.

sealed.compositionLimits.contextWindow.remediation: Changing a sealed compositionLimits field is a re-qualification event, not an edit of this file.

sealed.compositionLimits.maxInputTokens.remediation: Changing a sealed compositionLimits field is a re-qualification event, not an edit of this file.

sealed.compositionLimits.maxOutputTokens.remediation: Changing a sealed compositionLimits field is a re-qualification event, not an edit of this file.

sealed.compositionLimits.maxProviderTurn.remediation: Changing a sealed compositionLimits field is a re-qualification event, not an edit of this file.

sealed.compositionLimits.maxResponseByte.remediation: Changing a sealed compositionLimits field is a re-qualification event, not an edit of this file.

sealed.compositionLimits.timeoutMs.remediation: Changing a sealed compositionLimits field is a re-qualification event, not an edit of this file.

sealed.answerSubmission.maxRecordBytes.remediation: A composition's record byte bound is sealed by re-qualification (a reseal with the records capability), not an edit of this file.
sealed.answerSubmission.maxRecordBytes.rationale: Ceiling on the raw outer bytes of one submit_answer_record call, wrapper included, that any composition may admit (closed-schema-answer-records-decision.md §4.4, B4). It is the top rung of the premise probe's phase A (8 KiB); the 2026-10-06 Nemotron Super probe (#1967) admitted 12 of 12 single-record calls up to that rung. A composition's sealed value is the largest rung its probe admitted 3 of 3, and GO requires at least the largest real record call × 1.5 (4,085 B raw outer bytes on the committed answer-record corpus, whose largest call is 2,723 B). No composition records the records capability yet (design §7, MR 6).

sealed.answerSubmission.maxMessageBytes.remediation: A composition's per-message record byte budget is sealed by re-qualification, not an edit of this file.
sealed.answerSubmission.maxMessageBytes.rationale: Ceiling on the planned record bytes of one answer message (closed-schema-answer-records-decision.md §4.1 and §4.4, B4) - floor(inference.answerRecordAllowanceShareBasisPoints × the 8,192-token allowance × inference.answerRecordBytesPerTokenFloorMilli) = floor(0.8 × 8,192 × 2.86) = 18,743 B, the largest message the formula can plan before the largest phase B message a route admitted 3 of 3 lowers it. The 2026-10-06 probe on Nemotron Super (#1967) admitted no multi-record message, so that route plans one record per message (R9); the R9 amendment to the design record may change this row. No composition records the records capability yet (design §7, MR 6).

sealed.answerSubmission.maxPredictedTime.remediation: Return the records qualification to the design owner for an explicit review; do not increase a composition timer or this review threshold silently.
sealed.answerSubmission.maxPredictedTime.rationale: Accepted planning/review threshold from closed-schema-answer-records-decision.md §§4.3–4.4. This is a qualification decision boundary, not a general runtime timeout cap; a derived T* above it requires design-owner review.

recovery.logicalObjectMaxBytes.remediation: Reduce the individual logical object size, or qualify a reader representation for larger objects before raising this value. Existing manifest-recorded limits remain binding.
recovery.logicalObjectMaxBytes.rationale: Largest logical project object admitted by the current whole-string reader. Defaults to one code unit below the qualified 64-bit Node MAX_STRING_LENGTH for worst-case ASCII, 25 bytes below the approved 512 MiB allowance. The former 256 MiB value was an agent-selected heap margin, not a platform ceiling or owner decision. Restore memory remains a separate qualification.

recovery.legacyLogicalObjectMaxBytes.remediation: Raise recovery.legacyLogicalObjectMaxBytes in config/limits/recovery.yaml for legacy manifests.
recovery.legacyLogicalObjectMaxBytes.rationale: Bound assumed by producers that predate a manifest-recorded bound.

recovery.minimumLogicalObjectMaxBytes.remediation: Keep recovery.minimumLogicalObjectMaxBytes at or above 1 MiB outside a test fixture.
recovery.minimumLogicalObjectMaxBytes.rationale: Floor for any recovery bound, configured here or recorded in a manifest.

recovery.manifestMaxBytes.remediation: Raise recovery.manifestMaxBytes in config/limits/recovery.yaml, or shrink the manifest.
recovery.manifestMaxBytes.rationale: Largest bundle manifest, object inventory, or restore receipt a verifier reads.

recovery.logicalCiphertextOverheadBytes.rationale: Ciphertext allowance the storage adapter adds to the logical bound.

recovery.headroomWarnRatio.remediation: Keep recovery.headroomWarnRatio in (0, 1] and at or below the degraded ratio.
recovery.headroomWarnRatio.rationale: Share of the recovery bound at which a headroom report warns.

recovery.headroomDegradedRatio.remediation: Keep recovery.headroomDegradedRatio in (0, 1] and at or above the warn ratio.
recovery.headroomDegradedRatio.rationale: Share of the recovery bound at which a headroom report is degraded.

recovery.serviceHistoryMaxHostJobs.remediation: Raise recovery.serviceHistoryMaxHostJobs in config/limits/recovery.yaml, or accept that the logical export keeps only the newest host-job rows and leaves the rest in the physical image.
recovery.serviceHistoryMaxHostJobs.rationale: Newest host-job rows retained in the logical recovery export, defaulting to the existing admitted maximum. Older rows remain in the source cluster and encrypted physical image. A larger row window can enlarge the export; the independent logical object byte bound still applies.
recovery.serviceHistoryMaxHostJobs.docSummary: Newest host-job rows in a logical recovery export; older rows remain in the physical image.

recovery.backupRetentionDays.remediation: Keep recovery.backupRetentionDays within 1 to 30 days in config/limits/recovery.yaml. Raising the maximum needs a Privacy-approved change to the recorded retention commitment first.
recovery.backupRetentionDays.rationale: Age in whole days after which pilot backup packages and local staging bundles expire. After each backup that is stored and verified, the backup tool deletes Generic Package versions in the private GitLab recovery project and local staging bundles older than this, and always keeps the newest verified backup. Git history in the recovery repository (manifests, receipts, and logical exports) is not pruned by this bound; its cleanup needs owner and Privacy authorization (#1790). 30 days is the commitment in the DocsFab 0.0.1 record of processing activities, so the maximum equals the value and there is no host override. A lower value shortens the restore window.
recovery.backupRetentionDays.docSummary: Age after which pilot backup packages and local staging bundles are pruned; recovery-repository Git history is not pruned.

recovery.credentialStoreRequestTimeoutSe.remediation: Keep recovery.credentialStoreRequestTimeoutSeconds within 1 to 30 seconds in config/limits/recovery.yaml. A store that needs longer is unhealthy; the failed backup reports recovery-credential-store-unreachable and the next scheduled run retries.
recovery.credentialStoreRequestTimeoutSe.rationale: Deadline for each request a recovery operation makes to the external secret store that provides its credentials (login, one data read and one metadata read per credential, and token revocation). A healthy store answers in well under a second, so 30 seconds leaves wide headroom for a slow network without letting a scheduled backup hang on an unreachable store. A request that misses it fails the operation with a coded refusal; there is no retry inside the operation.
recovery.credentialStoreRequestTimeoutSe.docSummary: Deadline for each request to the external secret store that provides recovery credentials.

deploy.diskHeadroomOverBytes.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_DEPLOY_DISK_HEADROOM_OVER_BYTES so effective warn still exceeds over, or raise deploy.diskHeadroomOverBytes in config/limits/deploy.yaml. Keep deploy.diskHeadroomWarnBytes strictly greater than this floor.
deploy.diskHeadroomOverBytes.rationale: Absolute available-bytes floor at which docsfab-status reports disk headroom over (exit 3, never exit 1). 1342177280 is 1.25 GiB, the critical threshold already used by service-status.sh after the pilot host reached ~1.06 GiB free at 98% used. Percent-used is not the signal; available bytes are. A host override may only lower it. Effective deploy.diskHeadroomWarnBytes must exceed this floor.

deploy.diskHeadroomWarnBytes.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_DEPLOY_DISK_HEADROOM_WARN_BYTES so effective warn still exceeds over, or raise deploy.diskHeadroomWarnBytes in config/limits/deploy.yaml. The warn floor must stay strictly greater than deploy.diskHeadroomOverBytes.
deploy.diskHeadroomWarnBytes.rationale: Absolute available-bytes floor at which docsfab-status reports disk headroom warn (exit 3). 3221225472 is 3 GiB, the early-warning threshold already used by service-status.sh so one release or core-tooling refresh still fits. A host override may only lower it. Effective warn must exceed deploy.diskHeadroomOverBytes.

deploy.diskFreeMinBytes.remediation: Free space on the recovery staging volume, then retry the backup.
deploy.diskFreeMinBytes.rationale: First backup staging disk-free precondition. Sized to recovery.logicalObjectMaxBytes so one logical object can be staged. Available bytes at this floor pass; one byte less refuses rather than filling the volume. Catalog min is that one-logical-object floor. A host can restate the floor through DOCSFAB_DEPLOY_DISK_FREE_MIN_BYTES in recovery.env; install, systemd, the env -i backup transition, and backup start parse that override fail-fast. A value below one logical object refuses.

deploy.hostTimeoutStopSeconds.remediation: Keep TimeoutStopSec on docsfab-host.service equal to this named value. Changing it is a deployment change, not a live edit.
deploy.hostTimeoutStopSeconds.rationale: Fixed release invariant equal to TimeoutStopSec on docsfab-host.service. T2 audits that unit and the unset timeouts on docsfab-recovery.service without changing those defaults. Host configuration cannot override it.

deploy.statusProbeTimeoutSeconds.remediation: Configure a positive whole-second observation deadline within the supported safe-integer domain; a timed-out probe reports unavailable health.
deploy.statusProbeTimeoutSeconds.rationale: Preserves the five-second observation policy. On the supported 64-bit hosts curl secs2ms accepts LONG_MAX divided by 1000 seconds, which exceeds JavaScript MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; safe-integer seconds are therefore the narrower configuration domain. This is an observation deadline, not a job allowance or retry delay.

deploy.statusLogLines.remediation: Select a positive safe-integer line count with --log-lines or DOCSFAB_STATUS_LOG_LINES; logs remain streamed by tail from the selected regular file.
deploy.statusLogLines.rationale: Diagnostic output allowance at the supported configuration maximum. The deployed 64-bit tail accepts this count without an arbitrary 1000-line ceiling; JavaScript's exact integer domain is narrower than tail's signed 64-bit count. This does not change log contents, custody or credential screening.

deploy.coreLineageDocumentMaxBytes.remediation: Inspect the named document in the approved root session; the installer never writes one this large. Raise deploy.coreLineageDocumentMaxBytes in config/limits/deploy.yaml only through a reviewed change, then refresh the core tooling from that clone.
deploy.coreLineageDocumentMaxBytes.rationale: Largest document the installer's core-tooling lineage program reads before parsing it - a lineage receipt, a recovery-hook or core artifact transition backup plan, the feedback publication persistence receipt, and the deployment state. Each is a fixed-shape record of a few kilobytes that grows only with the core artifact count, so 128 KiB bounds a corrupt or hostile file without refusing any document the installer writes. The installer reads the value from the generated shell mirror installed beside it and has no default. The early warning fires on stderr at warnAt of the bound. Sealed, because a host override could make an already sealed lineage unreadable.

sources.revalidationMaxEntries.remediation: Revalidate fewer attached sources in one command by naming the label the source listing prints, or lower sources.revalidationMaxEntries in config/limits/sources.yaml.
sources.revalidationMaxEntries.rationale: One revalidation opens one tracked export, may read each targeted file to the version ceiling, and spends one forge identity resolution per targeted merged change. 32 keeps a single operator command inside one screenful and refuses beyond it rather than re-checking a prefix and reporting on the rest by silence. The host tier may only lower it.

sources.revalidationFreshnessWindowMinut.remediation: Revalidate again to take a current verdict, or lower sources.revalidationFreshnessWindowMinutes in config/limits/sources.yaml.
sources.revalidationFreshnessWindowMinut.rationale: A revalidation verdict is a statement about the repository at one moment, and a listing that keeps printing it makes a currency claim nothing re-checked. 15 minutes outlasts an operator attach-check-run loop and expires before a working branch ordinarily moves, so a lapsed verdict is marked rather than dropped. The host tier may only lower it.

sources.purgeMaxSessionsPerInvocation.remediation: Purge fewer sessions in one command by naming them in separate invocations, or lower sources.purgeMaxSessionsPerInvocation in config/limits/sources.yaml.
sources.purgeMaxSessionsPerInvocation.rationale: A purge is destructive and is authorized by one confirmation over one preview, so that preview has to be readable in full before the confirmation is given. Each named session contributes its own copy rows, affected run ids and remaining retention scope. 4 keeps one confirmation over something an operator can actually read, and refuses beyond it rather than authorizing a deletion nobody reviewed. The host tier may only lower it.

sources.purgePreviewMaxRows.remediation: Purge one session at a time so its copy rows fit the preview, or lower sources.purgePreviewMaxRows in config/limits/sources.yaml.
sources.purgePreviewMaxRows.rationale: A purge preview prints one row per owned copy, and an unbounded list scrolls the confirmation and the retention statement off the screen. 64 rows is a screenful on an ordinary terminal. Rows beyond it are counted and reported as withheld rather than dropped, and the confirmation is minted over every copy the purge would delete, so a capped preview still authorizes exactly what it says. The host tier may only lower it.

sources.claimMinWords.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_SOURCES_CLAIM_MIN_WORDS to a whole number from 1 through 64, or change sources.claimMinWords in config/limits/sources.yaml. A sentence below the floor is not checked for a citation, and an uncited sentence at or above it is recorded as a source-citation-gaps limitation, not a stop.
sources.claimMinWords.rationale: A sentence a write step adds to documentation is a material claim when it has at least this many words; only words with a letter or digit count. Three-word fragments are headings, list labels and transitions, not assertions about a source, so four is the smallest count that excludes those while admitting the shortest real claim. The host tier may raise it to label only longer sentences, or lower it to 1 to label every sentence. 64 words is about twice the longest sentence a technical style guide admits, so above it no ordinary sentence would count and the label would be off; that needs a reviewed change to this file, not a host setting. Every claim at 64 words still fits sources.citeMaxClaimCharacters, so it stays citable.

sources.citeMaxSpansPerCall.remediation: Cite fewer spans per call, or raise sources.citeMaxSpansPerCall in config/limits/sources.yaml.
sources.citeMaxSpansPerCall.rationale: The same per-call span ceiling docsfab_read_source already applies, so a citation cannot name more spans than a single read could have returned.

sources.citeMaxClaimCharacters.remediation: Cite fewer sentences per call, or raise sources.citeMaxClaimCharacters in config/limits/sources.yaml. A longer claim is refused rather than truncated.
sources.citeMaxClaimCharacters.rationale: A claim is one or a few sentences of the documentation the step writes. The ceiling exists so the citation channel cannot be used as unbounded storage that the host then digests and records.

sources.citeMaxClaimsPerCall.remediation: Cite fewer sentences per call, or raise sources.citeMaxClaimsPerCall in config/limits/sources.yaml. Beyond the bound the call refuses rather than silently registering a prefix.
sources.citeMaxClaimsPerCall.rationale: A model may cite a short run of sentences in one call rather than one call per sentence. Eight bounds how much a single call can register without making the receipt unreadable.

sources.listMaxEntries.remediation: Request fewer entries in one docsfab_list_sources or docsfab_read_review_change_side inventory call with maxEntries or maxFiles, then follow its next cursor. Raising sources.listMaxEntries requires a reviewed change to config/limits/sources.yaml; hosts cannot override the model-visible tool schema.
sources.listMaxEntries.rationale: Presentation. This retains the existing 256-entry default and maximum of docsfab_list_sources and shares them with the pinned review side inventory, so one source-list policy governs both model-visible page schemas. A page above the host output cap is explicitly marked and can be retried from the same cursor with a smaller requested size; entries are never silently skipped. The limit is sealed because the tool schema advertises its maximum before the model connects and must agree across hosts.

sources.readResponseCeilingBytes.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_SOURCES_READ_RESPONSE_CEILING_BYTES to at least the bytes named, up to 67108864, so one step can read every required source whole, or bind fewer or smaller sources, then start a new run.
sources.readResponseCeilingBytes.rationale: One workflow step's shared source-read budget across every bound source. Historical normalized reads charge extracted text bytes; exact-original-utf8 reads charge the actual serialized tool result or raw-attributable automatic-prompt bytes, including escaped text, source IDs, original offsets, identity labels and framing. Both modes spend the same budget in one attempt. A bound model with an attested input window lowers it to sources.readInputWindowShare of that window when that is smaller. The former 32 KiB default made a private requirements document exported at 39,789 bytes unreadable in one step, so it was cut by hand to 25,783 bytes and lost six feature sections; real requirements documents and RFCs run past 40 KB. 256 KiB holds six such documents whole. A normalized host read carries a span id and JSON framing beside every span, 1.6 to 2.6 times the extracted text for lines of 128 to 50 bytes, so a full 256 KiB budget estimates at about a fifth of the 1,000,000-token and larger windows of the pilot and benchmark compositions, and smaller windows take the share instead. Raw Git originals are charged for their measured serialization instead of this ratio; escaping may reduce how much fits. A source larger than what is left of the budget is still reachable. docsfab_read_source reads windows of whole spans from a byte offset, coverage counts every span any step of the run read, and a write step reads only the spans no step has read, so a source can be read across steps and attempts. A required source that is still not read whole is reported as partially read, with bytes read out of total and the limit that bound it, in the run record and the LIMITATIONS footer, and never as considered. A host override may raise the budget up to 64 MiB, the byte length the source-evidence contract admits for one representation. createSourceStepPolicy refuses a requested budget above this ceiling rather than clamping it. A retry restores the grant per attempt, less the bytes the host read into the step's prompt, and does not inherit bytes a prior failed attempt already spent.

sources.readInputWindowShare.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_SOURCES_READ_INPUT_WINDOW_SHARE, up to 1, so source reads may fill more of the model's input window, run with a model whose input window is larger, or bind fewer or smaller sources, then start a new run.
sources.readInputWindowShare.rationale: Share of the bound model's input window, after its context reserve, that one step's source reads may fill, at the host token estimator's 4 bytes per token. The per-step source-read budget is the smaller of sources.readResponseCeilingBytes and this share. An installed composition's window counts whatever its profile metadata says; with provider-side context admission, a profile that matches no installed composition and whose metadata is unknown or stale, such as the placeholder window docsfab setup writes for an endpoint that matches no installed composition (modelProfile.conservativeFallbackContextWindow), or no bound model, no host window is attested and the ceiling applies alone. Context packets count windows by the same rule. A normalized host read carries a span id and JSON framing beside every span, so its prompt section runs 1.6 to 2.6 times the extracted text for lines of 128 to 50 bytes, and the context governor adds a 5/4 margin, so at 0.15 a full budget of such text estimates at 30% to 49% of the window. An exact-original Git read instead spends its measured escaped tool or automatic-prompt serialization under the same smaller-of-ceiling-and-share rule; it can reach the bound sooner without silent clipping. With the 1,024-token context reserve docsfab setup writes, that is 38,707 bytes on a 65,536-token window, more than the former 32 KiB default, so a source that default read whole still reads whole there, and 76,185 on a 128,000-token one, so a 39,789-byte requirements document reads whole on 128,000 tokens and in part on 65,536, reported as partially read. A share of 0.1 gave a 65,536-token window 25,804 bytes at that reserve and left a 29,952-byte source that the former default read whole partly read. Windows of 437,931 tokens and more keep the 262,144-byte ceiling. A source of much shorter spans, such as structured values of a few bytes, carries more framing per byte and can still exceed a window; context admission then stops the step with a coded context-exhausted rather than truncating it.

sources.extractionMaxOriginalBytes.remediation: Bind a smaller source, such as a narrower merged-MR window or a smaller tracked file, or raise DOCSFAB_SOURCES_EXTRACTION_MAX_ORIGINAL_BYTES, up to 67108864, then start a new run.
sources.extractionMaxOriginalBytes.rationale: Default original-byte ceiling for source extraction. An original one byte over this bound is refused rather than truncated, and the refusal names the bytes it observed, this limit, and the remediation. A merged merge request's rendered diff is an original too, so a diff past this ceiling stops the run at bind. A host override may raise it up to 64 MiB, the byte length the source-evidence contract admits for one original, or lower it.

sources.extractionMaxDerivativeBytes.remediation: Bind a smaller file or a narrower selection, or raise DOCSFAB_SOURCES_EXTRACTION_MAX_DERIVATIVE_BYTES, up to 67108864, then start a new run.
sources.extractionMaxDerivativeBytes.rationale: Default derivative-byte ceiling for source extraction. Crossing it keeps the whole spans that fit and records byte-budget-truncated, with the full derivative size, on the sealed representation, so the operator summary cannot silently clip. A merged merge request's diff between this ceiling and sources.extractionMaxOriginalBytes binds in part this way. Diff spans are whole lines of about this ceiling divided by sources.extractionMaxSpans, so raising it also lengthens them. A host override may raise it up to 64 MiB, the byte length the source-evidence contract admits for one representation, or lower it.

sources.extractionMaxSpans.remediation: Bind a smaller file, or raise sources.extractionMaxSpans in config/limits/sources.yaml.
sources.extractionMaxSpans.rationale: Default span ceiling for source extraction. Crossing it records span-budget-truncated on the sealed representation. Override may only lower it.

sources.extractionMaxSpanBytes.remediation: Change sources.extractionMaxSpanBytes in config/limits/sources.yaml through a reviewed DocsFab change; a host cannot override it. A longer extracted line or value is split into spans of at most this size rather than refused.
sources.extractionMaxSpanBytes.rationale: Technical capacity. The longest span one extracted line, structured value, notebook cell, or valid-UTF-8 original chunk keeps. A longer one is split into consecutive spans on UTF-8 code-point boundaries, so docsfab_read_source can page through it by window instead of meeting one span larger than the step's read budget; every byte stays in exactly one span. 16384 is half the default 32 KiB per-call tool output cap, which is the default maxBytes of a docsfab_read_source window and counts span text only, so a default window returns two whole spans of a long line, and one span fits the per-step source-read budget of any attested input window of about 28,000 tokens or more at the default sources.readInputWindowShare. A smaller window reads such a span only through a coded budget refusal that names the budget. Ordinary lines and values are far shorter and keep one span each, and sources.extractionMaxSpans still bounds the total. A raw Git view additionally checks the fully escaped result against the live tool cap before an access receipt; this span ceiling alone does not promise that every worst-case escaped span fits the per-call cap. The value is part of the extractor options digest, so representations split at different values never share an identity, and it reads the same on every host. Catalog min is 4, the longest UTF-8 code point, so every span holds at least one whole code point.

sources.extractionMaxMs.remediation: Bind a smaller file, or raise sources.extractionMaxMs in config/limits/sources.yaml.
sources.extractionMaxMs.rationale: Default wall-clock budget for one source extraction. A parser that has not yielded inside this window is refused rather than left running. Override may only lower it.

sources.pdfMaxPages.remediation: Bind a shorter PDF, or raise sources.pdfMaxPages in config/limits/sources.yaml.
sources.pdfMaxPages.rationale: Page ceiling for the PDF.js text adapter. A longer document is read up to this page and records over-page-limit rather than claiming a complete extract. Override may only lower it.

sources.authorityMemberPathMaxChars.remediation: Shorten the named tracked path, commit the change, and rerun the same command. Raising sources.authorityMemberPathMaxChars in config/limits/sources.yaml changes the sealed original source authority contract and needs a DocsFab change, not an override.
sources.authorityMemberPathMaxChars.rationale: Longest repository-relative path, in UTF-16 code units, that the original source authority admits as a member. Every regular tracked file of a review or update run becomes a member, and sealed run evidence keeps each path, so this is the contract's own capacity and must read the same on every host; no override tier applies. 512 is the bound the member-path pattern carried before it moved to this catalog. Tracked-file reads admit paths up to 1,024 code units, so a longer tracked path stops here with this code and the path rather than with an uncoded error. A unified diff source's `diff` locators carry their file paths under the same bound; a longer diff path is carried as null with the file labeled unrepresentable-path, and the diff still binds.

sources.toolRefusalRecordMaxRows.remediation: Read tools.toolRefusals.overflowCount on the step, which counts every refused call that opened no row; its rows still name each distinct refusal up to the bound. Raising sources.toolRefusalRecordMaxRows in config/limits/sources.yaml changes the run record contract and needs a DocsFab change, not an override.
sources.toolRefusalRecordMaxRows.rationale: Distinct refusal rows a step attempt's tool summary keeps for source and git history tool calls. Identical refusals collapse into one row with a count, so a model that retries one refused call costs one row, and only distinct argument shapes, codes, and id classes open more. A row is content-free and under 400 bytes, so 64 rows stay under 25 KiB of run record per attempt. One attempt's refused calls are bounded by compositionExecution.maxToolCallsPerStep anyway; this keeps the record small when a model varies every call. A refused call past it is counted in overflowCount, never dropped silently. Run record decoders check rows against this value, so it must read the same on every host and no override tier applies.

sources.createAddedAuthoritySourcesMax.remediation: Propose fewer additional tracked sources in this run, or raise DOCSFAB_SOURCES_CREATE_ADDED_AUTHORITY_SOURCES_MAX within its supported range.
sources.createAddedAuthoritySourcesMax.rationale: Additional tracked files one create run may admit beyond its plan-bound source set. Three independent retained create runs (#2023) each identified one relevant tracked source outside the plan; 8 additions leave room for more than the observed need and two extra cross-cutting sources while keeping authority growth bounded per run. Each source still passes the repository member rules and normal source-read budgets. The maximum of 64 is the closed response's source-locator ceiling, so the admission count cannot exceed the number of distinct source paths one response could cite. Duplicate proposals for already admitted paths do not consume this bound.

changeSources.commitsMax.remediation: Narrow the --change range to fewer commits, or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_COMMITS_MAX up to 4096, then run again.
changeSources.commitsMax.rationale: Commits one --change range may carry. The host reads every commit object in the range to recompute its id, and the manifest observation lists each commit's id, parents and subject, measured at about 170 bytes plus the subject for a commit with SHA-1 ids. 256 covers a large merge request or a short release with room to spare and keeps the commit list near 60 KB with typical subjects. A whole release range can raise it through the host override. No count bounds subject or path lengths, so the host extracts the whole manifest, commits and changed paths together, under sources.extractionMaxDerivativeBytes and sources.extractionMaxSpans before any model call, and refuses with that limit and the observed size rather than truncate. The count is read with rev-list --count before any commit is listed, so a refusal reports the real number.

changeSources.changedFilesMax.remediation: Narrow the --change range so it changes fewer files, or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_CHANGED_FILES_MAX up to 4096, then run again.
changeSources.changedFilesMax.rationale: Changed paths one --change range may carry. It is also the rename-detection limit passed to git as -l, so rename detection is never silently degraded inside the admitted range. 512 covers merge requests that touch a generated tree or a vendored directory. The manifest observation measures about 350 bytes a changed path plus the path itself, once for an added or deleted file and twice otherwise, with SHA-1 ids, so 512 short paths make about 190 KB. Long paths or subjects can still outgrow extraction, so the host extracts the whole manifest under the source extraction limits before any model call and refuses with the observed size. A wider range refuses with the counted number rather than listing a prefix.

changeSources.diffMaxBytes.remediation: Narrow the --change range so its diff is smaller, or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_DIFF_MAX_BYTES up to 1048576, then run again.
changeSources.diffMaxBytes.rationale: Bytes of unified diff one --change range may bind as evidence, after file diffs over changeSources.fileDiffMaxBytes are omitted and labelled. The default uses the existing 1 MiB extraction ceiling so an ordinary source-and-documentation PR can bind its whole diff; the live review of nemotron-voice-agent PR 161 needed 424,773 bytes and exceeded the previous 256 KiB default. Acquisition capacity is independent of one step's bounded source-read response, which reads the admitted evidence in spans. The ceiling is sources.extractionMaxDerivativeBytes; the host checks that relation, and that the bound stays below the sealed hostInvoker.gitOutputMaxBytes that caps every git read, before any git read. Extraction adds a manifest of one summary row and one row per file, so the raw-byte relation is necessary, not sufficient. Before any model call the host extracts the diff whole under the run's source extraction limits and refuses one whose extracted form would cross a limit, naming that limit, the bound in force and the observed size, rather than bind part of it.

changeSources.fileDiffMaxBytes.remediation: The file stays listed in the manifest with its observed diff size; to bind its diff, raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_FILE_DIFF_MAX_BYTES up to changeSources.diffMaxBytes, then run again.
changeSources.fileDiffMaxBytes.rationale: Bytes of one file's diff that bind as evidence. A lockfile or generated bundle can change by megabytes while the rest of the change is small, so a file over this bound is omitted from the diff observation and labelled, with its observed size, in the manifest and the operator status, instead of refusing the whole range. A file whose computed upper bound already exceeds the sealed hostInvoker.gitOutputMaxBytes is omitted the same way without its diff being read, and labelled with that upper bound. 128 KiB keeps at least two full-size files inside the default changeSources.diffMaxBytes. It must not exceed changeSources.diffMaxBytes; the host checks that before any git read.

changeSources.shallowBoundaryCommitsMax.remediation: Unshallow the checkout with git fetch --unshallow, or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_SHALLOW_BOUNDARY_COMMITS_MAX up to 4096, then run again.
changeSources.shallowBoundaryCommitsMax.rationale: Shallow-boundary commits one --change range's exclusion walk may cross in a shallow checkout. Git walks a boundary commit as parentless, so to keep the diff base's own history out of the commit list the host follows each boundary commit's recorded parents itself, re-hashing that commit and checking its parents' presence, in a few local git reads per round. Git walks the history between boundaries, so the commit count behind the diff base is not what costs, and changeSources.commitsMax, which bounds the range's own commits after the walk, does not bound this; the two are independent, so the host checks no relation between them. Shallow clones of this repository at depths 20, 50 and 200 hold 4, 4 and 2 boundary commits, and a shallow clone that later fetched other branches adds about one per fetch, so 64 leaves wide room. The count is cumulative; the walk refuses as soon as it crosses one more than the limit, reporting the count it reached, rather than list a range it could not prove.

changeSources.mrDiscussionsMax.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_MR_DISCUSSIONS_MAX up to 4096, or reduce the merge request's total discussion count, then run again.
changeSources.mrDiscussionsMax.rationale: Discussions one merge request's review threads may carry, counted over every discussion GitLab lists, system and resolved ones included, before the selector narrows them. It also fixes the last page the reader asks for, ceil(limit / 100) + 1 at GitLab's page size of 100, so a listing past it refuses before that page is read. Measured on this project's own 1,674 merge requests, the busiest, !379, lists 107 discussions over two pages; the next ones list under 70, and recent ones 14 to 28. 256 is more than twice the busiest. A count over the limit refuses with the number read rather than bind a prefix.

changeSources.mrDiscussionsMaxBytes.remediation: Bind the merge request's unresolved discussions only, or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_MR_DISCUSSIONS_MAX_BYTES up to sources.extractionMaxDerivativeBytes, then run again.
changeSources.mrDiscussionsMaxBytes.rationale: Bytes of the rendered evidence original one merge request's bound discussions may make, every note's header and its whole body. Measured on this project, the busiest merge request, !379, holds about 230 KB of note bodies, !1030 about 172 KB, and recent ones 10 to 28 KB; one note header adds about 500 bytes. 512 KiB holds the busiest about twice over. The ceiling of 1 MiB is the default sources.extractionMaxDerivativeBytes, and the host checks that the effective value stays within sources.extractionMaxDerivativeBytes and sources.extractionMaxOriginalBytes before any read, so a bound original is never cut by extraction. Each GitLab answer is also capped by the command runner's output bound; a cut answer refuses as mr-discussions-page-bound and is never parsed. An original over the limit refuses with its measured size; no body is ever sliced.

changeSourcesGithub.pagesMax.remediation: Pass a smaller pull request or commit, check the change out and pass a local --change range, or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_GITHUB_PAGES_MAX up to 64, then run again.
changeSourcesGithub.pagesMax.rationale: Listing pages one GitHub --change resolution reads, at the GitHub REST maximum of 100 items a page. A pull request or a compare URL reads its compare listing, one page per 100 commits, so changeSources.commitsMax (256) needs 3 (a compare URL's two ref pins are single reads, not listing pages); a commit reads its file listing, one page per 100 files, so changeSources.changedFilesMax (512) needs 6. 8 covers both default bounds with one page to spare. Every page is one anonymous request, and GitHub allows 60 anonymous requests an hour from one address, so a raised bound spends that allowance faster. The resolution refuses before reading one page more than the bound, with the page count it would have reached, rather than bind a partial list; a raised changeSources.* bound may need this one raised too.

changeSourcesGithub.responseMaxBytes.remediation: Check the change out and pass a local --change range, or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_GITHUB_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES up to 67108864, then run again.
changeSourcesGithub.responseMaxBytes.rationale: Bytes of one GitHub API response body, counted while it streams. The largest response a resolution reads is a recursive Git tree. GitHub documents its own cap on that read as 100,000 entries or 7 MB and then marks the tree truncated (refused with change-source-github-tree-truncated), but does not say whether the 7 MB measures the JSON body. Each JSON entry also carries a url and a size, roughly 200 to 260 bytes, so a tree past about 32,000 entries can reach 8 MiB first and refuses with this bound's code and its remediation instead; that has not been measured against a live large tree. A compare page carries up to 300 files with their patches and a commit page 100, which stay well below it. A response one byte past the bound refuses with the bytes counted so far; nothing is parsed from a partial body.

changeSourcesGithub.redirectsMax.remediation: Check that the GitHub URL names the repository by its current owner and name, or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_GITHUB_REDIRECTS_MAX up to 10, then run again.
changeSourcesGithub.redirectsMax.rationale: Redirects one GitHub API request may follow, each within https://api.github.com; a redirect to any other origin refuses with change-source-github-redirect-cross-host whatever this bound. GitHub answers a renamed or transferred repository with one redirect to its /repositories/<id> path, and the same 3 the benchmark miner allows (benchmarkMining.redirectsMax) leaves room for a rename followed by a transfer without following a loop. The request that would follow one redirect more refuses with that count.

changeSourcesGithub.requestTimeoutMs.remediation: Check this host's network path to api.github.com, then run again, or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_GITHUB_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS up to 120000.
changeSourcesGithub.requestTimeoutMs.rationale: Wall-clock bound on one GitHub API request, its redirects counted separately, from sending it to the last byte of its body. The benchmark miner measured about 0.5 s a GitHub request in its 2026-10-01 smoke run and allows 30 s for a large recursive tree (benchmarkMining.githubRequestTimeoutMs); this reader uses the same 30 s and does not retry, so a resolution of about 6 requests fails within minutes, before any model call, instead of hanging. A request past the bound is aborted and refuses with the elapsed time.

changeSourcesGithub.acquisitionMaxBytes.remediation: Narrow the public PR's object range or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_GITHUB_ACQUISITION_MAX_BYTES up to 1073741824, then retry.
changeSourcesGithub.acquisitionMaxBytes.rationale: Aggregate admitted smart-HTTP response bytes, including pack, framing, control and progress, across an acquisition. 64 MiB covers a 512-path documentation change with two 64 KiB sides (64 MiB logical blob bytes) when compressed, and the ordinary 64-document fixture has substantial headroom. This is an application admission and retention limit, not a bound on bytes already received by TLS before the crossing chunk is refused.

changeSourcesGithub.packInflatedMaxBytes.remediation: Narrow the PR or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_GITHUB_PACK_INFLATED_MAX_BYTES up to 2147483648, then retry.
changeSourcesGithub.packInflatedMaxBytes.rationale: Sum of every pack entry's declared inflated payload, including delta instructions, charged before allocation across all packs. 256 MiB leaves room for tree/history objects and duplicate entries around a 64 MiB logical documentation change.

changeSourcesGithub.objectMaterializedMa.remediation: Narrow the PR or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_GITHUB_OBJECT_MATERIALIZED_MAX_BYTES up to 2147483648, then retry.
changeSourcesGithub.objectMaterializedMa.rationale: Sum of complete object target sizes declared by ordinary entries or delta target varints, with repeated objects charged again, before native Git reconstructs any delta. This bounds untrusted logical object payload rather than RSS or filesystem blocks.

changeSourcesGithub.objectsMax.remediation: Narrow the PR or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_GITHUB_OBJECTS_MAX up to 1048576, then retry.
changeSourcesGithub.objectsMax.rationale: Aggregate pack entries checked before array allocation and native import. 262144 provisionally admits two large tree closures plus history; actual count is reconciled in the preflight.

changeSourcesGithub.historyCommitsMax.remediation: Narrow the PR history or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_GITHUB_HISTORY_COMMITS_MAX up to 65536, then retry.
changeSourcesGithub.historyCommitsMax.rationale: Actual acquired commit objects needed to certify the merge base, including fork and merge ancestry, counted independently of changeSources.commitsMax proposal commits. The ordinary fork fixture spans more than 256 ancestor commits.

changeSourcesGithub.acquisitionTimeoutMs.remediation: Retry when GitHub and the local host are responsive, or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_GITHUB_ACQUISITION_TIMEOUT_MS up to 600000.
changeSourcesGithub.acquisitionTimeoutMs.rationale: Cumulative elapsed time across requests, pack preflight, native import and object reads. 120 seconds composes several existing 30-second request phases while bounding the full operation.

changeSourcesRelease.unitsMax.remediation: Name a release range with fewer first-parent commits, such as two adjacent release tags, or raise DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_RELEASE_UNITS_MAX up to 4096, then run again.
changeSourcesRelease.unitsMax.rationale: First-parent commits (units) one --change release range may enumerate. Every unit is listed in the units index, bound or not, so this bounds the index rather than the evidence a run binds, which changeSourcesRelease.unitsPerRunMax pages. This repository's v0.0.1-rc.1..v0.0.1-rc.2 holds 126 units (all merge commits) and v0.0.1-rc.1..main 254 units, measured on 2026-10-07; 512 holds twice the longer one. An index entry is about 500 bytes for a later-page unit and about 800 for a bound merge unit with its introduced commit, so 512 entries stay inside sources.extractionMaxDerivativeBytes, which the index is extracted under before any model call. The whole index must also fit one step's source-read budget (see changeSourcesRelease.unitsPerRunMax). At the 262,144-byte ceiling a range of about 450 units still binds a full page, and v0.0.1-rc.0..v0.0.1-rc.1 (389 units) does; on a smaller model window a long range binds a shorter page, or refuses with change-source-release-index-over-read-budget when not even one unit fits beside the listing. The count is read with rev-list --first-parent --count before any unit is listed, so a refusal reports the real number.

changeSourcesRelease.unitsPerRunMax.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_CHANGE_SOURCES_RELEASE_UNITS_PER_RUN_MAX or pass fewer --source files, then run again; the units index names the continuation selector for the units after this page.
changeSourcesRelease.unitsPerRunMax.rationale: Units one run resolves and binds as evidence, the first page of the release range, oldest first. Each bound unit adds two observations (its change-source record and its diff) and the release adds one units index, and a source binding holds at most 256 observations, so 127 units is the most one run can bind and the ceiling here. The units index is the release's one required read and a write step reads it whole, so before any model call the host also shortens the page until the index fits the source-read budget of the model the run binds (sources.readResponseCeilingBytes, or sources.readInputWindowShare of a smaller window), records that budget in the index, and names the shortened page in the status output; unit records and diffs are bound but optional, because requiring them split the budget into fragments (on v0.0.1-rc.1..v0.0.1-rc.2 they needed 1,002,483 bytes against 262,144, and the index was read at 3,370 of 103,400 bytes). Measured on 2026-10-07, this repository's v0.0.1-rc.1..v0.0.1-rc.2 release (126 merge units, about 15 changed files each) has a units index of about 103,600 bytes, so 126 binds it in one run at the default ceiling with room for three --source files; on a 128,000-token window (76,185 bytes) the same release pages. A longer range is paged, not refused - the index and the operator status list every unit after the page with the continuation selector release:<last bound unit>..<head> - and the host refuses before any model call, with the observed count, when the index, the page and the --source files would exceed the binding's cap.

sourceCitation.mintedMaxChars.remediation: Cite narrower line ranges so the admitted artifact's minted quotes together fit sourceCitation.mintedMaxChars; the step re-asks within its existing retry budget. Raising the value in config/limits/sourceCitation.yaml re-qualifies the summary readers and is not a retry.
sourceCitation.mintedMaxChars.rationale: Total UTF-16 characters of quote text the host mints from model-supplied line-range citations into one admitted artifact (a source readiness assessment or a repository bootstrap result); scope per-run because each run admits one such artifact. A citation is three integers that can name a whole file, so minting removes the bound the model's own output once placed on quoted text. Measured on lane D (Inference Hub, 2026-10-01) the admitted gpt-6-sol artifacts carried 473 characters over 8 sentence quotes (readiness dba0a124) and 156 and 238 characters (bootstrap 4f49cc03, 956fe458); whole-line minting widens a sentence to its lines, so 32768 admits 16 citations of 25 lines of 80 characters and keeps an artifact under 3.3% of the 1000000-character step summary readers. The maximum is runtime.contract.maxStringChars, so a single minted quote always re-decodes through the strict contract walk.

toolOutput.archiveCeilingBytes.remediation: Narrow the tool request (offset and limit, path, pattern, or glob) so its result fits the per-call cap, or raise toolOutput.archiveCeilingBytes in config/limits/toolOutput.yaml.
toolOutput.archiveCeilingBytes.rationale: Technical capacity. Bytes of original oversized tool results that one confined tool set holds for exact recall (#1043). The archive lives only as long as that tool set, which is one step attempt. The supported step workload fits. compositionExecution.maxToolCallsPerStep is 400 calls, and Pi truncates each read, grep, find, or ls result to 51,200 bytes, so the total is 20,480,000 bytes. The 32 MiB value leaves room for Pi notices and the quality tool. Identical results share one entry. A result that would pass the ceiling is refused by this name, and no older entry is evicted. The model then receives the capped excerpt without a handle. Override may only lower it.

toolOutput.recallPageBytes.remediation: Request a smaller byteLength and page through the archived result with byteOffset, or raise toolOutput.recallPageBytes in config/limits/toolOutput.yaml.
toolOutput.recallPageBytes.rationale: Presentation. The most bytes one docsfab_recall_tool_result call returns. It equals the default per-call output cap in harness/tool-output-cap.ts, so one recalled page costs no more context than one capped read. A larger byteLength is refused, not clamped. A page or request that cannot return one whole UTF-8 code point within that declared maximum is refused rather than returning more bytes than the maximum. Catalog min is 4, the longest UTF-8 code point, so every supported page setting can hold one code point. Override may only lower it.

toolOutput.excerptTailBytes.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_TOOL_OUTPUT_EXCERPT_TAIL_BYTES to an integer from 1 through 4096.
toolOutput.excerptTailBytes.rationale: Presentation and an implementation choice. The most bytes of an archived result's tail shown after the capped head. It is one eighth of the default 32 KiB cap, so the head keeps most of the per-call budget, and it never takes more than half of that budget. The marker names the exact byte ranges returned, and the omitted middle is recallable by handle. Override may only lower it.

gitHistory.logMaxEntries.remediation: Continue the walk with the cursor the previous docsfab_history_log page returned, or narrow it with a path or a range; a host may set DOCSFAB_GIT_HISTORY_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES from 1 through 200.
gitHistory.logMaxEntries.rationale: Presentation. The most commits one docsfab_history_log page lists. An entry is a full commit id, its parent ids, the committer date and the subject, about 200 bytes of JSON for an ordinary one-line subject, so 50 entries stay near 10 KB, a third of the default 32 KiB per-call tool output cap, and leave the rest for long subjects. A longer walk is never cut; the page returns a cursor for the next one, and gitHistory.responseMaxBytes still ends a page early when the subjects are long. The 200 maximum keeps 200 ordinary entries inside gitHistory.responseMaxBytes at its default.

gitHistory.responseMaxBytes.remediation: Keep gitHistory.responseMaxBytes at or below the per-call tool output cap (DOCSFAB_TOOL_OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES), or raise that cap; page through a larger file or diff with the cursor the previous page returned.
gitHistory.responseMaxBytes.rationale: Presentation. The most bytes of the rendered JSON one docsfab_history_show, docsfab_history_diff, docsfab_history_log, docsfab_history_search or docsfab_history_blame call returns, envelope, labels and cursor included. It equals the default per-call tool output cap in harness/tool-output-cap.ts, so one history page costs no more context than one capped read. The tool set refuses to start when it is above the effective cap, so the two bounds cannot disagree. A larger file, diff, blamed range or set of search matches is served in pages with a cursor, never cut, and a search match whose file list does not fit continues on the next page; one blamed line, or one search match with one file, too long for a page alone is refused by this name. The minimum and maximum are the tool output cap's own range.

gitHistory.pathsMaxPerCall.remediation: Name fewer paths in one docsfab_history_diff or docsfab_history_search call and read the rest in another call; a host may set DOCSFAB_GIT_HISTORY_PATHS_MAX_PER_CALL from 1 through 256.
gitHistory.pathsMaxPerCall.rationale: Technical capacity. The most paths one docsfab_history_diff or docsfab_history_search call may name, and the most changed files one diff page covers, so neither the argument list handed to git nor one page's file list grows with the change. The other history tools take at most one path. 64 files covers an ordinary merge request in one call; a larger change pages on with the cursor, and a longer path argument list is refused by this name rather than shortened.

gitHistory.cursorsMaxPerToolSet.remediation: Resume from cursors already issued, or narrow the history read so it needs fewer pages; a host may set DOCSFAB_GIT_HISTORY_CURSORS_MAX_PER_TOOL_SET from 1 through 1024.
gitHistory.cursorsMaxPerToolSet.rationale: Technical capacity. The most distinct continuation cursors one history tool set holds, shared by docsfab_history_show, docsfab_history_diff, docsfab_history_log, docsfab_history_search and docsfab_history_blame. A tool set lives for one step attempt, and the same page asked again reuses its cursor, so each distinct page costs one entry of a few hundred bytes plus its admitted path list and, for a search, its search string. 256 is more than half the per-step tool-call ceiling (compositionExecution.maxToolCallsPerStep, 400), so an attempt that pages all the way through a large diff, or searches a whole long history window by window, still fits. A call that would need one more is refused by this name; no older cursor is evicted.

gitHistory.revisionMinHexChars.remediation: Send at least gitHistory.revisionMinHexChars hex characters of the commit id, or the full id that docsfab_history_log returns.
gitHistory.revisionMinHexChars.rationale: Technical capacity. The shortest abbreviated commit id a history tool resolves. An abbreviation resolves by listing every object whose id starts with it, and each hex character fewer multiplies that list by 16, so a short prefix in a large repository is a large probe and usually ambiguous. 7 is git's default abbreviation, so an id copied from ordinary git output still resolves, and docsfab_history_log returns full ids. The minimum 4 is git's own shortest abbreviation and the maximum 40 is a full SHA-1 id. A shorter id is refused as history-revision-invalid, never padded or guessed.

gitHistory.blameMaxLines.remediation: Blame a shorter range in one docsfab_history_blame call and the rest in another call; a host may set DOCSFAB_GIT_HISTORY_BLAME_MAX_LINES from 1 through 20000.
gitHistory.blameMaxLines.rationale: Technical capacity. The most lines one docsfab_history_blame call may ask about, checked before git runs. It bounds git's work, not presentation; served lines page by gitHistory.responseMaxBytes with a cursor. Blame traces every asked line back through history, and every history read shares the sealed hostInvoker.gitTimeoutMs (10 s) and hostInvoker.gitOutputMaxBytes (8 MiB). Measured on 2026-10-06 in this repository on a shared laptop at load average 8 to 13 with git 2.50.1, blaming all 3046 lines of the planner harness source (112 commits) took 0.09 s, and all 7535 lines of the generated limits mirror (155 commits) took 0.12 s with about 125 bytes of porcelain output per line. 2000 lines covers a whole ordinary source or documentation file, or a large section of a long one, in one call, and leaves a deeper history two orders of magnitude of the timeout. The 20000 maximum keeps the porcelain output near 2.5 MB at that rate, inside the output bound. A longer range is refused with the asked count, never shortened.

gitHistory.pickaxeMaxCommitsScanned.remediation: Continue the search with the cursor the previous docsfab_history_search page returned, or narrow it with paths or a range; a host may set DOCSFAB_GIT_HISTORY_PICKAXE_MAX_COMMITS_SCANNED from 1 through 2000.
gitHistory.pickaxeMaxCommitsScanned.rationale: Technical capacity. The most commits one docsfab_history_search page scans for the search string. It bounds git's work, not presentation, and is never a refusal; a longer walk continues window by window with a cursor, even past a window with no match, so nothing is skipped. Each page runs three git reads over its window, all under the sealed hostInvoker.gitTimeoutMs (10 s) and hostInvoker.gitOutputMaxBytes (8 MiB) - the walk, a needle-free list of every name the window's commits changed, and the search itself - and the name list is the largest output, since a root or shallow cut lists its whole tree. Measured on 2026-10-07 in this repository (3548 commits) on a shared laptop at load average 12 with git 2.50.1 and a string found nowhere, the costliest 1000-commit window took 0.04 s to walk, 0.23 s and 1.7 MB to list names and 0.73 s to search; the costliest 2000-commit window took 0.04 s, 0.15 s and 3.0 MB, and 0.77 s; the whole history in one window took 0.22 s and 4.9 MB to list and 1.0 s to search. Generated files churn often, so cost differs by window. At 1000 a search of the whole history takes four pages, far inside gitHistory.cursorsMaxPerToolSet (256) and compositionExecution.maxToolCallsPerStep (400). Each page re-walks the commits earlier windows scanned to skip them, so a path-limited page costs more the deeper it starts; the walk stayed under 0.1 s at every offset measured. The 2000 maximum keeps the measured name list under half the output bound; a window whose names exceed it is refused as history-output-too-large, whose remediation narrows it with paths or a range.

gitHistory.searchNeedleMaxBytes.remediation: Search for a shorter string, such as the symbol's own name rather than the line around it; a host may set DOCSFAB_GIT_HISTORY_SEARCH_NEEDLE_MAX_BYTES from 1 through 4096.
gitHistory.searchNeedleMaxBytes.rationale: Technical capacity. The longest search string, in UTF-8 bytes, one docsfab_history_search call may send, checked before git runs. The string reaches git as one command-line argument and stays in the host's cursor state for the tool set's life, so its size bounds both. 256 bytes holds any ordinary identifier, option, configuration key or error message, and a short phrase; a search is for where a symbol appeared or vanished, not for a whole line or block. The 4096 maximum keeps the argument far inside every supported operating system's limit on one argument. A longer string is refused with its byte count, never shortened.

searchBrief.totalMaxChars.remediation: Narrow the step's search plan to fewer targets or required probes, or raise searchBrief.totalMaxChars in config/limits/searchBrief.yaml after confirming the supported context windows still fit.
