searchBrief.totalMaxChars.rationale: Budget. Characters of the search-brief section one model step prompt carries, framing included (its two header lines, the brief's JSON, and the omission notice); the run record keeps the full search evidence. 96 KiB is 24,576 tokens at the estimator's 4 characters per token, 30,720 with its 5/4 safety margin, under a quarter (30,976) of the 123,904 input tokens the smallest shipped profile window admits (contextWindow 128,000 minus contextReserveTokens 4,096 in packages/runtime/config/profiles/nvidia-llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b-v1.5.yaml). The largest shipped plan (release-documentation-readiness, 30 targets) measured a 32,826-character JSON brief on a 20-file repository, against 604,810 characters of raw evidence; the whole first request then estimated 22,274 input tokens at a 131,072-token window, against 201,004 before. Cited paths are the only part cut to fit, shared across targets smallest demand first; the brief, the run record's evidenceWarnings, and the operator LIMITATIONS footer state how many were left out. Fixed content that alone exceeds this refuses; every shipped search plan's worst case fits (test-proven). The 32,768-token conservative fallback window that setup writes for an unmatched endpoint is not admitted by the host (such profiles skip context admission), and 32,768 minus the measured 22,274-token release request leaves 10,494 tokens, below that profile's 16,384-token output allowance, so an endpoint on the fallback needs its real window configured; this budget is not sized for it.

repository.inventoryMaxEntries.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_REPOSITORY_INVENTORY_MAX_ENTRIES to at least the tracked entry count to inventory the whole tree, or narrow the repository. A tree past the workspace export's ceiling also needs DOCSFAB_REPOSITORY_WORKSPACE_EXPORT_MAX_TREE_ENTRIES raised.
repository.inventoryMaxEntries.rationale: Tracked-tree inventory cap; 20000 covers 10k-file repositories with room to spare. Crossing it degrades instead of failing. The sealed inventory records entry-limit-exceeded and omittedCount, governed search continues with an incomplete-index limitation, and every governed workflow records this limit's refusal line in the run's LIMITATIONS, so the clip is never silent. The inventory is bounded only here, where it is built; inventory decoders apply no node or array ceiling of their own (#1927). An inventory never holds more entries than the workspace export admits, so this limit's maximum is repository.workspaceExportMaxTreeEntries' own, the largest integer the override parser admits. A host that raises the export ceiling can raise this limit to match, and is never capped below it.

repository.inventoryTextMaxFileBytes.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_REPOSITORY_INVENTORY_TEXT_MAX_FILE_BYTES, or repository.inventoryTextMaxFileBytes in the host limits file, above the observed size of the largest left-out file (at most 536870887 bytes), then rerun the same command.
repository.inventoryTextMaxFileBytes.rationale: Largest tracked file the repository inventory reads into its text index, the text governed search's literal-text probes match (#1932). It replaces a hand-declared 1 MiB literal. Measured on vllm-project/semantic-router aec7a4ee5, the largest text file is a 3,162,828-byte generated catalog, so 8 MiB indexes every text file there and leaves 2.6 times headroom for generated specifications and lock files. A larger file is never read whole. Its first 8,000 bytes decide whether it is binary, as in Git's own heuristic, and a binary is excluded like a known binary format. A larger text file is left out of the text index, recorded by path as text-index-limit-exceeded with this limit and its size, and counted in the run's LIMITATIONS. A file is held as bytes and as a string while it is read, so the default costs at most about 24 MiB at a time. The maximum is the largest file one JavaScript string can hold, one code unit below the 64-bit Node MAX_STRING_LENGTH, as for artifacts.maxObjectBytes.
repository.inventoryTextMaxFileBytes.docSummary: Largest tracked file the repository inventory reads into the text index that governed search matches literal text against. A larger file is left out by path and counted in LIMITATIONS.

repository.inventoryTextMaxTotalBytes.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_REPOSITORY_INVENTORY_TEXT_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES, or repository.inventoryTextMaxTotalBytes in the host limits file, to at least the observed total, then rerun the same command. The index holds that much text in host memory while search runs.
repository.inventoryTextMaxTotalBytes.rationale: Bytes of tracked text the repository inventory holds in its text index, summed over files, for governed search's literal-text probes (#1932). It replaces a hand-declared 16 MiB literal that indexed 1,760 of the 10,334 text candidates of vllm-project/semantic-router aec7a4ee5 and left 8,561 out. Measured there with the 8 MiB file limit, the index holds 89,808,719 bytes of text from 10,308 files, about 8.4 KB per tracked file, so a 30,000-file repository of the same density needs about 253 MB and 512 MiB leaves twice that. The text stays in host memory as strings while governed search runs. Strings of small files live on the JavaScript heap, measured at 1.12 heap bytes per text byte on that repository, where nearly every file is small. Node holds a string decoded from a file over about 1 MiB outside the heap. Either way a byte of text costs at most 2 bytes of memory, so the default costs at most about 1 GiB of host memory. A file past it is never read whole. Its first 8,000 bytes decide whether it is binary, which is excluded rather than counted, and a text file is left out of the text index, recorded by path as text-index-limit-exceeded with this limit and the total the index needed, and counted in the run's LIMITATIONS. The text index never holds more than the workspace export writes, so the maximum is that limit's own, the largest integer the override parser admits.
repository.inventoryTextMaxTotalBytes.docSummary: Bytes of tracked text the repository inventory holds for governed search, summed over files. Past it, files are left out by path and counted in LIMITATIONS.

repository.workspaceExportMaxTreeEntries.remediation: The revision tracks more entries than the workspace export admits. Raise DOCSFAB_REPOSITORY_WORKSPACE_EXPORT_MAX_TREE_ENTRIES, or run on a revision that tracks fewer files.
repository.workspaceExportMaxTreeEntries.rationale: Tracked-tree entries one exact-tree workspace export admits. Past it the export stops in preflight with file-count-limit, before any file is written. The value keeps the former harness ceiling, which the issue 1932 audit found fits real repositories. Measured on 2026-10-05, kubernetes-sigs/kueue a1a12a6 tracks 12,830 entries and vllm-project/semantic-router aec7a4ee5 tracks 10,658. The same bound sizes the checked-tree walk and the original source authority's member list, so a host raise reaches all three. The maximum is the largest integer the override parser admits, so a host may raise it as far as its memory allows.

repository.workspaceExportMaxAggregateBy.remediation: The revision's tracked files hold more bytes than the workspace export admits. Raise DOCSFAB_REPOSITORY_WORKSPACE_EXPORT_MAX_AGGREGATE_BYTES, and keep DOCSFAB_REPOSITORY_WORKSPACE_EXPORT_MAX_SCRATCH_BYTES above it, or run on a revision that tracks fewer large files.
repository.workspaceExportMaxAggregateBy.rationale: Bytes of tracked regular files one workspace export writes, checked against the tree listing in preflight and again as bytes stream (aggregate-byte-limit). The value keeps the former 2 GiB harness ceiling. Measured on 2026-10-05, the largest field repository, vllm-project/semantic-router aec7a4ee5, exports 459,582,480 bytes, and kubernetes-sigs/kueue a1a12a6 exports 135,801,999. Checked-in binaries can pass the default, hence the upward override. It also bounds one original source authority member and the checked-tree walk. The scratch volume's free space is checked separately. The maximum is the largest integer the override parser admits.

repository.workspaceExportMaxScratchByte.remediation: The workspace export would use more scratch space than it admits. Raise DOCSFAB_REPOSITORY_WORKSPACE_EXPORT_MAX_SCRATCH_BYTES if the scratch volume has room, or run on a revision that tracks fewer or smaller files.
repository.workspaceExportMaxScratchByte.rationale: Scratch bytes one workspace export may plan and allocate, counted in preflight as file bytes plus 4,096 bytes per tree entry and during export as allocated blocks (scratch-space-limit). The value keeps the former 3 GiB harness ceiling, which leaves room for the 2 GiB byte ceiling plus per-entry overhead. Measured on 2026-10-05, vllm-project/semantic-router aec7a4ee5 plans about 503 MB. Independently, preflight refuses a plan larger than the scratch volume's free space. The maximum is the largest integer the override parser admits.

repository.workspaceExportMaxTreeMetadat.remediation: The revision's tree listing is larger than the workspace export reads. Raise DOCSFAB_REPOSITORY_WORKSPACE_EXPORT_MAX_TREE_METADATA_BYTES, or run on a revision that tracks fewer files.
repository.workspaceExportMaxTreeMetadat.rationale: Bytes of git ls-tree output one workspace export reads in preflight (tree-metadata-limit). The value keeps the former 32 MiB ceiling. Measured on 2026-10-05, the listing for kubernetes-sigs/kueue a1a12a6 (12,830 entries) is 1,563,785 bytes and for vllm-project/semantic-router aec7a4ee5 (10,658 entries) 1,332,606 bytes, about 120 bytes per entry, so the default fits roughly 250,000 entries. The maximum is the largest integer the override parser admits.

repository.workspaceExportStallMs.remediation: The workspace export made no progress for this long, so git or the disk stopped answering. Check that both respond, then retry. If they are healthy and one export step legitimately takes longer on this host, raise DOCSFAB_REPOSITORY_WORKSPACE_EXPORT_STALL_MS.
repository.workspaceExportStallMs.rationale: No-progress window for the exact-tree workspace export (issue 1921, owner decision option A on 2026-10-05, which revisits the 120 s freeze of issue 548). It replaces three wall clocks, 120 s on the whole export, 30 s on each file, and 30 s on each preflight Git command. Progress is any finished Git read, tree-listing chunk, created directory, written chunk of file bytes, or verified file, so an export that keeps moving is never stopped and its total time grows with the tree without a size term. A stall while a file's bytes stream stops with per-blob-timeout, any other stall with aggregate-timeout. Provisional default - 120 s is carried over from the former wall clock as an implementation choice, and the owner approved the mechanism, not the number. Every export the old wall clock admitted is still admitted, because no idle interval can exceed an export's total time. Detection is not always as early as before - a stuck file or a stuck preflight Git command was stopped after 30 s and is now stopped after 120 s, and a hang that begins partway through an export is reported 120 s after the last progress rather than 120 s after the start. Supported workload, measured on the benchmark Mac on 2026-10-05 at load average 86 to 161 - ten exports in one process (five each of vllm-project/semantic-router aec7a4ee5, 10,658 files, and kubernetes-sigs/kueue a1a12a6, 12,830 files) all completed at this default, in 217 s to 821 s. The longest gap without progress was not instrumented. With the window lowered to 10 s one of the ten stopped, so gaps of at least 10 s occur under that load. A filesystem call that never returns still holds the export until it returns, as before. A stall in the file sweep's mkdir, open, chmod, write or close is recorded at the window. `mkdtemp` and the workspace-root `mkdir` run before any watchdog, so a stall in them is judged only when the call returns, and observed is the whole call. The minimum, 1 ms, is the smallest timer delay. The maximum is one below the largest delay a Node timer honours (2^31 - 1 ms, about 24.8 days), because the watchdog arms the window plus 1 ms. A host override may raise or lower it within that range.

repository.trackedWriteAdmissionMaxBytes.remediation: Split the page into smaller pages, or remove a lowering override of repository.trackedWriteAdmissionMaxBytes. Its default is already its maximum, the largest page a run can write, and it cannot rise until authoring.plannedPageMaxBytes and the patch capture (repository.evidenceGitOutputMaxBytes, which the delivery patch readers share) are qualified with it.
repository.trackedWriteAdmissionMaxBytes.rationale: Bytes of one tracked file an authorized in-run write may hold when the workspace recaptures it, in repository/workspace/tracked-read.ts. Every written planned page, and the first-pass knowledge snapshot, is read whole into one buffer and digested before later reads and the candidate seal trust it. A file over the bound keeps its export identity and stays quarantined, so both authoring candidate seals check every written planned page first and refuse a larger one by this code instead of leaving it out without a code. It replaces the hand-declared 8 MiB literal (issue 2440). Measured 2026-10-02 the largest tracked Markdown page in representative documentation repositories was 234336 bytes, so 32 MiB is about 143 times the largest and admits generated reference pages that passed the former 8 MiB. Recapture holds at most one file at a time, so the default costs at most about 32 MiB of host memory. The maximum equals the default because the pipeline behind a written page is qualified only up to it. A created page at this size yields a patch of the page plus one byte per line, and a full rewrite yields about twice that, both of which the 80 MiB patch capture (repository.evidenceGitOutputMaxBytes), shared by the delivery patch readers, holds, and authoring.plannedPageMaxBytes may not exceed it. Override may only lower it.
repository.trackedWriteAdmissionMaxBytes.docSummary: Largest page a create or update run can write. A larger page is refused before the candidate seals. Override may only lower it.

repository.trackedWriteAdmissionMaxPathC.remediation: One eligible repository path for authorized tracked-write recapture exceeds this UTF-16 code-unit limit. Shorten that path, or raise DOCSFAB_REPOSITORY_TRACKED_WRITE_ADMISSION_MAX_PATH_CHARS (or repository.trackedWriteAdmissionMaxPathChars in host limits) to at least the observed length before retrying the same operation. The host filesystem and other contracts may impose independent limits.
repository.trackedWriteAdmissionMaxPathC.rationale: Length in UTF-16 code units of one eligible path at the public authorized tracked-write admission operation, checked for all candidates before any recapture-state mutation in that invocation. This registers the pre-existing inline 1024-unit default as provisional legacy policy; it is not a platform maximum, not a materialization-wide path ceiling, and not the independent 512-unit source or review-scope contract. The default admits the known NFD documentation path with substantial headroom. A host may override this recapture-only value after validating its filesystem and downstream contracts. The parser maximum is the largest safe integer representable in JavaScript, not a promise of filesystem support.

repository.navigationMaxSources.remediation: Reduce navigation source files, or raise repository.navigationMaxSources in config/limits/repository.yaml.
repository.navigationMaxSources.rationale: Maximum recognized navigation sources one observation reads. Crossing it records source-budget-exceeded. Override may only lower it.

repository.navigationMaxSourceBytes.remediation: Shrink the navigation source file, or raise repository.navigationMaxSourceBytes in config/limits/repository.yaml.
repository.navigationMaxSourceBytes.rationale: Maximum bytes of one navigation source. Crossing it records source-too-large. Override may only lower it.

repository.navigationMaxTotalSourceBytes.remediation: Reduce navigation sources, or raise repository.navigationMaxTotalSourceBytes in config/limits/repository.yaml.
repository.navigationMaxTotalSourceBytes.rationale: Combined byte budget across navigation sources. Crossing it records source-budget-exceeded. Override may only lower it.

repository.navigationMaxTargets.remediation: Reduce nav targets, or raise repository.navigationMaxTargets in config/limits/repository.yaml.
repository.navigationMaxTargets.rationale: Maximum documentation targets one navigation source may name. Crossing it records target-budget-exceeded. Override may only lower it.

repository.navigationMaxTargetBytes.remediation: Shrink the named target file, or raise repository.navigationMaxTargetBytes in config/limits/repository.yaml.
repository.navigationMaxTargetBytes.rationale: Maximum bytes of one navigation target. Crossing it records target-too-large. Override may only lower it.

repository.navigationMaxTotalTargetBytes.remediation: Reduce navigation targets, or raise repository.navigationMaxTotalTargetBytes in config/limits/repository.yaml.
repository.navigationMaxTotalTargetBytes.rationale: Combined byte budget across navigation targets. Crossing it records target-budget-exceeded. Override may only lower it.

repository.evidenceGitTimeoutMs.remediation: One git command that records the run's workspace evidence ran this long without finishing. Check that git and the disk respond. On a large repository or a heavily loaded host, raise DOCSFAB_REPOSITORY_EVIDENCE_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS.
repository.evidenceGitTimeoutMs.rationale: Longest one git command may run while recording a run's workspace evidence (issue 1932) - the baseline git add and commit when the run starts, and the git add, name-status diff, and patch diff that capture its changes. It replaces a fixed 30 s literal that stopped a NemoClaw trial (about 6k files) on the Linux benchmark runner at load average 80 or more on 2026-10-05. Git reports no progress for these commands, so this is a hang guard, not a progress window. Provisional default from measurement on the benchmark Mac, 2026-10-05 and 06. Eight concurrent baselines of NVIDIA/NemoClaw e3e5a06 (6,226 files, 114 MB) at load average 61 to 81 all failed under the 30 s literal and all completed under this limit, in 58 s each. Three concurrent baselines of vllm-project/semantic-router 6a387d5 (10,300 files, 458 MB) at load average 166 to 190 completed in 60 s each, and their captures in 11 s. A field proof on 2026-10-06, on vllm-project/semantic-router (10.6k tracked files) at load average about 160, took 29.6 s for the cold evidence git add alone, and the old 30 s literal stopped it in 1 of 4 runs. A baseline runs five git commands, so its time bounds the git add from above, and the default allows about ten times the longest baseline measured. A command may run for exactly the limit; one millisecond more stops it with this refusal. The minimum, 1 ms, is the smallest timer delay. The maximum is one below the largest delay a Node timer honours (2^31 - 1 ms, about 24.8 days), because the stop timer arms the limit plus 1 ms. A host override may raise or lower it within that range.

repository.evidenceGitOutputMaxBytes.remediation: One git command that records the run's workspace evidence, usually the patch diff, wrote more than this to one output stream. Raise DOCSFAB_REPOSITORY_EVIDENCE_GIT_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES, or make a smaller change.
repository.evidenceGitOutputMaxBytes.rationale: Most bytes one workspace-evidence git command may write to stdout or to stderr, held in memory and decoded into one string - the baseline commit, the change list, and the patch diff of the run's changes. The patch readers downstream (delivery preflight, impact patch evidence and the run summary's patch stats) read this same limit, so every patch the run captures stays readable. 80 MiB holds a full rewrite of one page at repository.trackedWriteAdmissionMaxBytes (32 MiB), whose patch carries the old and the new page plus one byte per line (72 MiB for lines averaging 8 bytes, far shorter than real Markdown), and is far above a documentation run's patch. It replaces the former 50 MiB literals (issue 2440). A write run's delivered patch is bounded separately by writeAuthority.maxPatchBytes. The maximum is the longest string Node can hold (MAX_STRING_LENGTH, 536,870,888 UTF-16 code units on qualified 64-bit Node), because the output is decoded into one string and each byte decodes to at most one code unit. A host override may raise or lower it within that range.
repository.evidenceGitOutputMaxBytes.docSummary: Largest patch of a run's changes the host captures and delivery reads back, enough for a full rewrite of one page at the page limit.

contentIndex.maxAssets.remediation: Raise contentIndex.maxAssets with DOCSFAB_CONTENT_INDEX_MAX_ASSETS to index every linked asset. Until then the index leaves out each asset past the bound and names it.
contentIndex.maxAssets.rationale: Technical capacity. Distinct linked assets (images and other files that are not pages) that one workspace content index hashes. Each asset is read once and only its digest is kept, so the cost is indexing time, not memory. An asset past the bound is left out of the index and named as a limitation; nothing stops. The previous fixed 256 stopped every write-capable run on a documentation site with more linked screenshots than that; 4,096 covers the 1k-10k-file repositories in the 2026-10-05 limits audit (row d). Override may raise it.
contentIndex.maxAssets.docSummary: Distinct linked assets one content index hashes; more are left out and named.

contentIndex.maxAssetBytes.remediation: Raise contentIndex.maxAssetBytes with DOCSFAB_CONTENT_INDEX_MAX_ASSET_BYTES to index a larger asset. Until then the index leaves the asset out and names it.
contentIndex.maxAssetBytes.rationale: Technical capacity. Bytes of one linked asset the content index reads to hash. The asset is held in memory once while it is hashed, so this bounds one read. A larger asset is left out of the index and named as a limitation; nothing stops. The previous fixed 8 MiB stopped every write-capable run on a page that linked a recorded demo or a large diagram; 64 MiB covers those. Override may raise it.
contentIndex.maxAssetBytes.docSummary: Bytes of one linked asset the content index hashes; a larger asset is left out and named.

contentIndex.maxTotalAssetBytes.remediation: Raise contentIndex.maxTotalAssetBytes with DOCSFAB_CONTENT_INDEX_MAX_TOTAL_ASSET_BYTES to index every linked asset. Until then the index leaves out each asset that would pass the total and names it.
contentIndex.maxTotalAssetBytes.rationale: Technical capacity. Combined bytes of the linked assets one content index reads to hash. Assets are read one at a time and only digests are kept, so the cost is indexing time. An asset that would pass the total is left out of the index and named as a limitation; nothing stops. The previous fixed 16 MiB stopped every write-capable run on a site with more than 16 MiB of screenshots; 1 GiB is the limits audit's value for 1k-10k-file repositories (row d). Override may raise it.
contentIndex.maxTotalAssetBytes.docSummary: Combined bytes of the linked assets one content index hashes; assets past it are left out and named.

contentIndex.maxSourceBytes.remediation: Split the page, or raise contentIndex.maxSourceBytes with DOCSFAB_CONTENT_INDEX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES, then rerun the same command.
contentIndex.maxSourceBytes.rationale: Technical capacity. Bytes of one Markdown, MDX, reStructuredText, or navigation source a workspace content index reads and parses. Parsing holds the whole page in memory, and every other page may link to it, so a page over the bound still stops the index with this code, naming the page and its size. Generated reference pages in large repositories can pass 4 MiB; override may raise it to 64 MiB.
contentIndex.maxSourceBytes.docSummary: Bytes of one page or navigation source a workspace content index parses; a larger page stops the index, naming it.

runs.deletionGateAttempts.remediation: Wait for the other local writer or deletion to finish. A complete private lock with a proven-dead owner is recovered automatically; inspect an unknown or incomplete lock before manual recovery.
runs.deletionGateAttempts.rationale: Maximum acquisition attempts for the local run and run-index maintenance gates. At the paired default retry pause this permits about 30 seconds of ordinary live-owner contention. A complete private lock with a proven-dead owner is reclaimed through pinned identity checks; an unknown or incomplete owner is never reclaimed. The run-deletion and crash-resume fixtures exercise this shared limit.

runs.deletionGateRetryPauseMs.remediation: Wait for the other local writer or deletion to finish; inspect the private maintenance lock only after verifying quiescence.
runs.deletionGateRetryPauseMs.rationale: Pause between bounded attempts to acquire a local run or run-index maintenance gate, avoiding a busy loop while retaining a finite refusal for a live or ambiguous owner. It shares the acquisition budget with runs.deletionGateAttempts.

runs.deletionGateHelperTimeoutMs.remediation: Check host CPU and filesystem load, then rerun the exact operation. An interrupted helper leaves the gate state unknown and requires inspection before another attempt.
runs.deletionGateHelperTimeoutMs.rationale: Longest time one isolated run-gate release or proven-dead owner recovery helper may execute before the caller kills it and refuses. Matches the separately measured 30-second SCM receipt helper ceiling; normal local filesystem exchanges are shorter. The helper has no captured output and only an exit-code protocol.

runs.deletionInventoryMaxEntries.remediation: Move unrelated historical state into another supported private root, or raise runs.deletionInventoryMaxEntries in config/limits/runs.yaml and preview again. Record and artifact byte-size limits remain separate.
runs.deletionInventoryMaxEntries.rationale: Provisional implementation choice for issue 1794. Maximum structural JSON containers and variable-length filesystem entries scanned while previewing deletion across a saved run, content objects, and retained owners. The supported 566156-byte successful review record has 2263 structural containers, and its artifact pool has 15 quality objects with 207 structural containers in total; the default of 10000 covers that combined journey with room for ordinary retained records. Record and object byte-size bounds independently limit scalar/string payloads. Refuse the whole preview instead of truncating an ownership scan.

runs.indexMaxBytes.remediation: Move the run-index directory aside and rebuild it from the saved records with docsfab runs import, or raise runs.indexMaxBytes in config/limits/runs.yaml or the host limits file.
runs.indexMaxBytes.rationale: Size of one append-only run index (#1184). docsfab runs query reads the whole file. The two eight-case matrices of September 23, 2026 index to about 200 KiB, so 64 MiB holds several hundred matrices. An append that would cross the bound is refused and recorded in the index overflow file, which every query reports; rows are never truncated.

runs.recordMaxBytes.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_RUNS_RECORD_MAX_BYTES, or the host limits file or config/limits/runs.yaml entry for runs.recordMaxBytes, above the record size (at most 536870887 bytes), then rerun the same command. The saved record is unchanged.
runs.recordMaxBytes.rationale: One bound for every reader of one saved run record (#1932), namely docsfab runs list and import, docsfab why, local publication preflight, delivery acceptance, the live agent's saved-run tool, and operator input fills. It replaces six separate ceilings of 2, 2, 4, 4, 10 and 16 MiB, two of which reported an oversized record as malformed or invalid. The largest record in the September 23, 2026 matrices was 810 KB (#1184) and a smoke record was 312 KB; a record grows with steps, telemetry and per-file limitations rather than with repository size, so 64 MiB leaves about eighty times headroom over the largest measured record. The maximum is the largest UTF-8 JSON record the whole-string reader can parse, as for recovery.logicalObjectMaxBytes. A larger record is refused or listed by this name with its observed size; docsfab runs import names it and still imports the rest.
runs.recordMaxBytes.docSummary: Largest saved run record any DocsFab reader loads, such as `docsfab runs list`, `docsfab why`, publication preflight, and the live agent's saved-run tool.

runs.indexImportMaxRecords.remediation: Import fewer state directories or harness batches per docsfab runs import invocation, or raise runs.indexImportMaxRecords in config/limits/runs.yaml.
runs.indexImportMaxRecords.rationale: Record files one docsfab runs import invocation considers across its paths (#1184), matching the 10,000-record docsfab runs list ceiling. Over the bound the import refuses before it writes any row.

runs.indexFieldMaxChars.remediation: Read the value from the saved run record with docsfab runs show, or raise runs.indexFieldMaxChars in config/limits/runs.yaml and re-import the record.
runs.indexFieldMaxChars.rationale: Longest identifier-like record value one index row copies, such as a rejection location, model name, or step ID (#1184). It matches the docsfab runs list field ceiling. A longer value, or one with control characters, is stored as unavailable and named in the row's omittedFields, which every query counts.

runs.summaryPatchFiles.remediation: Read every changed file in the retained patch named on the RECORD line, or with docsfab runs show <run-id> --json, or raise runs.summaryPatchFiles in config/limits/runs.yaml.
runs.summaryPatchFiles.rationale: Changed files the human PATCH section of a run result lists, one line each with its insertion and deletion counts, before a PATCH omitted count of the rest. Presentation only; the run record, the retained patch artifact, and the JSON result always carry every changed file. Migrated unchanged, Task(#1334), from a hand-declared presenter constant of the same value that the limits identifier rule did not match; 10 keeps a typical single-page documentation change fully listed while a bulk restructure stays short.

runs.credentialFindingLocationChars.remediation: Read the cut location's path from the repository with the digest the marker names, or set DOCSFAB_RUNS_CREDENTIAL_FINDING_LOCATION_CHARS (256 through 4096) on the host, or change runs.credentialFindingLocationChars in config/limits/runs.yaml, and run again to record longer locations whole.
runs.credentialFindingLocationChars.rationale: Longest location a credential-like-content finding keeps in a run record (#1807). A finding is heuristic and must never stop a record from decoding or publishing, so a longer location is not refused; it keeps its line number and is cut at a visible marker that carries a digest of the whole location, so two long paths stay distinct. Record readers accept any location up to the maximum, so changing the value leaves older records readable. The longest tracked path in the six benchmark checkouts audited for this change (#1807) and in this repository is 186 characters, so 1024 leaves more than five times that; 4096 is the longest Linux path.
runs.credentialFindingLocationChars.docSummary: Longest `credential-like-content` finding location a run record keeps; a longer one is cut at a marker that carries a digest of the whole location.

diagnosis.maxRuns.remediation: Narrow docsfab why to one run ID, --last, --batch, or --model, or raise diagnosis.maxRuns in config/limits/diagnosis.yaml or the host limits file.
diagnosis.maxRuns.rationale: Runs one docsfab why invocation diagnoses when it selects several runs, such as every run in a state directory, a batch, or a model. The newest runs are diagnosed first. The hosted-model verification of September 30, 2026 left 13 failed runs in one state directory, and two eight-case local-workflows matrices hold 16, so 50 covers several batches in one answer. Over the bound, the answer states how many runs it diagnosed out of how many matched, in the human output and in the JSON runs.clipped field, and names this limit; it never drops runs silently. The maximum matches runs.indexImportMaxRecords.

diagnosis.recurrenceLookbackRuns.remediation: Count older occurrences with the printed docsfab runs query command without its --since option, or raise diagnosis.recurrenceLookbackRuns in config/limits/diagnosis.yaml or the host limits file.
diagnosis.recurrenceLookbackRuns.rationale: Recent runs of the same provider and model that a diagnosis compares when it reports how often the same step failed with the same code, as N of the last M runs. Twenty covers two eight-case matrices and their reruns, which is the span in which a repeated cause usually belongs to one DocsFab revision and one serving route. The first-seen run is read from the whole index rather than from this window. When the window is shorter than the runs the index holds for that model, the recurrence line says so and its reproduce command carries the matching --since bound.

slackRoutes.documentMaxBytes.remediation: Shrink the installed registry, Slack map, activation state, dispatcher policy, identity map or grant snapshot, or raise slackRoutes.documentMaxBytes in config/limits/slackRoutes.yaml without exceeding the 1 MiB the activation-state validator itself reads.
slackRoutes.documentMaxBytes.rationale: Largest installed sealed document a Slack route operation reads before parsing. Defaults to the existing 1 MiB maximum, matching the activation-state validator; the documents still pass their existing schema and authority checks.
slackRoutes.documentMaxBytes.docSummary: Installed sealed document read by a Slack route operation.

slackRoutes.candidateMaxBytes.remediation: Stage a smaller single-route candidate, or raise slackRoutes.candidateMaxBytes in config/limits/slackRoutes.yaml.
slackRoutes.candidateMaxBytes.rationale: Largest staged single-route candidate the Slack route amendment reads, defaulting to the existing admitted maximum. Candidate shape and route authority remain independently validated.

slackRoutes.replacementCandidateMaxBytes.remediation: Declare fewer projects or routes in one replacement candidate, or raise slackRoutes.replacementCandidateMaxBytes in config/limits/slackRoutes.yaml.
slackRoutes.replacementCandidateMaxBytes.rationale: Largest staged desired-state candidate the Slack route replacement reads, defaulting to the existing admitted maximum. Project count, route count, and installed document bounds still apply independently.
slackRoutes.replacementCandidateMaxBytes.docSummary: Staged replacement candidate containing the desired routes.

slackRoutes.reasonMaxChars.remediation: State the reason in one shorter line that names the Task, or raise slackRoutes.reasonMaxChars in config/limits/slackRoutes.yaml.
slackRoutes.reasonMaxChars.rationale: Longest operator reason a Slack route receipt records, defaulting to the existing admitted maximum. Single-line and credential checks remain separate from this length allowance.
slackRoutes.reasonMaxChars.docSummary: Operator reason retained in a Slack route receipt.

slackRoutes.replacementMaxProjects.remediation: Name at most slackRoutes.replacementMaxProjects projects in one replacement candidate; the installed registry itself admits no more.
slackRoutes.replacementMaxProjects.rationale: Most projects one Slack route replacement may name. The ingress registry admits 1 through 32 project policies, so a candidate naming more than 32 projects cannot describe any installed registry and is refused before the registry is consulted.

slackRoutes.replacementMaxRoutesPerProje.remediation: Declare fewer routes for the project, or raise slackRoutes.replacementMaxRoutesPerProject in config/limits/slackRoutes.yaml.
slackRoutes.replacementMaxRoutesPerProje.rationale: Most desired routes one project may declare in a replacement candidate, defaulting to the existing admitted maximum. Candidate byte limits and route binding validation still apply.
slackRoutes.replacementMaxRoutesPerProje.docSummary: Desired routes for one project in a replacement candidate.

operatorAmendment.documentMaxBytes.remediation: Shrink the installed dispatcher policy, registry, Slack map, activation state, frozen context projection, identity map or staged candidate, or raise operatorAmendment.documentMaxBytes in config/limits/operatorAmendment.yaml.
operatorAmendment.documentMaxBytes.rationale: Largest installed or staged document the dispatcher-composition amendment, documentation-write upgrade and project-registry correction read before parsing. Defaults to the 512 KiB each of them already admitted; the documents still pass their own schema and authority checks.

operatorAmendment.registryCandidateMaxBy.remediation: Stage a smaller projection-policy candidate, or raise operatorAmendment.registryCandidateMaxBytes in config/limits/operatorAmendment.yaml.
operatorAmendment.registryCandidateMaxBy.rationale: Largest staged projection-policy candidate the project-registry correction reads, defaulting to the existing admitted maximum. Candidate shape and author resolution remain independently validated.

manifest.documentMaxBytes.remediation: Shrink the manifest or capture document, or lower manifest.documentMaxBytes in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.documentMaxBytes.rationale: Equals the activation-state read bound. Adopt and apply refuse a closed v1 document larger than this rather than parsing an unbounded operator file.

manifest.captureMaxBytes.remediation: Shrink the capture document, or lower manifest.captureMaxBytes in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.captureMaxBytes.rationale: Capture lists core artifacts (~60) and per-project custody tuples. Same ceiling as the activation-state read bound so adopt cannot ingest a larger fact document than the host already reads.

manifest.receiptMaxBytes.remediation: Shrink the apply receipt plan, or lower manifest.receiptMaxBytes in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.receiptMaxBytes.rationale: Mirrors the lineage receipt cap. One apply receipt must stay under this so a plan cannot grow without bound.

manifest.maxProjects.remediation: Name fewer projects in the manifest, or lower manifest.maxProjects in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.maxProjects.rationale: Registry intake already admits 1..32 projects. Adopt and apply share that ceiling rather than inventing a second one.

manifest.maxRoutesPerProject.remediation: Declare fewer Slack routes per project, or lower manifest.maxRoutesPerProject in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.maxRoutesPerProject.rationale: Named here so S1 can bound adopt without importing slackRoutes.* from !915. When that planner lands, this ceiling stays aligned with replacementMaxRoutesPerProject.

manifest.planMaxItems.remediation: Split the change across manifests, or lower manifest.planMaxItems in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.planMaxItems.rationale: One apply receipt must stay under receiptMaxBytes. 256 plan items is the named ceiling those later slices enforce.

manifest.reasonMaxChars.remediation: Shorten the reason to one bounded line, or lower manifest.reasonMaxChars in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.reasonMaxChars.rationale: Apply receipts carry one operator reason line. 256 characters matches the inference rejection reason bound so a reason cannot grow without a named ceiling.

manifest.lockWaitSeconds.remediation: Retry when the deployment lock is free, or lower manifest.lockWaitSeconds in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.lockWaitSeconds.rationale: Names the flock wait today's six amendment tools hard-code. Adopt takes a shared lock at most and uses this ceiling.

manifest.stopWaitSeconds.remediation: Inspect the unit and retry, or lower manifest.stopWaitSeconds in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.stopWaitSeconds.rationale: Matches TimeoutStopSec=30s. S1 does not stop the unit; later apply slices consume this name.

manifest.startAssertSeconds.remediation: Inspect the unit and retry, or lower manifest.startAssertSeconds in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.startAssertSeconds.rationale: Type=simple returns at fork. S1 does not start the unit; later apply slices consume this name.

manifest.clockSkewMs.remediation: Correct the host clock, or lower manifest.clockSkewMs in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.clockSkewMs.rationale: Names the five 5-minute skews once so later slices do not keep copying the literal.

manifest.historyKeep.remediation: Prune only above this floor, or lower manifest.historyKeep in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.historyKeep.rationale: Sealed manifests are never deleted below this floor. S1 records the bound; apply history uses it.

manifest.bindingExpiryWarnDays.remediation: Acknowledge the expiry or rotate via a supported primitive, or lower manifest.bindingExpiryWarnDays in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.bindingExpiryWarnDays.rationale: E2 has no status surface today. Apply later refuses binding-expiry-imminent inside this named window.

manifest.aclEntriesMax.remediation: Declare fewer ACL grants, or lower manifest.aclEntriesMax in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.aclEntriesMax.rationale: Matches adjudication's 128-line ACL bound so layout.aclGrants cannot grow past what the host already admits.

manifest.adoptReportMaxEntries.remediation: Fix the named non-derivable paths so the report shrinks, or lower manifest.adoptReportMaxEntries in config/limits/manifest.yaml.
manifest.adoptReportMaxEntries.rationale: Adopt-report arrays are operator output and must stay bounded. 1024 entries is a screenful of cmp misses, not an unbounded dump.

runtime.contract.maxNodes.remediation: Recover class. Reduce the decoded payload so it fits runtime.contract.maxNodes, then retry the same request.
runtime.contract.maxNodes.rationale: Shared contract-kit inert walk ceiling. 100000 admits real sealed records and still caps CPU and memory on every createContractKit contract.

runtime.contract.maxDepth.remediation: Recover class. Reduce nesting so it fits runtime.contract.maxDepth, then retry the same request.
runtime.contract.maxDepth.rationale: Sealed records are shallow closed schemas. 64 is far above any honest envelope and still small enough to bound recursion.

runtime.contract.maxArrayLength.remediation: Recover class. Shorten the array so it fits runtime.contract.maxArrayLength, then retry the same request.
runtime.contract.maxArrayLength.rationale: Same ceiling at the strict inert walk and the standard array helper. Large enough for real identifier lists; a huge array cannot hide behind a generic shape failure.

runtime.contract.maxStringChars.remediation: Recover class. Shorten the string so it fits runtime.contract.maxStringChars, then retry the same request.
runtime.contract.maxStringChars.rationale: Identifiers, hashes, and timestamps are tiny. 65536 UTF-16 code units is a generous scalar ceiling so a huge string is reported as this bound rather than as a typo.

runtime.delegatedTask.stateMaxBytes.remediation: Shrink the retained task record so it fits runtime.delegatedTask.stateMaxBytes, or lower DOCSFAB_RUNTIME_DELEGATED_TASK_STATE_MAX_BYTES. Raising the catalog value is a re-qualification.
runtime.delegatedTask.stateMaxBytes.rationale: Outcome bytes live in the private task record. The store refuses a larger pinned file before decode. 1048576 bytes (1 MiB) admits a paused outcome and still caps the allocation. A host override may only lower it.

runtime.planner.summaryMaxChars.remediation: Ask the planner for a shorter summary, or qualify the provider response envelope, the retained run record and the terminal framing together before raising this capacity.
runtime.planner.summaryMaxChars.rationale: Admitted length of one planner response summary, counted in UTF-16 units rather than bytes. The provider response carries its own separate byte check that is conditional on the composition policy, so this scalar is not interchangeable with a whole-response byte envelope; the inert contract decode string policy is a different and smaller scalar that must not be substituted for it.

nativePreflight.timeoutMs.remediation: Recover by inspecting the persisted native preflight observation, then rerun after the child finishes sooner, lower DOCSFAB_NATIVE_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS, or raise nativePreflight.timeoutMs in config/limits/nativePreflight.yaml.
nativePreflight.timeoutMs.rationale: Native preflight child timeout (no model request; the Codex account-catalog read is the only provider contact). Capture bound only; measured duration stays the actual elapsed time. Host override may only lower it.

nativePreflight.versionStdoutBytes.remediation: Recover by inspecting the persisted native preflight observation, then rerun after version stdout shrinks, lower DOCSFAB_NATIVE_PREFLIGHT_VERSION_STDOUT_BYTES, or raise nativePreflight.versionStdoutBytes in config/limits/nativePreflight.yaml.
nativePreflight.versionStdoutBytes.rationale: Capture ceiling for the fixed --version command. Overflow is reported; captured byte counts stay actual. Host override may only lower it.

nativePreflight.authenticationStdoutByte.remediation: Recover by inspecting the persisted native preflight observation, then rerun after authentication output shrinks, lower DOCSFAB_NATIVE_PREFLIGHT_AUTHENTICATION_STDOUT_BYTES, or raise nativePreflight.authenticationStdoutBytes in config/limits/nativePreflight.yaml.
nativePreflight.authenticationStdoutByte.rationale: Capture ceiling for the fixed authentication status command. Overflow is reported; captured byte counts stay actual. Host override may only lower it.

nativePreflight.catalogStdoutBytes.remediation: Recover by inspecting the persisted native preflight observation, then rerun after catalog stdout shrinks, lower DOCSFAB_NATIVE_PREFLIGHT_CATALOG_STDOUT_BYTES, or raise nativePreflight.catalogStdoutBytes in config/limits/nativePreflight.yaml.
nativePreflight.catalogStdoutBytes.rationale: Capture ceiling for the Codex model catalog command (bundled for the 0.147.0 pin, the authenticated account catalog for the 0.155.1 pin; the live account catalog was 645 KB on 2026-09-28). Overflow is reported; captured byte counts stay actual. Host override may only lower it.

nativePreflight.catalogModelCount.remediation: Recover by inspecting the persisted native preflight observation, then rerun after the provider catalog shrinks, lower DOCSFAB_NATIVE_PREFLIGHT_CATALOG_MODEL_COUNT, or raise nativePreflight.catalogModelCount in config/limits/nativePreflight.yaml.
nativePreflight.catalogModelCount.rationale: Maximum model entries parsed from a Codex model catalog. The account catalog is provider-controlled and can grow; exceeding the ceiling stops the preflight with a named evidence-limit notice instead of a malformed-output result. Host override may only lower it.

nativePreflight.catalogSlugCharacters.remediation: Recover by inspecting the persisted native preflight observation, then rerun after the provider catalog changes, lower DOCSFAB_NATIVE_PREFLIGHT_CATALOG_SLUG_CHARACTERS, or raise nativePreflight.catalogSlugCharacters in config/limits/nativePreflight.yaml.
nativePreflight.catalogSlugCharacters.rationale: Maximum characters in one Codex catalog model slug. Slugs come from a provider-controlled catalog; a longer slug stops the preflight with a named evidence-limit notice instead of a malformed-output result. Host override may only lower it.

nativePreflight.maxStderrBytes.remediation: Recover by inspecting the persisted native preflight observation, then rerun after stderr shrinks, lower DOCSFAB_NATIVE_PREFLIGHT_MAX_STDERR_BYTES, or raise nativePreflight.maxStderrBytes in config/limits/nativePreflight.yaml.
nativePreflight.maxStderrBytes.rationale: Capture ceiling for native preflight stderr. Overflow is reported; captured byte counts stay actual. Host override may only lower it.

nativePreflight.recordedDurationMs.remediation: Recover by inspecting the persisted native preflight observation durationMs, then rerun after the child finishes sooner, lower DOCSFAB_NATIVE_PREFLIGHT_RECORDED_DURATION_MS, or raise nativePreflight.recordedDurationMs in config/limits/nativePreflight.yaml.
nativePreflight.recordedDurationMs.rationale: Notice threshold for recorded native preflight duration. The persisted durationMs stays the measured value, including observations over this bound. Host override may only lower it.

nativePreflight.recordedStdoutBytes.remediation: Recover by inspecting the persisted native preflight observation stdoutBytes, then rerun after stdout shrinks, lower DOCSFAB_NATIVE_PREFLIGHT_RECORDED_STDOUT_BYTES, or raise nativePreflight.recordedStdoutBytes in config/limits/nativePreflight.yaml.
nativePreflight.recordedStdoutBytes.rationale: Notice threshold for recorded native preflight stdout. The persisted stdoutBytes stays the measured value, including observations over this bound. Host override may only lower it.

nativePreflight.recordedStderrBytes.remediation: Recover by inspecting the persisted native preflight observation stderrBytes, then rerun after stderr shrinks, lower DOCSFAB_NATIVE_PREFLIGHT_RECORDED_STDERR_BYTES, or raise nativePreflight.recordedStderrBytes in config/limits/nativePreflight.yaml.
nativePreflight.recordedStderrBytes.rationale: Notice threshold for recorded native preflight stderr. The persisted stderrBytes stays the measured value, including observations over this bound. Host override may only lower it.

autonomy.authorizationWindowMs.remediation: Recover by lowering the requested auto-cycle window or DOCSFAB_AUTONOMY_AUTHORIZATION_WINDOW_MS, then retry `docsfab auto --once`. Raise autonomy.authorizationWindowMs in config/limits/autonomy.yaml only when the host policy should admit a longer window.
autonomy.authorizationWindowMs.rationale: Maximum auto-cycle authorization window. Requested windows at this bound are admitted; one millisecond over refuses. DocsFab never silently shortens a requested window. Host override may only lower it.

autonomy.authorizationWindowDefaultMs.remediation: Recover by passing an explicit confirmation window at or under autonomy.authorizationWindowMs, or lower DOCSFAB_AUTONOMY_AUTHORIZATION_WINDOW_DEFAULT_MS, then retry `docsfab auto --once`. Startup refuses when the effective default exceeds the effective maximum.
autonomy.authorizationWindowDefaultMs.rationale: Default auto-cycle authorization window when confirmation omits windowMs. This is a default, not a silent clamp of a requested value. Host override may only lower it, and the effective default must stay at or under the effective maximum.

dogfood.proofReplayCount.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_DOGFOOD_PROOF_REPLAY_COUNT, or raise dogfood.proofReplayCount in config/limits/dogfood.yaml. The repository-event proof recipe is a developer dogfood script, so no host configuration file widens it.
dogfood.proofReplayCount.rationale: How many times the repository-event proposal-proof dogfood recipe replays one sealed delivery request against the same journal, to demonstrate that replay is idempotent. Two is the smallest count that can show idempotence at all - one attempt proves nothing about a second - and each extra attempt costs another full publish pass with no new evidence, so the default is the minimum that proves the property. Operators may only lower it, to one, which turns the replay assertion off rather than widening any external effect. This bounds a dogfood script's own loop, never a product path.

dogfood.proofManifestMaxBytes.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_DOGFOOD_PROOF_MANIFEST_MAX_BYTES, or raise dogfood.proofManifestMaxBytes in config/limits/dogfood.yaml. If a real run exceeds it, shrink the manifest rather than widening the bound.
dogfood.proofManifestMaxBytes.rationale: Largest composition manifest the repository-event proposal-proof dogfood recipe will write. Deliberately mirrors recovery.manifestMaxBytes, the existing bound on the largest manifest or restore receipt a verifier reads, so a proof artefact never outgrows what the verifier side of the same repository already accepts. The recipe compares before writing and refuses with this entry's own slug, so an oversized manifest is a named refusal and no partial file, not a silent truncation. Operators may only lower it.

dogfood.noDocLauncherMaxBufferBytes.remediation: Find out why the launcher printed that much, from the refused command's own log. If the output is expected, raise dogfood.noDocLauncherMaxBufferBytes in config/limits/dogfood.yaml and run `npm run generate:limits` from packages/runtime.
dogfood.noDocLauncherMaxBufferBytes.rationale: Largest stdout or stderr, per stream, that the create-documentation no-doc dogfood captures from one launcher command (list, init preview, init apply, and the create-documentation run, all with --json). Each prints one JSON document or a short listing, kilobytes in practice; the run record itself is read from its file, not from output. The value keeps the 32 MiB the script used before it was catalogued, so no run that passed then refuses now, and it still bounds the memory a runaway launcher can take. Node kills a child that crosses it and truncates the stream, so the script refuses with this entry's slug rather than parse the truncated output or report the command as having succeeded. This bounds a developer dogfood script, never a product path, so no host configuration widens it.

modelMatrix.maxConcurrentModels.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_MODEL_MATRIX_MAX_CONCURRENT_MODELS to fit provider and host capacity, or raise the catalog bound after measuring representative parallel runs.
modelMatrix.maxConcurrentModels.rationale: Maximum model-plus-route lanes active at once. Five lanes admit the representative five-model NIM rerun while keeping a useful ceiling on provider pressure; operators can lower it for constrained accounts or raise it after measuring route capacity.

modelMatrix.cellTimeoutMs.remediation: Read the cell's log and run record to see which step was still running. Raise DOCSFAB_MODEL_MATRIX_CELL_TIMEOUT_MS for a deliberately long matrix, or fix the stalled step. A cell stopped here is a harness fault, not a model result, so rerun it rather than scoring it.
modelMatrix.cellTimeoutMs.rationale: Wall clock for one `docsfab run` cell in the model-comparison harness. The CLI has no run-level wall of its own; its time limits are per step attempt (compositionExecution.timeoutMs, execution.normalModeMaxElapsedMs, both one hour). The harness therefore refuses to start unless this bound is larger than the larger of those per-attempt ceilings, so the runtime's own coded attempt stop always lands before the harness kill. On 2026-10-01 the Inference Hub matrix lanes measured 227 to 379 seconds for completed 8-step and 9-step runs, and up to about 39 minutes for runs that kept retrying a throttled step. Three hours keeps every measured run, including a full retry ladder on one slow step, while still ending a hung child within one working session. It replaces the old per-config `execution.timeoutMs` (1800000), which killed long lane D cells.

modelMatrix.judgeSourceMaxFiles.remediation: Name fewer judge sources in the corpus tasks.json, or version the corpus with a smaller source set. Raise modelMatrix.judgeSourceMaxFiles in config/limits/modelMatrix.yaml only with a measured judge that still grades within its window.
modelMatrix.judgeSourceMaxFiles.rationale: Most repository files the independent judge receives as source truth for one cell. The routing-task-guide-v2 corpus declares 11 source files plus the tracked-file inventory, and its whole repository is 21 tracked files. 24 covers the whole fixture, so a corpus can never be refused by declaring every file, while a corpus that tries to hand the judge an unbounded tree is refused by name rather than clipped.

modelMatrix.judgeSourceMaxBytes.remediation: Name fewer or smaller judge sources in the corpus tasks.json, or version the corpus. The harness never truncates a source, because a clipped contract would make the judge mark correct claims as unsupported.
modelMatrix.judgeSourceMaxBytes.rationale: Total bytes of the judge's source section for one cell, the declared source files plus the revision's tracked-file inventory. The routing-task-guide-v2 sources measure about 24 KiB including the inventory. 64 KiB is 2.7 times that, so a corpus revision that grows its contract stays admitted, and the bound still keeps the source section a small, known share of the judge request.

modelMatrix.judgeOutputMaxBytes.remediation: The cell's output is larger than the judge can grade whole. Read it directly; if it is a legitimate output, raise modelMatrix.judgeOutputMaxBytes in config/limits/modelMatrix.yaml and confirm that judge.contextWindowTokens still admits the request.
modelMatrix.judgeOutputMaxBytes.rationale: Bytes of the judged output bundle for one cell. For a write task that is every target's before and after document. For a read-only task it is the run-result projection (disposition, review findings, quality decision) plus the declared report-step summaries. The largest measured bundle on 2026-10-01 was a 28-finding focused review projection at 54 KiB. A complete task guide before and after is about 12 KiB. 128 KiB is 2.4 times the largest measurement. It replaces a silent 60,000-character slice. An over-size output now refuses by name and is never graded in part.

modelMatrix.judgeRequestTimeoutMs.remediation: Rerun judge.mjs; judging resumes per cell. If the judge route is persistently slow, raise DOCSFAB_MODEL_MATRIX_JUDGE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS.
modelMatrix.judgeRequestTimeoutMs.rationale: Wall clock for one judge chat-completions request. It keeps the five minutes the harness used as an unnamed default before it was catalogued. The judge answers with one bounded JSON object, so a request that takes longer is a stalled route, recorded as a coded judge error for that cell and retried on the next judge pass.

modelMatrix.judgeMaxOutputTokens.remediation: The judge reply was cut at this bound. Raise modelMatrix.judgeMaxOutputTokens in config/limits/modelMatrix.yaml; a cut reply is recorded as a judge error, never parsed as a partial score.
modelMatrix.judgeMaxOutputTokens.rationale: Output allowance for one judge reply. The reply holds an integer per rubric dimension, a rationale of at most a few hundred characters, and a list of unsupported claims with their source references. Ten claims at about 60 tokens each, plus the scores and the rationale, are about 1,000 tokens. 4096 is four times that. The old 1200-token config value had no room for the claims list.

modelMatrix.judgeContextWindowTokens.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_MODEL_MATRIX_JUDGE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS to the input window of the judge you configured, or shrink the judged output. A request that does not fit is refused before the call and recorded as a judge error for that cell.
modelMatrix.judgeContextWindowTokens.rationale: Input window of the configured judge, against which every judge request is checked before it is sent. The harness counts prompt bytes plus modelMatrix.judgeMaxOutputTokens, and every token is at least one byte, so the check never admits a request the window cannot hold. 200000 is the shipped judge's window (Claude Opus 4.7 through Inference Hub). The largest request measured on 2026-10-01 was about 44 KB, so the default leaves more than four times headroom. An operator who configures a different judge sets its window through the override; the catalog keeps it visible in docsfab doctor --limits rather than buried in a matrix config.

host.slack.liveAgentTurnTextMaxBytes.remediation: Reduce pasted text and point DocsFab at repository files, or restore the configured question allowance up to its qualified maximum before submitting again.
host.slack.liveAgentTurnTextMaxBytes.rationale: Qualified full-message capacity, not an asserted inbound Slack limit. 40,000 text characters at four UTF-8 bytes each require 160,000 bytes. The live-agent event, aggregate frozen-input and wire capacities derive their extra space from this capacity and actual JSON framing; the existing non-live workflow envelopes remain unchanged.
host.slack.liveAgentTurnTextMaxBytes.docSummary: UTF-8 question bytes admitted before a job is created. You can lower this allowance.

host.slack.transportTextChars.remediation: Split the Slack result into messages within the configured transport bound, or restore DOCSFAB_HOST_SLACK_TRANSPORT_TEXT_CHARS up to the documented Slack maximum, then retry the same request.
host.slack.transportTextChars.rationale: Slack chat.postMessage truncates text above 40,000 characters (https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.postMessage/). The host refuses oversized writes before transport. Slack recommends 4,000 for readability; that recommendation is not its protocol ceiling. JavaScript UTF-16 length conservatively counts supplementary characters twice.
host.slack.transportTextChars.docSummary: Maximum text sent in one Slack message.

host.slack.liveAgentAnswerChunkBudget.remediation: Use a message allowance no greater than host.slack.transportTextChars; reduce it for shorter messages without reducing the complete answer.
host.slack.liveAgentAnswerChunkBudget.rationale: Per-message allowance including the actual sequence marker, defaulting to the documented Slack transport maximum. The shared planner derives payload space from that marker and delivers every safe retained answer chunk. This setting does not truncate the total answer.
host.slack.liveAgentAnswerChunkBudget.docSummary: Message allowance including its sequence marker. A smaller value produces more messages.

host.slack.liveAgentAnswerMaxChunks.remediation: Remove the obsolete positive chunk-count override or set DOCSFAB_HOST_SLACK_LIVE_AGENT_ANSWER_MAX_CHUNKS=0 for complete answer delivery. Use the per-message chunk budget for shorter messages.
host.slack.liveAgentAnswerMaxChunks.rationale: Compatibility setting fixed at zero, meaning complete delivery with no separate total-message policy cap. Positive historical truncation overrides refuse with migration guidance so retained conversation history never contains an unseen answer tail. Finite delivery derives from the bounded retained record.
host.slack.liveAgentAnswerMaxChunks.docSummary: Compatibility setting for complete delivery. Positive legacy values are rejected with migration guidance.

host.slack.liveAgentRunRecordMaxBytes.remediation: Inspect the retained terminal record and its configured provider/output budgets; a record over this existing CAS read envelope cannot be projected as a complete Slack answer.
host.slack.liveAgentRunRecordMaxBytes.rationale: Names the existing 4 MiB live-agent terminal CAS read guard without raising it. The complete terminal record, including metadata, must fit. Answer decoding derives its finite byte and nonempty-chunk envelope from this guard; this is not a new total-message policy cap.

host.slack.askTargetCandidateMax.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_HOST_SLACK_ASK_TARGET_CANDIDATE_MAX, or raise it within max, then ask again; a narrower target name also produces fewer near matches.
host.slack.askTargetCandidateMax.rationale: Nearest tracked pages named in the one refusal reply when a Slack question targets a page that is not tracked at the revision the run would freeze. Five keeps the reply readable in a Slack thread and bounds the cost of a wrong name; the list is a courtesy beside the exact path and revision, never the answer itself, so a lower value loses no required information. It is not a review-scope bound, because a question carries exactly one target by grammar.

host.slack.askTargetLookupTimeoutMs.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_HOST_SLACK_ASK_TARGET_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS within max if the project mirror is routinely slower than this, or reduce contention on the mirror; a question whose lookup times out is still accepted and verified when it runs.
host.slack.askTargetLookupTimeoutMs.rationale: Wall-clock ceiling for the one bounded read of the project mirror that answers whether a question's target is a tracked page, before anything is queued. The requester is waiting in a Slack thread, so this is far below the general git invocation ceiling the same reader already applies. Exceeding it is a failure to read and never evidence that the page is absent, so the question is still admitted and the exact check runs again when the job starts. Its maximum matches that general git ceiling so it can never be raised past it.

host.gitlab.noteBodyMaxChars.remediation: Shorten the review or status note, or raise DOCSFAB_HOST_GITLAB_NOTE_BODY_MAX_CHARS up to the catalog max, then retry the same request.
host.gitlab.noteBodyMaxChars.rationale: Longest GitLab MR note body the host posts for a review summary or forge status note. Producers clip with an omitted-character notice. Transport refuses a longer body rather than letting GitLab fail as a generic post error. Override may only lower it.

host.gitlab.safeLabelMaxChars.remediation: Shorten the workflow safe label, or raise DOCSFAB_HOST_GITLAB_SAFE_LABEL_MAX_CHARS up to the catalog max, then retry the same request.
host.gitlab.safeLabelMaxChars.rationale: Longest safe-label workflow name a GitLab MR note records. A longer label is refused with this code rather than silently clamped. Override may only lower it.

host.gitlab.mrNotePatchFiles.remediation: Name fewer changed files in the status note, or raise DOCSFAB_HOST_GITLAB_MR_NOTE_PATCH_FILES up to the catalog max, then retry the same request.
host.gitlab.mrNotePatchFiles.rationale: Most patch file rows a forge status-block note lists. Further portable paths are counted in a PATCH omitted notice rather than dropped. Override may only lower it.

host.dispatcher.writableTreeEntries.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_WRITABLE_TREE_ENTRIES in the supported host limits configuration within the declared representation range.
host.dispatcher.writableTreeEntries.rationale: Ordinary resource allowance. Entries inspected in an authorized writable tree; increasing this work allowance does not change path or write authority. The default uses the configured maximum; host overrides may lower it. The maximum is the exact-integer representation boundary, not measured machine capacity.

host.dispatcher.privateGitIndexBytes.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_PRIVATE_GIT_INDEX_BYTES in the supported host limits configuration within the declared representation range.
host.dispatcher.privateGitIndexBytes.rationale: Ordinary resource allowance. Bytes permitted for the private Git index copy; filesystem identity and private namespace checks remain independent. The default uses the configured maximum; host overrides may lower it. The maximum is the exact-integer representation boundary, not measured machine capacity.

host.dispatcher.privateGitLinkBytes.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_PRIVATE_GIT_LINK_BYTES in the supported host limits configuration within the declared representation range.
host.dispatcher.privateGitLinkBytes.rationale: Ordinary resource allowance. Bytes permitted for parsing the private Git link; exact syntax and containment checks remain independent. The default uses the configured maximum; host overrides may lower it. The maximum is the 64-bit Node UTF-8 string carrier maximum for worst-case ASCII, buffer.constants.MAX_STRING_LENGTH, not measured machine capacity.

host.dispatcher.stderrExcerptBytes.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_STDERR_EXCERPT_BYTES in the supported host limits configuration within the declared representation range.
host.dispatcher.stderrExcerptBytes.rationale: Diagnostic-output allowance. Bytes retained in the diagnostic tail; credential screening still applies at every size. The default uses the configured maximum; host overrides may lower it. The maximum is the 64-bit Node UTF-8 string carrier maximum for worst-case ASCII, buffer.constants.MAX_STRING_LENGTH, not measured machine capacity.

host.dispatcher.stderrBytes.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_STDERR_BYTES in the supported host limits configuration within the declared representation range.
host.dispatcher.stderrBytes.rationale: Diagnostic-output allowance. Total standard-error bytes permitted from the child; changing this allowance cannot release a process before close. The default uses the configured maximum; host overrides may lower it. The maximum is the exact-integer representation boundary, not measured machine capacity.

host.dispatcher.stderrDrainMs.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_STDERR_DRAIN_MS in the supported host limits configuration within the declared representation range.
host.dispatcher.stderrDrainMs.rationale: Cleanup timing. Wait for diagnostic collection only; confirmed close remains mandatory afterward. The default preserves the existing value; host overrides may raise or lower it. The maximum is the Node timer representation boundary; larger delays are coerced to one millisecond.

host.dispatcher.terminateGraceMs.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_TERMINATE_GRACE_MS in the supported host limits configuration within the declared representation range.
host.dispatcher.terminateGraceMs.rationale: Cleanup timing. Grace between process-group TERM and KILL; confirmed close remains mandatory afterward. The default preserves the existing value; host overrides may raise or lower it. The maximum is the Node timer representation boundary; larger delays are coerced to one millisecond.

host.dispatcher.workerCountRepresentatio.remediation: Supply a valid explicit worker count or scheduling policy within the declared representation domain.
host.dispatcher.workerCountRepresentatio.rationale: Configuration representation boundary for explicit operator-selected worker counts. Capacity remains required service configuration; this value is never selected as a worker allocation default.

host.dispatcher.interactiveReservation.remediation: Supply a valid explicit worker count or scheduling policy within the declared representation domain.
host.dispatcher.interactiveReservation.rationale: Initial scheduling policy. Reserve interactive-only workers within each static project allocation while retaining at least one shared worker; the scheduler clamps this to allocation-1 regardless of this value, so raising it cannot starve the shared lane. Raised from 1 to 2 (Task CAPACITY, 2026-09-30) so a live-agent turn (J1) and a merge semantic comparison (J4) each get their own reserved worker instead of alternating on one, paired with the pilot's reviewed worker-capacity default of 5 (2 reserved + 3 shared) so review-documentation jobs (J3) also run concurrently. This is configurable dispatch policy, not a job or model allowance.

host.dispatcher.classQuantum.remediation: Supply a valid explicit worker count or scheduling policy within the declared representation domain.
host.dispatcher.classQuantum.rationale: Initial scheduling policy. Consecutive shared dispatch opportunities per class when both classes are eligible. The default alternates classes; no running attempt is preempted.

host.dispatcher.pollIntervalMs.remediation: Supply a valid explicit worker count or scheduling policy within the declared representation domain.
host.dispatcher.pollIntervalMs.rationale: Queue polling and retry cadence, preserving the existing default. Completions can wake selection sooner. The maximum is the Node timer representation boundary, not a service-latency promise.

host.dispatcher.statusBytes.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_STATUS_BYTES within the declared representation domain; inspect degraded status rather than treating it as free capacity.
host.dispatcher.statusBytes.rationale: Status JSON byte allowance, defaulting to the 64-bit Node string representation maximum for worst-case ASCII. This covers aggregate project records without an invented project-count or status-size ceiling; physical memory is not qualified by the representation range.

host.dispatcher.statusFreshnessMs.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_STATUS_FRESHNESS_MS within the declared representation domain; inspect degraded status rather than treating it as free capacity.
host.dispatcher.statusFreshnessMs.rationale: Preserves the existing status freshness window. Older queue polls or child heartbeats report unknown capacity and degraded health. The range is the exact-integer timestamp-difference representation, not a scheduling SLA.

host.dispatcher.statusClockSkewMs.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_STATUS_CLOCK_SKEW_MS within the declared representation domain; inspect degraded status rather than treating it as free capacity.
host.dispatcher.statusClockSkewMs.rationale: Preserves the existing future-clock tolerance for status observations. This is an explicit operator timing policy; larger tolerances do not authorize job claims or relax their fences.

host.dispatcher.shutdownGraceMs.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS within the declared representation domain; inspect degraded status rather than treating it as free capacity.
host.dispatcher.shutdownGraceMs.rationale: Preserves the existing supervisor TERM-to-KILL grace. The supervisor awaits confirmed child exit after escalation; the timer never reports a live child as reaped. The maximum is the Node timer representation boundary.

host.dispatcher.semanticSourceBytes.remediation: Configure the source-read allowance within the existing readTracked port domain; preserve downstream semantic evidence admission and never truncate a source.
host.dispatcher.semanticSourceBytes.rationale: The actual readTracked port accepts maximumBytes from 1 through MAX_GIT_OUTPUT (1 MiB), returns complete bytes and their digest, and refuses overflow. This caller now defaults to that supported port maximum. The semantic snapshot consumer still independently validates its evidence budget and fatal UTF-8 decoding; this read allowance does not enlarge those contracts.

host.dispatcher.attemptEvidenceMaxBytes.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_ATTEMPT_EVIDENCE_MAX_BYTES within the declared range and no higher than host.dispatcher.attemptEvidenceRetainedBytes. A larger record is logged over-bound with its size and is not copied.
host.dispatcher.attemptEvidenceMaxBytes.rationale: Largest saved run record the dispatcher copies as evidence when a review attempt ends without a result (a deadline, a service stop, a moved head, a crashed worker) or settles a worker-reported failed terminal, whose full record is already retained separately in project CAS without this bound. The default is four times the largest step-boundary record measured on a pilot review, about 2.0 MB. The maximum is the dispatcher's single retained-object carrier, 16 MiB, the maximum of semantic.comparisonChunkBytes. A record over the bound is not copied, its size is logged and observed, and the row reads over.

host.dispatcher.attemptEvidenceRetention.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_ATTEMPT_EVIDENCE_RETENTION_DAYS within the declared range. Copy any evidence file still needed out of the attempt-evidence directory before lowering it.
host.dispatcher.attemptEvidenceRetention.rationale: Age in whole days after which the next capture in the same project deletes a retained attempt-evidence file. Pilot failures were diagnosed within one deploy cycle and re-read within a day; two weeks spans a weekend and a handover. The maximum, 90 days, is one quarter, beyond which a record describes a release long replaced. Not observed, because a max-merged age would sit near the value and warn permanently.

host.dispatcher.attemptEvidenceRetainedB.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_ATTEMPT_EVIDENCE_RETAINED_BYTES within the declared range and no lower than host.dispatcher.attemptEvidenceMaxBytes. The oldest evidence files are deleted first to stay within it.
host.dispatcher.attemptEvidenceRetainedB.rationale: Total bytes of attempt evidence kept per project. After each capture the oldest files are deleted until the directory fits, and the file just written is always kept. 256 MiB holds about 128 records at the largest measured size, against about 12 failed reviews a day at the busiest pilot release, and stays far under the disk headroom floors (warn 3 GiB, over 1.25 GiB) for the one or two projects a pilot host runs. The exposure is per project, so a host with N projects can hold N times this budget, so a host near host.ingress.projectsMax should lower it. The maximum, 1 GiB, stays under the over floor. The observation is the directory total after that deletion.

host.dispatcher.attemptEvidenceReasonCha.remediation: Set DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_ATTEMPT_EVIDENCE_REASON_CHARACTERS within the declared range. A longer reason is cut to the bound and ends with a truncation marker; the full text is not kept anywhere else.
host.dispatcher.attemptEvidenceReasonCha.rationale: Longest error message the attempt-evidence log line carries in its reason field; for an attempt that ends by throw before any failure line, or that settles a worker-reported failed terminal, it is the bounded copy of that message beside the unbounded one on the adjacent failure line. Dispatcher-authored messages run to about 120 characters; 4096 keeps any realistic message whole, including one that quotes a path list, while holding one service-log line to a few KiB on a host with little free disk. The minimum leaves room for the truncation marker and the credential-withheld digest. The maximum, 64 KiB, bounds a single line. The observation is the untruncated length, so over means a reason was cut.

host.ingress.projectsMax.remediation: Preserve the installed registry contract; changing its admitted project count requires coordinated registry and operator consumers.
host.ingress.projectsMax.rationale: Canonical name for the existing ingress-project-registry v1 admission contract of 1 through 32 project policies. Registry parsing and the status projection consume this same definition. This is not a worker-capacity default or a claim of host resource headroom.

host.ingress.httpBodyBytes.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_INGRESS_HTTP_BODY_BYTES within the declared caller domain; preserve independent authority, shape and transport checks.
host.ingress.httpBodyBytes.rationale: Existing startIngressHttpServer maximumBodyBytes API admits 1 KiB through 2 MiB. Default remains its supported maximum; complete-body collection and authenticated forge intake still refuse oversize payloads.

host.ingress.httpRequestMs.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_INGRESS_HTTP_REQUEST_MS within the declared caller domain; preserve independent authority, shape and transport checks.
host.ingress.httpRequestMs.rationale: Preserves the HTTP request observation deadline. Node22 ConnectionsList::Expired converts this millisecond field with Uint32 before scaling to nanoseconds, so the supported maximum is UINT32_MAX.

host.ingress.httpHeadersMs.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_INGRESS_HTTP_HEADERS_MS within the declared caller domain; preserve independent authority, shape and transport checks.
host.ingress.httpHeadersMs.rationale: Preserves the HTTP header observation deadline. Node22 ConnectionsList::Expired converts this millisecond field with Uint32 before scaling to nanoseconds; header timing remains no greater than request timing.

host.ingress.httpKeepAliveMs.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_INGRESS_HTTP_KEEP_ALIVE_MS within the declared caller domain; preserve independent authority, shape and transport checks.
