host.ingress.httpKeepAliveMs.rationale: Preserves the five-second idle connection policy. Supported Node22.19 and25 add a 1000 ms keep-alive timeout buffer before socket.setTimeout; INT32_MAX minus that buffer avoids the Node timer clamp.

host.ingress.httpHeadersCount.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_INGRESS_HTTP_HEADERS_COUNT within the declared caller domain; preserve independent authority, shape and transport checks.
host.ingress.httpHeadersCount.rationale: Full supported positive header-pair carrier. Node _http_server assigns parser.maxHeaderPairs using maxHeadersCount << 1; values above INT32_MAX shifted right by one can wrap negative and disable the count check. Node header-byte admission and signature checks remain independent.

host.ingress.httpStartupCloseMs.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_INGRESS_HTTP_STARTUP_CLOSE_MS within the declared caller domain; preserve independent authority, shape and transport checks.
host.ingress.httpStartupCloseMs.rationale: Preserves the startup-failure close grace. The existing closeServer API admits positive timeouts through 30000 ms; this row records that caller contract without changing its maximum.

host.ingress.httpCloseMs.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_INGRESS_HTTP_CLOSE_MS within the declared caller domain; preserve independent authority, shape and transport checks.
host.ingress.httpCloseMs.rationale: Preserves the normal HTTP shutdown grace. The existing closeServer API admits positive timeouts through 30000 ms; this row is also the canonical shared maximum for its two callers.

host.ingress.slackCredentialTtlMs.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_INGRESS_SLACK_CREDENTIAL_TTL_MS within the declared caller domain; preserve independent authority, shape and transport checks.
host.ingress.slackCredentialTtlMs.rationale: The existing opaque Slack credential handle expires after 180 days. This is an authority lifetime, not a model or output allowance. A supported override may shorten that lifetime; this change does not grant a longer credential lifetime.

host.ingress.healthPollMs.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_INGRESS_HEALTH_POLL_MS within the declared caller domain; preserve independent authority, shape and transport checks.
host.ingress.healthPollMs.rationale: Preserves the ingress health observation cadence. The maximum is the Node interval timer representation boundary; this is not a job execution allowance.

host.ingress.healthFreshnessSeconds.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_HEALTH_FRESHNESS_SECONDS within the declared caller domain; preserve independent authority, shape and transport checks.
host.ingress.healthFreshnessSeconds.rationale: Canonical domain of the existing required installed health-freshness setting, 1 through 300 seconds. The installer selects30 seconds for the current deployment; milliseconds are derived with the exact seconds-to-milliseconds conversion.

host.dispatcher.postgresConnections.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_POSTGRES_CONNECTIONS within the declared caller domain; preserve independent authority, shape and transport checks.
host.dispatcher.postgresConnections.rationale: Preserves the existing explicit two-connection per-project resource allocation. The pg pool accepts a positive numeric maximum; safe integers define supported configuration, not actual machine headroom or a model allowance. N-worker acceptance retains the default two-connection allocation.

host.dispatcher.policyBytes.remediation: Inspect the complete protected dispatcher policy; raise DOCSFAB_DISPATCHER_POLICY_BYTES within max, or change host.dispatcher.policyBytes in config/limits/host.yaml, then reload the policy. Policy custody and grant checks are unaffected by this allowance.
host.dispatcher.policyBytes.rationale: The dispatcher policy loader and the fresh protected policy reread share one complete UTF-8 JSON admission. The default is the previously shipped installed-policy ceiling and narrows no existing policy; the maximum is the supported 64-bit Node single-string representation for worst-case ASCII. This is a representation boundary, not measured memory throughput or authority.

host.grants.mergeScopePathsMax.remediation: Leave the merge request for a human to merge; a PRM-update merge request that changes more paths than this is not one DocsFab queues itself. Changing the bound needs a reviewed catalog change.
host.grants.mergeScopePathsMax.rationale: Most entries a queue-own-prm-merge scope may carry in either of its lists, the merge request's changed paths and the projection entries. One PRM-update merge request changes one native version (three files), the history and index files, files in the source thread of its input and the projection documents it regenerates. The largest source thread in the reference model today holds 145 files in all and the whole reference model 399, and an approved model names at most eight documentation targets. So 256 still holds an update that rewrote the whole of the largest thread together with a version, the history, the index and every target (158 entries), about 1.6 times over; an update that rewrites most of the reference model is left for a human. Above it the evaluator refuses the scope by this bound's refusal name rather than reading part of it, and the merge request stays open for a human.

host.grants.mergeScopePathMaxChars.remediation: Leave the merge request for a human to merge; a path longer than this is not one a DocsFab delivery can carry. Changing the bound needs a reviewed catalog change.
host.grants.mergeScopePathMaxChars.rationale: Longest repository-relative path a queue-own-prm-merge scope may name. The longest tracked path in the repository today is 177 characters and the longest in the reference model 166 (content-addressed artifact paths). 512 is the path bound a delivery request already enforces, so no path a DocsFab delivery can carry is refused here.

host.retention.slackTextDays.remediation: Keep host.retention.slackTextDays within 1 to 30 days in config/limits/host.yaml, refresh the core tooling so the installed limits mirror carries it, and rerun the redaction. Raising the maximum needs a Privacy-approved change to the recorded retention commitment first.
host.retention.slackTextDays.rationale: Most days the pilot may hold raw Slack message text after the job that used it completes (the POR-D09 amendment of 2026-10-02 on issue 72, and the DocsFab 0.0.1 record of processing activities). The scheduled redaction replaces that text with content-free digests in the locations it covers once a completed job is this old, less two redaction intervals, so covered text is gone by this age while the timer runs; job and audit records stay. Copies it does not cover yet are tracked in issue 1820. 30 days is the commitment, so the maximum equals the value and there is no host override. A lower value redacts sooner and shortens the window in which a thread follow-up still sees its earlier exchanges.
host.retention.slackTextDays.docSummary: Days after a job completes before its raw Slack text is redacted to digests.

host.retention.slackTextRedactionInterva.remediation: Keep host.retention.slackTextRedactionIntervalMinutes within 1 to 1440 in config/limits/host.yaml and set OnUnitActiveSec in docsfab-retention-redaction.timer to the same number of minutes, then reinstall the timer.
host.retention.slackTextRedactionInterva.rationale: How often the scheduled Slack text redaction runs, and therefore how early it redacts. Each run redacts text whose job completed more than host.retention.slackTextDays minus two intervals ago. The timer starts a run at most one interval and one second after the previous start, so the second interval absorbs that slack and the run time, so covered text is gone by host.retention.slackTextDays while the timer keeps its cadence, and is never removed more than two intervals early. Hourly keeps the early margin to two hours at the cost of one short database statement an hour. The maximum is one day; a longer interval would redact text more than two days before the committed age. The timer's OnUnitActiveSec must equal this value, which a deploy test holds.
host.retention.slackTextRedactionInterva.docSummary: How often the Slack text redaction runs; it redacts up to two intervals before the retention age.

host.selfDocumentationCandidateGitTimeou.remediation: Inspect the candidate workspace Git operation and retry after repairing the local repository; changing the deadline requires qualification of the candidate materializer.
host.selfDocumentationCandidateGitTimeou.rationale: Historical per-command Git deadline for reading and constructing an immutable self-documentation candidate. The materializer kills a command that exceeds it rather than using partial output. This owner is separate from the host-invoker hardened Git helper.

host.selfDocumentationCandidateGitOutput.remediation: Narrow the candidate's changed-path scope or repair the repository before retrying; changing this Git output bound requires qualification of the candidate materializer.
host.selfDocumentationCandidateGitOutput.rationale: Historical maximum accumulated output of one self-documentation candidate Git command. A command exceeding this value is killed; its partial output is never accepted as a complete tree, patch, or path inventory.

host.selfDocumentationCandidatePatchMaxB.remediation: Split the candidate into smaller independently reviewed changes; a patch above this historical materialization bound cannot be applied as one candidate.
host.selfDocumentationCandidatePatchMaxB.rationale: Historical byte limit on the candidate patch itself before materialization. It is distinct from the Git subprocess output limit even though both historical values are eight MiB.

host.selfDocumentationCandidateChangedPa.remediation: Split an oversized authoring candidate into smaller changes and review each candidate independently.
host.selfDocumentationCandidateChangedPa.rationale: Historical number of unique repository-relative paths one self-documentation candidate may change. It is a candidate write-scope bound, not the count of focused review targets. The source manifest and final candidate receipt must agree on every path and refuse an oversized set rather than silently dropping paths.

host.selfDocumentationReviewerGitTimeout.remediation: Inspect the immutable review target and retry after repairing the local repository; changing the deadline requires qualification of the installed reviewer.
host.selfDocumentationReviewerGitTimeout.rationale: Historical per-command deadline for the installed independent reviewer to verify that target paths exist in the immutable review commit. This caller uses its own Git operation and does not borrow the host-invoker helper's deadline merely because the current numbers agree.

host.selfDocumentationReviewerTargetList.remediation: Review fewer paths in one candidate or repair a malformed repository tree before retrying; changing the listing size requires qualification of the independent reviewer.
host.selfDocumentationReviewerTargetList.rationale: Historical buffer limit for one immutable Git tree listing used by the independent reviewer. It inspects a single requested target and refuses excess bytes rather than interpreting a clipped listing as proof that the target is present.

host.selfDocumentationReviewerRunRecordR.remediation: Narrow the candidate review run or inspect an oversized retained record before retrying; never consume a partial reviewer run record.
host.selfDocumentationReviewerRunRecordR.rationale: Historical maximum CAS read size for the installed reviewer's retained runtime record. This is a distinct object from the reviewer receipt and from Slack live-agent records.

host.selfDocumentationReviewerReceiptRea.remediation: Inspect an oversized reviewer receipt and retry only after its complete retained evidence fits the declared reader; never consume a partial receipt.
host.selfDocumentationReviewerReceiptRea.rationale: Historical maximum CAS read size for the installed reviewer's dispatcher receipt, separate from the runtime record and Git tree listing.

reviewScope.maxTargets.remediation: Name the first batch of pages (or one page with --context-path), then continue with a second command targeting the rest. A whole-documentation-set review that needs more target entries than this splits the same way.
reviewScope.maxTargets.rationale: Most entries one review target may hold - the pages a focused review names, or the host-derived evaluation target of a whole-documentation-set review (one entry per page, or per directory whose documents are all in scope). Structural input validation for named pages, so a malformed or hostile producer cannot hand the parser an unbounded array, and a cap on the step 8 prompt, which states the evaluation target. The evaluator does not echo the target - the host writes evaluation.target.paths - so it costs prompt input, not output allowance. Measured 2026-10-01 - this repository's whole-set target is 81 entries serialized in 3,165 characters (about 0.8k tokens); its longest tracked documentation path is 174 characters, so a target at this bound is at most about 44.5k characters (about 11k input tokens), within the 131,072-token context the measured step 8 runs used. How many named pages a run actually covers is still decided from measured page sizes; anything the budget cannot cover is deferred and reported rather than dropped. No override tier, because raising it would raise the parser's exposure and the evaluator prompt rather than an operator allowance.

reviewScope.pathMaxChars.remediation: Name a shorter repository-relative documentation path, or raise reviewScope.pathMaxChars in config/limits/reviewScope.yaml.
reviewScope.pathMaxChars.rationale: Longest repository-relative documentation path a focused review target or a hosted native task may name. Structural input validation against a malformed or hostile producer; shape rules on the same path - no leading slash or tilde, no backslash, no empty or dot segment, no whitespace or comma, no credential shape - stay separate from this length allowance. The default of 512 characters is several times the longest documentation path this repository tracks, which is 80 characters.

reviewScope.continuationTextMaxChars.remediation: Shorten the rendered continuation, or qualify its producer and this reader together before raising the text capacity.
reviewScope.continuationTextMaxChars.rationale: Admitted length of the continuation text a deferred review scope carries, counted in UTF-16 units. It exists so a rendered continuation keeps a complete command and its omitted-page accounting; it is this contract's own capacity and not an asserted chat-transport character limit.

reviewDelivery.snapshotUniqueOriginalByt.remediation: Narrow the review source range, or raise DOCSFAB_REVIEW_DELIVERY_SNAPSHOT_UNIQUE_ORIGINAL_BYTES_MAX together with any smaller source-acquisition materialization bound, then rerun before model dispatch.
reviewDelivery.snapshotUniqueOriginalByt.rationale: Distinct verified original Git blob bytes retained for one review, charged once by object id rather than once per side or file. The 256 MiB default matches changeSourcesGithub.objectMaterializedMaxBytes, so its default acquisition can be retained without a second smaller ceiling. It is a design admission and disk-retention budget, not a measured peak RSS bound; preflight must still measure the full run and retained graph.
reviewDelivery.snapshotUniqueOriginalByt.docSummary: Maximum distinct original source bytes retained for one review run.

reviewDelivery.snapshotPartBytes.remediation: Increase DOCSFAB_REVIEW_DELIVERY_SNAPSHOT_PART_BYTES when a smaller part size creates too many objects, or raise artifacts.maxObjectBytes for serialized fit; the source bytes are never clipped.
reviewDelivery.snapshotPartBytes.rationale: Target maximum raw bytes per stored snapshot part, matching the existing sealed hostInvoker.gitOutputMaxBytes default. This is fragmentation, not an input ceiling. The writer still checks each JSON/base64 part against effective artifacts.maxObjectBytes and splits it further when required.
reviewDelivery.snapshotPartBytes.docSummary: Raw bytes in one retained review source snapshot part before serialized-object fit.

githubReview.bodyMaxBytes.remediation: Inspect the saved review inventory and narrow the requested review, or raise DOCSFAB_GITHUB_REVIEW_BODY_MAX_BYTES within the validated host range after checking the target's policy; retry only a fresh unpublished delivery.
githubReview.bodyMaxBytes.rationale: Internal UTF-8 byte budget for one GitHub pending-review body, separate from the complete native inline-comments batch. A valid admitted default review measured 66498 rich-body bytes versus 277 legacy bytes, so the default selects a fixed compact partial body while preserving the complete inline batch and saved inventory. First-party gh-aw uses a 65000-character tool policy; 65000 bytes is a conservative DocsFab presentation choice, not a GitHub REST maximum or an acceptance guarantee. The 256-byte minimum permits an actionable pre-publication stop when even the fixed compact body does not fit. The 131072-byte host-override maximum is a provisional internal range above the measured example, not measured provider capacity. An oversized explicit overview refuses before POST; committed potentially invoked reviews retain exact sealed bytes regardless of later policy changes.
githubReview.bodyMaxBytes.docSummary: Internal byte budget for one GitHub pending-review body; native inline comments have separate transport bounds.

reviewFindings.resultSummaryMaxChars.remediation: Shorten a legacy standalone review summary or preserve the full source issue in the V3 issue graph without clipping it.
reviewFindings.resultSummaryMaxChars.rationale: Legacy V1 and V2 review result finding, question, and check prose was admitted at this length before V3. This declared structural ceiling preserves those closed envelopes while complete V3 issue actions and source fact text retain their own original length. It is not a cap on the new issue graph.

reviewFindings.coverageDeferredMaxCount.remediation: Continue the review in another focused scope or use the existing durable continuation plan to account for further deferred pages.
reviewFindings.coverageDeferredMaxCount.rationale: The closed review result coverage block admits at most this many explicitly named deferred pages. This is a per-result transport list, separate from the number of requested review targets even though both historical values happen to be 256. The remaining scope must be retained by the review plan and reported as unlisted or deferred rather than silently omitted.

reviewFindings.coverageContinuationMinCh.remediation: Use a continuation allowance large enough for the complete command and its source bindings.
reviewFindings.coverageContinuationMinCh.rationale: Historical review result admission refused an accounting continuation allowance below this value because a useful bound command needs room for its scope, revision, and at least one path. This is the lower validity threshold of the coverage field, not a limit on issue facts, actions, or host output.

reviewFindings.summaryTopN.remediation: Read every admitted finding with docsfab runs show <run-id> --json, or raise reviewFindings.summaryTopN in config/limits/reviewFindings.yaml to print more of them in the human result.
reviewFindings.summaryTopN.rationale: Admitted review findings the human REVIEW FINDINGS section prints as sentences for review-documentation and authoring runs, ranked by severity, error then warning then info, then by finding id. Presentation only; the JSON reviewFindings array and the run record always carry every admitted finding, and the section always prints a Findings shown N of M line with a pointer to that JSON when it prints fewer than it admitted, so a clipped tail is never silent. Each finding takes four lines, so 5 keeps the section to about 20 finding lines. The first retained review measured in Epic(#1436), run 1aba893c, admitted 27 findings, and its top 5 by this ranking are the evaluator's five warning-level synthesized findings. The maximum matches the review projector's own admitted-finding ceiling, 256, so the bound can show every finding a run can admit. No override tier; a caller who needs every finding reads the JSON.

reviewFindings.auditFooterFindings.remediation: Read every product finding code with docsfab runs show <run-id> --json, where product.findings lists them all, or raise reviewFindings.auditFooterFindings in config/limits/reviewFindings.yaml.
reviewFindings.auditFooterFindings.rationale: Workflow outcome finding codes the review-documentation PRODUCT section prints, one line per code with its glossary phrase, before a Product findings omitted count. Migrated unchanged from a hand-declared presenter constant of the same value, previously an allowlisted literal, Task(#1027) identifier-rule expansion. Separate from reviewFindings.summaryTopN because these are one-line workflow outcome codes, not the four-line admitted review findings, and the audit outcome rarely carries more than a few codes. Presentation only; the JSON product.findings array always carries every code.

productFeedback.gitBlobMaxBufferBytes.remediation: Shrink the Git blob read or raise productFeedback.gitBlobMaxBufferBytes in config/limits/productFeedback.yaml.
productFeedback.gitBlobMaxBufferBytes.rationale: Spawn buffer for one cat-file of a product-feedback Git blob. 32 MiB matches the previous fixed maxBuffer.

productFeedback.gitPathListMaxBufferByte.remediation: Shrink the model version listing or raise productFeedback.gitPathListMaxBufferBytes in config/limits/productFeedback.yaml.
productFeedback.gitPathListMaxBufferByte.rationale: Spawn buffer for the version-directory name list. 1 MiB matches the previous fixed maxBuffer.

productFeedback.gitCommandTimeoutMs.remediation: Retry the local Git read or raise productFeedback.gitCommandTimeoutMs in config/limits/productFeedback.yaml.
productFeedback.gitCommandTimeoutMs.rationale: Ceiling for one local product-feedback Git read. 30 seconds matches the previous fixed timeout.

productFeedback.gitBlobMaxBytes.remediation: Remove the oversized blob from the model tree or raise productFeedback.gitBlobMaxBytes in config/limits/productFeedback.yaml.
productFeedback.gitBlobMaxBytes.rationale: Largest Git blob a product-feedback materializer will hash. 16 MiB matches the previous fixed refusal.

productFeedback.comparisonPageLimit.remediation: Narrow the comparison page or raise productFeedback.comparisonPageLimit in config/limits/productFeedback.yaml.
productFeedback.comparisonPageLimit.rationale: Page size for one stored comparison read during materialization. 100 matches the previous fixed page.

technicalCorrection.maxIssueJudgments.remediation: Return fewer issue judgments, or lower technicalCorrection.maxIssueJudgments in config/limits/technicalCorrection.yaml.
technicalCorrection.maxIssueJudgments.rationale: Canonical technical-correction issue-judgment ceiling. 256 matches the previous host-fill cap. Override may only lower it.

technicalCorrection.maxJudgmentFactIds.remediation: Link fewer fact or obligation ids on one judgment, or lower technicalCorrection.maxJudgmentFactIds in config/limits/technicalCorrection.yaml.
technicalCorrection.maxJudgmentFactIds.rationale: Identifiers one technical-correction judgment may name. 32 matches the previous host-fill cap. Override may only lower it.

technicalCorrection.identifierMaxChars.remediation: Shorten the obligation or judgment id, or lower technicalCorrection.identifierMaxChars in config/limits/technicalCorrection.yaml.
technicalCorrection.identifierMaxChars.rationale: Host-issued obligation and judgment identifiers are short labels. 63 is the accepted OBL grammar maximum (OBL- plus 59 identifier characters). Override may only lower it.

technicalCorrection.fieldMaxChars.remediation: Shorten the statement or location, cite fewer or shorter evidence locators on one rejection, or lower technicalCorrection.fieldMaxChars in config/limits/technicalCorrection.yaml.
technicalCorrection.fieldMaxChars.rationale: Replacement statement and judgment location ceiling, and the ceiling of the host's per-rejection demotion evidence limitation (#1254). 4096 matches the previous host-fill cap and the fact-inventory limitation entry bound. Override may only lower it.

technicalCorrection.proseMaxChars.remediation: Shorten the uncertainty or reason, or lower technicalCorrection.proseMaxChars in config/limits/technicalCorrection.yaml.
technicalCorrection.proseMaxChars.rationale: Uncertainty and rejection-reason ceiling. 2048 matches the previous host-fill cap. Override may only lower it.

technicalCorrection.maxDemotionEvidenceL.remediation: Cite fewer distinct admitted source locators across the rejections of one dimension, or lower technicalCorrection.maxDemotionEvidenceLocators in config/limits/technicalCorrection.yaml.
technicalCorrection.maxDemotionEvidenceL.rationale: Admitted source locators the evidenceLocators of one rejection, and their union over one demoted dimension, may name (#1254). The host makes that union the demoted dimension's sourceLocators, and the fact-inventory validator admits at most 64 locators per dimension, so 64 is the largest value that dimension can carry. Override may only lower it.

technicalCorrection.coverageReasonMaxCha.remediation: Keep each coverage reason to the sentence that names the page claim and the admitted source it was compared with, or raise technicalCorrection.coverageReasonMaxChars in config/limits/technicalCorrection.yaml up to 2048, the prose ceiling the rest of the judgment uses. On a review-documentation judgment an over-length reason is truncated and recorded as a host limitation rather than refused, so this bound shapes the answer the model plans instead of rejecting it.
technicalCorrection.coverageReasonMaxCha.rationale: Characters one coverage entry reason may hold (#645). Coverage carried no length bound at all, so the judgment contract permitted answers no output budget could finish - the 2026-09-25 probe run answered 8 coverage entries and was cut at the 32,768-token output limit after 78,394 retained characters, about 9,800 characters per entry. 512 keeps eight entries inside 4,096 characters, about three percent of the whole-answer budget, which leaves the judgments and accounting the rest. Override may only lower it below the prose ceiling of 2048.

technicalCorrection.coverageEvidenceMaxE.remediation: Cite the few admitted source locators that actually establish the page claims for one coverage entry, or raise technicalCorrection.coverageEvidenceMaxEntries in config/limits/technicalCorrection.yaml up to 64, the locator ceiling one fact-inventory dimension carries. On a review-documentation judgment the entries past this bound are dropped and recorded as a host limitation rather than refused.
technicalCorrection.coverageEvidenceMaxE.rationale: Evidence locators one coverage entry may name (#645). The coverage validator required distinct non-empty strings and bounded neither their count nor their length, which is half of why the 2026-09-25 probe answer ran to 78,394 characters over 8 entries. 8 locators is the widest citation a single page needs when the same sources are already itemised in the obligation ledger, and 64 is the ceiling a fact-inventory dimension may carry, so the override range cannot exceed what the rest of the record admits.

technicalCorrection.coverageEvidenceEntr.remediation: Cite one admitted source locator per coverage evidence entry, in path or path-and-line form, or raise technicalCorrection.coverageEvidenceEntryMaxChars in config/limits/technicalCorrection.yaml up to 4096, the ceiling a judgment location already uses. On a review-documentation judgment an over-length entry is truncated and recorded as a host limitation rather than refused.
technicalCorrection.coverageEvidenceEntr.rationale: Characters one coverage evidence entry may hold (#645). An evidence entry is a repository locator, and the locator grammar the evidence validators parse admits a path of at most 512 characters plus a line range or a label of at most 256, so 256 characters holds every locator form the host can resolve and nothing else. 4096 is the judgment location ceiling, which is the most any single evidence field elsewhere in the same answer may hold.

technicalCorrection.answerCharsPerOutput.remediation: This is the conversion the host uses to state a whole-answer character budget to the model, not an enforced ceiling on any field. Lower it to state a smaller budget when answers keep arriving cut; raising it above the measured compact-JSON range would state a budget the output limit cannot carry.
technicalCorrection.answerCharsPerOutput.rationale: Characters of compact JSON the host counts against one output token when it states the whole-answer budget in the judgment contracts (#645). The four retrievable pilot records of 2026-09-23 were cut after 63,545 to 82,789 characters against a 32,768-token budget, which is 1.9 to 2.5 characters per token; the 2026-09-25 probe retained only 78,394 characters for 65,536 output tokens, 1.2, because output the harness does not retain never reaches the answer. 2 is the low end of the measured compact-JSON range, so the stated budget understates rather than overstates what one output budget plus its continuations can finish.

technicalCorrection.proposalMaxBytes.remediation: Narrow the review scope, for example to one directory or a named set of pages, then run it again. The host writes one coverage entry for every target page and one accounting row for every source obligation, so a rerun of the same scope stops at the same bound.
technicalCorrection.proposalMaxBytes.rationale: Technical-capacity constraint on the sealed technical-correction record, set as a provisional implementation choice rather than from a measured provider or platform limit. Canonical JSON UTF-8 bytes of one technical-correction proposal, which every record reader re-validates, so it is sealed rather than overridable. The proposal grows with the scope, by a host-filled coverage entry per target page and an accounting row per source obligation. Measured with the recorded 18-obligation ledger, the all-host floor proposal is 108,837 bytes over 256 real target pages and 471,270 bytes over the 1,313-page probe 7 documentation set, after that set's reply was refused at this bound; the floor's note names the refused reply's rejection code, so its size moves by a few bytes with that code. Run 549a2968 (2026-10-05) stopped at this bound over 1,410 whole-repository pages, whose host-filled coverage alone is 466,289 bytes. Each host-filled coverage entry costs its path's UTF-8 bytes plus 255 bytes, so reviewScope.maxTargets pages pass the run-start check while their paths average at most 768 UTF-8 bytes. The widest ASCII focused scope, reviewScope.maxTargets pages of reviewScope.pathMaxChars characters, carries 196,354 bytes and passes with the rest left for obligation accounting; reviewScope.pathMaxChars counts UTF-16 characters, so the same scope of two-byte characters (324,098 bytes) or three-byte characters (451,842 bytes) is refused. A whole-documentation-set review has no reviewScope and is refused before its first model call when its host-filled coverage alone exceeds this bound.
technicalCorrection.proposalMaxBytes.docSummary: Canonical JSON of one technical-correction proposal. A review whose host-filled coverage alone exceeds it is refused before the first model call; narrow the scope.

technicalCorrection.evidenceMaxBytes.remediation: Narrow the review scope, for example to one directory or a named set of pages, then run it again. The evidence carries the whole proposal plus one source check per cited source, so a rerun of the same scope stops at the same bound.
technicalCorrection.evidenceMaxBytes.rationale: Technical-capacity constraint on the sealed technical-correction record, set as a provisional implementation choice rather than from a measured provider or platform limit. Canonical JSON UTF-8 bytes of the complete technical-correction evidence, which holds the proposal, its digests, and the admitted source checks. Every record reader re-validates it, so it is sealed. Twice technicalCorrection.proposalMaxBytes, so a proposal at its own bound leaves the same number of bytes again for source checks.
technicalCorrection.evidenceMaxBytes.docSummary: Canonical JSON of the complete technical-correction evidence, which carries the proposal and its source checks.

technicalCorrection.derivedResultMaxByte.remediation: Narrow the review scope, for example to one directory or a named set of pages, or link fewer facts to each issue judgment, then run it again. The host writes each finding from the facts its judgment links, so a rerun of the same scope and judgments stops at the same bound.
technicalCorrection.derivedResultMaxByte.rationale: Technical-capacity constraint on the sealed technical-correction record, set as a provisional implementation choice rather than from a measured provider or platform limit. Canonical JSON UTF-8 bytes of the verification result the host derives from a proposal, which holds coverage, the fact inventory, and one finding per issue judgment, each restating the facts it links. Every record reader re-derives it, so it is sealed. Three times technicalCorrection.proposalMaxBytes; the derived result repeats fact text into findings, which the proposal does not.
technicalCorrection.derivedResultMaxByte.docSummary: Canonical JSON of the verification result the host derives from a technical-correction proposal.

sourceObligation.maxObligations.remediation: Split the documentation work into focused runs with fewer source obligations while retaining every established claim and its evidence.
sourceObligation.maxObligations.rationale: Provisional structural capacity inherited from the source-obligation decoder's MAX_OBLIGATIONS value, not a measured model or provider ceiling. One ledger and its durable V1/V2 readback admit at most 256 obligations; the downstream technical fact inventory independently admits at most 256 facts. This value is sealed because changing it on a later host could invalidate an already recorded ledger. A one-page review with 18 recorded obligations fits this cap and the complete host-filled proposal under the combined defaults.

sourceObligation.maxPerDimension.remediation: Split the documentation work into focused runs with fewer obligations in each technical dimension while retaining every established claim and its evidence.
sourceObligation.maxPerDimension.rationale: Provisional structural capacity inherited from the source-obligation decoder's MAX_PER_DIMENSION value, not a measured model or provider ceiling. Durable V1/V2 ledger readback checks the same cap; the downstream technical fact inventory independently admits at most 128 facts per dimension. This value is sealed so a later host cannot reject an already recorded ledger merely because of an override. The representative one-page review has fewer than 128 obligations in every dimension.

sourceObligation.maxLocators.remediation: Split the documentation work into focused runs if the ledger must cite more distinct admitted sources or source spans; keep every locator needed to establish each claim.
sourceObligation.maxLocators.rationale: Provisional structural capacity inherited from the source-obligation decoder's MAX_LOCATORS value, not a measured model or provider ceiling. It bounds source identities and each dimension or obligation locator array in durable V1/V2 ledgers. The downstream technical fact inventory has its own independent 64-locator cap. This value is sealed because durable ledger readback uses the same decoder and must remain valid after a host restart. The representative one-page review cites fewer than 64 locators per array.

benchmarkMining.apiPageSize.remediation: Keep benchmarkMining.apiPageSize in config/limits/benchmarkMining.yaml at or below the GitHub REST page maximum of 100.
benchmarkMining.apiPageSize.rationale: Items per page the candidate miner requests from GitHub search, pull request lists, merge commit files, and timelines. 100 is the GitHub REST maximum, so each page costs the fewest requests against the hourly budget; the same precedent as localWorkflows.canaryApiPageSize for GitLab.

benchmarkMining.queryPagesMax.remediation: The run report counts every listing that stopped at this bound under query-pages-exhausted; nothing past it was examined and its cursor stays in progress.json. Raise benchmarkMining.queryPagesMax in config/limits/benchmarkMining.yaml if seeds legitimately need deeper listings. DOCSFAB_BENCHMARK_MINING_QUERY_PAGES_MAX may only lower it.
benchmarkMining.queryPagesMax.rationale: Most pages the miner reads from one listing (one seed search, one repository's closed pull requests, one merge commit's files, or one timeline). At benchmarkMining.apiPageSize it reaches 1000 items, which is the GitHub search result cap, so a deeper search page could never answer. In the 2026-10-01 smoke run (target 10, 100 seeded repositories) no listing reached the bound. A listing that reaches the bound is counted, never read as complete; a files listing cut by it is excluded as changed-files-incomplete. The host override may only lower it.

benchmarkMining.triggersPerRepositoryMax.remediation: The run report counts every repository that stopped at this bound under repository-trigger-cap-reached; its remaining pull requests were not examined. Raise benchmarkMining.triggersPerRepositoryMax in config/limits/benchmarkMining.yaml for a deeper scan of fewer repositories. DOCSFAB_BENCHMARK_MINING_TRIGGERS_PER_REPOSITORY_MAX may only lower it.
benchmarkMining.triggersPerRepositoryMax.rationale: Most merged-or-closed pull requests the miner examines in one repository, so one busy repository cannot fill the whole 150-candidate corpus and the corpus spreads across repositories and platforms. At the 20-30 percent yield the plan estimates, 40 triggers give about 8-12 candidates from one repository, under a tenth of the 150 target. In the 2026-10-01 smoke run one repository reached it with all 40 triggers excluded (GitHub reported no recognised license at their base commits), and the bound stopped it from consuming the run. The host override may only lower it.

benchmarkMining.gapReportScanCap.remediation: The run report counts every repository that stopped at this bound under gapReportScanCapReached; its remaining closed issues were not examined. Raise benchmarkMining.gapReportScanCap in config/limits/benchmarkMining.yaml for a deeper issue scan of fewer repositories. DOCSFAB_BENCHMARK_MINING_GAP_REPORT_SCAN_CAP may only lower it.
benchmarkMining.gapReportScanCap.rationale: Most closed issues the miner examines in detail for gap reports in one repository, past the listing filters (closed as completed with a docs-scope label), counted apart from benchmarkMining.triggersPerRepositoryMax so the pull request scan and the issue scan each keep their own share. An issue examined in detail costs its timeline and, when it links one merged pull request, that pull request's detail, files, license and tree, about 6 requests, so 40 issues cost at most about 240 requests, under a twentieth of benchmarkMining.githubRequestsPerRunMax; listing-only issues cost only their share of a listing page. Measured 2026-10-02 in three 20-candidate smoke runs (cutoff 2026-07-01) - 7 repositories scanned their issues, 22 closed issues were listed, 1 was examined in detail (at most 1 in any repository), and the issue scan sent 9 of 696 GitHub requests; no gap-report candidate was found, so the cost per gap-report candidate is still unmeasured. The value stays provisional, the same as the pull request bound, until the 150-candidate run measures it. The host override may only lower it.

benchmarkMining.githubRequestsPerRunMax.remediation: The run stopped before its next GitHub request and kept progress.json; rerun the same command with --resume <run-dir> to continue with a fresh budget. Raise benchmarkMining.githubRequestsPerRunMax in config/limits/benchmarkMining.yaml only if the token's hourly allowance is larger. DOCSFAB_BENCHMARK_MINING_GITHUB_REQUESTS_PER_RUN_MAX may only lower it.
benchmarkMining.githubRequestsPerRunMax.rationale: GitHub requests one miner invocation sends, counting redirects and retries. 5000 is the authenticated GitHub REST core allowance per hour, so one invocation cannot outrun it. The plan estimate is 4-6 requests per examined trigger and 500-750 triggers for 150 candidates, about 2000-4500 requests, so a full corpus needs about one invocation and --resume covers the rest. Measured 2026-10-01 smoke run - 191 requests for 10 candidates (19.1 per candidate, about 3.1 per trigger examined in detail), which projects about 2900 requests for 150. The host override may only lower it.

benchmarkMining.rateLimitWaitMaxMs.remediation: GitHub asked the miner to wait longer than this bound after a secondary rate limit. The run stopped with progress.json kept; wait for the time GitHub named, then rerun with --resume <run-dir>. DOCSFAB_BENCHMARK_MINING_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT_MAX_MS may only lower it, which also shortens the wait after a secondary limit that names no retry-after.
benchmarkMining.rateLimitWaitMaxMs.rationale: Longest retry-after wait the miner honors in place after a GitHub secondary rate limit before it stops and leaves the rest to --resume, and the wait it uses when a 403 or 429 names a secondary rate limit in its message without retry-after. GitHub documents waiting at least one minute when no retry-after is sent, and its search allowance resets every minute, so 60 s covers the documented secondary waits without holding a run idle for longer; a secondary limit that outlasts benchmarkMining.requestRetriesMax waits refuses with progress kept and never excludes the repository. A primary limit (x-ratelimit-remaining 0) never waits; it stops and names the reset time. The host override may only lower it.

benchmarkMining.dogbenchPayloadMaxBytes.remediation: The pinned DoGBench item list is larger than this bound, so no repository was mined. Check that the miner fetched the DoGBench revision its exclusion data pins, then raise benchmarkMining.dogbenchPayloadMaxBytes in config/limits/benchmarkMining.yaml. DOCSFAB_BENCHMARK_MINING_DOGBENCH_PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES may only lower it.
benchmarkMining.dogbenchPayloadMaxBytes.rationale: Largest DoGBench items.jsonl body the miner reads to build its in-memory exclusion set. The pinned revision measured 676813 bytes on 2026-10-01 (HEAD content-length), so 4 MiB leaves about six times headroom for a pinned-revision bump while keeping an unexpected body from exhausting memory before parsing. The host override may only lower it.

benchmarkMining.githubResponseMaxBytes.remediation: One GitHub response was larger than this bound and the run stopped with progress.json kept. The usual cause is a very large recursive tree; raise benchmarkMining.githubResponseMaxBytes in config/limits/benchmarkMining.yaml and rerun with --resume <run-dir>. DOCSFAB_BENCHMARK_MINING_GITHUB_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES may only lower it.
benchmarkMining.githubResponseMaxBytes.rationale: Largest single GitHub response body the miner reads. GitHub caps a recursive tree response at 100000 entries and 7 MB and marks it truncated past that, and every other response the miner reads is one page of at most benchmarkMining.apiPageSize items, so 16 MiB holds the largest legitimate answer with room for JSON overhead. The host override may only lower it.

benchmarkMining.githubRequestTimeoutMs.remediation: GitHub did not answer within this bound after every retry; the run stopped with progress.json kept. Check connectivity to api.github.com, then rerun with --resume <run-dir>. DOCSFAB_BENCHMARK_MINING_GITHUB_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS may only lower it.
benchmarkMining.githubRequestTimeoutMs.rationale: Wall-clock bound on one GitHub request, retried up to benchmarkMining.requestRetriesMax times. Provisional; the 2026-10-01 smoke run sent 191 GitHub requests in 102 s of wall time, about 0.5 s each including processing. 30 s leaves room for a large recursive tree. The host override may only lower it.

benchmarkMining.huggingFaceRequestTimeou.remediation: Hugging Face did not answer within this bound, so no exclusion list was loaded and nothing was mined. Check connectivity to huggingface.co and rerun. DOCSFAB_BENCHMARK_MINING_HUGGING_FACE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS may only lower it.
benchmarkMining.huggingFaceRequestTimeou.rationale: Wall-clock bound on the one DoGBench item-list fetch, redirects included. Provisional; the 676813-byte file downloaded in about a second on 2026-10-01. The host override may only lower it.

benchmarkMining.requestRetriesMax.remediation: A GitHub request kept failing with a server error, a timeout, or a secondary rate limit after this many retries; the run stopped with progress.json kept. Rerun with --resume <run-dir> once GitHub answers. DOCSFAB_BENCHMARK_MINING_REQUEST_RETRIES_MAX may only lower it.
benchmarkMining.requestRetriesMax.rationale: Retries after a GitHub 5xx, a network failure or timeout, or a secondary rate limit, each spaced by benchmarkMining.retryBackoffMs times the attempt number or by GitHub's retry-after. Provisional; three retries ride out a transient error without hiding a persistent one. A 404, a 403 whose message names no rate limit, and a primary rate limit are never retried. The host override may only lower it.

benchmarkMining.retryBackoffMs.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_BENCHMARK_MINING_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS for faster retries, or raise benchmarkMining.retryBackoffMs in config/limits/benchmarkMining.yaml if GitHub needs longer to recover.
benchmarkMining.retryBackoffMs.rationale: Base spacing between retries of one GitHub request when GitHub sends no retry-after; attempt n waits n times this value, so three retries wait 12 s in total. Provisional and unmeasured. The host override may only lower it.

benchmarkMining.redirectsMax.remediation: An upstream request redirected more times than this bound and the run stopped. Check the requested URL; raise benchmarkMining.redirectsMax in config/limits/benchmarkMining.yaml only for a known redirect chain. DOCSFAB_BENCHMARK_MINING_REDIRECTS_MAX may only lower it.
benchmarkMining.redirectsMax.rationale: Redirects the miner follows for one request. The pinned DoGBench item list answered with one same-origin redirect on 2026-10-01, and GitHub answers a renamed repository with one; 3 leaves room without following a loop. The Authorization header is dropped on any redirect away from https://api.github.com. The host override may only lower it.

factInventory.maxLimitations.remediation: Raise factInventory.maxLimitations in config/limits/factInventory.yaml (up to 256), or narrow the run to fewer source obligations, for example by splitting the documentation page. Retaining obligations the source does not establish is not a remedy.
factInventory.maxLimitations.rationale: Limitations one technical fact inventory may hold, in the source-obligation ledger, a model-authored verification result, and the host-built judgment inventory, where each rejected obligation adds one (#1254). 64 is the previous hand-declared value in both decoders. An override may raise it to 256, the fact-inventory fact ceiling, so each obligation's limitation can fit.

factInventory.maxHostLimitations.remediation: This bound is reached only when every technical dimension degraded at once, so read the limitations the inventory already carries; each one names the dimension that lost its source locators. Raising it above the number of technical dimensions cannot help, because the host authors at most one note per dimension.
factInventory.maxHostLimitations.rationale: Host-authored limitations one source-obligation ledger may hold above the model's own limitations bound, one per technical dimension whose cited source locators the host could not read (#1401). Without headroom a model that had already filled factInventory.maxLimitations would make the host's own degradation note fail the step it was added to keep alive. 6 is the number of technical fact dimensions, which is the most notes the host can author.

factInventory.maxDegradedLocatorChars.remediation: Locators past this budget are counted in the same note instead of quoted, so the note still says how many were removed. Lower it to quote less; it cannot be raised, because the quoted list must fit inside the dimension reason bound with the fixed host sentence around it.
factInventory.maxDegradedLocatorChars.rationale: Characters of removed source-locator text one host degradation note quotes before it summarises the rest as a count (#1401). The note is both a dimension reason and a limitations entry, each bounded text, so the quoted list needs a bound of its own that leaves room for the fixed host sentence around it. 1024 is half the dimension reason bound, which fits the longest sentence the host builds around it.

factInventory.minDimensionReasonChars.remediation: Explain in the dimension reason why the dimension has the status it has, in at least this many characters, or lower factInventory.minDimensionReasonChars in config/limits/factInventory.yaml. A one-word reason cannot be acted on by the reviewer who reads it.
factInventory.minDimensionReasonChars.rationale: Characters a source-obligation dimension reason must hold before it counts as an answer (#1401). This is a minimum, not a capacity allowance, so raising it refuses more replies rather than admitting more text. 12 is the previous hand-declared value at this position, kept so no existing reply changes meaning; the ceiling of 256 is the smallest value factInventory.maxDimensionReasonChars may be overridden to, so the pair can never invert.

factInventory.maxDimensionReasonChars.remediation: Shorten the dimension reason, or raise factInventory.maxDimensionReasonChars up to 4096, which is the bounded-text ceiling the rest of the ledger uses. A reason longer than the statement it explains is usually a sign the obligation belongs in more than one dimension.
factInventory.maxDimensionReasonChars.rationale: Characters one source-obligation dimension reason may hold, model-authored or host-authored (#1401). 2048 is the previous hand-declared value at this position, kept so no existing reply changes meaning. It also bounds the host degradation note, which is a dimension reason, so factInventory.maxDegradedLocatorChars must stay below it with room for the fixed host sentence.

sourceAcquisitionProof.installedInvocati.remediation: Shorten the installed run, or raise sourceAcquisitionProof.installedInvocationTimeoutMs in config/limits/sourceAcquisitionProof.yaml. The cell is recorded with this refusal code and is never counted as passed.
sourceAcquisitionProof.installedInvocati.rationale: Wall-clock ceiling for one installed docsfab run or do invocation driven by scripts/source-acquisition-proof.mjs. A qualifying installed cell is a full model-backed workflow, so the former fixed 30 s refused every real run; the value is the shared live-model job ceiling (ci.liveModel.jobTimeoutMs) because one cell cannot usefully outlive the job that hosts installed collection. A host override may only lower it.

sourceAcquisitionProof.installedOutputMa.remediation: Reduce the installed invocation's output, or raise sourceAcquisitionProof.installedOutputMaxBytes in config/limits/sourceAcquisitionProof.yaml. The cell is recorded with this refusal code and is never counted as passed.
sourceAcquisitionProof.installedOutputMa.rationale: Spawn buffer for the stdout or stderr of one installed invocation driven by scripts/source-acquisition-proof.mjs. Under --json the collector reads one run-result or operator-error envelope line; 16 MiB matches the previous fixed maxBuffer. A host override may only lower it.

localWorkflows.idleStallMs.remediation: Read the stream.log saved in the case directory to find the last activity. If the case was still legitimately working without visible progress, raise localWorkflows.idleStallMs in config/limits/localWorkflows.yaml; DOCSFAB_LOCAL_WORKFLOWS_IDLE_STALL_MS and --idle-stall-ms may only lower it.
localWorkflows.idleStallMs.rationale: Idle window after which benchmarks/local-workflows/run.mjs declares a case stalled. It is not a wall-clock budget; a case keeps running while its process produces new terminal output or file activity under its case directory, and a live-agent heartbeat redraw that only advances its elapsed counter is not progress. The value is one step attempt at its effective cap, sealed.compositionLimits.timeoutMs (30 min), which clamps compositionExecution.timeoutMs; that is the longest a step, and so a CLI case that prints only at step boundaries, can legitimately stay silent. Measured basis, one sample (gpt-5.4 live runs, 2026-09-22) - longest step 83.5 s (evaluate-document-quality), a complete live workflow about 4 min, live startup a few seconds. The former fixed 60 s PTY and 120 s per-case timeouts voided every live case (issues 1118 and 1119). Revisit once report.json per-case durations accumulate. The host override and --idle-stall-ms may only lower it.

localWorkflows.auxCommandTimeoutMs.remediation: Check that git and docsfab respond on this host (a stuck credential helper or file lock is the usual cause), then rerun. DOCSFAB_LOCAL_WORKFLOWS_AUX_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS may only lower this bound.
localWorkflows.auxCommandTimeoutMs.rationale: Provisional, unmeasured; refuses loudly. Wall-clock bound for each auxiliary lookup benchmarks/local-workflows/run.mjs makes outside a case (command -v docsfab, docsfab --version, and repository status, revision, or patch apply on the fixture repository). The value is the 30 s literal the runner used before issue 1118; the lookups are local and fixture-sized, but no latency has been measured. A lookup that exceeds it refuses with this code instead of being read as an empty result. Replace this value with a measured one. The host override may only lower it.

localWorkflows.exitDrainMs.remediation: Find and stop the process still holding the case output or still in a case process group, then rerun; the case stream.log shows its last output. DOCSFAB_LOCAL_WORKFLOWS_EXIT_DRAIN_MS may only lower this bound.
localWorkflows.exitDrainMs.rationale: Provisional, unmeasured; refuses loudly. After a case process exits or is stopped, benchmarks/local-workflows/run.mjs kills its process groups with SIGKILL and waits this long for them to become empty and for the output pipes to close. The 5 s value is not measured. It matters only for a descendant that left the case process group (for example with setsid) and still holds the output; that case is reported as local-e2e-containment-failed and never passes, so the value decides only how soon the failure is reported. The host override may only lower it.

localWorkflows.streamLineMaxChars.remediation: Nothing is dropped from stream.log by this bound. If a case legitimately draws a longer unfinished line or escape sequence that should still count toward progress or prompt recognition, raise localWorkflows.streamLineMaxChars in config/limits/localWorkflows.yaml.
localWorkflows.streamLineMaxChars.rationale: Provisional, unmeasured. The longest unfinished terminal line, unfinished heartbeat frame, or unterminated escape sequence benchmarks/local-workflows/run.mjs holds while it judges progress and recognizes prompts and driver notes as output arrives; past it the held text is judged as it is and an open escape sequence is treated as ended. It bounds that parser state and its per-chunk work (a review probe spent 6.2 s and 219 MB rescanning one unbounded 16 MB line). Product terminal lines are rendered at terminal width, far below 1 MiB. The host override may only lower it.

localWorkflows.streamBufferMaxChars.remediation: The case stream.log marks where its middle was not kept, and report.json records how many characters (streamTruncated). Raise localWorkflows.streamBufferMaxChars in config/limits/localWorkflows.yaml if cases need their whole output kept.
localWorkflows.streamBufferMaxChars.rationale: Provisional; truncates loudly. Applies to each case, not to the run as a whole. The scope vocabulary has no per-case value, so, like other per-step bounds, it is filed per-run. The raw output of one case that benchmarks/local-workflows/run.mjs keeps in memory until the case ends, when it redacts the whole text once and writes stream.log. Past the bound it keeps the first and the most recent halves and marks the dropped middle with this code, so memory stays bounded and the start and end of a stall survive. A run holds up to this much for every case running at once (at most the eight matrix cases), and writes one stream at a time. Measured 2026-09-23 on macOS with Node 25. Redacting and writing one full stream peaked at about 0.3 GB runner RSS for prose, and at 0.76 GB for a stream of blank lines, which the line-by-line pattern stage makes the worst case. The independent review measured 1.6 to 1.8 GB for eight concurrent 20 MiB cases. It matches sourceAcquisitionProof.installedOutputMaxBytes, the existing bound on one installed docsfab run output. The host override may only lower it.

localWorkflows.secretValueMinChars.remediation: A known credential shorter than this is redacted only by pattern, and so is a piece of one shorter than this. Lower DOCSFAB_LOCAL_WORKFLOWS_SECRET_VALUE_MIN_CHARS to redact shorter values and pieces by value too, at the cost of redacting matching ordinary text.
localWorkflows.secretValueMinChars.rationale: Provisional, unmeasured. Shortest known credential value (from the docsfab configuration root or a credential-named environment variable) that benchmarks/local-workflows/run.mjs redacts by value in case streams and reports, and the fragment length it matches. Every run of this many characters of a known value, or of one of its encoded forms, is redacted wherever it appears, so a value cut at the dropped middle or the end of output, soft-wrapped by the chat renderer, or interleaved with other output such as a table column, loses every piece at least this long. Matching shorter values or fragments across whitespace would redact ordinary words; such values are left to pattern redaction and counted in report.json. The host override may only lower it.

localWorkflows.secretValuesMaxChars.remediation: The run refuses before any case starts, because it redacts every known credential value and never skips one. Remove values the docsfab children do not need from the credential file or from credential-named environment variables, or raise localWorkflows.secretValuesMaxChars in config/limits/localWorkflows.yaml.
localWorkflows.secretValuesMaxChars.rationale: Technical capacity. Total characters of the known credential values that benchmarks/local-workflows/run.mjs loads (the credential file the docsfab children read, plus credential-named environment variables) and builds one matcher over, at localWorkflows.secretValueMinChars. The matcher holds every fragment of every encoded form of each value, so its build time and memory grow linearly with this total. Measured 2026-09-23 on macOS with Node 25. 256 characters take 8 ms and 8 MB. 4,096 take 95 ms and 74 MB. 16,384 take 0.48 s and 248 MB. 65,536 take 1.7 s and 736 MB. A supported credential file fits with room to spare. Two or three API tokens total well under 1,000 characters. An RSA-4096 private key in PEM is about 3,300 characters, and a service-account JSON is about 2,400. Past the bound the run refuses with this code, the observed total, and the source; it never loads some values and skips others. The host override may only lower it.

localWorkflows.reportExcerptMaxChars.remediation: The full text is in the case stream.log or run record named in the report. Raise localWorkflows.reportExcerptMaxChars in config/limits/localWorkflows.yaml if reports need longer excerpts.
localWorkflows.reportExcerptMaxChars.rationale: Provisional, unmeasured; shortens loudly. Longest free-text excerpt (error detail, failed step, step detail, artifact detail) that benchmarks/local-workflows/run.mjs puts in REPORT.md, report.json, or JUnit, after redaction. Reports carry structured fields and short excerpts; the full text stays in the case stream.log or run record, and a shortened excerpt ends with this code and the number of characters left out. Messages the runner writes itself fit well inside it. The host override may only lower it.

localWorkflows.artifactTranscriptMaxChar.remediation: The review artifact was not inspected. Read the case stream.log and run record; if a review case legitimately prints more, raise localWorkflows.artifactTranscriptMaxChars in config/limits/localWorkflows.yaml.
localWorkflows.artifactTranscriptMaxChar.rationale: Provisional, unmeasured; refuses loudly. The unredacted terminal text of a review case that benchmarks/local-workflows/run.mjs keeps in memory, never on disk, for the review artifact check (redacted text could fail a correct review). Past the bound the check refuses with this code instead of grading partial text; the saved stream.log is unaffected. It matches sourceAcquisitionProof.installedOutputMaxBytes, the existing bound on one installed docsfab run output. The host override may only lower it.

localWorkflows.canaryRepeats.remediation: Rounds that did not start are listed in the canary summary.json and CANARY.md with their reason code. Lower the repeats with DOCSFAB_LOCAL_WORKFLOWS_CANARY_REPEATS or --repeats, or raise localWorkflows.canaryRepeats in config/limits/localWorkflows.yaml together with ci.liveModel.jobTimeoutMs in config/limits/ci.yaml.
localWorkflows.canaryRepeats.rationale: Rounds of the eight-case matrix that benchmarks/local-workflows/canary.mjs runs per canary (issue 1183), so each case reports a rate instead of one verdict (issue 1120). Three is the smallest count that separates the !1023 update-cli regression (0/3) from a flake at localWorkflows.canaryAlertMaxPValue. Rounds run one after another; a round starts only when the slowest round so far still fits before the job deadline, and a round that does not start is reported with its reason, never dropped. A canary with fewer complete rounds still compares on the trials it measured. The host override and --repeats may only lower it.

localWorkflows.canaryJobReserveMs.remediation: Read CANARY.md for the rounds that did not start, each round's duration, and the job deadline. Lower localWorkflows.canaryRepeats, or raise ci.liveModel.jobTimeoutMs in config/limits/ci.yaml. The canary refuses a reserve that is not below ci.liveModel.jobTimeoutMs.
localWorkflows.canaryJobReserveMs.rationale: Provisional, unmeasured. Time the runtime:workflow-canary job keeps after its matrix rounds to write summary.json and upload artifacts. The matrix deadline is CI_JOB_STARTED_AT plus ci.liveModel.jobTimeoutMs minus this reserve, so setup time (npm ci, pins, packing, install, configuration) is measured rather than guessed, and each round's per-case ceiling is the time left before that deadline. The comparison runs in the separate runtime:workflow-canary:trend job and needs none of this reserve. Writing a summary takes milliseconds; the rest is artifact upload headroom.

localWorkflows.canaryBaselineRuns.remediation: TREND.md shows each case's baseline runs and admission decision. Raise localWorkflows.canaryBaselineRuns in config/limits/localWorkflows.yaml for a longer memory, or lower it so a changed rate becomes the baseline sooner after a clean night.
localWorkflows.canaryBaselineRuns.rationale: Rolling window, per case, of earlier admitted canary runs that the trend comparison pools as that case's baseline (issue 1183). Seven nightly runs are one week, or 21 trials per case at localWorkflows.canaryRepeats. The windows are carried forward in each trend.json, so artifact expiry does not shorten them. A case's data from a run is admitted only when that case shows no change at localWorkflows.canaryBaselineAdmitMaxPValue; another case's alert never keeps it out. The oldest admitted run leaves a case's window when a new one joins.

localWorkflows.canaryPendingRuns.remediation: TREND.md names each held-out run and each run folded into the baseline without confirmation. Raise localWorkflows.canaryPendingRuns in config/limits/localWorkflows.yaml to pool a longer run of suspect nights before accepting them.
localWorkflows.canaryPendingRuns.rationale: Most held-out runs carried per case. A case's data is held out when it dips at localWorkflows.canaryBaselineAdmitMaxPValue (unconfirmed) or is part of a confirmed or silenced change (confirmed). Whenever the case has unconfirmed held data, the next night is also tested pooled with it, so 0/3 then 1/3 against a 17/21 baseline alerts on the second night (1/6, p 0.002) instead of folding the 0/3 night in, and 0/3 nightly against 14/21 alerts every second night. Confirmed data is never pooled or admitted. Seven matches localWorkflows.canaryBaselineRuns. Past the bound the oldest held-out data is folded into the baseline (unconfirmed) or discarded (confirmed), and TREND.md counts both per case; nothing is dropped silently.

localWorkflows.canaryAlertMaxPValue.remediation: TREND.md lists every compared case with its p-value. Lower localWorkflows.canaryAlertMaxPValue in config/limits/localWorkflows.yaml if known flaky cases alert, or raise it if a real regression was missed.
localWorkflows.canaryAlertMaxPValue.rationale: Provisional. Largest one-sided binomial p-value at which the canary reports a drop in a case or step pass rate, or a rise in a failure code rate, against the pooled baseline with add-one smoothing. At 3 repeats and a 21-trial baseline, a case that always passed alerts at 0/3 or 1/3, a case that passed two thirds of the time does not alert at 0/3 alone (p 0.04) but does when two held-out nights pool to 0/6, and the first comparison against one 3/3 baseline still flags 0/3 (p 0.008). Each case, step, and code is tested separately, so the false-alarm rate per canary is higher than this value; tune it from recorded TREND.md results.

localWorkflows.canaryBaselineAdmitMaxPVa.remediation: TREND.md says whether each run was admitted, held out, or folded in. Raise this threshold to hold out more runs, or lower it toward localWorkflows.canaryAlertMaxPValue if too many ordinary nights are held out. The canary refuses a value below the alert threshold.
localWorkflows.canaryBaselineAdmitMaxPVa.rationale: Provisional; the statistics are being redesigned in issue 1223. 0.25 was chosen over 0.1 on the !1086 trade-off (decision note 71024886 under the owner's delegation). A case's data joins its baseline when its own night shows no pass-rate or step drop and no code rise at this one-sided p-value against its baseline, and, when it has held data, no alert pooled with that data. Silences do not apply here. A night that is not significant at this threshold is admitted, so a change whose single nights stay above it lowers the baseline without an alert, including a later, milder night of a regression that already alerted or is silenced. Measured at 0.25 with 3 repeats and a 21-trial baseline. 0/3 is admitted on a baseline at or below about 7/21, so a case at 7/21 that drops to 0/3 falls to 0/21; a case at 14/21 that is held on its first 0/3 night, alerts on its second, and then runs at 1/3 admits each 1/3 night (p 0.28) and drifts to 8/21 with no further alert; among 200 simulated regressions from 0.95 to 0.5 that alerted, 20 of 179 never alerted again within 10 nights. An always-passing case is held out at 2/3 (p 0.13), so 21/21 then 2/3 nightly alerts every third night with the baseline unchanged. In 200 simulated step regressions from 0.95, a drop to 0.6 was missed within 14 nights in 41 runs and a drop to 0.4 in 3 (96 and 28 at 0.1); a slow decline from 1.0 to 0.5 over 60 nights never alerted in 38 of 100 runs (62 at 0.1). On 400 simulated stationary nights with 8 cases at 3 repeats (3 seeds), the baseline stays within 0.03 of the true rate at 0.8 and 0.02 at 0.9, and nights with an alert run 1.0 to 3.8 times the rate of admitting every run (seed 4242 - 3 against 3 at 0.97, 31 against 12 at 0.9, 48 against 14 at 0.8, 42 against 11 for mixed rates); at 0.1 the same process alerted on 24 nights at 0.8.

localWorkflows.canaryBaselineScanPipelin.remediation: TREND.md lists each scheduled pipeline examined and why it held no usable trend.json. Raise localWorkflows.canaryBaselineScanPipelines in config/limits/localWorkflows.yaml (at most one GitLab page of 100) if canary pipelines are sparser than that, or set DOCSFAB_CANARY_ALLOW_NEW_BASELINE=1 on the schedule for one run to start a new chain deliberately.
localWorkflows.canaryBaselineScanPipelin.rationale: Most scheduled main pipelines older than the current one, newest first, that the canary trend job examines through the GitLab API to find the latest intact trend.json. With the nightly live-model schedule and a nightly canary schedule that is about two weeks. A run starts a new baseline only when this scan covers the whole schedule history and finds no earlier trend.json or expired canary artifacts, or when the operator allows it; otherwise the verdict is chain-broken and the run is never a baseline. It is one API page, so GitLab's 100-item page maximum is its ceiling.

localWorkflows.canaryApiPageSize.remediation: Keep localWorkflows.canaryApiPageSize at or below GitLab's page maximum of 100.
localWorkflows.canaryApiPageSize.rationale: GitLab API page size the canary trend job requests when it lists one pipeline's jobs. 100 is GitLab's maximum, so a pipeline of about 60 jobs fits one page.

localWorkflows.canaryPipelineJobPagesMax.remediation: The trend job refused instead of reading part of a pipeline's job list. Raise localWorkflows.canaryPipelineJobPagesMax in config/limits/localWorkflows.yaml if scheduled pipelines legitimately grew past that many pages of localWorkflows.canaryApiPageSize jobs.
localWorkflows.canaryPipelineJobPagesMax.rationale: Most pages of jobs the canary trend job reads for one scheduled pipeline while looking for the earlier trend job. Scheduled main pipelines have about 60 jobs (pipeline 69429173), one page at localWorkflows.canaryApiPageSize; three pages leave room for growth. Past it the lookup refuses with this code and the verdict is chain-broken, never a partial scan.

localWorkflows.canaryDocumentMaxBytes.remediation: The canary refused to parse an oversized summary.json or trend.json. Inspect the document; if the case, step, and code counts legitimately grew, raise localWorkflows.canaryDocumentMaxBytes in config/limits/localWorkflows.yaml.
localWorkflows.canaryDocumentMaxBytes.rationale: Largest summary.json or trend.json the canary trend job reads, from the matrix job artifact or a downloaded earlier trend. A summary of 8 cases with their steps and codes is tens of KiB, and a trend carries at most localWorkflows.canaryBaselineRuns plus localWorkflows.canaryPendingRuns summaries, well under 1 MiB. The bound keeps untrusted input from exhausting the job before validation.

localWorkflows.canaryCasesMax.remediation: The trend job refused a summary.json or trend.json with more cases than this. The matrix has 8 cases; if cases were legitimately added, raise localWorkflows.canaryCasesMax in config/limits/localWorkflows.yaml.
localWorkflows.canaryCasesMax.rationale: Most cases a canary summary or carried trend state may hold. The matrix has 8 cases (4 workflows by 2 entry points), so 64 leaves room for growth while bounding the per-case state the trend job reads before localWorkflows.canaryDocumentMaxBytes alone would; per-case baseline and held-out lengths are bounded by the catalog maxima of localWorkflows.canaryBaselineRuns and localWorkflows.canaryPendingRuns.

localWorkflows.canarySilenceMaxDays.remediation: Set the silence's expires date no more than this many days ahead, and renew it through a reviewed change if the regression is still open.
localWorkflows.canarySilenceMaxDays.rationale: Longest time a canary silence may run ahead of the evaluation day. A silence mutes the alert and keeps the muted nights out of the baseline, but other nights during it follow localWorkflows.canaryBaselineAdmitMaxPValue, so a regression milder than that threshold can still be absorbed; after expiry the case alerts only when a night, or pooled held nights, is significant against the baseline as it stands then. A silence stays active through the end of its expires day. In a simulated sweep at 0.25 (baselines 8/21 to 21/21, regressed rates 0/3 to 2/3, silences of 1 to 12 nights), a still-broken case with no night admitted during the silence alerted again within its hold cycle, up to five canaries after expiry for a mild regression (15/21 at 1/3, 20/21 at 2/3); a regression milder than the admission threshold may be absorbed during the silence and never alert, whatever the shape of the baseline (for example 17/21 at 2/3 and 11/21 at 1/3). An open-ended silence would hide a lasting change indefinitely; 30 days forces a reviewed renewal about monthly, which matches the artifact retention of ci.liveModel.evidenceRetentionDays.

runtimeContribution.cellMaxTotalTokens.remediation: Read the cell's provider accounting in its result record to see which requests consumed the budget. If representative work legitimately needs more, raise runtimeContribution.cellMaxTotalTokens in config/limits/runtimeContribution.yaml and qualify a new campaign; DOCSFAB_RUNTIME_CONTRIBUTION_CELL_MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS and --max-total-tokens may only lower it.
runtimeContribution.cellMaxTotalTokens.rationale: Accounted tokens one benchmark cell may use across every provider request, retry, and conservative reservation, identical for all three conditions. Accounting uses the provider's reported total, which includes cached prompt tokens. Measured basis, one round (gpt-6-sol, local-workflows matrix, main 2d499b21, 2026-09-28) - DocsFab used 0.5M to 2.3M reported tokens per case on a one-file fixture, mostly cached prompt, with 16 to 27 requests. The pilot fixtures are larger, so the value allows about 2.5 times the largest measured case. The former 100000 literal (2026-09-14, gpt-5.4) sat below every measured DocsFab case, so a campaign under it measured the budget rather than the product. The scope vocabulary has no per-cell value, so it is filed per-run. The host override may only lower it.

runtimeContribution.cellMaxRequests.remediation: Read the cell's provider accounting to see whether the requests were productive turns or a retry loop. If representative work legitimately needs more turns, raise runtimeContribution.cellMaxRequests in config/limits/runtimeContribution.yaml and qualify a new campaign; DOCSFAB_RUNTIME_CONTRIBUTION_CELL_MAX_REQUESTS may only lower it.
runtimeContribution.cellMaxRequests.rationale: Provider attempts one benchmark cell may send, identical for all three conditions, as a guardrail beside the token budget. Measured basis, one round (gpt-6-sol, local-workflows matrix, 2026-09-28) - DocsFab used 16 to 27 requests per case. The baseline arms are ordinary tool-using agents with one request per turn and no measured basis on the current model, so the value leaves about 5 times the largest measured DocsFab case. The former 60 literal dates from 2026-09-14. The scope vocabulary has no per-cell value, so it is filed per-run. The host override may only lower it.

runtimeContribution.cellTimeoutMs.remediation: Read the cell's retained records to find the last completed step. If representative work legitimately needs longer, raise runtimeContribution.cellTimeoutMs in config/limits/runtimeContribution.yaml and qualify a new campaign; DOCSFAB_RUNTIME_CONTRIBUTION_CELL_TIMEOUT_MS may only lower it.
runtimeContribution.cellTimeoutMs.rationale: Wall-clock bound for one benchmark cell, identical for all three conditions. Measured basis, one round (gpt-6-sol, local-workflows matrix, 2026-09-28) - DocsFab cases took 4.7 to 7.0 minutes with 8 host CPUs, while pilot cells run in containers limited to 2 CPUs with larger fixtures. One DocsFab step may legitimately run up to its sealed 30 minute attempt bound, so the value is that bound plus 15 minutes for the remaining steps. The former 600000 literal dates from 2026-09-14. The scope vocabulary has no per-cell value, so it is filed per-run. The host override may only lower it.

runtimeContribution.campaignMaxTotalToke.remediation: The campaign stopped before a cell whose full budget no longer fits; completed cells are retained and the remaining cells are named in the phase output. Review the accounted usage, then raise runtimeContribution.campaignMaxTotalTokens in config/limits/runtimeContribution.yaml and qualify a new campaign, or accept the partial matrix as reported; DOCSFAB_RUNTIME_CONTRIBUTION_CAMPAIGN_MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS may only lower it.
runtimeContribution.campaignMaxTotalToke.rationale: Accounted tokens for a whole campaign. The runner starts a cell only when a full cell budget still fits, so the value is the fixed 30-cell matrix times runtimeContribution.cellMaxTotalTokens, and a full matrix can never be cut short by this ceiling. Accounted tokens include cached prompt tokens and conservative reservations; they are not a cost estimate. The former 3000000 literal (2026-09-14) was 30 times the old per-cell budget. The host override may only lower it.

runtimeContribution.transientRetriesPerR.remediation: A cell that exhausts these retries stops with provider-throttled (429) or provider-unavailable (502, 503, 504) in its terminal reasons, and its provider events show every retried response and backoff. Wait for the provider's rate limit or availability to recover, or reduce concurrent traffic on the same deployment, then qualify a new campaign. DOCSFAB_RUNTIME_CONTRIBUTION_TRANSIENT_RETRIES_PER_REQUEST may only lower it; 0 restores the fail-closed stop on the first such response.
runtimeContribution.transientRetriesPerR.rationale: Times the shared provider interceptor re-sends one request after an HTTP 429, 502, 503, or 504 that reports no usage, identical for every condition, so a transient provider rate limit or outage does not decide a cell. HTTP 500 is not retried because it can report a deterministic request failure. Each re-send is an accounted attempt under runtimeContribution.cellMaxRequests. A 429 is refused before processing and charges no tokens; a 502, 503, or 504 may hide provider work and charges its conservative reservation. Measured basis (2026-09-29) - the first gpt-6-sol pilot canary lost both baseline cells to a 429 on their first request with zero retries; after 429 retries were added, 14 of one baseline cell's 24 requests were 429 and another cell stopped on a 503. With the backoff bounds, eight retries wait at most about four minutes for one request. The scope vocabulary has no per-request value, so it is filed per-run. The host override may only lower it.

runtimeContribution.transientBackoffInit.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_RUNTIME_CONTRIBUTION_TRANSIENT_BACKOFF_INITIAL_MS only to test the retry path; raise this value in config/limits/runtimeContribution.yaml if the provider needs longer to recover.
runtimeContribution.transientBackoffInit.rationale: Provisional, unmeasured. First wait after a retried provider response that has no numeric Retry-After header; each later retry doubles it up to runtimeContribution.transientBackoffMaxMs. A numeric Retry-After from the provider replaces the doubling, still capped by the maximum. The host override may only lower it.
