GitLab parses each build's test report asynchronously after the build finishes, so a summary read just after the pipeline's last update can miss a build; reusing it would keep that gap for good. Sixty minutes, one hourly refresh, lets every finished pipeline be read once more before its totals are reused. Provisional planning value, not measured against GitLab's report parsing time.

dashboard.bench.fetchPipelines.remediation: Read the problem fetch-bench.mjs names in fetch-bench.json. If the Bench project's newest scheduled pipelines on main ran without a successful bench:dashboard-snapshot job, fix that job; if its schedule also starts pipelines without the job, raise dashboard.bench.fetchPipelines in config/limits/dashboard.yaml. The pair already fetched stays on the page either way.
dashboard.bench.fetchPipelines.rationale: How many of the Bench project's newest scheduled pipelines on main fetch-bench.mjs looks through, in one listing page, for the newest successful bench:dashboard-snapshot job. The fetch keeps the last good snapshot when it finds none, so a short run of failed jobs only delays the panel; twenty covers most of a day of an hourly schedule, or nearly three weeks of a daily one, while a fetch never walks the project's whole history. GitLab lists at most 100 items a page, hence the maximum. Provisional planning value, not measured; the Bench schedule's cadence, not yet decided, is the basis to revisit it.

dashboard.progress.trendWindowDays.remediation: Read the window the progress page names beside its trailing average. If the owner moves the goal to another window, change dashboard.progress.trendWindowDays in config/limits/dashboard.yaml; a shorter window can only resolve larger changes.
dashboard.progress.trendWindowDays.rationale: Days of comparable daily runs that the progress page pools for its trailing average, its chance band, its margins over the two alternative agents, and the goal check, and that it compares with the same span before. The owner set the goal on the seven-day pooled done-well rate on 2026-10-08. At 20 tasks a day, seven days pool 140 paired tasks per agent, which resolves a change of about 8 to 10 points where a single day swings by 2 or 3 tasks by chance. Owner decision, not measured.

dashboard.progress.sparklineDays.remediation: Read the span the progress page's chart and sparklines name. If readers need a longer or shorter view, change dashboard.progress.sparklineDays in config/limits/dashboard.yaml; the local history keeps every run either way.
dashboard.progress.sparklineDays.rationale: Days of daily runs drawn in the progress page's chart and in each headline sparkline, and counted for the daily run's on-schedule share. Fourteen days show two trailing windows side by side, so this week's average can be read against last week's on the same axis. Approved with the page's mockup on 2026-10-08. Provisional planning value, not measured; revisit once a month of daily runs exists.

dashboard.progress.staleHours.remediation: Read which source the progress page marks stale and its age. Restart the missed source, such as the nightly benchmark schedule, the pilot snapshot, or the CI fetch. If a source legitimately reports less often, change dashboard.progress.staleHours in config/limits/dashboard.yaml.
dashboard.progress.staleHours.rationale: Age at which the progress page marks a daily source stale, turns its chip red, greys its numbers, and keeps them out of the headline row. The daily benchmark, the pilot snapshot, and the CI snapshot are each expected at least once a day. Twenty-four hours plus two hours of grace lets a run that starts late or runs long stay current, while a missed day turns red before the next morning's reading. Owner rule for the daily run, 2026-10-08.

dashboard.progress.monthlyKeyLimitUsd.remediation: Read the month-to-date benchmark spend the progress page shows, and the runs whose spend is unknown. When the owner raises the benchmark provider key's monthly limit, raise dashboard.progress.monthlyKeyLimitUsd in config/limits/dashboard.yaml to match; the page only warns and never stops a run.
dashboard.progress.monthlyKeyLimitUsd.rationale: The benchmark provider key's monthly spending limit. The owner raised the bench Hub key to 9000 USD per month on 2026-10-12, from 4000 USD. The progress page warns when this month's benchmark spend reaches its warnAt share, or could have reached it once each run of unknown spend is counted at its cap, so the six-hourly DocsFab runs and the full nightly never reach the key's limit unannounced. It is a warning only, and nothing refuses or stops on it.

dashboard.progress.historyDays.remediation: Read the window fetch-nightly.mjs names in its manifest. If the fetch was paused for longer, raise dashboard.progress.historyDays in config/limits/dashboard.yaml for one run, or pass --pipeline for each missed pipeline; files already in the history are kept either way.
dashboard.progress.historyDays.rationale: Days of bench:nightly pipelines each fetch looks back over before it stops. The fetch copies every run it finds into a local history and never deletes one, so the page keeps showing runs after their CI artifacts expire. Four weeks covers the chart's two weeks plus the trailing window behind its first point and leaves two weeks to recover from a paused fetch, while a pipeline whose artifact has expired is not requested again on every refresh. Provisional planning value, not measured.

dashboard.progress.providerOutageShare.remediation: Read the run the progress page flags (it names its provider errors or timeouts and a count such as 12 of 20 cells that ran) and its cause table. The flag only labels a run; it changes no rate and stops nothing. If provider noise of that size is ordinary, raise dashboard.progress.providerOutageShare in config/limits/dashboard.yaml; if a smaller burst should be flagged, lower it.
dashboard.progress.providerOutageShare.rationale: Share of the cells one agent ran in a daily run (a cell that never ran, or whose execution is unknown, could not end on a provider cause) that ended on a provider error, a model-unavailable stop, or a cell timeout, above which the progress page flags the run for provider errors or timeouts and names the count, such as 12 of 20 cells that ran. The benchmark contract counts those cells as failures of the agent that stopped on them, so a burst of them lowers DocsFab's done-well rate; the flag tells the reader the dip may be infrastructure and changes no rate. A run is flagged when its share is strictly above this value. Measured basis, the eight measured daily runs of 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-13 (160 DocsFab cells, 27 of them on those causes) had 0 to 2 of the cells that ran on those causes in six runs (0 to 10 percent, one of them 1 of 13 that ran) and 10 and 12 of 20 in the other two (50 and 60 percent). 0.25, more than five of 20 cells, sits between the two groups, so ordinary provider noise stays unflagged and a burst is flagged. Provisional planning value; revisit after a month of runs.

sourceAcquisitionChecker.safeIdMaxLength.remediation: Shorten the case or fact identifier, or raise sourceAcquisitionChecker.safeIdMaxLength in config/limits/sourceAcquisitionChecker.yaml.
sourceAcquisitionChecker.safeIdMaxLength.rationale: Scope is per-run because it applies per independent checker.py invocation grading one SourceAcquisitionQualificationV1 envelope (#802), not a host- or project-wide bound; the closed scope enum has no test-harness tier. Ceiling for caseId and factId values accepted by checker.py's SAFE_ID pattern; a value outside it fails independent checking with the caller's own invalid-case/invalid-facts code. 512 matches the previously unregistered literal. Registered without a host override because checker.py does not read DOCSFAB_* overrides; add one only alongside real override support.

sourceAcquisitionChecker.reasonCodeMaxLe.remediation: Shorten the reason code, or raise sourceAcquisitionChecker.reasonCodeMaxLength in config/limits/sourceAcquisitionChecker.yaml.
sourceAcquisitionChecker.reasonCodeMaxLe.rationale: Scope is per-run because it applies per independent checker.py invocation grading one SourceAcquisitionQualificationV1 envelope (#802), not a host- or project-wide bound; the closed scope enum has no test-harness tier. Ceiling for reasonCode values accepted by checker.py's REASON pattern; a value outside it fails independent checking with the caller's own invalid-record/invalid-limitations code. 128 matches the previously unregistered literal. Registered without a host override because checker.py does not read DOCSFAB_* overrides; add one only alongside real override support.

ci.liveModel.jobTimeoutMs.remediation: Shorten the job or raise ci.liveModel.jobTimeoutMs in config/limits/ci.yaml.
ci.liveModel.jobTimeoutMs.rationale: GitLab job timeout for the jobs that reach a real model provider, currently runtime:mr-assessment (#1087) and runtime:workflow-canary (#1183), plus the canary's model-free runtime:workflow-canary:trend job. All three extend the same generated .ci_live_model_platform_bounds include, which projects this catalog value as a GitLab duration; GitLab cannot call limit(). The canary ends its matrix localWorkflows.canaryJobReserveMs before this timeout, counted from CI_JOB_STARTED_AT, and refuses a reserve that is not below it, so raising this value also lets more canary rounds start. runtime:live-model and runtime:live-journey (#1046) are deliberately NOT on this list -- neither fits 45 minutes, so each carries its own ceiling (ci.liveModelAcceptance.jobTimeoutMs and ci.liveJourney.jobTimeoutMs) and extends its own generated include.

ci.liveModelAcceptance.jobTimeoutMs.remediation: Raise ci.liveModelAcceptance.jobTimeoutMs in config/limits/ci.yaml, or shorten the acceptance run. GitLab admits a job timeout longer than the project build timeout but not longer than a runner's maximum timeout, and the bwrap-userns runners set none.
ci.liveModelAcceptance.jobTimeoutMs.rationale: GitLab job timeout for runtime:live-model, which runs the whole acceptance harness in one job -- clean install, the repository's full npm run check, build, catalog, the offline and live doctors, and two live readiness runs. The check runs the whole runtime suite on CI test budgets (test.ciTimeoutMs) with two Vitest workers. On main pipeline 73039655 the four two-worker runtime:test shards took 3679 s together and the heavy test files CI runs in separate jobs another 819 s, so the check should take roughly 60 to 75 minutes; the 2026-10-11 scheduled check took 1790 s on four workers with 5 s local budgets, and the live phases after it have never run. Three hours is about twice the expected total, so only an extreme run reaches it. GitLab admits a job timeout longer than the project's 3600 s build timeout but not longer than a runner's maximum, and the bwrap-userns runners report no maximum_timeout (read 2026-10-12). Separate from ci.liveModel.jobTimeoutMs so the canary's round deadline and runtime:mr-assessment keep their own ceiling. The generated .ci_live_model_acceptance_platform_bounds include projects this catalog value as a GitLab duration; GitLab cannot call limit().

ci.liveModel.evidenceRetentionDays.remediation: Shorten artifact retention or raise ci.liveModel.evidenceRetentionDays in config/limits/ci.yaml.
ci.liveModel.evidenceRetentionDays.rationale: GitLab artifact expiry for the minimized terminal evidence of jobs that reach a real model provider, currently runtime:live-model, runtime:mr-assessment (#1087), and runtime:workflow-canary (#1183), plus runtime:workflow-canary:trend, whose trend.json carries the canary baseline chain, and runtime:live-journey (#1046). runtime:mr-assessment and the two canary jobs extend the generated .ci_live_model_platform_bounds include, runtime:live-model extends .ci_live_model_acceptance_platform_bounds, and runtime:live-journey extends .ci_live_journey_platform_bounds; all three project this one catalog value as expire_in, so every real-model evidence artifact expires together. Each trend.json carries the whole baseline window forward, so only the newest intact one must survive this expiry; the trend job reports expired canary artifacts as a broken chain instead of starting over.

ci.artifacts.handoffRetentionDays.remediation: Shorten handoff artifact retention to reclaim project storage, or raise ci.artifacts.handoffRetentionDays in config/limits/ci.yaml when a later job must read a handoff after that many days.
ci.artifacts.handoffRetentionDays.rationale: GitLab artifact expiry for artifacts that exist to hand files to later jobs in the same pipeline -- runtime:prepare's derived trees and package candidate, the runtime:test and runtime:isolation coverage lanes that runtime:coverage merges, and runtime:package:verify's verified tarball that the agent-image and npm publish jobs consume. They were the bulk of the project's 50 GB of job artifacts on 2026-09-28 (about 17 MB per pipeline at about 400 pipelines a day, kept 14 to 30 days). The durable copies are the published npm package and agent image, and each coverage lane's failure message names its failures in the job trace. Three days keeps a failed lane's blob and the handoffs available for a retry of a downstream job across a weekend. Each job extends the generated .ci_handoff_artifacts include; GitLab artifact expiry cannot call limit().

ci.artifacts.reportRetentionDays.remediation: Shorten report artifact retention to reclaim project storage, or raise ci.artifacts.reportRetentionDays in config/limits/ci.yaml when reviewers need older reports.
ci.artifacts.reportRetentionDays.rationale: GitLab artifact expiry for the small reports reviewers read after a pipeline -- runtime:smoke's JUnit, runtime:coverage's summary, runtime:comparison-model's JUnit, and documentation:freshness's report. Fourteen days is the value those jobs declared by hand before this entry and covers a normal merge-request review window. Real-model evidence keeps its own ci.liveModel.evidenceRetentionDays, and the semgrep-sast report keeps GitLab's instance default because governance/security/sast-baseline.md pins individual reports by job. Each job extends the generated .ci_report_artifacts include; GitLab artifact expiry cannot call limit().

ci.liveJourney.jobTimeoutMs.remediation: Scope the journey gate down, or raise ci.liveJourney.jobTimeoutMs in config/limits/ci.yaml. GitLab admits a job timeout longer than the project build timeout but not longer than a runner's maximum timeout, and the bwrap-userns runners set none.
ci.liveJourney.jobTimeoutMs.rationale: GitLab job timeout for runtime:live-journey (#1046), the one job that runs a governed review-documentation review and a live-agent-turn ask end to end through the hosted invoker against a real provider. Separate from ci.liveModel.jobTimeoutMs, whose 45 minutes one journey does not fit -- the review workflow has eight steps, and the measured 2026-09-24 run of its first three and a half steps over three pages took 2600 s (423, 954, 30 and 1192 s per step). The scheduled job had not reached a journey before 2026-10-12, so the whole run is unmeasured; three hours leaves about twice the time eight such steps would take over three pages, while the gate reviews one page. GitLab admits a job timeout longer than the project's 3600 s build timeout but not longer than a runner's maximum, and the bwrap-userns runners report no maximum_timeout (read 2026-10-12). The gate writes its evidence after each journey, so a platform stop still leaves the completed journey's record behind. The generated .ci_live_journey_platform_bounds include projects this catalog value as a GitLab duration; GitLab cannot call limit(). The journey gate expires its evidence capsule at this same value, so a capsule can never outlive the job that minted it.

ci.wsl2.jobTimeoutMs.remediation: Scope the installed-product lane to fit the project build timeout; do not raise the GitLab job timeout above the project ceiling.
ci.wsl2.jobTimeoutMs.rationale: GitLab's 3600-second project build timeout read on 2026-10-11 is the ceiling for the converted-host installed-product lane. The generated CI mirror projects this ceiling because GitLab cannot call limit(). The guest work deadline and cleanup reserve remain separate and must be set from admitted-host measurements before activation; this entry does not assert that the full journey fits yet.

ci.wsl2.automaticRetries.remediation: Reconcile the prior owned guest run before starting a fresh protected-main job; do not replay uncertain host work automatically.
ci.wsl2.automaticRetries.rationale: A Runner system failure or timeout can leave owned Linux or Windows work alive on the persistent converted host. This safety policy disables GitLab's inherited automatic retry for the installed-product job; a fresh invocation must pass the guest lock and exact recovery controls before another payload starts. The generated CI mirror projects the zero retry value because GitLab cannot call limit().

ci.wsl2.cleanupReserveMs.remediation: Preserve one original job clock and reserve the final ten minutes for exact Windows and Linux descendant cleanup and evidence; reduce the candidate work scope if it cannot finish before this boundary.
ci.wsl2.cleanupReserveMs.rationale: The accepted converted host completed package install/offline, six standard/two alias controls, and the fixture in 263.067 seconds at UID 1001. Actual Job Object and guest broker-loss controls then showed scoped termination and recovery within seconds. A 600-second cleanup reserve under the fixed 3600-second project ceiling leaves 3000 seconds for the combined installed journey while giving the independent supervisors time to close both OS process sets and retain evidence after a failed phase. No phase resets either deadline.

ci.wsl2.windowsCommandMaxChars.remediation: Stage the exact pinned helper through the short SFTP launcher and execute it by path; never split or truncate an oversized encoded command.
ci.wsl2.windowsCommandMaxChars.rationale: The converted Windows host's cmd.exe command-line boundary of 8191 characters was observed during conversion when an inline launcher exceeded it before any action. The broker checks its actual encoded remote PowerShell command against this platform capacity before SSH. Larger owned helpers must use staged files with verified digests and a short invocation, rather than a guessed smaller output cap or a hidden truncation.

ci.wsl2.controlPollMs.remediation: Keep the exact Windows child and cleanup observations under the original run deadline; change the control poll interval only with a measured host control review.
ci.wsl2.controlPollMs.rationale: Poll interval for the Windows Job Object control's owned child-generation file and process-exit readback. One tenth of a second resolves child creation and teardown without resetting the original job deadline; it is observation granularity, not a work, output, or corpus cap. A timed-out control refuses with retained evidence instead of omitting a child.

ci.wsl2.unixSocketPathMaxBytes.remediation: Use the uniquely owned short native TMPDIR for WSL alias controls; refuse a projected alias socket path longer than Linux sockaddr_un permits.
ci.wsl2.unixSocketPathMaxBytes.rationale: Linux unix(7) specifies 108 bytes for sockaddr_un.sun_path including a terminating NUL, leaving 107 pathname bytes. The accepted source17 conversion alias path measured 102 bytes; the first composed run used a 148-byte alias path and failed the WSL socket hop with ENOENT. The guest computes the qualifier's projected alias pathname from its actual selected WSL_INTEROP basename and refuses overlong paths before package work.

ci.wsl2.shortTmpTokenHexChars.remediation: Derive the exact short TMPDIR token from the full run ID and retain the owner ledger; refuse any pre-existing token directory rather than adopting it.
ci.wsl2.shortTmpTokenHexChars.rationale: A 16-hex-character SHA-256 run token gives a 64-bit run-specific directory name under /home/docsfab/c. Exclusive creation and a full run-ID owner ledger make a collision a refusal. This keeps the unchanged source17 bwrap alias socket path below Linux's 107-byte pathname capacity without weakening its Windows/UNC positive controls or using a symlink to a long path.

ci.sast.semgrepRuleTimeoutSeconds.remediation: Lower the Semgrep per-rule/file timeout, or raise ci.sast.semgrepRuleTimeoutSeconds in config/limits/ci.yaml and repeat the same-revision before/after trace comparison governance/security/sast-baseline.md requires.
ci.sast.semgrepRuleTimeoutSeconds.rationale: Per-rule/file timeout for the semgrep-sast job, raised per governance/security/sast-baseline.md's "Bounded remediation and next evidence" section from the Semgrep analyzer's five-second default to a finite reviewed value. The generated CI include projects this catalog value into the job's SAST_SCANNER_ALLOWED_CLI_OPTS variable; GitLab job variables cannot call limit().

ci.sast.maxTargetBytes.remediation: Raise ci.sast.maxTargetBytes in config/limits/ci.yaml to scan larger files, or lower it to skip more and speed the job, and repeat the same-revision before/after trace comparison governance/security/sast-baseline.md requires.
ci.sast.maxTargetBytes.rationale: Per-file size skip bound for the semgrep-sast job, matching governance/security/sast-baseline.md's "Bounded remediation and next evidence" section's instruction to preserve the one-megabyte target bound while making path coverage explicit elsewhere. Was previously the analyzer's own unconfigured 1,000,000-byte default (Semgrep's own --max-target-bytes default); now an explicit, governed value. The generated CI include projects this catalog value into the job's SAST_SCANNER_ALLOWED_CLI_OPTS variable; GitLab job variables cannot call limit().

ci.coverageShard.failureReportMaxEntries.remediation: Open the lane's blob artifact for the omitted entries, or raise ci.coverageShard.failureReportMaxEntries in config/limits/ci.yaml.
ci.coverageShard.failureReportMaxEntries.rationale: Failed or incomplete files, tests, and unhandled errors that one runtime coverage lane failure message names before it states how many it omitted (issue 1050). The recorded train-car failures named one file and one test each; 25 lists every entry of a typical flake or small regression while keeping a whole-lane collapse readable in the job trace. The complete list stays in the lane's blob artifact.

ci.coverageShard.failureMessageMaxChars.remediation: Open the lane's blob artifact for the full error, or raise ci.coverageShard.failureMessageMaxChars in config/limits/ci.yaml.
ci.coverageShard.failureMessageMaxChars.rationale: Characters of the first error line that one runtime coverage lane failure entry quotes before it states how many it omitted (issue 1050). The recorded receipt-store failures had first lines of 49 and 110 characters; 400 keeps a typical assertion message whole without letting a serialized value flood the trace.

ci.trainReuse.apiPageSize.remediation: Keep the protocol page size within the supported range in config/limits/ci.yaml; all returned pages must still be consumed.
ci.trainReuse.apiPageSize.rationale: GitLab REST API page size for offline-qualified train metadata discovery. This is the server page size, never a total-row or total-page ceiling; discovery must follow every valid next link.

ci.trainReuse.apiResponseMaxBytes.remediation: Reduce an individual metadata response or adjust ci.trainReuse.apiResponseMaxBytes within its supported range in config/limits/ci.yaml.
ci.trainReuse.apiResponseMaxBytes.rationale: Maximum streamed wire body for one GitLab metadata response. The observed complete 62-job response was 209276 bytes; 1 MiB provides roughly five times that response while the independent aggregate budget bounds the whole discovery.

ci.trainReuse.evidenceMaxBytes.remediation: Retry the metadata discovery after the provider returns smaller complete responses; do not omit pages or records. See config/limits/ci.yaml.
ci.trainReuse.evidenceMaxBytes.rationale: Fixed aggregate allowance for all received metadata bodies across list/detail/jobs rereads plus normalized public output. Four observed 62-job inventories for retried/default reconciliation total about 837104 bytes before small overhead, so 16 MiB admits roughly twenty such units without introducing a row or page cap.

ci.trainReuse.discoveryTimeoutMs.remediation: Retry discovery when the GitLab metadata API is responsive; do not reset or extend the single discovery deadline per request. See config/limits/ci.yaml.
ci.trainReuse.discoveryTimeoutMs.rationale: Fixed elapsed-time budget for the entire metadata discovery, including all pages, rereads, normalization, and output. Developer-host API round trips were about 0.4 to 1.1 seconds; native-runner qualification remains required before any future activation.

churn.windowDays.remediation: Lower churn.windowDays in config/limits/churn.yaml, or accept a longer lookback window.
churn.windowDays.rationale: scripts/orchestration/churn-report.sh's first-parent-merge lookback window, in days, counted backward from the reported revision's committer date (inclusive on both ends). 14 matches Epic(#1304)'s hand-produced baseline table, 641 merged MRs over 14 days to cc86e7278, Task(#1318), so a re-run reproduces that table byte-for-byte. No CLI flag overrides this value, override is null; a future per-invocation need becomes a catalog DOCSFAB_* environment override validated against min/max at startup, per the limits contract, not a bare script flag.

churn.reviewThreshold.remediation: Assign an owner and a split plan for the flagged file, or raise churn.reviewThreshold in config/limits/churn.yaml after confirming the new floor still catches real magnets.
churn.reviewThreshold.rationale: A hand-written file whose first-parent-merge touch count over churn.windowDays is strictly greater than this value is flagged for review as a merge magnet, comparator is `>`, matching Epic(#1304)'s "above" wording; a file at exactly this count is not flagged. 30 is the floor of Epic(#1304)'s own 12-row Evidence table, config/limits-allowlist.json at 30 touches, the table's lowest-ranked row, so the same baseline revision cc86e7278 flags every row that table names. Generated mirrors, packages/runtime/src/config/limits.generated.ts and similar, are never flagged regardless of count; they are covered by Investigation(#1173), item 3, not by per-file ownership.

churn.topN.remediation: Raise churn.topN in config/limits/churn.yaml to see further down the ranked list, or lower it to shorten the report; the full hand-written and generated totals are always disclosed separately regardless of this bound.
churn.topN.rationale: Hand-written rows shown by scripts/orchestration/churn-report.sh's default, non-JSON, report, ranked by touch count descending then path ascending, before generated mirrors are excluded from ranking, they are listed separately, never consuming a top-N slot. 20 is sized so every one of Epic(#1304)'s 12 Evidence-table rows appears at the baseline revision cc86e7278 -- the table's lowest-touch row, config/limits-allowlist.json, 30 touches, is hand-written rank 16 counting only present-at-rev generated exclusions, or rank 17 if the two paths absent at cc86e7278, packages/host/src/config/limits.generated.ts and packages/runtime/src/native-compositions/generated-comparison-kit-pins.ts, both themselves generated mirrors so this only affects bookkeeping and not candidacy, are kept as ranked-but-unresolvable rows rather than dropped; 20 clears both countings with headroom. Output always discloses a "showing N of M files" line so a clipped tail is never silent.

conflictPrediction.maxHeads.remediation: Narrow the snapshot to the heads that matter, dropping merged or stacked rows, or raise conflictPrediction.maxHeads in config/limits/conflictPrediction.yaml after accepting the extra fetch and merge-tree cost of each additional head.
conflictPrediction.maxHeads.rationale: Other heads scripts/orchestration/predict-conflicts.sh compares one candidate against in a single run, counting every open merge request plus every active merge-train car named by the snapshot; the run refuses when the observed head count is strictly greater than this value, comparator is `>`, so a snapshot naming exactly this many heads still runs. 25 is sized against the measured population rather than a guess, Task(#1393), namely 6 open merge requests and 0 active cars at 2026-09-25T01:44Z, unchanged on a re-read ten minutes later, and single-digit concurrent open merge requests across the 719 merge requests created since 2026-09-10. Each compared head costs one ref fetch and two `git merge-tree --write-tree` runs, so this is a cost ceiling on an advisory read-only report, never a correctness bound; a run that legitimately needs more heads is a signal to narrow the candidate set first. No CLI flag overrides this value, override is null; a future per-invocation need becomes a catalog DOCSFAB_* environment override validated against min/max at startup, per the limits contract, not a bare script flag.

conflictPrediction.snapshotMaxAgeMinutes.remediation: Re-read the snapshot with scripts/orchestration/predict-conflicts.sh --live, or raise conflictPrediction.snapshotMaxAgeMinutes in config/limits/conflictPrediction.yaml if a deliberately older snapshot is being replayed.
conflictPrediction.snapshotMaxAgeMinutes.rationale: Maximum age of the snapshot's `generated_at` timestamp, measured against the clock at run time, before scripts/orchestration/predict-conflicts.sh refuses to report from it; the run refuses when the observed age is strictly greater than this value, comparator is `>`, so a snapshot at exactly this age still runs. 15 minutes bounds the gap between reading the open merge-request list and comparing against it, which is the interval over which a prediction can actually be trusted, Task(#1393). It deliberately does not attempt to make the active merge-train car list fresh, because a car is created and removed within one second, so no age bound makes a car list trustworthy; the report instead discloses the snapshot timestamp on every run so a reader never mistakes a replayed car list for live state. No CLI flag overrides this value, override is null; a future per-invocation need becomes a catalog DOCSFAB_* environment override validated against min/max at startup, per the limits contract, not a bare script flag.

judgement.hostSuccessWindowDays.remediation: Widen or narrow judgement.hostSuccessWindowDays in config/limits/judgement.yaml, and re-export the host job snapshot if the new window is wider than the export carries.
judgement.hostSuccessWindowDays.rationale: Trailing window, in whole UTC days ending on the export's own snapshot day inclusive, over which the read-only judgement pass counts host job outcomes per project and workflow. It is anchored at the snapshot rather than at the run clock because the export cannot carry a job created after the host was observed, so a run-anchored window would always leave its newest day empty and silently drop the oldest day the export does cover. A project's workflow with at least one job in this window and zero succeeded is reported as no-host-success. 7 is the breakdown width of the 2026-09-24 orchestration lessons, lesson 1, whose 7-day table read review-documentation 0 succeeded / 180 failed / 2,706 cancelled and live-agent-turn 2 succeeded / 2 failed; the gap that lesson describes ran 9 days, so a 7-day window surfaces it on the first day it can be seen rather than after the fact. Not the export width, judgement.exportWindowDays, which is deliberately wider so one export serves several windows.

judgement.reviewDurationBoundMinutes.remediation: Raise judgement.reviewDurationBoundMinutes in config/limits/judgement.yaml once reviews routinely finish slower for a benign reason, or shorten the review budget so the journey can produce a success.
judgement.reviewDurationBoundMinutes.rationale: A host job that had already been queued or running more than this many minutes when the export was taken is reported as review-past-limit, comparator strictly greater than, so a job at exactly this age is not reported. The age is measured from the export's snapshot instant, never from the run clock, because the export is carried off the installed host by a maintainer and is deliberately tolerated for judgement.snapshotMaxAgeHours, so a run-clock age would add the whole transport delay to every queued and running job and report all of them. Named for the review journey that motivated it and applied to every active workflow, because the same starvation shape is not review-specific. 15 is the observation recorded in the 2026-09-25 deploy-window summary, W9 correction, that on a day of continuous merges a review taking over about 15 minutes rarely finishes before its own merge request merges; the four cancelled post-restart reviews had run 13 to 32 minutes when their merge request landed.

judgement.cancelledReviewRatioBound.remediation: Raise judgement.cancelledReviewRatioBound in config/limits/judgement.yaml only with evidence that the cancellations are benign; otherwise fix the cancellation cause the report names.
judgement.cancelledReviewRatioBound.rationale: Cancelled jobs divided by terminal jobs, succeeded plus failed plus cancelled, per project and workflow over judgement.hostSuccessWindowDays. Above this ratio, comparator strictly greater than, the workflow is reported as review-past-limit with kind cancelled-ratio; a workflow at exactly the bound is not reported. Queued, running, needs-input and needs-human-decision jobs are excluded from the denominator because they have not yet chosen an outcome. 0.5 sits below both measured cases it must catch, 2,706 of 2,886 terminal review jobs, 0.94, in the 2026-09-24 lessons, and 4 of 5 post-restart reviews, 0.8, in the 2026-09-25 window summary, while leaving room for a journey that cancels a minority of its jobs by design.

judgement.snapshotMaxAgeHours.remediation: Re-export the host job snapshot, or raise judgement.snapshotMaxAgeHours in config/limits/judgement.yaml if a slower export cadence is accepted.
judgement.snapshotMaxAgeHours.rationale: An export whose snapshot timestamp is older than this many hours, comparator strictly greater than, yields a snapshot-stale finding printed first, ahead of every other finding, and the run still reports and exits zero. It is deliberately not a refusal. The export transport needs a VPN session, the maintainer's own key and a sudo credential cache that can expire over a weekend, and only credentials and write or publish authority fail closed in this release; a refusal here would print no sitrep header at all, which is exactly the silence the 2026-09-24 lessons, lesson 1, forbids. 24 matches the daily sitrep cadence, so a sitrep opened on the day of its export never warns and one opened on a stale export always does.

judgement.repeatFailStreak.remediation: Raise judgement.repeatFailStreak in config/limits/judgement.yaml if two consecutive failures of one class prove too noisy to act on; the report never blocks a merge either way.
judgement.repeatFailStreak.rationale: Consecutive critic rounds for one merge request, all with a FAIL verdict and all blocking on one finding class, at or above this count, comparator greater than or equal, are reported as repeat-fail-class. A round is a reviewed head rather than a report, because several critic instances review one head and a split verdict is settled by the FAIL, and a gap in the round numbers is named rather than bridged. Only the class tokens of the items in a report's blocking section are counted, never the ones under residue, which are explicitly non-blocking. Delta reports, which re-review one head after a rebase rather than advancing a round, never join a streak. 2 is the survey recommendation this slice implements, two consecutive failures of the same finding class, and it is also the round cap, because a slice that fails twice on one class has exhausted its rounds and needs escalation rather than a third round.

judgement.exportWindowDays.remediation: Raise judgement.exportWindowDays in config/limits/judgement.yaml, then re-run the printed export query, when a wider window is needed than the current export carries.
judgement.exportWindowDays.rationale: Trailing width, in days, of the read-only host job export query the judgement pass prints for an operator to run, and the width that export declares back. The query is scoped to the newest deployment epoch of each project the deployment serves, so one project's workflows can never vanish from the export and be read as idle. It is deliberately wider than judgement.hostSuccessWindowDays so one export serves a wider window without a second database round trip; an export declaring a width narrower than the window actually being reported is refused rather than silently reported over missing days. 30 is one sitrep month, four times the reported window, and small enough that the export stays a single modest result document on the installed host.

test.localTimeoutMs.remediation: Make the runtime test faster, or give that one case a larger local budget through testTimeoutMs() in packages/runtime/test/helpers/test-timeouts.ts.
test.localTimeoutMs.rationale: Default Vitest testTimeout for runtime tests outside CI. Keeps local and L0 smoke runs failing fast; the four slow suites tracked by issue 974 are measured against this value.

test.ciTimeoutMs.remediation: Make the runtime test faster, or raise test.ciTimeoutMs in config/limits/test.yaml after measuring the slowest supported CI runner.
test.ciTimeoutMs.rationale: Default Vitest testTimeout for runtime tests when CI is set, and the floor for every per-case budget declared through testTimeoutMs(). Shared runners such as content-engineering run far slower under load than a developer host (issue 1009).

test.localHookTimeoutMs.remediation: Make the runtime test hook faster, or pass that one hook a larger timeout.
test.localHookTimeoutMs.rationale: Default Vitest hookTimeout for runtime tests outside CI.

test.ciHookTimeoutMs.remediation: Make the runtime test hook faster, or raise test.ciHookTimeoutMs in config/limits/test.yaml after measuring the slowest supported CI runner.
test.ciHookTimeoutMs.rationale: Default Vitest hookTimeout for runtime tests when CI is set. Shared CI runners run far slower under load than a developer host.

test.pairingProducerLocalHookTimeoutMs.remediation: Profile the pairing producer setup and its teardown, or revise this test-owned local allowance after measuring a supported local host.
test.pairingProducerLocalHookTimeoutMs.rationale: Inherited local scheduling allowance for pairing producer setup before all outcome consumer assertions, preserving the existing 150000 ms local behavior. This is not a measured local duration. A successful normal-user Windows 11 WSL2 CI diagnostic on 2026-10-14 completed producer setup in 179101.422 ms and every unchanged consumer case with clean teardown; that CI observation supports applying the existing test.ciHookTimeoutMs floor through hookTimeoutMs(), not a local timing claim or a global budget increase. A hook timeout neither cancels nor joins unfinished producer setup.

test.journeyLocalTimeoutMs.remediation: Make the journey faster, or raise test.journeyLocalTimeoutMs in config/limits/test.yaml after measuring the slowest journey in packages/runtime/test/journeys.
test.journeyLocalTimeoutMs.rationale: Local Vitest budget for one scripted journey case under packages/runtime/test/journeys (shipped entry point, knowledge first pass, real PiHarness steps, run store). Measured on a shared 11-core developer host with two Vitest workers on 2026-10-07, the slowest journey (create to a patch) took 11.5 s to 15.9 s and review took 12.4 s to 15.3 s; 60000 leaves about 3.7 times the slowest run for host contention while still failing a hung journey within a minute. In CI testTimeoutMs() raises it to test.ciTimeoutMs.

test.applicationExecutionTimeoutMs.remediation: Profile the CLI, live-agent, or native-simulation write applications and their evidence retention, or revise this test-owned budget after measuring a supported host.
test.applicationExecutionTimeoutMs.rationale: Test scheduling budget for complete scripted write applications through CLI, live-agent, and native simulation runners, including source preservation, durable patches, directed-update decision and replay, and stdout-bound writer custody assertions. On normal-user Windows 11 WSL2 on 2026-10-09, the original sequential CLI/live-agent case completed in 22.23 seconds; the directed-update case completed every original assertion in 19.84 seconds after a combined-suite run exceeded its former 20-second deadline; the paired exact/wrong-path native writer case completed every original assertion in 31.44 seconds after exceeding its former 30-second deadline. The unchanged 60000 value leaves scheduling headroom for these measured workloads without changing production execution limits. The CI-aware test helper retains its existing larger floor.

test.nativePilotReplayTimeoutMs.remediation: Profile historical compilation and campaign preparation, or revise this test-owned budget after measuring a supported host.
test.nativePilotReplayTimeoutMs.rationale: Test scheduling budget for three native-pilot campaigns, historical runtime compilation, durable cross-campaign replay refusal, and nonce reuse refusal. The original normal-user Windows 11 WSL2 case completed every unchanged assertion in 75.80 seconds on 2026-10-09; 180000 permits compilation and filesystem variability while preserving the existing CI floor. This is a harness choice, not a model or production authority limit.

test.offlineDeliveryAcceptanceTimeoutMs.remediation: Inspect per-case delivery timings and the final restart and evidence-chain assertions; diagnose an incomplete run before increasing this test-owned budget.
test.offlineDeliveryAcceptanceTimeoutMs.rationale: Test scheduling budget for the complete offline delivery failure matrix, duplicate invocation, three real process restarts, and artifact-chain tampering checks. Normal-user Windows 11 WSL2 measurements on 2026-10-09 show fixture preparation taking 34 to 36 seconds and completed restart cases taking 68 to 80 seconds; the former 600-second deadline interrupted the final restart case and raced teardown. The original case completed every unchanged assertion and clean teardown in 641.73 seconds under the 1200000 budget. This measured host headroom grants no production or publication authority.

test.deployShellSuiteTimeoutMs.remediation: Inspect the completed phase timings on the native Linux runner; if the whole suite still approaches this budget, diagnose the slow phase before reconsidering this test-owned bound.
test.deployShellSuiteTimeoutMs.rationale: Provisional scheduling budget for the complete deploy grant-amendment and renewal shell suites, including all existing phase and refusal assertions. A successful main CI run completed the binding suite in 171.209 seconds, while repeated MR runs reached the former 180-second cap; 360000 leaves about 2.1 times the observed successful CI duration for shared-runner variability. The bound is provisional until the unchanged suites pass through their host:test wrappers on native Linux at the candidate head; it is not a measured necessary or sufficient duration.

test.hostedEditorialRetentionCaseTimeout.remediation: Compare the hosted editorial-retention cases' durations in recent full-lane host:test traces with each job's whole-suite duration; if a case approaches this budget on a lightly loaded runner, find its slow phase before reconsidering this test-owned bound.
test.hostedEditorialRetentionCaseTimeout.rationale: Test scheduling budget for every acceptance case in the host package's hosted editorial-retention test file, and the sealed deadline of each case's one dispatcher attempt. A case runs the installed worker, the editorial replay child and a cold replay child, whose CPU and disk work slows when the runner is loaded, while the host suite runs its other test files concurrently. Across 808 full-lane host:test jobs from 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-14, the case that retains a run record above one physical CAS object passed in 26 to 172 seconds (median 48, 99th percentile 149) and hit the former 180-second budget 12 times, each in one of the 20 jobs whose whole host suite ran slowest. The author case also timed out twice and once passed at 179 seconds (issue 2329). A passing run cannot show a need above 180 seconds, so the need comes from the timeouts. In the slowest, the attempt alone ran 228 seconds before settlement, and the steps after an attempt take about a fifth as long again, about 270 seconds in all. 540000 is about twice that, and the file's six long cases at 540 seconds each (3240 seconds) stay under the 3600-second project job timeout. This test budget grants no production deadline.

test.sourceAcquisitionLocalTimeoutMs.remediation: Profile the complete fixture on supported hosts, retain the existing CI-aware scheduling floor, and revise local allowances only with matched measurements.
test.sourceAcquisitionLocalTimeoutMs.rationale: Retains the existing local thirty-second allowance for source-acquisition cases. The three cases that failed under Windows 11 WSL2 CI passed on exact-source macOS Node.js 25.9 in 13.869, 13.068 and 26.119 seconds. Test registrations use the existing CI-aware helper so loaded CI retains its already declared floor; this is a local allowance, not a new completion claim.

test.sourceAcquisitionReadLocalTimeoutMs.remediation: Profile the complete fixture on supported hosts, retain the existing CI-aware scheduling floor, and revise local allowances only with matched measurements.
test.sourceAcquisitionReadLocalTimeoutMs.rationale: Retains the existing local 120000-millisecond allowance for complete source-reading, window and extraction cases. Applying the existing CI-aware helper restores the declared CI floor without changing this local deadline, assertions, model turns or production source budgets. This centralization is not a new measurement.

test.sourceAcquisitionRaisedLimitsLocalT.remediation: Profile the complete fixture on supported hosts, retain the existing CI-aware scheduling floor, and revise local allowances only with matched measurements.
test.sourceAcquisitionRaisedLimitsLocalT.rationale: Retains the existing local 180000-millisecond allowance for the source case that compares default and raised extraction limits. The CI-aware helper preserves that value on both local and current CI defaults. This test scheduling allowance does not change any source extraction or production execution limit.

test.packedProfileFixtureLocalTimeoutMs.remediation: Profile the complete fixture on supported hosts, retain the existing CI-aware scheduling floor, and revise local allowances only with matched measurements.
test.packedProfileFixtureLocalTimeoutMs.rationale: Centralizes the packed profile-probe fixture existing local 120000-millisecond allowance, including its unchanged child-process deadlines. The full Windows 11 WSL2 run hit the bare outer allowance at 121.452 seconds. The existing CI-aware helper supplies its already declared CI floor to the outer case. This is not a successful completion measurement and does not scale child deadlines, hide cleanup failures or alter real-model qualification criteria.

delivery.readOnlyCommandTimeoutMs.remediation: Check the selected local git or forge CLI and host load, then retry the read. Lower DOCSFAB_DELIVERY_READ_ONLY_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS only to fail faster.
delivery.readOnlyCommandTimeoutMs.rationale: Longest time the existing read-only git/glab runner, now also used for gh auth token, permits one child process to run. Migrates its former 20,000 ms timeout without changing the default. A caller may already provide a separate output bound; this timeout is independent. Operators may lower it to fail faster.

delivery.readOnlyCommandMaxBufferBytes.remediation: Check whether the selected local git or forge CLI produced unexpected output. Reduce its output or use an existing caller-specific maxOutputBytes override when that caller owns a justified larger read.
delivery.readOnlyCommandMaxBufferBytes.rationale: Largest stdout/stderr buffer for one existing read-only git/glab runner command, now also used for gh auth token, when its caller supplies no maxOutputBytes. Migrates the former 2 MiB maxBuffer unchanged. A caller-provided maxOutputBytes continues to replace this default; operators may lower the default to fail faster.

delivery.receiptHelperTimeoutMs.remediation: Check host CPU and filesystem load, then rerun the exact publication recovery command. Lower DOCSFAB_DELIVERY_RECEIPT_HELPER_TIMEOUT_MS only to fail faster.
delivery.receiptHelperTimeoutMs.rationale: Longest time one SCM delivery receipt-store helper (plan, journal, merge-request lease acquisition, or lease cleanup) may run before the store kills its process group and refuses with helper-failed. Moves the former 30 s literal into the catalog without changing it (issue 1050). Coverage runs on the loaded shared CI runner finished whole delivery-receipt-store cases, each several helper exchanges, in 5 to 1,425 ms (jobs 452388748 and 452497486), so 30 s is at least 20 times that worst case. It stays above delivery.receiptPublicationSettleMs so a reader refuses with receipt-invalid before the store kills it. Operators may only lower it.

delivery.receiptPublicationSettleMs.remediation: Check host filesystem load, then rerun the exact publication recovery command. A publication alias that outlives this budget is refused as receipt-invalid; remove it only after no DocsFab publisher is running.
delivery.receiptPublicationSettleMs.rationale: Longest time a receipt-store reader waits for a concurrent writer's publication alias (the second hard link between the writer's link, fsync, and unlink) before refusing the receipt or plan as receipt-invalid. Replaces the former hard-coded 100 polls of 5 ms, about 0.5 s, which a loaded shared disk can exceed during that fsync (issue 1050). On September 22, 2026, locked secrets.env writes including two fsyncs held for at most 215 ms on a loaded macOS shared host; 5 s is about 23 times that and stays below delivery.receiptHelperTimeoutMs. Operators may only lower it.

delivery.mergeRequestLeaseAttempts.remediation: Check whether the publisher process named in the refusal is a DocsFab publisher still delivering the same run; let it finish or stop it, then rerun the exact publication recovery command. If that process is not a DocsFab publisher, stop DocsFab publishers for the receipt root and remove the named lock directory. Lower DOCSFAB_DELIVERY_MERGE_REQUEST_LEASE_ATTEMPTS only to fail faster.
delivery.mergeRequestLeaseAttempts.rationale: Lease helpers one publisher starts while another live publisher holds the merge-request lease for the same delivery before it refuses with receipt-conflict. Moves the former 1,200-attempt literal into the catalog without changing it (issue 1166). Each attempt also waits delivery.mergeRequestLeaseRetryPauseMs, so the publisher waits at least 30 s plus one helper start per attempt. The lease covers one merge-request create-or-adopt exchange, and a lock whose recorded publisher has exited is reclaimed on the next attempt, so only a live holder spends this budget. Operators may only lower it.

delivery.mergeRequestLeaseRetryPauseMs.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_DELIVERY_MERGE_REQUEST_LEASE_RETRY_PAUSE_MS within its catalog range, or raise delivery.mergeRequestLeaseRetryPauseMs in config/limits/delivery.yaml together with a review of delivery.mergeRequestLeaseAttempts.
delivery.mergeRequestLeaseRetryPauseMs.rationale: Pause between two merge-request lease attempts while another publisher holds the lease. Moves the former 25 ms literal into the catalog without changing it (issue 1166). With delivery.mergeRequestLeaseAttempts it sets the minimum wait for a held lease; each attempt also starts one helper process, which costs more than the pause. Operators may only lower it, which shortens the total wait.

delivery.mergeRequestLeaseRecordMaxBytes.remediation: Treat an oversized lease owner record or helper line as tampering; stop DocsFab publishers for the receipt root, inspect the lock, then rerun the exact publication recovery command. DOCSFAB_DELIVERY_MERGE_REQUEST_LEASE_RECORD_MAX_BYTES may only lower the bound to no less than 193 bytes.
delivery.mergeRequestLeaseRecordMaxBytes.rationale: Largest merge-request lease owner record a helper reads, and largest READY or HELD line the store accepts from a lease helper, before it refuses. Replaces the former 256-byte owner and READY literals and the cleanup helper's 384-byte owner literal (issue 1166). DocsFab writes an owner record of at most 193 bytes (two 64-character digests and a safe-integer process ID), which is the minimum, a READY line of at most 54 bytes, and a HELD line of at most 22 bytes. 256 bytes admits every record DocsFab writes and bounds what a tampered one can make a helper read. Operators may only lower it, not below 193.

delivery.runDeliveryIndexEntryMaxBytes.remediation: Treat an oversized run delivery index entry as tampering or a path that exceeds the platform limit; inspect the entry the refusal names, then rerun `docsfab runs show` or the exact publication recovery command. DOCSFAB_DELIVERY_RUN_DELIVERY_INDEX_ENTRY_MAX_BYTES may only lower the bound.
delivery.runDeliveryIndexEntryMaxBytes.rationale: Largest run delivery index entry the publisher writes and `docsfab runs show` reads before it refuses. An entry holds fixed digests, a merge-request URL that the publication-result decoder already caps at 2,048 characters, two branch names capped at 200 characters each, the project path, and the receipt root path, which the platform caps at 4,096 bytes on Linux and 1,024 on macOS. The largest such entry is under 8 KiB, so 16 KiB admits every entry DocsFab writes and bounds what a tampered file can make a reader load. Operators may only lower it; a lowered bound that refuses a write surfaces as run-delivery-index-write-failed with the recovery command.

delivery.runDeliveryIndexEntriesPerKey.remediation: A run or merge request that has reached this many recorded deliveries is outside the supported revision journey; open a new draft merge request from a new run. Lower DOCSFAB_DELIVERY_RUN_DELIVERY_INDEX_ENTRIES_PER_KEY only to fail faster.
delivery.runDeliveryIndexEntriesPerKey.rationale: Most entries one run-delivery index key (one run id, one merge request, or one merge-request path) may hold. Each write reads every entry in its key to skip replays; each run or MR lookup reads its key history and verifies each candidate receipt sequentially to order actual opened transitions, and a path lookup can inspect the numeric history of each distinct project id named by its path key. This bound times delivery.runDeliveryIndexEntryMaxBytes caps bytes read from each index key at about 16 MiB, but receipt reads add bounded time and memory per candidate and path lookup can read multiple keys; it is not a total lookup-byte bound. A run normally has one delivery and a merge request gains one per revision, so 1,000 is far above a revision journey. Entry files use six-digit sequence names, so the maximum must stay at or below 999,999. Operators may only lower it; a write that would exceed it refuses as run-delivery-index-write-failed with the recovery command and drops no entry.

delivery.gitPushTimeoutMs.remediation: Check the network path to the GitLab remote, then rerun the exact publication recovery command. A push that outlives this budget is killed and the delivery stops with push-failed; the receipt keeps the committed state, so the retry pushes the same commit. Lower DOCSFAB_DELIVERY_GIT_PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS only to fail faster.
delivery.gitPushTimeoutMs.rationale: Longest time one leased git push to the publication remote may run before the publisher kills it. It covers the first publication's branch-creating push, an advance's push leased on the observed MR head, and the leased delete of an exact branch revision, which transfers no objects and so fits inside the same budget. Moves the former 120 s literals in git-publisher.ts into the catalog without changing them. A publication push carries one commit over the run's patch, which is bounded by the patch size the preflight accepts. Operators may only lower it.

delivery.gitCommitTimeoutMs.remediation: Check host CPU and filesystem load, then rerun the exact publication recovery command. A commit-tree that outlives this budget is killed and the delivery stops with commit-failed before any ref moves. Lower DOCSFAB_DELIVERY_GIT_COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MS only to fail faster.
delivery.gitCommitTimeoutMs.rationale: Longest time the publisher's local git commit-tree may run while it writes the one publication commit over an already written tree. Moves the former 30 s literal in git-publisher.ts into the catalog without changing it. commit-tree writes one small commit object and reads no working tree, so it matches the 30 s default every other local publisher git command uses. Operators may only lower it.

delivery.gitLsRemoteTimeoutMs.remediation: Check the network path to the GitLab remote, then rerun the exact publication recovery command. An observation that outlives this budget is killed and the delivery stops before it pushes. Lower DOCSFAB_DELIVERY_GIT_LS_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_MS only to fail faster.
delivery.gitLsRemoteTimeoutMs.rationale: Longest time one git ls-remote of the exact publication branch may run before the publisher kills it. The publisher reads the remote branch before and after every push and on every retry, and an advance relies on it to see that the branch still names the observed head. Moves the former 60 s literal in git-publisher.ts into the catalog without changing it. One exact-ref ls-remote transfers a single advertised ref. Operators may only lower it.

delivery.gitConfigurationListingMaxBytes.remediation: Remove from your Git configuration what makes `git config --includes --show-origin --null --list` print more than this many bytes (`git config --includes --show-origin --null --list | wc -c` shows its size), or raise DOCSFAB_DELIVERY_GIT_CONFIGURATION_LISTING_MAX_BYTES within its maximum, then run the same command again. The delivery stops with git-checkout-unverified, and a publication keeps its preserved write.
delivery.gitConfigurationListingMaxBytes.rationale: Largest output of git config --includes --show-origin --null --list that delivery preflight and the host publisher each read before they apply the Git configuration policy to it (#2363). One bound serves both, so a listing that preflight admits is a listing the publisher admits. It replaces preflight's 2 MiB command buffer and the publisher's 1,000,000-byte command output cap, which let a listing between the two pass the check before the model run and fail at publication as remote-drift. Each entry prints its origin, so a listing grows by about 40 to 120 bytes per setting. A developer workstation printed 134,089 bytes for 1,140 settings, and 10,000 aliases in one checkout file printed 371,287 bytes, so 2 MiB is about 15 times the workstation and keeps the former preflight allowance. Both readers hold the output in memory once per check. Operators may lower it, or raise it to 16 MiB for a configuration that includes very many settings.

delivery.validationCandidateCheckoutTime.remediation: Check host CPU and filesystem load, or keep the checkout and the DocsFab state directory on a faster disk, then retry the publication. For a very large repository, raise DOCSFAB_DELIVERY_VALIDATION_CANDIDATE_CHECKOUT_TIMEOUT_MS within its maximum.
delivery.validationCandidateCheckoutTime.rationale: Longest time publication preflight's private copy of the run base plus the verified patch may take to read its tree into the private index, to check the patch against it with git apply --check, or to check that index out, each, before preflight kills the command and refuses (#2359). Before this limit the delivery command runner's 30 s default killed a slow checkout and preflight silently bound the operator checkout instead, which delivery then refused as invalid-delivery-input. Delivery reads at most a 4 MiB ls-tree listing, about 45,000 files. A 30,000-file checkout took 6 to 8 s on a loaded workstation and a 250,000-file checkout took 53 s, so 120 s is about twice the largest measured case. Operators may raise it to 600 s for slow filesystems or lower it to fail faster.

providerAttempt.maxAttemptsPerTurn.remediation: Lower providerAttempt.maxAttemptsPerTurn in config/limits/providerAttempt.yaml, or pass a smaller maxAttempts on the connection's providerTurnRetry policy.
providerAttempt.maxAttemptsPerTurn.rationale: Physical provider requests one governed turn may spend, the first included. Eight is the measured window of live defect 30 (three of 56 route-fault bursts outlasted the former three-attempt window).
providerAttempt.maxAttemptsPerTurn.docSummary: Physical provider requests one governed turn may spend, the first included.

providerAttempt.maxBlankAttemptsPerTurn.remediation: Lower providerAttempt.maxBlankAttemptsPerTurn in config/limits/providerAttempt.yaml; it can never exceed providerAttempt.maxAttemptsPerTurn, whichever is smaller wins.
providerAttempt.maxBlankAttemptsPerTurn.rationale: Physical requests one governed turn may spend on EMPTY provider turns. Held below the transport bound because every replay of an empty turn re-bills the whole input context, which a transport fault that never reached the model does not.
providerAttempt.maxBlankAttemptsPerTurn.docSummary: Physical requests one governed turn may spend on empty provider turns.

providerAttempt.baseDelayMs.remediation: Lower providerAttempt.baseDelayMs in config/limits/providerAttempt.yaml; it must stay at or below providerAttempt.maxDelayMs.
providerAttempt.baseDelayMs.rationale: First deterministic in-turn backoff. No jitter, so replay evidence stays reproducible.
providerAttempt.baseDelayMs.docSummary: First deterministic in-turn backoff; no jitter.

providerAttempt.maxDelayMs.remediation: Lower providerAttempt.maxDelayMs in config/limits/providerAttempt.yaml; a server-requested Retry-After is clamped to it.
providerAttempt.maxDelayMs.rationale: Ceiling on one in-turn backoff, including a honoured Retry-After. Under a fifteenth of the smallest sealed composition timeoutMs.
providerAttempt.maxDelayMs.docSummary: Ceiling on one in-turn backoff, a honoured `Retry-After` included.

providerAttempt.maxTotalDelayMs.remediation: Lower providerAttempt.maxTotalDelayMs in config/limits/providerAttempt.yaml; the composition attempt deadline still bounds every wait.
providerAttempt.maxTotalDelayMs.rationale: Summed backoff across every replay of one governed turn. The seven default waits total 51,500 ms and fit inside it.
providerAttempt.maxTotalDelayMs.docSummary: Summed in-turn backoff across every replay of one governed turn.

providerAttempt.maxPhysicalRequestsPerSt.remediation: Lower providerAttempt.maxPhysicalRequestsPerStep in config/limits/providerAttempt.yaml; the runtime reads the generated catalog mirror, so no host environment variable can widen it.
providerAttempt.maxPhysicalRequestsPerSt.rationale: Physical provider requests one step attempt may spend across all of its governed turns. The per-turn attempt bound bounds one turn only, so without this a step could multiply it by every turn it is allowed. 12288 is the sealed compositionLimits.maxProviderTurns ceiling of 512 times providerAttempt.maxThrottledAttemptsPerTurn, the larger of the two per-turn bounds, so no sealed composition can reach it; operators may only lower it.
providerAttempt.maxPhysicalRequestsPerSt.docSummary: Physical provider requests one step attempt may spend across all of its governed turns.

providerAttempt.maxThrottledAttemptsPerT.remediation: Lower providerAttempt.maxThrottledAttemptsPerTurn in config/limits/providerAttempt.yaml; a turn that runs out ends its step attempt throttled, which then spends the step's transport retries.
providerAttempt.maxThrottledAttemptsPerT.rationale: Physical requests one governed turn may spend while the provider answers HTTP 429, the first included. On build.nvidia.com (runs 28b5d50f and e1fa56af, 2026-10-01) the chance of another 429 stayed near 0.7 after each of 0 to 6 consecutive 429s while the wait grew from 0.5 s to 20 s, so waiting longer does not help and more attempts do. At 0.71, eight attempts leave about 6.5% of turns throttled out, which ended 15 of 31 step attempts in those runs after up to 61 turns of progress; 24 leaves about 0.03% per turn, about 2% across a 60-turn attempt. The rate past 7 consecutive 429s is extrapolated, not measured (pooled 15 of 27 at 7); a turn that still runs out ends its attempt throttled and spends the step's transport retries, not its contract retries. Other transport faults keep providerAttempt.maxAttemptsPerTurn.
providerAttempt.maxThrottledAttemptsPerT.docSummary: Physical provider requests one governed turn may spend while the provider answers HTTP 429.

providerAttempt.maxThrottledTotalDelayMs.remediation: Lower providerAttempt.maxThrottledTotalDelayMs in config/limits/providerAttempt.yaml; the composition attempt deadline still bounds every wait.
providerAttempt.maxThrottledTotalDelayMs.rationale: Summed in-turn backoff across the replays of one governed turn while the provider answers HTTP 429. The 23 default waits of providerAttempt.maxThrottledAttemptsPerTurn total 371,500 ms and fit inside it; other transport faults keep providerAttempt.maxTotalDelayMs. Under a composition that seals a 300,000 ms attempt timer the attempt deadline ends the turn first, and the attempt ends throttled for the step's transport retry.
providerAttempt.maxThrottledTotalDelayMs.docSummary: Summed in-turn backoff across the replays of one governed turn while the provider answers HTTP 429.

secrets.lockWaitMs.remediation: Let the other docsfab setup finish, then rerun docsfab setup. If no docsfab process is running, remove the named lock file.
secrets.lockWaitMs.rationale: Longest time an explicit setup change waits for the configuration-root lock before refusing. The lock covers the whole change, which replaces secrets.env, a model profile, and host.yaml, each through a flushed temporary file. On September 30, 2026, 300 whole-change holds on a loaded macOS shared host (load average about 21) measured p50 89 to 96 ms, p95 259 to 322 ms, and max 453 ms. A September 22, 2026 measurement of secrets.env-only writes found max 215 ms. 15 s therefore queues about 33 writers at the observed worst case and more than 150 at p50, and it stays above secrets.lockStaleMs so a waiter can recover an abandoned lock. A live same-host holder is never taken over, so a longer stall ends in this coded refusal rather than a lost update. Operators may only lower it.

secrets.lockStaleMs.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_SECRETS_LOCK_STALE_MS so effective stale stays below secrets.lockWaitMs, or lower secrets.lockStaleMs in config/limits/secrets.yaml. A live same-host holder is never taken over.
secrets.lockStaleMs.rationale: Age after which a secrets.env lock is treated as abandoned, applied only when its owner cannot be checked, such as a lock written from another host or an unreadable owner record. A lock whose owner runs on this host is never aged out; it is recovered only after that process is gone. 10 s is about 22 times the 453 ms worst whole-change hold measured for secrets.lockWaitMs and stays below that wait bound. A holder that is aged out anyway rechecks its lock token before each file rename, stops with secrets-env-lock-lost, and puts back only the files it replaced that no newer writer has replaced since. Operators may only lower it.

secrets.lockRetryMs.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_SECRETS_LOCK_RETRY_MS, or lower secrets.lockRetryMs in config/limits/secrets.yaml.
secrets.lockRetryMs.rationale: Pause between exclusive-create attempts on the secrets.env lock. It paces the wait loop; secrets.lockWaitMs bounds the total wait. Operators may only lower it.

secrets.configuredCredentialMinChars.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_SECRETS_CONFIGURED_CREDENTIAL_MIN_CHARS, or secrets.configuredCredentialMinChars in the host limits file, to compare a shorter configured credential, or configure a longer credential. docsfab doctor names each configured credential this minimum leaves uncompared.
secrets.configuredCredentialMinChars.rationale: Shortest configured credential value the exact-match screens compare (#1807). This is a minimum, not a capacity allowance. After the owner decision (#1807), an exact match against DocsFab's own credentials is the one credential check that fails closed, so a value short enough to occur by chance in repository text or a model reply would stop runs that carry no credential. 12 is the length the strict credential-value rule and the diagnostic secret redaction already use, and the model keys and the GitLab and Slack tokens DocsFab configures are longer. Operators may lower it, down to 8, the shortest memorized secret NIST SP 800-63B permits, to compare a shorter credential. A value that short can also occur in ordinary text, such as a common word or an identifier, so more runs refuse content that holds no credential. They may raise it, to at most 64, to compare fewer values. docsfab doctor names every configured value the effective minimum leaves uncompared, never the value or its length.
secrets.configuredCredentialMinChars.docSummary: Shortest configured credential value the exact-match screens compare. You can lower it to 8 to compare shorter values, or raise it to 64 to compare fewer.

secrets.configuredCredentialFragmentChar.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_SECRETS_CONFIGURED_CREDENTIAL_FRAGMENT_CHARS, or secrets.configuredCredentialFragmentChars in the host limits file, so that only a longer piece of a configured credential matches. A longer piece lets a shorter truncated echo through.
secrets.configuredCredentialFragmentChar.rationale: Shortest piece of a configured credential the exact-match screens match, so a truncated echo, such as an error message that cuts a key short, still matches (#1807). This is a minimum, not a capacity allowance. 16 is longer than the longest public prefix of a credential DocsFab configures (13 characters, for Anthropic keys), so every piece holds secret characters. Pieces come only from whitespace-free values that are not URLs, and only from the signature of a JWT, so a PEM header, a URL host, or a JWT header that other credentials share never matches. Operators may raise it, to at most 64, so that fewer partial echoes match. It cannot go lower, because a shorter piece could hold only the public prefix of a configured key and would match every example of that key's format.
secrets.configuredCredentialFragmentChar.docSummary: Shortest piece of a configured credential that matches, so a truncated echo is still found. You can raise it to 64 so that only longer pieces match.

secrets.configuredCredentialMinDistinctC.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_SECRETS_CONFIGURED_CREDENTIAL_MIN_DISTINCT_CHARS, or secrets.configuredCredentialMinDistinctChars in the host limits file, to compare a repetitive configured credential, or configure a credential with more distinct characters. docsfab doctor names each configured credential this minimum leaves uncompared.
secrets.configuredCredentialMinDistinctC.rationale: Fewest distinct characters a configured credential value, or a piece of one, needs before the exact-match screens compare it (#1807). This is a minimum, not a capacity allowance. A run such as xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx, a mask left in an environment variable, or the tail of a fixture token of one repeated letter would otherwise match masks, digests, and padding throughout documentation and stop runs that carry no credential. A real credential is random, so every 16-character piece of one holds far more, about 14 distinct characters for base62, 10 for hex, and 8 for the digit runs inside a Slack token. 5 removes repetition and alternation and keeps every one of those. Operators may lower it, down to 1, which turns the rule off, to compare a repetitive password such as one built from a repeated word, and masks and padding then match too. They may raise it, to at most 16, the most a piece of the default length holds, to compare fewer repetitive values.
secrets.configuredCredentialMinDistinctC.docSummary: Fewest distinct characters a configured value, or a piece of one, needs to be compared. You can lower it to 1, which turns the rule off, or raise it to 16.

authority.serviceConfigurationBytes.remediation: Shrink the protected authority service configuration or raise authority.serviceConfigurationBytes in config/limits/authority.yaml.
authority.serviceConfigurationBytes.rationale: Protected authority configuration allowance at the existing declared 1 MiB maximum. It also bounds the accepted job packet a root operator import reads back through the local PostgreSQL peer beside that configuration, and the operation record the import's retain step hands its register step to compare, records far smaller than the configuration they are read with. Custody and parser validation remain required.

authority.credentialFileBytes.remediation: Inspect the protected credential or DSN file and its required format; an oversized substituted payload cannot be accepted as a credential.
authority.credentialFileBytes.rationale: Protected credential/DSN file read allowance at the existing declared 1 MiB maximum. Increasing read capacity neither supplies credentials nor bypasses credential shape, ownership or disclosure checks.

authority.planFileBytes.remediation: Inspect the authority plan file; raise authority.planFileBytes in config/limits/authority.yaml only for a measured plan.
authority.planFileBytes.rationale: Authority plan input allowance at the existing declared 256 MiB maximum. The plan remains data and cannot supply missing owner, credential or publication authority.

authority.projectorTimeoutMs.remediation: Inspect the reference-model projector on the authority host. Restore a lowered allowance to the declared maximum if appropriate; the default is already the supported Node timer maximum. A longer operation requires resumable execution, not a larger timer.
authority.projectorTimeoutMs.rationale: Reference-model projector completion allowance at the supported Node timer maximum, 2147483647 ms. It does not change retry delays, cancellation or authority checks.

authority.projectorOutputBytes.remediation: Inspect the projector output. A lower configured allowance can be restored to the declared maximum; a larger snapshot requires a streaming or paged representation.
authority.projectorOutputBytes.rationale: Reference-model JSON stdout is decoded into one JavaScript string. The declared maximum and default are the supported Node single-string capacity, 536870888 bytes; this is representable capacity, not a measured working-set promise.

semantic.comparisonChunkBytes.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_SEMANTIC_COMPARISON_CHUNK_BYTES within 4096..16777216; retain the sealed value for an existing revalidation directive. Complete payload framing and provider context admission still apply.
semantic.comparisonChunkBytes.rationale: Full supported dispatcher CAS object capacity of 16 MiB, with exact retained payload checks. New budgets above the historical 128 KiB envelope include canon bytes; smaller sealed budgets retain their original partition formula. This is a byte carrier allowance, not a promise of model tokens or permission to truncate sources.

semantic.mergeComparisonTurnBytes.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_SEMANTIC_MERGE_COMPARISON_TURN_BYTES within 4096..16777216; the sealed chunk-budget carrier checks in semantic.comparisonChunkBytes still apply on top of this value.
semantic.mergeComparisonTurnBytes.rationale: One merge comparison's own per-provider-turn byte carrier ceiling, distinct from semantic.comparisonChunkBytes's dispatcher CAS-object capacity. The pilot's hash-heavy JSON measured about 2.3 bytes per provider token (2,334,156 bytes against 1,009,642 tokens), so the former 2 MiB default plus canon and framing reached the 1,000,000-token window. A 1 MiB chunk plus the observed canon and framing leaves substantial room for the configured output allowance and later tool results at that measured density. The approved model's 141 claims (about 88 KB), canon (83-98 KB), and one working merge's 90 KB evidence fit together. Operators can raise this limit for a qualified model or lower it for denser input; provider context admission and lossless narrowing still apply.

semantic.mergeComparisonNarrowings.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_SEMANTIC_MERGE_COMPARISON_NARROWINGS within the declared integer domain; increase it when a retained context or output-limit failure needs more lossless chunk splits.
semantic.mergeComparisonNarrowings.rationale: Number of smaller admissions after a merge comparison chunk fails from exhausted context or a cut answer. The two existing halvings take the former 2 MiB turn through 1 MiB and 512 KiB; the lower 1 MiB default now ends at 256 KiB. The loop also stops when another halving would cross semantic.mergeComparisonTurnBytes's minimum, so increasing this count does not create an unbounded zero-byte turn.

semantic.mergeComparisonCutAnswerRetries.remediation: Leave this at zero to split an output-limited comparison after its first cut; to enable a same-input retry, raise this and the global cut-answer retry budget together within the declared domains.
semantic.mergeComparisonCutAnswerRetries.rationale: The J4 comparison must assess every evidence item. The pilot's 204-item chunk used its full 32,768-token output allowance twice on identical input; an identical retry cannot make the required answer fit. A zero comparison-only cut retry hands the retained output-limit failure to the host's lossless narrowing after the first attempt. Other workflows keep retry.maxCutAnswerRetries.

semantic.stateIndexBytes.remediation: Inspect the immutable index and its logical reference; lower configured admission may be restored within the supported string representation range.
semantic.stateIndexBytes.rationale: UTF-8 JSON index admission uses the supported 64-bit Node single-string representation ceiling for worst-case ASCII. The default admits the full representation and preserves legacy padded indexes; complete logical records remain in independently verified artifact pages. This is not a memory-throughput qualification.

semantic.comparisonRequestBytes.remediation: Reduce the sealed comparison chunk or qualify a coordinated carrier change; this is the widest serialized worker request any workflow may present, and the worker refuses a larger descriptor before parsing it.
semantic.comparisonRequestBytes.rationale: Names the complete worker-request boundary for a governed semantic comparison. The chunk travels as an object inside a request that also carries canon as a JSON string, so the boundary reserves JSON's longest encoding of every admitted chunk byte on top of the ordinary request envelope, less the ordinary frozen-input aggregate the chunk replaces. It is a representation boundary, not measured memory throughput, and it is the pre-parse descriptor ceiling for every workflow.
