semantic.jobPollIntervalMs.remediation: Configure DOCSFAB_SEMANTIC_JOB_POLL_INTERVAL_MS within the declared domain, or supply an explicit cadence inside it; the submitted comparison still ends at the project's configured executor timeout.
semantic.jobPollIntervalMs.rationale: Journal poll cadence while a submitted semantic comparison job runs. Ten observations a second keeps a short comparison responsive without holding the journal open continuously; a slower journal can be given a wider cadence. The maximum is the Node timer representation boundary, not a completion promise, and the refusal that ends a run is still the configured executor timeout.

semantic.suggestionRationaleMaxChars.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_SEMANTIC_SUGGESTION_RATIONALE_MAX_CHARS up to 1000, or leave it and let the comparison write a shorter rationale; an over-long rationale is dropped and the message carries DocsFab's default suggestion instead.
semantic.suggestionRationaleMaxChars.rationale: Longest rationale that may sit beside a suggested reply on the first Slack message of a PRM decision. The line is one plain sentence read at a glance, so the default allows about two lines of Slack text, enough to name what the claim says and why the merge does or does not change it. A longer rationale is never cut. The comparison's suggestion is dropped, the drop is named on the comparison result, and the message shows DocsFab's own default suggestion marked as such. Fresh comparison replies use the effective allowance; a stored comparison outcome is read back under the catalog maximum, so lowering the allowance never invalidates one. The ceiling of 1000 characters keeps the line well inside the first message's part allowance beside its other fields.

feedback.git.metadataOutputBytes.remediation: Inspect the sealed Git configuration. Restore a lowered allowance to the declared maximum if appropriate; larger metadata requires streaming or paging instead of one buffered string.
feedback.git.metadataOutputBytes.rationale: Git config stdout is decoded as UTF-8 into one JavaScript string before NUL-separated key parsing. The maximum and default use the supported Node single-string capacity, 536870888 bytes, also used for projector output. This is representable capacity, not a measured working-set promise. Parsing and protected-path checks apply independently.

feedback.git.commandTimeoutMs.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_FEEDBACK_GIT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS within max on a slow host or change feedback.git.commandTimeoutMs in config/limits/feedback.yaml; then rerun the complete witness.
feedback.git.commandTimeoutMs.rationale: Largest supported Node timer delay for one fixed local Git command. The default is 2147483647 ms; this is a completion allowance, not a retry delay. Cancellation and outer job deadlines remain effective.

feedback.git.commandOutputBytes.remediation: Inspect the complete Git observation; adjust this protected allowance within the supported representation range and retry the complete observation.
feedback.git.commandOutputBytes.rationale: Fixed local Git command output is consumed as UTF-8 tree and commit metadata or exact blob bytes. The default admits the full supported 64-bit Node single-string representation for worst-case ASCII; current read grants and complete source custody remain independent. This is not measured machine throughput.

feedback.git.blobBytes.remediation: Inspect the complete Git observation; adjust this protected allowance within the supported representation range and retry the complete observation.
feedback.git.blobBytes.rationale: Complete Git source blobs are independently retained and interpreted as UTF-8 when supported. The default admits the full supported 64-bit Node single-string representation for worst-case ASCII, with explicit extraction obligations for other content. No source is truncated to this allowance.

feedback.deliveryRequestMaxBytes.remediation: Reduce the candidate's retained file set or cited source inventories, or raise feedback.deliveryRequestMaxBytes in config/limits/feedback.yaml and re-freeze the service catalog so the SQL mirror moves with it.
feedback.deliveryRequestMaxBytes.rationale: Largest canonical JSON a single feedback delivery request may occupy in the mailbox. The default, 16777216 bytes, matches the existing content-addressed object bound so a submitted request cannot exceed what its custody store already admits. The PostgreSQL retain function repeats this number as a frozen mirror because the database refuses independently of the caller.

feedback.mailboxReadBatch.remediation: Lower feedback.mailboxReadBatch in config/limits/feedback.yaml so one anchor lookup reads fewer rows before the delivery pump refuses; raising it only widens what a duplicated or corrupted namespace may stream back.
feedback.mailboxReadBatch.rationale: Rows one merged-change anchor lookup may read before the delivery pump refuses. The lookup is pinned to exactly one merge request key, so a healthy namespace answers with exactly one row and the pump refuses every other count as a source collision. The default, 100 rows, is the ceiling on what a duplicated or corrupted namespace can stream back before that refusal. There is no cursor and no second pass, so one lookup reads one anchor.

feedback.workerLeaseMs.remediation: Raise or lower feedback.workerLeaseMs in config/limits/feedback.yaml within its declared range; the database refuses the same range independently, so a value outside it is rejected at the claim rather than silently clamped.
feedback.workerLeaseMs.rationale: How long one publication-authority claim on a delivery request stays valid before another worker may take it. The default, 30000 ms, leaves a crashed worker's request claimable within half a minute while a live worker renews well inside it. The declared minimum and maximum are mirrored verbatim by the SQL claim and renew functions, which refuse independently of the caller.

feedback.workerPollMs.remediation: Lower feedback.workerPollMs in config/limits/feedback.yaml for a shorter wait between publication passes, or raise it within max to reduce idle database load; it is a wait, never a deadline.
feedback.workerPollMs.rationale: How long a released delivery request waits before the publication authority may claim it again, and the cadence at which an idle worker asks for one. The default, 5000 ms, matches the component status heartbeat cadence so one idle pass and one heartbeat share a rhythm. This is a retry delay, not an operation timeout.

feedback.workerHeartbeatFloorMs.remediation: Raise feedback.workerHeartbeatFloorMs in config/limits/feedback.yaml if a very short lease makes renewals too frequent for the database; the effective cadence is the larger of this floor and a quarter of the lease.
feedback.workerHeartbeatFloorMs.rationale: Shortest interval between two lease renewals while a publication pass holds a claim. The effective cadence is the larger of this floor and one quarter of the lease, so a lease at its declared minimum still renews three times before expiry without issuing renewals faster than this floor. The default, 100 ms, keeps a minimum-lease renewal loop off the busy path.

feedback.claimRetryMaxMs.remediation: Lower feedback.claimRetryMaxMs in config/limits/feedback.yaml to shorten the longest accepted back-off a release may ask for; the SQL release and advance functions repeat this ceiling and refuse a larger value independently.
feedback.claimRetryMaxMs.rationale: Largest back-off a publication pass may request when it releases or advances a delivery request. The default, 86400000 ms, is one day, and a request parked longer than that is an operator matter, not a retry. The SQL release and advance functions carry this number as a frozen mirror because the database refuses independently of the caller.

governance.maxCompactions.remediation: Lower the override or reduce context pressure.
governance.maxCompactions.rationale: Successful compaction spends one provider turn. The effective allowance is clamped to the admitted attempt turn envelope; this catalog ceiling follows the largest admitted provider-turn envelope, not a separately guessed compaction cap.

governance.maxConsecutiveLengthStoppedTo.remediation: Keep tool arguments within the output limit or lower the override.
governance.maxConsecutiveLengthStoppedTo.rationale: A rejected truncated tool batch still spends one admitted provider turn. Default permits recovery through the admitted turn envelope; the effective allowance and remaining turns both bound continuation, while cumulative tokens and elapsed time remain authoritative.

governance.minRecentToolTurns.remediation: Reduce context pressure or lower the preservation minimum to at least one group.
governance.minRecentToolTurns.rationale: Inherited preservation policy retains one recent complete tool group. This is a minimum rather than a capacity allowance; increasing it reduces compaction freedom. The largest useful preservation count is the largest admitted provider-turn envelope; the default deliberately preserves existing semantics.

execution.grepGroupCleanupMs.remediation: Inspect and terminate the named grep process group if it remains alive, then retry the step. Raise the catalog value only after confirming why cleanup exceeded the deadline.
execution.grepGroupCleanupMs.rationale: One wall-clock deadline for credential-safe grep completion and cleanup, starting when a valid result is accepted or an abort or failure enters cleanup. It covers cooperative worker close, any hard stop of the owned process group, and confirmation that the child and group are gone. Normal local cleanup completes in milliseconds; five seconds allows slow shared hosts without granting a second budget after a cooperative stall. A timed-out cleanup reports the owned group ID and retains its process state for operator recovery. Operators may only lower it.

execution.grepGroupPollMs.remediation: Lower DOCSFAB_EXECUTION_GREP_GROUP_POLL_MS for finer process-group cleanup observation.
execution.grepGroupPollMs.rationale: Interval between observations of the owned credential-safe grep process group after SIGKILL. Twenty-five milliseconds keeps cleanup responsive without a busy loop; the separate cleanup deadline bounds the total wait. Operators may only lower it.

execution.normalModeTokenBudgetTurns.remediation: Reduce cumulative token use or revise normal-mode budget admission.
execution.normalModeTokenBudgetTurns.rationale: Existing normal-mode cumulative token authority multiplies the selected per-turn token limits by this count. Recovery allowance changes preserve that budget; separate capacity work may revise its admission.

execution.normalModeMaxElapsedMs.remediation: Reduce attempt duration or revise normal-mode budget admission.
execution.normalModeMaxElapsedMs.rationale: Existing normal-mode elapsed-time authority. Recovery allowance changes preserve this timer; it is independent of composition timeout configuration.

execution.readLoopRepeatStreak.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_EXECUTION_READ_LOOP_REPEAT_STREAK (up to 400) if a step legitimately re-reads one unchanged result many times, or narrow the step's scope.
execution.readLoopRepeatStreak.rationale: Re-reads of one unchanged result, within one step attempt and with no new progress call (write, edit, claim, conflict gap, artifact or quality candidate) between, that the host still re-sends in full with a notice before it sends only the notice. A re-read counts only when the same read-class call returns the same model-visible bytes in the same context epoch, so nothing new, changed, from another range, or lost to a compaction is ever withheld, and the earlier bytes are still in context. Counted per result because every measured loop re-read one result. On the 2026-10-01 Inference Hub matrix (development evidence) Ultra 7d8293c8 and bad283ee made one read per turn at exactly 29 output and +73 input tokens for 90+ turns, and Super 6b60e933 and 644e2300 made 120 reads in a 20-file, 25 KB fixture at a steady +78 to +110 input tokens per turn, the signature of one small file. A legitimate verification pass re-reads many results once each and is never withheld by this bound; execution.readLoopUnchangedReReads bounds the total across results. Steps that finished read at most 22 times (gpt-6-sol), 17 (Super) and 16 (Ultra) on the same fixture, so 8 re-reads of one result is far beyond a legitimate re-check, and it costs at most 8 wasted turns against 100 or more. The maximum restates the per-step tool-call ceiling, compositionExecution.maxToolCallsPerStep, at which the notice-only stage never arms.
execution.readLoopRepeatStreak.docSummary: Re-reads of one unchanged result the host still re-sends in full before sending only a notice.

execution.readLoopWithheldReads.remediation: The step re-read unchanged content instead of finishing. Retry the step (the correction policy decides), narrow its scope, or raise DOCSFAB_EXECUTION_READ_LOOP_WITHHELD_READS (up to 400).
execution.readLoopWithheldReads.rationale: Further re-reads of one unchanged result the host answers with a notice only, after execution.readLoopRepeatStreak, or of any unchanged result after execution.readLoopUnchangedReReads, before it ends the attempt as no-progress. A new successful write, edit, claim, conflict-gap, artifact or quality-candidate call resets every count; an identical repeat of such a call does not. It gives the model as many notice-only turns to finish as it had full repeats, so a loop's worst case is 8 + 8 + 1 = 17 re-reads of one result instead of the 126-call cap or the 300 s attempt timer seen in the same matrix runs (7d8293c8, bad283ee, 6b60e933, 644e2300). The stop is recoverable through the step correction policy, which owns the no-progress retry decision. On that retry, every tool call the host denies after it withdraws the tools and asks for the answer spends the same allowance, so a model that ignores the ask stops with this code within 8 more calls rather than running denied calls up to compositionExecution.maxToolCallsPerStep (400 in a scripted probe). The maximum restates the per-step tool-call ceiling, compositionExecution.maxToolCallsPerStep.
execution.readLoopWithheldReads.docSummary: Notice-only re-reads, of one unchanged result or past the cross-result allowance, plus tool calls denied after a conclude-now ask, before the host ends the step attempt as no-progress.

execution.readLoopUnchangedReReads.remediation: The step cycled through results it had already read instead of finishing. Retry the step (the correction policy decides), narrow its scope, or raise DOCSFAB_EXECUTION_READ_LOOP_UNCHANGED_RE_READS (up to 400).
execution.readLoopUnchangedReReads.rationale: Unchanged re-reads across all results, within one step attempt and with no new progress call between, that the host still re-sends in full. Past it every further unchanged re-read is answered with a notice only, and execution.readLoopWithheldReads more notice-only answers end the attempt as no-progress through the same stop and conclude-now retry as the per-result bound. It closes the gap the per-result count leaves, where a model that cycles through several unchanged results never re-reads any one of them 17 times. A compaction does not reset the count, but a re-read after a compaction is new evidence and is not counted, so nothing missing from the context is withheld. Keeping the count through compactions also closes a second gap - a model that re-reads one file in every epoch between compactions, which resets the per-result count each time, now stops on this code. Measured with docsfab runs query over the indexed run records of the 2026-10-01 Inference Hub matrix rounds and worker lanes (development evidence), from 2026-10-01T16:04Z, when records began to carry the read-loop counters - 331 succeeded attempts in 71 runs made at most 12 unchanged re-reads, counting the live runs of the change that added this bound, while Super 62f25796 evaluate-document-quality cycled 7 results for 84 unchanged re-reads (at most 13 of one) and Ultra 53646a46 test-audience-understanding made 65 (at most 2 of one), each ending at the 126-call tool ceiling. 16 leaves 33 percent headroom over the largest finished attempt, and the stop at 16 + 8 + 1 = 25 unchanged re-reads lands near call 70 of 62f25796 instead of 126. A pure one-result loop still stops at 17 under the per-result bound. The maximum restates the per-step tool-call ceiling, compositionExecution.maxToolCallsPerStep.
execution.readLoopUnchangedReReads.docSummary: Unchanged re-reads across all results, with no progress call between, the host still re-sends in full before it sends only a notice and starts spending the notice-only allowance.

execution.readerSourceNominations.remediation: Name fewer reader sources. A continued run re-admits the original run's reader sources plus the files its InputAsk fills add, so start a new run with `docsfab run update-documentation` and fewer --reader-source options.
execution.readerSourceNominations.rationale: Reader sources one update run admits, explicit --reader-source nominations plus change-scope paths, counted before any source is read. Reader admission introduced the value in 4cbec2eda (2026-09-14) as a hand-declared constant; this entry catalogs it unchanged, so no supported run that admitted before is refused now. It bounds per-run admission work ahead of the per-source and retained byte bounds. The run record's readerEvidenceRequest decoder and the do --continue union of retained and filled sources enforce the same value, so a continuation never admits more than the original admission could and the writer never keeps a list a strict reader refuses. There is no override, because the decoder checks stored records against this value, and a record written under a raised host value would not decode on a host at the default.
execution.readerSourceNominations.docSummary: Reader sources one update run admits, explicit `--reader-source` nominations plus change-scope paths. A continued run counts the original run's sources plus the files its InputAsk fills add.

execution.styleResourceMaxBytes.remediation: Shorten the bound style profile's delivered files, or name fewer of them in packages/quality/profiles/product-default.json, then run npm run generate:quality-pack from packages/runtime.
execution.styleResourceMaxBytes.rationale: Most bytes of judgment text the host admits from the bound style profile, counted over every file the product-default declaration delivers. The writer, reviewer, and evaluator steps each receive the whole text in their prompt, so this bound caps how much one style resource adds to each of those prompts. The host resolves the resource once at run admission, before any model call, and an oversized one refuses the run there with this code, the observed size, and the resource id. The host never delivers part of a rule. Measured 2026-10-05 - the bound profile:nvidia-technical-documentation delivers style-guide.md (2,810 bytes) and TERMINOLOGY.md (1,433 bytes), 4,243 bytes or about 1.1k input tokens per step. 32,768 bytes is about 8k input tokens, which leaves room for a fuller guide and is an eighth of the smallest context window a registered composition declares (65,536 tokens in packages/runtime/model-compositions/composition-registry.json). No override tier, because the resource is product-authored Pin C content and a larger guide is a qualification change, not an operator allowance.
execution.styleResourceMaxBytes.docSummary: Bytes of judgment text the host admits from the bound style profile and gives to the writer, reviewer, and evaluator steps.

writeAuthority.maxPatchBytes.remediation: Produce a smaller patch, or qualify the grant minting, the worker patch evidence, the sealed terminal encoder and the reading line ceiling together before raising the patch capacity.
writeAuthority.maxPatchBytes.rationale: One shared raw-patch admission for a minted scoped-write grant, the worker's patch evidence and the sealed terminal. A sealed terminal carries the patch inside JSON with metadata and escaping, so a patch at this capacity does not fit a terminal line of the same size; the complete encoded terminal is measured on its own and must not be treated as the same envelope.

writeAuthority.maxTargets.remediation: Narrow the grant's target list, or qualify the minting producer and this reader together before raising the count.
writeAuthority.maxTargets.rationale: Admitted number of write targets in a minted scoped-write grant and in the worker's patch evidence. The count is a work allowance only, and target identities, preimage object ids, the permitted file mode and the path ceiling stay independent authority checks that a larger count cannot relax.

writeAuthority.maxCeilingEntries.remediation: Express the write scope with fewer ceiling entries, or qualify the minting write-scope policy and this reader together before raising the count.
writeAuthority.maxCeilingEntries.rationale: Admitted number of path-ceiling entries in a sealed scoped-write grant. The minting policy and this reader already share one exported constant, so they cannot drift apart; the number is an allowance and not the cardinality of a closed enumeration.

writeAuthority.maxWriteStepIds.remediation: Mint a grant whose write-step list fits the admitted shape; a longer installed write-step catalog needs this capacity and the installed workflow qualified together.
writeAuthority.maxWriteStepIds.rationale: Admitted length of the write-step identifier list on a scoped-write grant. It is a shape bound only, and the grant's write steps are still compared for exact identity against the installed workflow's write steps, so a caller-minted count can never widen write authority.

authoring.plannedPageMaxBytes.remediation: Split the planned page into smaller pages, or remove a lowering override of authoring.plannedPageMaxBytes; its value in config/limits/authoring.yaml already equals its maximum, the maximum of repository.trackedWriteAdmissionMaxBytes, and cannot rise.
authoring.plannedPageMaxBytes.rationale: Bytes of one planned page the authoring host reads into memory when it copies sealed candidate 0 into the revision workspace and when it restores candidate 0 before a revision retry. There the observed value is the page's byteLength in candidate 0's sealed snapshot, and every page is checked before any is read or written, so a refusal reads no page bytes and restores no page. Measured 2026-10-02 on representative documentation repositories the largest tracked Markdown page was 151133 bytes (DocsFab), 67262 bytes (NeMo Curator) and 234336 bytes (a generated report page), so 32 MiB is about 143 times the largest. The maximum is the maximum of repository.trackedWriteAdmissionMaxBytes, the bound in repository/workspace/tracked-read.ts that recaptures every written planned page before a candidate seals. A page over the admission bound in force never seals, so a higher value would be dead. Both candidate seals refuse such a page by the admission bound's code before admission, so a lowering override of this limit binds only at the copy and the reset. Override may only lower it.

authoring.workspaceSnapshotMaxEntries.remediation: Run authoring against a repository with fewer tracked entries, or raise authoring.workspaceSnapshotMaxEntries in config/limits/authoring.yaml after qualifying the snapshot digest and record size.
authoring.workspaceSnapshotMaxEntries.rationale: Tracked entries in one complete authoring workspace snapshot. Each candidate seal, revision preparation, observation, reset and selected promotion lists every tracked entry and digests them as one record, and an incomplete snapshot would authenticate nothing. Measured 2026-10-02 the representative repositories carried 6119 (DocsFab), 2062 (NeMo Curator) and 4114 (a catalog repository) tracked entries, so 100000 is 16 times the largest. Override may only lower it.

authoring.workspaceSnapshotMaxBytes.remediation: Run authoring against a smaller repository, or raise authoring.workspaceSnapshotMaxBytes in config/limits/authoring.yaml after qualifying the workspace export and snapshot together.
authoring.workspaceSnapshotMaxBytes.rationale: Sum of tracked regular-file bytes one complete authoring workspace snapshot admits. The snapshot records each entry's size and digest, not its bytes, so this bounds the authenticated repository, not memory. The observed value is the complete sum, not the running sum at the crossing. Measured 2026-10-02 the representative repositories held 85921640 (DocsFab), 36009272 (NeMo Curator) and 51190732 (a catalog repository) tracked bytes, so 2 GiB is about 25 times the largest. Override may only lower it.

authoring.candidatePatchMaxBytes.remediation: Plan fewer or smaller pages so the candidate patch is smaller. Raising authoring.candidatePatchMaxBytes in config/limits/authoring.yaml needs the authoring candidate record's patch size bound raised and qualified with it.
authoring.candidatePatchMaxBytes.rationale: Bytes of one sealed authoring candidate patch artifact the host reads back into memory, verifies and retains for the selected candidate. Sealed because the authoring candidate record admits patchBytes up to the same value, and a reader below the record it verifies would refuse a candidate it had already sealed; the record still declares that value itself, a remaining catalog migration onto this entry. The git patch capture buffers at most repository.evidenceGitOutputMaxBytes (80 MiB), so every patch it can produce fits; one created planned page at authoring.plannedPageMaxBytes yields a patch of that size plus one byte per line.

authoring.pageTemplateGuidanceMaxBytes.remediation: The planner and writer still run without that template's guidance, and the prompt names the omission. Raise authoring.pageTemplateGuidanceMaxBytes in config/limits/authoring.yaml, or set DOCSFAB_AUTHORING_PAGE_TEMPLATE_GUIDANCE_MAX_BYTES, to include it.
authoring.pageTemplateGuidanceMaxBytes.rationale: Bytes of one governed template's structure guidance, measured as its JSON text, that the host adds to a documentation planner or writer prompt. Each selected template is stated once per step however many planned pages map to it. Measured 2026-10-08 over template-set-v1, the largest guidance was 6071 bytes (about-feature-myst) and the smallest 1612 bytes (key-features-gfm), so 32 KiB is about 5 times the largest and leaves room for a larger template revision, while a prompt carries at most one copy of each template. Guidance over the bound is omitted with this observation, never truncated.

reconciliation.answerTextMaxBytes.remediation: Reduce the reply or restore the configured answer allowance up to the full Slack message capacity.
reconciliation.answerTextMaxBytes.rationale: Full-message capacity for a structured Slack decision, including its field headers. 40,000 characters at four UTF-8 bytes each require 160,000 bytes. Fresh intake uses the effective allowance; retained authority and knowledge replay use the catalog maximum so lowering intake never invalidates an accepted decision.

reconciliation.sourceFailuresMax.remediation: Raise the configured source-failure allowance only after the cause is known to be transient; a permanent cause quarantines on its first pass regardless.
reconciliation.sourceFailuresMax.rationale: Transient source-stage failures one merged change may record before it is quarantined. The source stage runs before any coordination attempt exists, so neither the generation budget nor the convergence budget covers it. Three spaced failures absorb a busy mirror or a dropped connection without holding the outbox open; a deterministic cause never consumes the budget at all. The ceiling of 16 matches the generation bound, above which a stuck effect would outlive an operator's attention.

reconciliation.sourceRetrySpacingMs.remediation: Restore the configured spacing so a transient cause cannot exhaust the source-failure allowance inside a single drain pass.
reconciliation.sourceRetrySpacingMs.rationale: Spacing between two durably recorded failures of one kind for one merged change. The source and convergence budgets have no lease to wait on, so without spacing two of three failures burn in one pump run and the one-second poll wake produces the third, quarantining a real merge within about a second. Sixty seconds matches the lease margin a generation already waits. Zero is admissible for a test clock; the one-hour ceiling keeps a mistyped value from parking an effect past an operator's shift.

reconciliation.ownPrmMergePromotionWaitM.remediation: Restore the configured wait; while the feedback publication component is stopped, its own PRM merges are compared as ordinary merges once this wait passes.
reconciliation.ownPrmMergePromotionWaitM.rationale: How long the reconciliation of DocsFab's own accepted-PRM merge waits for the publication authority to promote that merge as the next approved generation before it is compared as an ordinary merge, measured from the merge. A healthy component promotes within a few of its polls; six hours covers a component restart or a stopped-host window with about twice the headroom, and a stalled promotion never holds the merge's comparison past a working day. Zero compares at once, which a test clock uses; the week-long ceiling keeps a mistyped value from parking a merge indefinitely.

reconciliation.slackPartMaxChars.remediation: Restore the configured Slack part allowance, or reduce the offered statement and scope text.
reconciliation.slackPartMaxChars.rationale: One Slack message renders about 3,000 characters before the client collapses it behind a show-more control. A complete offer must stay readable without truncation, so the split point is set below that rendering threshold with room for the leading part marker. The text is never shortened; a longer offer becomes more parts. The root message of a decision opens with a header (the owner, the project and the merge, and the reply line) that needs about 220 characters with a short project name and a repository link, beside the first part of the details, so the allowance cannot go below 500, because a smaller one could not hold even the header. A header whose names are long enough to need more is refused with this limit's code when it is built.

reconciliation.offerPartsMax.remediation: Restore the configured part allowance, or split the decision into separate claims so each offer fits.
reconciliation.offerPartsMax.rationale: The whole offer is posted as one thread of consecutive messages that a Maintainer has to read before replying. Sixty-four parts at the per-part character allowance carry about 180,000 characters, far beyond any real statement and scope delta, and bound both the posting burst and the persisted delivery record.

reconciliation.reminderBusinessHours.remediation: Set a whole number of business hours no longer than the longest business-time span, 720 business hours.
reconciliation.reminderBusinessHours.rationale: Business hours an asked question waits without an answer before one reminder is posted in its thread. Only hours inside the deployment's business days count, so a weekend or a company closure never shortens the wait. One business day is the owner's default. The ceiling of 720 business hours is thirty business days, the longest business-time span the host computes.

reconciliation.widenBusinessHours.remediation: Set a whole number of business hours no longer than the longest business-time span, 720 business hours.
reconciliation.widenBusinessHours.rationale: Business hours an asked question waits before it is widened from the people it first asked to every admitted Maintainer. Counted on business days only. Two business days is the owner's default, one business day after the reminder. The ceiling matches the longest business-time span the host computes.

reconciliation.productOwnerBusinessHours.remediation: Set a whole number of business hours no longer than the longest business-time span, 720 business hours.
reconciliation.productOwnerBusinessHours.rationale: Business hours the asked Maintainers have to reach consensus before the designated product owner is asked to make the final call. Counted on business days only. Four business days is the owner's default, after the widening. The ceiling matches the longest business-time span the host computes. This is a known, unresolved conflict. Today the reconciliation severity policy seals each question to close at most seven calendar days after it is asked, and in a week with company closures four business days can take longer than that, so the product owner's call can land after the question has stopped taking answers. Question sealing must count business time before this timer is used.

reconciliation.questionExpiryBusinessDay.remediation: Set a whole number of business days from 1 through 30.
reconciliation.questionExpiryBusinessDay.rationale: Business days an asked question is meant to stay open before it expires unanswered. A business day is 24 business hours counted only inside the deployment's business days. Seven business days is the owner's default. The ceiling of thirty business days, about six calendar weeks, is the longest business-time span the host computes; elapsed-time and deadline computations both refuse a longer span, which also bounds how many calendar days one computation walks. This is a known, unresolved conflict. Today the reconciliation severity policy seals each question to close at most seven calendar days after it is asked, which comes before seven business days whenever the span holds a weekend day or a closure, so this expiry takes effect only once question sealing counts business time.

reconciliation.businessCalendarMaxBytes.remediation: Remove years that no open question can still reach from the business calendar record, or restore the configured allowance.
reconciliation.businessCalendarMaxBytes.rationale: Largest sealed business-calendar record the host reads at start. A year of company closures is about twenty dated entries of under a hundred bytes each, so decades of closures fit in 64 KiB. The bound refuses a mistaken file, such as a log or an archive, before it is parsed.

reconciliation.businessCalendarClosedDat.remediation: Remove years that no open question can still reach from the business calendar record, or restore the configured allowance.
reconciliation.businessCalendarClosedDat.rationale: Most closed dates one business calendar record may list. Twenty closures a year for twenty-five years is five hundred. The bound keeps the record, and every business-time computation that consults it, small.

reconciliation.businessCalendarExpiryWar.remediation: Renew the business calendar record with the next year's closures through a receipted registry amendment before its last vouched date, or restore the configured warning window.
reconciliation.businessCalendarExpiryWar.rationale: Calendar days before a business calendar's last vouched date on which the host names it expiring rather than current. Renewing it takes the next year's published closures, a review and a stopped-host amendment window; sixty days leaves room to schedule all three. Past the last vouched date holidays count as business time, so the warning has to come first. The ceiling of 366 days, one year, is as far ahead as a yearly renewal can usefully warn.

projectDecision.optionsMax.remediation: Reduce the numbered options on the tracker issue to the configured allowance, or split the decision into separate issues.
projectDecision.optionsMax.rationale: Numbered options a project-decision question offers a Maintainer in one Slack message. The reply names a single ordinal, so a single-digit ordinal keeps the answer one unambiguous token and keeps the offered set and the replied set comparable without a parser. Two is the floor because a question with one option is not a decision. Nine is the ceiling because a tenth option needs a second digit and because an unbounded list is not a bounded human question; a longer list belongs in the issue body the question cites.

projectDecision.optionMaxChars.remediation: Shorten the numbered option on the tracker issue to a one-paragraph summary and keep the detail in the issue body.
projectDecision.optionMaxChars.rationale: One numbered option, and the issue title the question cites, rendered into the question message and into the recorded decision card. An option is a one-paragraph summary a Maintainer reads on a phone; the supporting detail stays in the issue the question cites and is never copied into the channel. Forty characters is the floor because a shorter option cannot carry a distinguishable choice. A thousand characters is the ceiling because the whole question, with its options and its reply grammar, must still fit one Slack message.

projectDecision.questionMaxChars.remediation: Shorten the decision title or its numbered options on the tracker issue so the rendered question fits one message.
projectDecision.questionMaxChars.rationale: The whole rendered decision question, posted as exactly one message. A Slack client renders about three thousand characters before it collapses the message behind a show-more control, and a decision question that a Maintainer cannot read whole is a question they answer partly informed. This question is never split into parts, unlike a merge-reconciliation offer, because an ordinal reply must be bound to one visible option list. Two hundred characters is the floor because the reply grammar and the authority sentence alone need that much.

projectDecision.fieldMaxChars.remediation: Shorten the Rationale or Reversibility line in the reply and keep the long form in the tracker issue.
projectDecision.fieldMaxChars.rationale: One structured reply field, the rationale or the reversibility sentence a Maintainer types. Both become fields of the decision card that is pasted onto the tracker issue, where they have to stay readable next to the chosen option rather than becoming a document. One character is the floor so a deployment may demand only that the field be present and non-empty. Four thousand is the ceiling; it stays inside the full-message allowance the structured Slack answer intake already applies to the whole reply, so a field bound can never admit text the intake refuses.

projectDecision.questionTtlMs.remediation: Restore the configured decision-question lifetime; re-ask the decision after it expires rather than extending a question nobody answered.
projectDecision.questionTtlMs.rationale: How long a posted decision question stays answerable before a reply is refused as expired. A project decision waits on a human calendar, not on a stalled merge, so the lifetime is a week rather than the day a merge-conflict question gets, because the named authority may be away and re-asking is cheap while an answer bound to a stale option list is not. One hour is the floor so a test clock and a same-day decision are both expressible. Thirty days is the ceiling because a question open longer than a month is evidence that nobody owns the decision, and the issue it cites will have moved underneath it.

projectDecision.openQuestionsMax.remediation: Answer or let the open decision question expire before asking another, or raise the configured allowance for concurrent decisions.
projectDecision.openQuestionsMax.rationale: Decision questions one project may have open in its channel at once. Every open question is an unanswered interruption addressed to the same small group of Maintainers in the same thread-bearing channel, and two of them race for the same attention while making it ambiguous which thread a bare ordinal answers. One is the default because a project that cannot finish one decision does not benefit from a second. Eight is the ceiling, because beyond that the channel is a queue and a queue needs its own surface rather than a larger allowance.

projectDecision.issueDocumentMaxBytes.remediation: Shorten the tracker issue description, or raise the configured document allowance only if the forge's own description ceiling has risen.
projectDecision.issueDocumentMaxBytes.rationale: Largest single tracker-issue document the decision reader parses for its labels and its numbered options. The forge caps an issue description at 1,048,576 characters and the JSON envelope that carries it roughly doubles that, so this is the provider's own ceiling expressed in bytes rather than a tuning choice; a larger body is refused before parsing rather than during it. Sixty-four kibibytes is the floor because a real decision issue with its options and its template card already approaches it.

publicExport.checksBudgetMs.remediation: Read the check's log to see where it stalled and fix it in the exported tree, or raise publicExport.checksBudgetMs in config/limits/publicExport.yaml while it stays below the project's job timeout.
publicExport.checksBudgetMs.rationale: The deadline of one unit of a public-export dry run. A run is split into units, one per CI matrix job -- the tree checks (gitleaks, the boundary gate, npm ci, check:static, check:pins), each of the four runtime fast-lane shards, the runtime isolation tests, and the knowledge, quality and skills suites -- and each unit's checks run in order against a deadline of their own, which starts at the unit's first check. A run with no --group runs every unit in turn, so it takes at most eight deadlines and never lets one unit spend another's; --group runs one group's units, and --shard one runtime shard. A check still running at its unit's deadline has its process group killed and is reported as timed out, and every later check of that unit is reported as not run, with this refusal code and the unit's name or, for a check that needs one that did not pass, with that check's name, so the report and summary always name what did not run. The five tree checks took 602 s together on the exported tree of 7518c9f73, built on a contended developer host without a warm npm cache on 2026-09-29 (npm ci 347 s, check:static 238 s, gitleaks 11 s, check:pins 6 s); on CI runners with their npm cache, runtime:static (npm ci plus check:static) took 38 to 91 s across the six successful main pipelines 70327514 to 70438241. The source's own CI jobs for the other suites, in main pipelines 70668871 to 70686237, took 238 to 249 s (knowledge:test), 72 to 95 s (quality:acceptance), 377 to 520 s for each of the four runtime:test lanes, about 1900 s together, and 195 to 451 s for each of the three runtime:isolation lanes, 1025 to 1118 s together, each job time including its own npm ci. The whole runtime fast lane would pass one deadline, so it is four units. In the dry-run matrix of merged-results pipeline 70699825 on 2026-09-30, the units' checks took 26 s (tree), 62 s (package-tests), 207 to 270 s (each runtime shard, npm ci included) and 558 s (isolation). On a contended developer host (load average 20 to 25 on 11 cores) the package-tests unit took 1414 s on the exported tree of 9a8a34366. 1800000 ms leaves every unit at least 1.6 times its CI time, and the slowest local measurement room to spare, and it leaves half of the project's 3600 s job timeout for the clone, the export build and the artifact upload. The max keeps any raised deadline 600 s below that job timeout. No CLI flag or environment variable overrides it.

publicExport.reportTailLines.remediation: Open logs/<check>.log in the job artifact for the full output, or raise publicExport.reportTailLines in config/limits/publicExport.yaml.
publicExport.reportTailLines.rationale: Last lines of each failing check's output that the public-export dry run quotes in its report.md. A longer log is quoted by its last lines, with its total line count and the path of the full log, which the job always uploads, so nothing is dropped silently. On the exported tree of 7518c9f73 on 2026-09-29 the failing check:pins log was 11 lines, npm ci 13 lines and a whole check:static run 99 lines, whose failing step prints last; npm 11 appends no error block of its own to a failing script. 60 lines quote each of those failures whole, or the end of a check:static run, without letting one check bury the others. No CLI flag or environment variable overrides it.

publicExport.jobLogReportBytes.remediation: Open report.md in the job artifact, which is never clipped, or raise publicExport.jobLogReportBytes in config/limits/publicExport.yaml while it stays well below the runner's job log limit.
publicExport.jobLogReportBytes.rationale: Bytes of report.md that the public-export dry run prints to its job log. A longer report is printed up to this many bytes, cut at a character boundary rather than a line, so one minified line cannot escape it, and followed by a line that names this bound, the bytes shown and the report's total; report.md and summary.json in the job artifact stay complete. GitLab Runner's default output_limit stops a job log at 4096 KiB, and this job's log also carries its own test run and the gitleaks install. On main at dca7d08b3 on 2026-09-29 the printed report was 24225 bytes (623 lines, the longest 554 bytes) in a 32444-byte job log, with 81 gitleaks findings listed. 262144 bytes is about ten times that report and a sixteenth of the runner default. The min still holds the result line, the check table and the first failing check; the max keeps a raised value at half the runner default. No CLI flag or environment variable overrides it.

publicExport.pushGitTimeoutMs.remediation: Read the job log for the git command that stalled and check that GitHub is reachable from the runner, then play the job again; raise publicExport.pushGitTimeoutMs in config/limits/publicExport.yaml only when the transfer itself needs longer.
publicExport.pushGitTimeoutMs.rationale: The deadline of each git network command of the public-export push to the public repository, which are the ls-remote of its main, the fetch of that branch's history, and the push. A command still running at the deadline has its process group killed, and the push stops with this refusal code, naming the command, the deadline and how long it ran. The first push carries the whole exported tree. On main at 5b7719f00 on 2026-09-30 the exported repository held 3335 files, a 9.58 MiB pack, which a push to a repository on the same disk sent in 0.26 s, so the rest of any push's time is the network's. Each later push sends only the blobs a changed tree adds, and each fetch the public history, which grows by one such commit per pushed tree. The dry-run tree job on the same runners downloads its pinned gitleaks release from github.com, so those runners reach GitHub. 600000 ms carries the 9.58 MiB first push at 16 KiB/s, far below a working link, and still reports a stalled connection within one job; the max keeps three commands at their deadline 900 s under the project's 3600 s job timeout, for the clone and the artifact download. There is no automatic retry. A stopped push leaves the remote branch where it was or at the commit the push made, and playing the job again re-reads it and knows that commit as the export's. No CLI flag or environment variable overrides it.

modelProfile.nvidiaNemotron3SuperHostedM.remediation: Set MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS to 32768 or less for experimental discovery on the NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super hosted API Catalog endpoint.
modelProfile.nvidiaNemotron3SuperHostedM.rationale: The NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super hosted API Catalog Chat Completions endpoint documents max_tokens up to 32768 (https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/reference/nvidia-nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b-infer). This is the endpoint's documented request allowance, not evidence that a DocsFab workflow needs or reliably uses that many output tokens. The scope vocabulary has no per-request value, so per-run is the closest catalog scope; runtime applies this as a cap on each provider request's configured output allowance. Applied only by explicit experimental answer-record discovery for this exact installed composition and route; the sealed composition remains unchanged.
modelProfile.nvidiaNemotron3SuperHostedM.docSummary: Documented output-token request ceiling for explicitly selected Nemotron 3 Super hosted-endpoint discovery.

modelProfile.conservativeFallbackMaxOutp.remediation: Set maxOutputTokens in the model profile YAML to the output limit your endpoint serves, or change modelProfile.conservativeFallbackMaxOutputTokens in config/limits/modelProfile.yaml and regenerate the mirrors.
modelProfile.conservativeFallbackMaxOutp.rationale: Output allowance `docsfab setup` writes for an endpoint that matches no installed composition, and so the per-turn max_tokens an unmatched endpoint receives until the operator edits the profile. It must hold the longest single DocsFab answer without a cut. On September 30, 2026, a hosted Nemotron 3 Super review-documentation run with reasoning off produced a 32,254-character quality evaluation answer of 7,750 output tokens; the former 4,096 cut it, and the one continuation dropped characters at the seam. 16,384 holds twice that answer. It is a request allowance, not a context ceiling; the provider still enforces its own window.
modelProfile.conservativeFallbackMaxOutp.docSummary: Output tokens per turn that setup writes for an endpoint that matches no installed composition.

modelProfile.conservativeFallbackContext.remediation: Set contextWindow and maxInputTokens in the model profile YAML to the window your endpoint serves, or change modelProfile.conservativeFallbackContextWindow in config/limits/modelProfile.yaml and regenerate the mirrors.
modelProfile.conservativeFallbackContext.rationale: Context and input window `docsfab setup` writes for an endpoint that matches no installed composition. An unmatched, unattested profile skips DocsFab context admission, so this value is not an executable ceiling; a profile's output allowance must not exceed its window, so it is twice modelProfile.conservativeFallbackMaxOutputTokens, which also leaves room for the context reserve if the operator later attests the profile.
modelProfile.conservativeFallbackContext.docSummary: Context window that setup writes for an endpoint that matches no installed composition.

endpointProbe.requestTimeoutMs.remediation: Rerun the probe when the provider responds faster, or raise endpointProbe.requestTimeoutMs in config/limits/endpointProbe.yaml.
endpointProbe.requestTimeoutMs.rationale: Longest wait for one live probe request from docsfab profile probe --live or docsfab doctor --live (#1691), the timeout the model-matrix probe has used since it was written. Each probe asks for one short sentence, one tool call, or one short JSON object. A request that exceeds it is reported as an availability timeout with provider-capacity ownership, never as a pass.

endpointProbe.reasoningSampleMaxTokens.remediation: Raise endpointProbe.reasoningSampleMaxTokens in config/limits/endpointProbe.yaml when a model needs more output tokens to show where its text arrives.
endpointProbe.reasoningSampleMaxTokens.rationale: Output budget for each reasoning-split sample (#1691). A sample only has to show whether text arrives in content or in reasoning_content, which the first tokens settle; the model-matrix probe has used 128 since the September 2026 hosted-model probes.

endpointProbe.maxOutputTokens.remediation: Probe with docsfab doctor --live, which uses the configured effective output limit, or raise endpointProbe.maxOutputTokens in config/limits/endpointProbe.yaml.
endpointProbe.maxOutputTokens.rationale: Output limit docsfab profile probe --live sends with its tool-call and JSON requests when no host profile supplies one (#1691). On September 30, 2026, hosted DocsFab runs sent 4,096 output tokens per turn and first-pass turns are bounded at 4,096, so a model that cannot finish one tool call inside 4,096 tokens cannot finish a DocsFab turn. The same day a hand-built 1,024-token probe cut Nemotron 3.5 Lightning off before its tool call. A cut is reported as an output-limit finding, never as a missing capability.

endpointProbe.providerMessageMaxChars.remediation: Raise endpointProbe.providerMessageMaxChars in config/limits/endpointProbe.yaml to keep a longer provider error body.
endpointProbe.providerMessageMaxChars.rationale: Characters of a refused probe response body that DocsFab reads to quote the provider's own message (#1691). Provider end-of-life, not-found, and rate-limit bodies observed on September 30, 2026 were under 200 characters; 400 is the bound the model-matrix probe already used. A longer body is marked truncated in the verdict.

endpointProbe.credentialEchoMinChars.remediation: Lower endpointProbe.credentialEchoMinChars in config/limits/endpointProbe.yaml when a provider echoes shorter fragments of the credential; raise it only if ordinary provider wording is being removed.
endpointProbe.credentialEchoMinChars.rationale: Shortest run of characters copied from the probe credential that DocsFab removes from provider text before it bounds or quotes it (#1691). Raw, JSON-escaped, and URL-encoded echoes count, and invisible characters or line breaks inside the run do not split it. A provider that masks a key shows a prefix and a suffix, such as 8 characters, four asterisks, and the last 6; at 6 both visible halves are removed, and at most 5 characters of the key can survive anywhere. For a 70-character random base-62 key, any 6 characters of provider wording match one of its runs with a probability near one in a billion, so ordinary words stay. At 4, provider wording such as x-api-key would lose `api-`, which every nvapi- key contains.

endpointProbe.answerSubmissionSamples.remediation: Raise endpointProbe.answerSubmissionSamples in config/limits/endpointProbe.yaml when a route's answers to the same probe request disagree and more samples are needed to say which way it usually goes; each sample is one live request per variant.
endpointProbe.answerSubmissionSamples.rationale: Requests docsfab doctor --live --answer-submission sends for each of its variants (#1707). The nominal plan is V1, V3, V4 and V6, so 12 requests; the typed-shell contingency (V2, then V3, V4 and V6 typed) runs only with --answer-submission-typed-contingency. The probe binds the composition's temperature-0, top_p-1 request policy, so repeat samples do not measure model sampling; they detect server-side nondeterminism, such as batching, routing across replicas, or a tool-call parser that differs from call to call. Three identical outcomes make a systematic property of the route, and any disagreement is itself recorded as a finding.

endpointProbe.answerSubmissionTransportR.remediation: Raise endpointProbe.answerSubmissionTransportRetries in config/limits/endpointProbe.yaml only when V6 transport failures keep a probe inconclusive and the cost owner approves the extra requests; each retry is one more live V6 request.
endpointProbe.answerSubmissionTransportR.rationale: Most V6 requests docsfab doctor --live --answer-submission re-sends after a transport failure (HTTP status 0) that is not a response byte bound (#1707). Only V6 is retried, each sample at most once. The one transport failure observed so far was a V6 sample, the large, long-running turn, under the old 120-second probe timeout; V6 now runs on the bound attempt timer. Smaller variants have shown no transport failures, so theirs make the probe inconclusive without a retry. Two retries let two of V6's three samples each recover once. At the defaults one run sends at most 14 requests without the typed-shell contingency and at most 26 with --answer-submission-typed-contingency, which needs the cost owner's approval.

endpointProbe.answerRecordSamples.remediation: Keep endpointProbe.answerRecordSamples in config/limits/endpointProbe.yaml at 3 or lower; more seeds per rung need a budget amendment from the cost owner, because each seed is one live request per rung.
endpointProbe.answerRecordSamples.rationale: Seeds docsfab doctor --live --answer-records sends at each rung (#1967, design closed-schema-answer-records-decision.md §6.1). The plan is phase A at 0.5, 2, 4 and 8 KiB, phase B at about 6 KiB, 10 KiB and the per-message budget maximum, and phase C at 4 KiB, so 8 rungs and 24 requests at 3 seeds, the approved MR 1a spend (O10). The composition's temperature-0 policy makes repeat seeds a check of server-side nondeterminism and of distinct real records, and a rung counts only when every seed is admitted.

endpointProbe.answerRecordTransportRetri.remediation: Keep endpointProbe.answerRecordTransportRetries in config/limits/endpointProbe.yaml at 2 or lower; the approved probe spend shares 2 transport retries across the 1a and 1b runs.
endpointProbe.answerRecordTransportRetri.rationale: Most requests docsfab doctor --live --answer-records re-sends after a transport failure (HTTP status 0) that is not a response byte bound (#1967, design §4.4 and §6.1, N20). Each sample is re-sent at most once, and a re-send is withheld when it would push the run past endpointProbe.answerRecordInputTokenBudget. The approved spend (O10) is 2 retries shared across the untyped (1a) and typed (1b) runs, so a 1b run takes what 1a left, which the 1a observation records. The small-group run (--answer-record-small-groups) never draws on them; its re-sends spend only the slice-1a remainder (decision of October 7, 2026).

endpointProbe.answerRecordRequestBudget.remediation: Lower endpointProbe.answerRecordSamples, or ask the cost owner for a budget amendment before raising endpointProbe.answerRecordRequestBudget in config/limits/endpointProbe.yaml.
endpointProbe.answerRecordRequestBudget.rationale: Most planned requests one docsfab doctor --live --answer-records run may send, transport retries excluded (#1967, design §6.1 and O10, approved October 6, 2026). The 1a plan is 12 phase A, 9 phase B and 3 phase C requests at endpointProbe.answerRecordSamples = 3. The probe refuses before any request when its plan exceeds this.

endpointProbe.answerRecordTypedRequestBu.remediation: The typed 1b request tranche is exhausted or too small for the A-t plan. Review retained typed-shell observations and the current recorded allocation before raising the host override; do not exceed the authorized typed request ceiling.
endpointProbe.answerRecordTypedRequestBu.rationale: Default typed-shell allocation remains 17. The declared override range admits the separately approved one-time 28-request tranche for the exact qualification matrix; retained typed requests are charged against that cumulative ceiling. This request tranche does not create an independent input-token allowance.

endpointProbe.answerRecordInputTokenBudg.remediation: Use the approved task-local host override only for the exact pinned qualification matrix; the padding target P comes from the committed answer-record corpus. Preserve the 600000 default and do not exceed the authorized cumulative ceiling.
endpointProbe.answerRecordInputTokenBudg.rationale: Default cumulative input ceiling remains 600000. The declared override range admits the separately approved one-time 800000 cumulative ceiling for the exact typed qualification matrix (194034 planned incremental tokens after 579352 retained); the probe refuses before any request when its planned total exceeds the effective limit and withholds any request or retry that would cross it. This limit is charged across retained 1a and 1b observations.

endpointProbe.answerRecordGroupRequestBu.remediation: Nothing or too little of the approved record-probe requests is left after the runs recorded under answer-record-probes/. Ask the cost owner for a budget amendment before raising endpointProbe.answerRecordGroupRequestBudget in config/limits/endpointProbe.yaml; never remove a retained observation to free budget.
endpointProbe.answerRecordGroupRequestBu.rationale: Approved requests for the record-probe slice that docsfab doctor --live --answer-records --answer-record-small-groups draws on, as a ledger (#1967; R9 decision of October 7, 2026). The approval is 24 requests (O10). Each small-group run takes off every request the untyped probe's retained observations under answer-record-probes/ sent, re-sends included, plus any reservation a run left unfinished, which charges all that was left when it started (typed-shell premise runs spend a separate approval), and the premise run (evidenceSha256 a556782a…0605, 13 requests) must be among them, so the first small-group run has 11. The plan is 6 requests (2 and 3 records per message × 3 seeds). The probe refuses before any request when the plan exceeds what is left, and never sends a re-send past it. Re-sends are paid from it, never from endpointProbe.answerRecordTransportRetries, which stays for the typed (1b) run.

endpointProbe.answerRecordGroupInputToke.remediation: Nothing or too little of the approved record-probe input tokens is left after the runs recorded under answer-record-probes/. Ask the cost owner for a budget amendment before raising endpointProbe.answerRecordGroupInputTokenBudget in config/limits/endpointProbe.yaml; never remove a retained observation to free budget.
endpointProbe.answerRecordGroupInputToke.rationale: Approved input tokens for the record-probe slice that docsfab doctor --live --answer-records --answer-record-small-groups draws on, as a ledger (#1967; R9 decision of October 7, 2026). The approval is 600,000 input tokens (O10). Each small-group run takes off what the untyped probe's retained observations under answer-record-probes/ charged, each sample at the larger of its reported and estimated input, the rule the runs themselves charge by, plus any reservation a run left unfinished, which charges all that was left when it started. The premise run (evidenceSha256 a556782a…0605) charged 78,193 (the provider reported 66,258), so the first small-group run has 521,807. The plan pads 6 prompts to P (60,588 tokens in the 2026-10 corpus), about 363,500 tokens, which leaves room for 2 padded re-sends. The probe refuses before any request when the plan exceeds what is left, and withholds a request or re-send that the reported counts say would cross it.

endpointProbe.answerRecordDecodeWindowMi.remediation: Change endpointProbe.answerRecordDecodeWindowMinBasisPoints in config/limits/endpointProbe.yaml only with a probe observation whose tool-call argument timing shows a different stream shape; a lower value lets a burst at the end of the response pass as a decode window.
endpointProbe.answerRecordDecodeWindowMi.rationale: Shortest share of a sample's elapsed time, prefill included, in basis points, that the window from its first to its last tool-call argument delta must cover before docsfab doctor --live --answer-records computes the decode rate r from that window (#1967). On build.nvidia.com Nemotron 3 Super on October 6, 2026 every single-record call streamed its arguments in one burst at the end (TTFT within 0.2 s of elapsed), and the old rate, output tokens over elapsed minus TTFT, read 25,980 tokens/s against about 100 measured end to end. A route that streams arguments as they decode covers most of the elapsed time. One that sends each call whole when it completes covers the decode of all but the first call, about (k − 1)/k of the decode in a k-call message, and less of the elapsed time once a padded prompt's prefill is counted, so a 2-record message of short records can land near 25% and the rate source can differ from one seed to the next; every rate names its source. A burst at the end covers well under 25%. Below it the probe reports the end-to-end rate, output tokens over elapsed time with prefill included, and labels its source.

answerRecords.maxOpenRecordsPerSet.remediation: Withdraw or replace an open-set record before adding another; raise answerRecords.maxOpenRecordsPerSet in config/limits/answerRecords.yaml only with a new content-free corpus measurement that shows real answers need more.
answerRecords.maxOpenRecordsPerSet.rationale: Most records one open set (step 8 findings) may hold at once (closed-schema-answer-records-decision.md §4.4); the only record count the declaration does not fix. Measured on 2026-10-07 over content-free statistics committed for issue 1969 (internal evidence answer-record-limits-2026-10) - the 22 staged Nemotron Super step 8 answers (!1430, !1426) hold 0 to 14 findings (median 3, p90 8), all 82 staged evaluations across five models at most 14, and the 14 recorded S6 answers at most 10 - so 1.5 × the largest (14) gives 21. With 36 required and 3 optional step 8 keys and answerRecords.maxRefusalsPerKey, it sizes the derived record-call ceiling at (36 + 3 + 21) × 4 = 240 calls per step.

answerRecords.maxRefusalsPerKey.remediation: Inspect the refused record key's receipts and codes in the saved run, then start a new run; raising answerRecords.maxRefusalsPerKey in config/limits/answerRecords.yaml above retry.maxRetries gives one record more corrections than a whole answer gets.
answerRecords.maxRefusalsPerKey.rationale: Most refusals one record key may take in one step before the next refusal stops the step with answer-record-exhausted (closed-schema-answer-records-decision.md §3.3 and §4.4, N20). A record gets the corrections a whole answer gets per step, so it equals retry.maxRetries (3); it is a separate limit because its scope is one key in one step, not one step attempt. It also sizes the derived record-call ceiling, (required keys + optional keys + answerRecords.maxOpenRecordsPerSet) × (1 + answerRecords.maxRefusalsPerKey) per step.

qualityValidator.maxOutputBytes.remediation: A locked quality validator or the deriver wrote more than qualityValidator.maxOutputBytes to stdout or stderr, so the host stopped it and the check failed; inspect the retained run, and raise the value in config/limits/qualityValidator.yaml only with a new measurement of validator output.
qualityValidator.maxOutputBytes.rationale: Most bytes the quality validator host reads from one python3 spawn's stdout, and separately its stderr, before it stops the spawn and fails the check (closed-schema-answer-records-decision.md §1.2 and §4.4, N10; was MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES in quality-validator-host.ts). Measured on 2026-10-07 (#1969 internal evidence answer-record-limits-2026-10) over 325 spawns of the evaluation, score, and report validators and the deriver on the quality fixtures, 82 archived staged step 8 answers, and synthetic worst cases - largest stream 11,004 B (evaluation validator stderr with every dimension broken; 2,362 B on real answers; the report validator at most 1,803 B with every summary field broken). 2 × that maximum is 22,008 B, so the existing 65,536 B fits and stays.

qualityValidator.timeoutMs.remediation: A locked quality validator or the deriver ran past qualityValidator.timeoutMs, so the host stopped it; check the host's python3 runtime and load, and raise the value in config/limits/qualityValidator.yaml (at most its max) only with a new wall-time measurement.
qualityValidator.timeoutMs.rationale: Longest wall time the quality validator host gives one python3 spawn of a locked validator or the deriver (closed-schema-answer-records-decision.md §1.2 and §4.4, N10; was DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS and the constructor's 60,000 ms ceiling in quality-validator-host.ts, now this row's value and max). Measured on 2026-10-07 at a host load average near 17 (#1969 internal evidence answer-record-limits-2026-10) - p100 239 ms for the evaluation validator, 101 ms for the score validator, 243 ms for the report validator, and 206 ms for the deriver, so p100 × 2 is under 500 ms. The 15,000 ms default stays as headroom for a cold python3 start on a loaded CI runner; a host may pass a lower timeout up to the max.

qualityValidator.maxDerivedArtifactBytes.remediation: The deriver wrote a larger output file than qualityValidator.maxDerivedArtifactBytes, which is a DocsFab defect (quality-derivation-failed); report it with the retained run, and raise the value in config/limits/qualityValidator.yaml only with a new measurement of the largest step 8 answer and fact.
qualityValidator.maxDerivedArtifactBytes.rationale: Largest derivation output file the quality validator host reads back from the deriver (closed-schema-answer-records-decision.md §1.2 and §4.4, N10, N12) - 2 × (41,465 B, the largest recorded step 8 answer, run f339f3d0, + 30 facts × 836 B, the largest recorded fact) = 133,090 B. The largest measured deriver output is 39,912 B (fixture b), about 30% of it (#1969 internal evidence answer-record-limits-2026-10). A larger, missing, symlinked, or undecodable output stops the step with quality-derivation-failed.

requestIntent.maxTargets.remediation: The interpretation proposed more targets than one request may name and is re-asked for fewer; split the request into smaller requests if the operator really means more pages.
requestIntent.maxTargets.rationale: Targets one request-intent proposal may name, across write and companion roles. The largest pilot shape (restructure-sdk-reference) splits one reference page into about four task pages plus its navigation file, five targets; thirty-two leaves more than six times that headroom for a section restructure while keeping per-target admission and the list shown back to the operator small.

requestIntent.maxQuotes.remediation: The interpretation quoted more passages than one request may carry and is re-asked for fewer; shorten or split the request if it really holds more clauses.
requestIntent.maxQuotes.rationale: Quotes in one proposal, counted over every quote-bearing field together (targets, sources, preserve, exclusions, constraints, and the authority preference). Each quote is grounded against the whole instruction, so this caps grounding work at this count times the instruction length. The longest pilot request has about ten clauses; sixty-four is six times that.

requestIntent.maxQuoteChars.remediation: The interpretation quoted a passage longer than the bound and is re-asked for a shorter quote of the clause it relies on.
requestIntent.maxQuoteChars.rationale: Length of one proposal quote in UTF-16 code units before normalization. A quote is a slice of the operator's instruction, and the pilot requests run from 172 to 326 characters; two thousand admits a quote of a whole multi-paragraph request with six times headroom over the longest one seen.

requestIntent.maxQuestionChars.remediation: The interpretation wrote a question or consequence longer than the bound and is re-asked for a shorter one.
requestIntent.maxQuestionChars.rationale: Length of the model's question text, and separately of its stated consequence, in UTF-16 code units. One decision question is read whole in a chat message; this matches projectDecision.fieldMaxChars, the precedent for one rendered decision field, so the full question with its options fits one message.

requestIntent.maxQuestionOptions.remediation: The interpretation offered more options than one question may carry and is re-asked for fewer.
requestIntent.maxQuestionOptions.rationale: Options one question offers. Matches projectDecision.optionsMax, the precedent for a decision question a person answers with one ordinal; a single-digit ordinal keeps the reply one unambiguous token.

requestIntent.maxOptionChars.remediation: The interpretation wrote an option longer than the bound and is re-asked for a shorter one.
requestIntent.maxOptionChars.rationale: Length of one question option in UTF-16 code units. Matches projectDecision.optionMaxChars, the precedent for a one-paragraph option a person reads on a phone.

requestIntent.maxInventoryEntries.remediation: The host passed a larger repository inventory than request-intent admission accepts; reduce the tracked tree, or raise requestIntent.maxInventoryEntries together with repository.inventoryMaxEntries.
requestIntent.maxInventoryEntries.rationale: Inventory paths the host passes to admission so an inventory-chosen target can be checked by exact membership. The inventory comes from the tracked-tree inventory, so this equals repository.inventoryMaxEntries; a smaller value would refuse a repository the inventory already admits.

requestIntent.maxNavigationEntries.remediation: The host passed more navigation and index files than request-intent admission accepts; reduce the tracked tree, or raise requestIntent.maxNavigationEntries together with requestIntent.maxInventoryEntries and repository.inventoryMaxEntries.
requestIntent.maxNavigationEntries.rationale: Existing navigation and index files the host passes so a companion target can be checked by exact membership. Every entry is a tracked file, so the set is never larger than the tracked-tree inventory; this equals requestIntent.maxInventoryEntries, and a smaller value would refuse a repository the inventory already admits.

requestIntent.maxWriteScopeEntries.remediation: The host passed more write-scope entries than request-intent admission accepts; pass fewer, broader documentation roots, or raise requestIntent.maxWriteScopeEntries.
requestIntent.maxWriteScopeEntries.rationale: Entries in the write scope the host passes, roots and single files together. The shipped producer passes the run's resolved documentation roots, at most thirty-two because .docsfab.json admits no more, plus one file entry for each target the roots do not govern (an update target chosen from the inventory, or a restructure target), at most requestIntent.maxTargets. Sixty-four is that sum, which a test pins, and caps the per-target scope comparison at that count.

requestIntent.maxDocsRootEntries.remediation: The host passed more documentation roots than request-intent admission accepts; pass fewer, broader roots, or raise requestIntent.maxDocsRootEntries.
requestIntent.maxDocsRootEntries.rationale: Documentation roots the host passes, under which a create target must sit. The shipped producer passes the run's resolved documentation roots, at most thirty-two because .docsfab.json admits no more; the same sixty-four as requestIntent.maxWriteScopeEntries keeps the two lists interchangeable and caps the per-target root comparison at that count.

requestIntent.maxPromptInventoryEntries.remediation: The repository holds more tracked documentation pages under the documentation roots than one interpretation prompt lists. Raise requestIntent.maxPromptInventoryEntries with DOCSFAB_REQUEST_INTENT_MAX_PROMPT_INVENTORY_ENTRIES or the host limits file, up to its maximum, or narrow documentationRoots in .docsfab.json. The larger prompt must still fit the bound model profile's input window, or the run stops with request-intent-model-input-budget before any model call.
requestIntent.maxPromptInventoryEntries.rationale: Tracked Markdown and MDX pages under the documentation roots that one interpretation prompt lists, each with its path and title, so the model can choose an existing page instead of inventing one. Measured 2026-10-06, a FastMCP checkout holds 598 such pages under docs/ and a Kueue checkout 1014 under site/content; the DocsFab repository held 115 (2026-10-05). Two thousand is more than three times FastMCP and about twice Kueue. A measured FastMCP prompt costs about 23 estimated tokens per page, and a test pins that two thousand pages with 80-character paths and titles, under every root admission accepts, fit the smallest shipped model profile's input window. With every path and title at their bounds a page costs about 133 tokens, so near nine hundred such pages the prompt passes the smallest window; the interpretation then stops with request-intent-model-input-budget before any call instead of listing a subset, because a page left off the list would read as absent. The maximum equals requestIntent.maxInventoryEntries, since the prompt lists a subset of the tracked inventory; an operator may raise this limit up to it for a profile with a larger window.

requestIntent.maxInventoryTitleChars.remediation: A page title longer than the bound is shown to the model cut with an ellipsis; the run record and the INTENT section count every cut title. Shorten the page title if the cut hides what the page is.
requestIntent.maxInventoryTitleChars.rationale: Characters of one page title or navigation label in the interpretation prompt inventory, in UTF-16 code units. A title identifies the page; the DocsFab documentation titles run under 80 characters. The interpretation cuts a longer title with an ellipsis and counts the cut on the run record instead of refusing, because the path, not the title, is what the model names and admission matches.

requestIntent.maxInventoryPathChars.remediation: A tracked documentation page path is longer than the interpretation prompt lists; rename or move the page to a shorter path.
requestIntent.maxInventoryPathChars.rationale: Characters of one page path in the interpretation prompt inventory, in UTF-16 code units. A path is what the model names and admission matches exactly, so it is never cut; the interpretation refuses a longer one. Measured 2026-10-05 the longest DocsFab documentation page path is 80 characters; 256 is three times that and bounds the prompt budget together with requestIntent.maxPromptInventoryEntries.

requestIntent.interpretationTimeoutMs.remediation: The request interpretation did not finish before its deadline and the run stopped with request-intent-model-deadline before any step; retry once the provider responds, or check the provider with docsfab doctor --live.
requestIntent.interpretationTimeoutMs.rationale: Wall-clock deadline for the whole request interpretation, every model call and re-ask included, before the first workflow step. The effective deadline is the smaller of this and the bound composition's timeoutMs. One interpretation is one bounded prompt and at most retry.maxRetries re-asks; five minutes leaves each of the four calls more than a minute for a prompt near the smallest shipped input window. Override may only lower it.

artifacts.maxObjectBytes.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_ARTIFACTS_MAX_OBJECT_BYTES, or artifacts.maxObjectBytes in the host limits file, above the observed size (at most 536870887 bytes), then rerun the same command. Stored objects are unchanged.
artifacts.maxObjectBytes.rationale: Largest single object the durable artifact store writes or reads when its caller names no tighter bound, and the per-object bound hosted editorial evidence retention applies to the same objects (#1932). It replaces a hand-declared 16 MiB literal that stopped vLLM Semantic Router (about 10,000 tracked files) before any model call, because its 17,410,521-byte content index was written as one object. The content index now splits into parts whenever it exceeds this bound, so repository size alone never reaches it; 128 MiB keeps the whole index of a repository of about 79,000 tracked files (1.7 KB each) in one object. The maximum is the largest UTF-8 JSON object the whole-string reader can parse, one code unit below the 64-bit Node MAX_STRING_LENGTH for worst-case ASCII, as for recovery.logicalObjectMaxBytes. An object over the bound is refused by this name with its observed size, never truncated.
artifacts.maxObjectBytes.docSummary: Largest single object the durable artifact store writes or reads, locally and in hosted editorial evidence retention. A larger content index is stored in parts instead of being refused.

artifacts.hostedRetentionMaxObjects.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_ARTIFACTS_HOSTED_RETENTION_MAX_OBJECTS, or artifacts.hostedRetentionMaxObjects in the host limits file, above the observed count (at most 32768), and artifacts.hostedRetentionManifestMaxBytes with it if the manifest then refuses, then rerun the same request.
