artifacts.hostedRetentionMaxObjects.rationale: Objects one hosted editorial attempt store may hold when the dispatcher retains it in project CAS (#1932). It replaces a hand-declared 1,024 literal. The largest graph the editorial host writes today is about 1,000 objects (content index parts, up to 128 reader sources and 128 admitted artifacts, decision, context and rationale records, and up to 645 step associations), so 16,384 leaves sixteen times headroom while its manifest, about 300 bytes per object, stays near 5 MiB, inside artifacts.hostedRetentionManifestMaxBytes. The maximum keeps a full manifest inside one 16 MiB dispatcher CAS object. Counted before any object is copied.
artifacts.hostedRetentionMaxObjects.docSummary: Objects one hosted editorial attempt may retain in project CAS.

artifacts.hostedRetentionMaxTotalBytes.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_ARTIFACTS_HOSTED_RETENTION_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES, or artifacts.hostedRetentionMaxTotalBytes in the host limits file, above the observed total, then rerun the same request. Check free space in the project CAS first.
artifacts.hostedRetentionMaxTotalBytes.rationale: Bytes one hosted editorial attempt may retain in project CAS, summed over every object (#1932). It replaces a hand-declared 64 MiB literal that could not hold the 17.4 MB content index of a 10,000-file repository together with 128 reader sources of up to 1 MiB, each stored as base64 (about 1.37 MiB). A content index runs about 1.7 KB per tracked file, so 1 GiB holds the index and every reader source for a repository of more than 400,000 files. A disk-use guard only; the maximum keeps a mistyped value from disabling it. Objects are read and copied one at a time, so this is not a memory bound.
artifacts.hostedRetentionMaxTotalBytes.docSummary: Bytes one hosted editorial attempt may retain in project CAS, summed over its objects.

artifacts.hostedRetentionManifestMaxByte.remediation: Raise DOCSFAB_ARTIFACTS_HOSTED_RETENTION_MANIFEST_MAX_BYTES, or artifacts.hostedRetentionManifestMaxBytes in the host limits file, above the observed size (at most 16777216 bytes), then rerun the same request.
artifacts.hostedRetentionManifestMaxByte.rationale: Size of the canonical manifest that lists one hosted editorial attempt's retained objects (#1932). It replaces a hand-declared 512 KiB literal that held only about 1,700 entries. At about 300 bytes per object, 8 MiB holds the default artifacts.hostedRetentionMaxObjects with room for split-object segment entries. The manifest is one dispatcher CAS object, so the maximum is that object's 16 MiB capacity.
artifacts.hostedRetentionManifestMaxByte.docSummary: Manifest that lists one hosted editorial attempt's retained objects.

checks.commandTimeoutMs.remediation: Run the check yourself before you merge the change, or raise DOCSFAB_CHECKS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS (up to 86400000 ms) so the check finishes in the isolated check executor.
checks.commandTimeoutMs.rationale: Technical capacity. Wall clock for one repository check command in the isolated check executor, for each repository-required and repository-native documentation check (#1932). The default equals the delivery validation backend's 10-minute command timeout (DOCSFAB_VALIDATION_BACKEND_POLICY_V1 in delivery/worktree/validation-backend.ts), so a documentation build such as mkdocs build, sphinx-build, or a Docusaurus build on a 1,000 to 10,000-file repository fits; the previous 30-second clamp stopped them. At the limit the executor stops the command's whole process group; a required check that stops there is a recorded limitation, not a failure, and the patch is still delivered (#1918). The same limit bounds each Git command that presents Git metadata for the checked copy before any check runs (#1918). The maximum stays inside one Node.js timer. Override may raise it.
checks.commandTimeoutMs.docSummary: Wall clock for one repository check command in the isolated check executor. A required check that reaches it is recorded as a limitation that names this setting, and the patch is still delivered.

checks.outputRetainedBytes.remediation: Read the retained head and tail with docsfab runs show <run-id>, or raise DOCSFAB_CHECKS_OUTPUT_RETAINED_BYTES (up to 262144 bytes) to keep more of each check's output.
checks.outputRetainedBytes.rationale: Presentation. Bytes of one check command's output kept in the lint-documentation evidence, half from the start and half from the end, with the omitted byte count between them (#1932). Output volume never stops a check; the previous 16 KiB cap killed a noisy build and recorded it as failed. The default keeps 16 KiB per check, so the run record does not grow. Every check's retained output shares one step summary, which the publication run-record reader admits up to 1,000,000 characters, so raise this with the number of checks in mind. Override may raise it.
checks.outputRetainedBytes.docSummary: Output kept from one check command, half from the start and half from the end, with the omitted byte count between them. Output volume never stops a check.

checks.nativeCommandMax.remediation: Run the remaining documentation checks yourself, or raise DOCSFAB_CHECKS_NATIVE_COMMAND_MAX (up to 256) so one lint step runs them. Repository-required checks always run.
checks.nativeCommandMax.rationale: Cost. Repository-native documentation checks, which DocsFab discovers from package scripts and Make targets, that one lint-documentation step runs after every repository-required check (#1932). Required checks are never capped; the previous 8-command batch left required checks past the eighth unrun and refused the patch. Native checks inform review and never gate a proposal. Checks past the limit are recorded in the step evidence with this limit's name and the number discovered. The default keeps the previous 8. Override may raise it.
checks.nativeCommandMax.docSummary: Discovered documentation checks, such as a `lint:docs` script or a `docs-check` Make target, that one lint step runs. Repository-required checks always run and do not count.

checks.credentialScanMaxEntries.remediation: Run the required checks yourself, or raise DOCSFAB_CHECKS_CREDENTIAL_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES (up to 100000000) so the credential scan covers the whole checkout.
checks.credentialScanMaxEntries.rationale: Cost. Directory entries the check executor's credential scan visits before it masks credential files and runs any repository command (#1932). The scan must finish, so a checkout it cannot cover runs no check, and its required checks become recorded limitations (#1918). The default is ten times the workspace export's 100,000-entry tree bound, so every exported workspace fits with its directories. Raising it widens the scan; it never unmasks a credential file. Override may raise it.
checks.credentialScanMaxEntries.docSummary: Directory entries the check executor's credential scan visits before any check runs. A larger checkout runs no check, and its required checks are recorded as limitations.

derived.lockWaitMs.remediation: Verify that no derived generation is still running in this checkout, because an unrelated process can reuse a stopped holder's process id, then remove the named lock file and rerun. If a regeneration legitimately runs longer, raise derived.lockWaitMs in config/limits/derived.yaml and run npm run generate:limits from packages/runtime.
derived.lockWaitMs.rationale: Longest time the shared derived-generation step (scripts/ensure-derived.mjs) waits on another process's checkout-level generation lock before refusing. Build, typecheck, every Vitest run, and the source-checkout docsfab launcher reach that wait, so a lock left by a stopped holder whose process id was reused must not stall them without a bound. On October 7, 2026, regenerating all four hook families (skill crate, quality pack, limits, model output) took 3.5 to 3.9 s of wall clock per run, three runs, on an 11-core macOS host at load average 6 to 7; the lock is held for less than that. 180 s is about 46 times the worst run, above the 36 times DocsFab allows between its local and CI test budgets (test.localTimeoutMs and test.ciTimeoutMs), so a slow shared runner still finishes inside it. A stopped holder is reclaimed at once; this bound only ends a wait on a holder that still looks live.

conversion.maxNestingDepth.remediation: Flatten the nesting the message names in the source page (directives, block quotes, list items, or emphasis and links inside one another), or raise conversion.maxNestingDepth with DOCSFAB_CONVERSION_MAX_NESTING_DEPTH, then rerun the same command.
conversion.maxNestingDepth.rationale: Technical capacity. Containers nested inside one another along one path in one page that a documentation conversion reader turns into the conversion IR, counting block containers (directive bodies, block quotes, list items, footnotes) and inline containers (emphasis, strong, links). The reader, the construct resolver, and every emitter walk the IR recursively, so the bound keeps one generated or hostile page from exhausting the stack. Real MyST pages nest tab sets, tab items, dropdowns, lists, and emphasis well under 16 levels; 32 leaves headroom. A page past the bound stops the read with this code, naming the page and line; nothing is truncated. Override may raise it to 256.
conversion.maxNestingDepth.docSummary: Containers nested inside one another in one page a conversion reader reads; a deeper page stops the read, naming it.

tensorrtPilot.commandOutputBytes.remediation: Inspect the named offline command and retained Stage A report without copying private child output into the report. If a supported installed command needs more output, measure it and raise tensorrtPilot.commandOutputBytes in config/limits/tensorrtPilot.yaml through review, then regenerate mirrors and rerun the same candidate.
tensorrtPilot.commandOutputBytes.rationale: Maximum bytes captured from each local Git, tar, npm, or installed-CLI child stdout or stderr stream in pilot preparation. Isolated offline source-CLI measurements on 2026-10-14 were 57 bytes for --version, 3298 bytes for --help and 1875 bytes for test --json, each with zero stderr, so 16384 bytes leaves almost five times the largest observed output while preventing unbounded child diagnostics from entering memory. The retained-artifact verifier and offline installer receive this bound only from the pilot harness; their other callers preserve existing behavior. Installed-candidate qualification has not run. No host override is provided for this one-off repository-owned harness.

tensorrtPilot.commandTimeoutMs.remediation: Inspect the named offline command and the isolated host load. If a representative installed command legitimately takes longer, measure it and raise tensorrtPilot.commandTimeoutMs in config/limits/tensorrtPilot.yaml through review, then regenerate mirrors and rerun the same candidate.
tensorrtPilot.commandTimeoutMs.rationale: Per-command wall clock ceiling for local Git, tar, npm, and installed --version, --help, and test --json children. Isolated offline source-CLI measurements on 2026-10-14 were 299, 1570 and 1181 milliseconds respectively; clean-install acceptance documents a 10000 millisecond offline cycle budget. This preparation permits up to three times that accepted cycle budget so a loaded developer host can still report a slow installed check honestly. The retained-artifact verifier and offline installer receive this timeout only from the pilot harness; their other callers preserve existing behavior. These source timings are not installed-candidate qualification. No host override is provided.

tensorrtPilot.installedManifestBytes.remediation: Inspect the installed candidate identity and package.json in the isolated prefix. If the exact supported package legitimately needs a larger manifest, measure it and raise tensorrtPilot.installedManifestBytes in config/limits/tensorrtPilot.yaml through review, then regenerate mirrors and rerun the same candidate.
tensorrtPilot.installedManifestBytes.rationale: Maximum bytes read from the installed package.json before JSON parsing. The current runtime source package manifest is 9064 bytes on 2026-10-14; 65536 bytes leaves more than seven times that size for a distributed manifest while limiting one package-identity read. The harness opens a regular single-link file without following symlinks and reads at most this bound plus one byte to classify overflow. No host override is provided.
